review_text:
Beautiful, warm and cozy interior by Roman and Williams. Cute little bar area. Gorgeous open kitchen.
The menu has three sections, small tapas like plates, starters and mains. We started with the white bean salad with crispy pig and anchovy and the fried eel with curry. Both were wonderfully light but packed with subtle flavor. Our neighbors at the next table let us try their artichoke and egg. It was sort a cross between a scotch egg and eggs Benedict, but cold. Very nice.
For our starter we shared the veal head with creme fraiche and caviar. Over the top decadent. A crispy little pocket filled with unctuous head meat topped with the cream and caviar.
For our mains my wife had the beef that came with gratin potatoes with oxtail, an incredible meal in itself. I had the bourride, beautiful seafood in an ethereal fish broth. 
We finished off with a wonderful cheese plate and a rice pudding that was lighter than air.
We had an excellent bottle of red Chinon from Bernard Baudry.
Beautiful space and excellent celebratory food.

Love to have this place in the hood.  Bartender is cool. Management a bit too stuffy and boarder line arrogant.  
Only had a drink at opening night. Ready to change rating if Starr's menu blow me away next time.

I had never been to Spring in Paris, so was really curious to check this out. The entry-room and dining room were gorgeous, not too stuffy. Had an IPA from Wyoming to start which I hadn't seen before - very good. The menu had truly unique food options. I started with the fried eel which was quite light and tasty, not the least bit oily. My colleague ordered warm oysters which were also excellent. A few of the following courses were so outstanding, that I have a total appreciation for what this chef is doing. The lobster-stuffed baby sea bream served very lightly chilled with a yogurt sauce was perfect. The veal tongue with creme fraiche and caviar could not have been better - Worth every penny. And the 'full' rabbit entree will be recognized as one of the best courses in NYC. The first part was served kinda 'au feu' in a broth, perfectly cooked. The second part was a bowl of rich leg meat in an incredibly decadent sauce that at the same time was not heavy. Serious stuff. The duck with cherries & foie gras was also great, but something we could have potentially experienced in another top restaurant. I didn't try any cocktails but wine list offered a lot of options with age at reasonable prices - very cool. We had a white wine from 2004 that still tasted young. Will definitely be back to try more dishes!

We were a little concerned since the restaurant opened only 2 days ago but the A team was in place. The rooms are beautifully done. The service is professional, attentive but not fussy. And most of all, the food was very good. We started with oysters (bigger ones would be better) but the sauce was incredible. Next leeks, lobster salad, scallops - all shared. For entries  - duck and steak. The foie gras that accompanied the duck was generous and delicious and were the potatoes with marrow. Wine selection was pricey but the helpful wine director suggested a wonderful petite Chablis at our requested $100 price point. For the entries, good choices of red by the glass. Last, we had the best rice pudding ever and gratis sorbet profiteroles. Too much to eat but thoroughly enjoyable evening. Th only problem will likely be getting a reservation when the press catches up. With the trip even from the upper east side.

Fantastic food from a fantastic chef; a very obliging, accommodating and knowledgeable waitstaff; personal ambience, despite high ceilings and possibly because of the exposed cream city bricks that make up a majority of the walls in the (large) space...these are all thoughts I had while dining at Le Coucou last night.

While not necessarily for vegetarians (I don't think many real French restaurants are), the wine list alone would make up for that, were one vegetarian. 

In short, go. It's worth it. I'll be back.

With so many great, new restaurants opening in NYC these days, it's hard to keep up.
But, after reading the interesting NYT article (April 18, 2016) on Le Coucou and how an American chef became very successful in Paris, embracing French tradition, this new restaurant by Stephen Starr was a must visit for me.

As for the ambiance, beautiful interior with an open kitchen.

No tasting menu yet (in the works), so ordered many dishes and created our own, with recommendations from the staff.

Highlight dishes:  All, including the wonderful desserts. 
Most of the dishes are reasonably priced (most appetizers less than $15; mains bet. $20-45).

Highest compliments to executive chef Daniel Rose and his pastry chef Daniel Skurnick for the wonderful dinner tonight.

Many thanks to Frank & Estelle for the impeccable service and great wine recommendations.

My vote for one of the best new restaurants NYC 2016, along w/ L'Appart in Le District.

Highest recommendation.

: 10 calendars

Not feeling this place. Ate there last Saturday night. Wine list is very poor with majority are off brands that are poorly rated and overpriced. 
The food was average. Had the duck. Flavor was good but a little chewy. Would rather have seen it cut thin. 
Three people had the Dover sole and were underwhelmed. Desserts were average. Wouldn't be hurrying back with so many better choices in NYC.

This was Paris in New York. Devine is allI can say!!Raves for this beautiful addition to the NYC dining scene.    It is so many notches above. Raises the fine dining level in the city!!  The  duck could not have been better in juxtaposition with foie gras and cherries!  The  steak was tender and cooked perfectly in a wonderful sauce.  The eel was a must have!  Quenelles were the best I ever had.  The halibut was presented artfully and was Devine.  On and on I could write a book about the desserts and ambience. Service was a little slow but after all only a few weeks old.  Can't wait to return if I can snag a booking!

Ellie

This is an excellent new restaurant with delicious food and service that (mostly) befits it.

We were very excited to try this place because of *both* the chef and the designers, the latter who have created a lovely space that feels very French yet very New York at the same time. It is a lovely environment to have a lovely meal.

We were greeted by three extraordinarily friendly hostesses who made us feel very welcome, almost as though they were genuinely excited to see us. And, for the most part, the evening continued with more of the same. Our water glasses were never empty (my barometer for attentive service); virtually every interaction came with a smile and a warm tone of voice; and the food was delicious from beginning to end.

Choosing a cocktail seemed like a fun activity at the start. At least right now, they're merely numbered #1 through #6 (except for #5, which is, perhaps too winkily, something like #528). There were no cutesy names, which was a bit of a relief. Except that some of the ingredients were a little obscure . . . and even a little under-table Googling provided no insight. With a little elucidation from one of the servers, we made our choices--except apparently even they were confused about which cocktail is which, because we were served the wrong ones, even though they were announced by the correct number. Perhaps this system can be smoothed out.

For appetizers, we chose from the hors d'oeuvre menu (there was a "gourmandises" section of the menu that had pricier delicacies as appetizers, as well): the fried eel (out-of-this-world good!) and the veal terrine (also delicious). Both are recommended.

Unfortunately, the menu is in French with English translations OR descriptions OR elaborations. It's difficult to process--and I might say TOO difficult to process. My co-Yelper and I are adventurous eaters (and drinkers), and there were too many things we didn't know. (My co-Yelper lived in France and is fluent in French, so that's no excuse.) The restaurant has fallen into the recently popular trap of sounding fancy at the expense of clarity. If the menu is going to be in French: fine. But throw us a bone by being consistent and clear. (This, by the way, is the only reason I didn't give Le Coucou five stars.)

For mains, we selected the duck with cherries (and foie gras) and the halibut. The duck was exquisite, and the halibut was very good (flaky and smothered in a white butter sauce). I would order the cherry-duck dish again and again and again. A selection of three cheeses (for $18) was a perfect cheese course to finish the meal.

The restaurant is pricy, and it mostly merits the digits. It needn't try so hard in the area of the menu, though. Try hard with the hostesses, with the very nice bathrooms (Aēsop soap!), with the preparation of the cheese monger. All of these things are wonderful and make me very excited to go back. But a menu should empower diners, make them feel excited about the meal they're about to enjoy, not outsiders uninitiated in the culinary mysteries--which also happen, unfairly, to trip up the servers.

Otherwise, a five-star experience.
Excellent excellent excellent. From the service to decor to the food. Oddly enough there are few places that are fine dining in the French category that get it. Happy to have you le cou cou.

We are big fan of a very special restaurant in Paris, France and we spent years seeking for a similar restaurant in NYC ever since we moved here. We used to go to chef Daniel Rose's Spring in Paris and of course we are very pleased that he brought the new definition of decadence back in US. We love every single dish and the pairing wine we ordered and specially that Lobster tail and that beautiful lauris sauce will sure make me go back there again and again. Great ambience, love the decor, friendly staff, great open kitchen, not noisy even when packed, nice WC music and it's fun to sense the subway passing to remind us that we are not in Paris. XD

Really great experience dining at Le Coucou.  They have an elegant space which is very tastefully executed.  Think upscale and welcoming both at the same time.  The service is another area that shines, 5 stars all the way with what seemed like a entire team of people who were both attentive and sincere (but never intrusive) attending to our meal.  They really strive to accommodate, and they hit the mark.  The food is by acclaimed chef Daniel Rose, and everything we tried was very good.  The rabbit "tout le lapin" and the veal "langue de veau" being two that stood out in particular.  Overall a great experience.  Looking forward to going back, there were numerous other dishes (Bourride and the Duck) which looked very appealing that I would like to try.

Breakfast review. The French love their oeuf's and it's done right at this star of Stephen Starr's restaurant empire. Located in the Blond Hotel(really) this is a glam spot with sumptuous velvet banquettes and velvet baked chairs. Modern chandeliers hang over the space. Fancy French country open kitchen.
Ate:
Pain au chocolat
Oeuf's special
Cafe
The pain au chocolat arrives warm, made in house. The poached eggs with choron sauce  (bernaise with tomato) are perfect served over pomme Darphin- perfectly crisped French hash browns. La Colombe coffee made this a rock star breakfast.

Upshot: glad to have tried it but overall a disappointment, in part because of the hype surrounding the place and the chef.

I had dinner with two friends here tonight. It was a loud scene. Get ready to shout to hear your companion(s). Space is charming but acoustics are terrible.

Service: servers were uniformly terrific. But, the number of staff hovering around us (including what seemed to be several layers of managers) got to feel oppressive, particularly after we had been asked three times in under 2 minutes how we were enjoying our entrees. No joke.

Wine list was hard to navigate and there was no sommelier to be found (odd, given the staffing levels). Menu itself (set up as basically bites, apps, mains) needs a restructure - no need for this level of complication. It should not require multiple questions to clarify what things are and how the meal is supposed to work. 

Food: 

-bread was terrific but I'm not sure we needed both artisanal butter and a smoky/salty/what-the-heck-is-this lard spread (which, again, we had to ask about) as toppings.

-wine: delicious. See above re the formatting of the list. 

-starters: I had the leeks (good but unremarkable and underseasoned) and my companions had the quail (excellent - basically like fried chicken) and the scallop (also apparently very good).

-entrees: I had the lobster-stuffed squash blossoms (just plain bizarre, would not order them again) and my companions had the halibut (good but underseasoned) and the duck (excellent).

-desserts: superb! We had three of them -- red wine cherries (interesting in a great way), chocolate mousse (outstanding) and apricots with thyme sorbet and almond cake (again, very interesting/innovative and the cake was delicious). 

It was on the pricey side, but for a new scene-y downtown restaurant I suppose that's to be expected. 

On the whole this is a wait and see...but at this point they are no Rebelle.

I don't usually write reviews but felt that due to the hype of this restaurant I'd let you know my experience.

Atmosphere: Decor is stunning although the acoustics are strange. Generally more mature crowd. 

Service: Impeccable! attentive + very friendly. I do think that there were a few too many people running around + sometimes our plates were whipped up as soon as I would place my knife on the plate. 

Wine: Very good + sommelier very friendly and understood our needs. 

Food: Here's were I thought there were some fails, this is what my husband and I had:
Bread: Amazing, but like a fellow reviewer mentioned the lard wasn't necessary + I think it could have been a show stopper if they added more seasoning.
Appetizers 
Leek: average, under seasoned.
Lobster tail: again average, but well cooked. 
Entrees: 
Lamb: Perfectly cooked although under seasoned, garnishing were average. 
Bourride: Shrimp was over cooked, but other ingredients incl bass cooked impeccably. Stock lovely and sophisticated but the aioli was so strong in garlic that even the tiniest of drops made you regret your choice. Not good for a Friday night. And without the Aioli the Bourride did lack flavor. 

Desserts: ASTOUNDING!!!!!! One of the most memorial dessert experiences for me. We had the Chiboust à la vanilla with red wine cherries and the Fraises et estrogen which was a gorgeous berry platter that came with profiteroles filled with berry sorbet + whipped cream. 

Price: $320 incl 20% tip for above food, bottle of wine, 2 cocktails + beer. 

We had fun and we did like the place but I don't know if it's quite lived up to the hype.

My wife and I were in NYC for a birthday. Le Coucou was recommended by our nephew. Upon arrival we were seated at a table close to the open kitchen where we could watch the preparation. We were served by a staff of extremely competent and knowledgeable people. My wife had the duck and I had the lamb as our main course. We also enjoyed several appetizers that were heavenly. To our surprise we were even able to meet chef Daniel Rose. The wines chosen by our som paired beautifully with our meals. Overall one of the best dining experiences ever and a great example of NYC food and culture.

Almost perfect...but---sooo new, greeters are still learning to welcome diners.   Rooms are gorgeous, and lighting is divine, so why is the toilet area too dark??  [ Makeup repair is difficult]  The food is delicious, but perhaps the chef could rethink the artichoke bottom to the egg and salmon appetizer, and the halibut entree is too, too, white, and while tasty, suggests blandness. The mousse desert is a delightful surprise, and the wine list offers something for everyone..will revisit, as the overall experience was a good one.

Very warm welcome and a subdued elegant and beautiful room.Lovely bar and open kitchen are enchanting.The food and service reminds one of the extravagant meals of the high flying 80's and is an updated version of the richly flavored and heavily textured meals from Le Caravelle and Le Grenouille.Quenelles!Poached Lobster!Dover Sole!Duck!The Whole Rabbit!
Service was knowledgeable and a little overbearing with requests to top off your wine glass a dozen times in 30 minutes- I must look like my I'm incapable of pouring a bottle?
There are tons of staff milling around and often missing the little details....like dropping some red wine on the menu after pouring and never explaining why lard was being served with the very good bread.
If your in the mood for a trip back to the future the complex and very rich cooking is done very well.The tomato salad was ethereal and the potatoe galette with oxtail a accompanying the beef was a tasty home run.
We passed on dessert since we felt like Eddie Murphy in the Klumps movies by then-hugely satiated and needed a gym workout.

Disclaimer - meal was expensed so not factoring in cost (which the bill, I'm sure was hefty). Might have hurt the wallet for the amount of food we ordered so basing it Solely on amazing service, ambience and great food. Portions were a bit on the small side for the price. 

Space was intimate, cozy and beautiful. Loved the open kitchen and service was impeccable. Some stand out dishes were the chicken and foie gras (larger app) and oysters. For entree- The steak with bone marrow jus and oxtail was divine. The steak was so flavorful and topped with bone marrow and the oxtail accompaniment with potatoes was perfect and luxurious. My friends ordered the lamb and they loved it. Another friend ordered the Dover sole which came recommended by the waiter but it had a heavy brown sauce..which was okay but expected something lighter. If you are getting dessert, pave Au chocolate was the standout dessert. 

Overall amazing dining experience but again we literally sampled everything on the menu without looking at the bill. But really, I'm not complaining!

Great food, good service, nice space 

Fancy without being pretentious; great wine list and they're happy to make suggestions on a smaller budget 

We highly recommend:
#3 drink
Oysters
Tomato and pea salad
Pike quenelle (!!)
Duck
Filet with Oxtail potatoes (!)
Chocolate mousse
Chiboust w sour cherries 

Perfect dinner minus expensive bill, well worth it though

This brought me back to classic New York, well dressed people dining.... Manager coming up to say hi & check on things... Attentive staff, great drinks & wine list... PRISTINE BATHROOMS....
Food:
Amazing!!!
Was so flavorful. One of the best meals I have had in a long time, no corner cutting with this chef and it shows!!!
Will be going back & I rarely go back as there is so much to eat in this city...
Tip:
Go with the Dover Sole!!!

Atmosphere & decor on point as well! Just over all a great experience!!!

Bon Apetit!

We stopped in here last month and OMG, I cant wait to go back.  The service and food was amazing.  There was always someone looking out for us and made it a thoroughly wonderful evening.

Let's start with the bread.  We got spelt and white.  It had excellent texture and flavor.  And then along with butter we were served lard.  While that might sound disgusting.  It isn't.  It was delicious!

For beverages we kept it simple starting with a #3 (gin, cynar, thyme and tonic).  It was their take on a GnT and the cynar added some new dimensions.  Winewise, we went with a glass of the Chinon (a 2007 Cabernet Franc) and Haut Medoc (a 2010 Sejenac) which complemented our mains nicely.

I had the fried quail to start while my wife had the scallop.  The friend quail was super crispy and actually easy to eat despite the bones.  The sauce was lovely with it and it was thoroughly enjoyable.  It's a big starter as well fyi.

For mains, she had the fillet of beef and I had the duck.  The duck was absolutely amazing.  It was perfectly cooked meat along with olives, cherries and foie gras that delivered a perfect bite eater's dream entree.  I tried about every combination I could and was not disappointed in a single bite.  The beef was amazing with the marrow sauce and then my wife had this whole other plate with potatoes and oxtail that could have been its own main.  It was out of this world good and I was glad she had enough to share.  

So I might have been leading going into dessert by a hair, but my wife blew by me with the Chiboust.  Holy cow!  This was amazing and crushed my riz au lait.  The warmth of the baked pastry cream with the flavor of the cherries was fantastic and again, I was glad it was big enough for me to have a few bites.  

Overall, this was an amazing meal and experience. I would not hesitate to return and hope we get the chance before too long

Me and my boyfriend went here for dinner in its first opening weeks and WOW. To say we were impressed is an understatement. We started off with an amazing cheese plate, asking one of their cheese specialists what she recommended. Deciding on the main dish was difficult at first for me as I am a vegetarian and sadly there was not any vegetarian items on the menu, but our waiter was so nice and said he would discuss the issue with the chef. The chef ended up making me a personal dish! It was mixed vegetables and the sauce was mouth-watering. My boyfriend and I got three different bottles of wine throughout the night and each bottle was more delicious than the previous. We are definitely going to come back again. Highly recommend this spot for an upscale date too.

Went for the first time last evening. Can't wait to go back. I had the sweet bread, the tomato salad, fried quail, the veal, rack of lamb, the Dover Sol, the lobster wrapped flower, and every single dessert on the menu. 

You better call 28 days in advance to book your table. Request the table closest to the kitchen to see Chef Daniel Rose and his squad in action. This place is definitely the beez-neez and talk of the town. 

My advice to you readers and reviewers: do not sleep on it. 

Thanks Chef Daniel Rose, you're killing the game.

As close to perfect as I've seen in a while. Food choices, presentation and execution are undeniably excellent. The room is memorable in a city of great restaurants. I believe it is the service that sets this new restaurant apart. From the greeting to the presentation of the check the staff was friendly, accommodating, professional and most clearly passionate. Three stars for certain.

Seldom do you find a restaurant where food, setting and service are this good!  Le Coucou may be new, but the venue is clearly run by seasoned professionals who think of all aspects of the dining experience.  Share it with a good friend or loved one, they'll thank you for it.  Another note, the sound level is able to conduct a good conversation, something I find refreshing.

Here is the deal, I went with my mom and 2 others as a special event. Food was good, but the ATTITUDE was not and quickly ruined any good memory I had here.

Poor rating was for them running my card 3 times and then telling me it was declined. I didn't know it at the time so I was super apologetic, however they were not. they quickly treated me and the table different. I also think they were annoyed we took 2 hours and only tipped 20%.

In NYC food is everything, but so is a restaurants vibe and the way it treats its customers. Far better places to have good food and great service..........

Stephen Starr becomes a Frenchman?   I don't think so, but who cares.

Le Coucou is one of the prettiest dining rooms in the city for sure.  

I liked the service better than the food.
Service was A+   Not pretentious, and very warm.  No attitudes here.
 
Nice wines by the glass ($25. per glass for a Crozes Hermitage and $18 martini, so keep that in mind when ordering 6 glasses!  ;) ).

Salmon w/ soft boiled egg and artichoke way too rich for my blood, bring me a bagel for that cream cheese........same goes for my halibut, so rich with the velvety beurre blanc sauce.....but the filet de boeuf w/ the oxtail and bone marrow was oooh la la delish.

Bread was really special w/ the most delicious butters w/ mangalitsa pork flecks.

A nice evening, however if it's Francais you are looking for, head to Cafe Boulud (same price point and better food), Le Bernardin or Raoul's in Soho (a true French meal and much less $).

I don't know if I would go back to Chinatown or Soho or wherever the hell Le Coucou was by Canal Street, but it was a pleasant evening.

:)

Service and atmosphere , service is nothing short of excellent. 
Uniq French food  with twist.   
Highly recommended it. 
If u around Soho you should try It.

Excellent. Lovely room; floor to ceiling Windows on to Lafayette St., pale washed brick interior walls. Service attentive but not fussy or pretentious. Liked the food a great deal. Had the rabbit dish, Tout le Lapin, prepared three ways which was just superb. Desserts outstanding. No bargains, but that is not what it's here for.
This will be one of my new go to restaurants. The food was out of this world! Can't complain about anything we ordered. Staff was accommodating and wonderful. Absolutely will be going back.

Oh ok, hi "sweet crazy." 

It had been a rainy day. 

Coming in from out of the humid air was nice. PS- only 5pm reservations seemed to be available so, there was that. 

Lovely ambience, we got the corner table next to the window. Perfect spot to see the whole restaurant. The kitchen is in the back of the room and the pass is open and well-lit so that you can peek at the food creations as you walk by. I loved the long-stem candles on the tables. As most articles and reviews indicated, the clientele was a little older and seemed more traditional? 

Menu is clear cut (divided into "lighter" appetizers, middle-sized, and then entrees split into fish and red meat sections yet pleasingly surprising. Basically we picked everything with the words "veal," "caviar," and "foie gras." Does it sound obnoxious? Well, I'm not denying it at least. 

Started with some really nice champagne. I chose the chenin blanc next (hmm, interesting) and he had a pinot noir. 

The veal terrine was only ok, and probably the least impressive of the whole meal. But that probably says more about the loveliness of everything else than the terrine itself. It just paled a tiny bit in comparison to the rich creaminess of the sweetbreads soaked in tomato cream sauce, which was worth asking for more bread. 

Duck was the star of the show as I'd suspected. Melty, perfect stacked with everything else on the plate (mmm foie gras and figs) or by itself. 

Halibut was basically drenched in sticks of butter so, how could it be bad? My date was gracious enough to trade me plates after I'd drowned in enough Lactaid for the meal.

I explained later to one of the chefs as I was passing the kitchen that we could have had two orders of the chocolate mousse. His eyes sparkling, he said, "well, you should say what you want."

Good. I'll remember next time. For both men and for food.

Cheers, sweet craziness.

I am in love with the French again :) I mean French cooking. This time at Le Coucou.

Before coming down here I was concerned this is another over hyped hot-and-new. Yet it does live up to its fame. The service is the best part - at tentative without being pretentious; really patient and fri badly staff. 

Beautiful decoration and dimly lit, def date spot.

Now let's talk about the food. Everything looks great and delicious on the menu. My fave section is the Gourmandies which consist of mostly savory small plates. We opted for the lobster tail salads in sauce Laurie which is made of mayo, creme and paprika. Amazing . The presentation is simple and elegant. We also had the sweetbread in tomato creme sauce. Oh boy, this is prob some of the best seeetbread I have had in the city. 

For entree I got the rabbit three ways. One word, mind-blowing. It served in stew form, baked with caramelized onions and creme, and seared rabbit leg topped with rabbit liver in its own jus. It took me back to my dinner at Chez L'Ami Jean - rabbit with spring veggie in pot. The soup in the stew is the essence of the rabbit think bonito dash I in Japanese cooking. I will come back again just for this.  Grind got the duck breast which she def adored tho I didn't try (got pulled away for a business call, at 9:30 pm, bloody Corp America :/ ).

To wrap up the dinner we got comp sort meant of dessert including dark chocolate with sea salt , some citrus jelly and cookies. Nice but nothing exceptional.  

The wine list is another bright spot of Le Coucou. If you think know which to go with, ask the sommelier. 

It certainly not the restaurant I will come back every week. But I shall def come back every now and then.

I don't understand this restaurant. Plain and simple - I don't resonate with the hype that comes with Le Cou Cou. 

What is this restaurant trying to achieve here besides dancing in French decor? My amazement at the menu stopped when my squash blossoms arrived. The dish died from flavor and fled from depth. 

The only thing that prevents me from giving this restaurant two stars is the impeccable service and team spirit. Waiters and waitresses weren't pretentious and snobby. I felt like they really made recommendations to my party from the bottom of their hearts and not high noses. I loved the service but am ultimately disappointed at the dishes that Le Cou Cou offers. 

I still intend to visit this restaurant again and give it another chance because the service team makes me believe!

This is a beautiful place with many kinks to work out. Showed up for a 2pm reservation on a Saturday. My table was not ready as it is to be expected in NYC. I sit in the diminutive lounge and the bar is not tended. No one in sight. After 10 minutes I ask a "confused-looking" staffer about the bartender. He didn't know.

Finally someone shows up behind the bar and I order 2 glasses of wine. By this time we are called to out table and have to transfer the order to the table.

The brunch menu is incredibly limited. Le CouCou is a big disappointment

Another Stephen Starr restaurant done well!!! It's a beautiful French Restaurant that we can't wait to go back to!

We went for Brunch on a Sunday around 12:15. It was only the second day they were open for brunch and things were a bit of a mess. Le CouCou only has a breakfast menu currently but we were told there is going to be a brunch menu in the future. The service was great but everything took forever. The kitchen was definitely having trouble keeping up with the brunch service. 

To start we ordered a Pastry Basket which was supposed to include the chocolate croissant, queen's cake and another puffed pastry with gruyere cheese. That puffed pastry they had sold out of by the time we ordered so we never got to try it. But our waiter did try his best to find one, even going to the hotel kitchen to see if they had any left for their patrons! It took a really long time to get the other pastries but it was worth the wait. The chocolate croissant was perfect. The star was the queen's cake which i don't remember the French name. It is puffed pastry with butter and sugar served warm! We loved it so much! 

For meals, my brother had the Ouef Special which was two poached eggs served on potato pancakes with a creamy hollandaise sauce and tomato jam at the recommendation of our server. It was the star of the brunch. I kept using his sauce on my egg's because it was that good.  I had the regular breakfast with 2 eggs, bacon, potato pancake and toast. The toast is great. The eggs lacked flavor and were bland but once you add salt and pepper it was good! The potato pancake is scrumptious. It has no onions which I loved because I hate onions and is just crispy delicious potato!! My mom had the omelette without the herbs and agreed the eggs needed salt and pepper. 

Overall, Le CouCou was a wonderful experience. We all want to go back but it just has some kinks it needs to work out!

Le Coucou is a gorgeous, traditional french restaurant on the border of Soho and Chinatown. I'm glad to see a transition away from modern, hip, tapas-style restaurants and back to traditional dining. 

The restaurant almost belongs uptown, with the elegant interior, professional servers and white tablecloths and real candles, without all the stuffiness and formality. 

The portions here are surprisingly generous. I came here for a really early 5pm dinner and got the rabbit 3-way, which is a must-get. The 3 different cooking methods offer variety in a single "dish" and it feels like you're eating 3 separate entrees. 

They have a beautiful bar by the entrance, I'd recommend coming a bit early and grabbing a drink by the bar if possible.

Went for our anniversary, Mario Batali and family at the next table, so this is a serious place. My reaction to Coucou was extremely positive, thought the design was terrific, and the service was really great. The kind of restaurant you feel special in. The food was quite good, but not to the level of the design or service. Everything was really good, just didn't quite hit the highest notes. Also got a nice bottle of red at a fair price.  Same food at a different place would be a 3 star review, but the place is really special and I'll definitely go back.

Le coucou was a fantastic experience all around. The service was on point- extremely attentive and friendly and polished. The food was all excellent- we had the oysters, leeks, pike with lobster sauce and filet. All of the food was well executed and flavorful with great textures. I also had the #6 cocktail and a glass of the burgundy wine. I would recommend both. The ambience was classic with a bit of edge- beautiful bathrooms and appropriately loud music, but most of the pleasant sound level came from open kitchen and conversation. A classic and thoughtful restaurant in a downtown setting- not a common combination.

Dare I say it, it was better than 90% of the food I had in France? I came here for my birthday, not knowing anything about the fuss and how hard reservations are for this place. They recommended the rabbit threeways which was good but I could say the same about chicken. I would order the warm oysters and sweetbreads again so delicious!! However I will definitely make it back here just for the prime filet with boke marrow jus!!

Well though brunch probably is the least representative among all meals Le Coucou serves, and the menu was quite limited to be honest, I can still confidently say that it was both delicious and pleasant.

We arrived an hour earlier than our original reservation time (don't judge) and were seated without any issue. Each got the avocado toast with greens, we also shared the fruit salad with coconut yogurt. Size might be a potential complaint here as the fruit salad was literally only several tiny bites, but trust me, it was good! They used the thick whole wheat bread for our avocado toast - very crunchy. The poached egg laying on top, was so oily and carried a fluid texture. Simply loved every bite of it!

Welcome back, chef Daniel Rose; and thanks for bringing your French cuisine back home! I've gotta try the main dishes some other time!

I'd give a 4.5 if I could.

Must get: wagyu tripe, quenelle, and cote de boeuf! They're all amazing and leaves you wanting more. The cote de boeuf is one of the most expensive dishes on the menu but totally worth it. It comes with a baked sliced potato with delicious shredded oxtail. Just thinking about it makes me drool.

Don't get: desserts...we tried the rice pudding, the chocolate pave and chiboust, all of them were disappointing and not worth it. 

When to go: great spot for a dinner date! Candlelit dinner but it's not too dark. Romantic ambiance and impeccable service. 

Other tips: if you can, request the tables near the kitchen on the inner part of the restaurant. It's more beautiful. 

More details: the endives appetizer is average so not a must get. Decent wine selection. Average age of the diners here is higher and price point is higher but definitely worth coming!!!
Loved the ambiance and decor, also the crows was quite interesting. The menu was short and limited, but for a French restaurant it was on the light side. Enjoyed it, would definitely go back again.

I had my second dinner at Le Coucou last night. Love love love this restaurant. Everything was great, food, service, wine, atmosphere, just perfect. As a wine lover, perfect pairing of wine and great food is very important, so I always ask somelier for wine picking. Last time I was there  as party of 5. Somelier Stephanie picked 4 great bottles for us, last night I was there with my friend,  again she picked fantastic bottle of white, and 2 glasses of red. What I like about Stephanie is she understand what I want right away. I highly recommend to talk to her to pick wine either you know or don't know wine.

My new favorite NYC restaurant! A very difficult reservation to get but well worth the effort. 

This space is elegant and chic, sophisticated and hip all at the same time. I love that they have moved away from the small plates trend that has become so common and instead that each guest is encouraged to order their own hors d'oeuvre, appetizer and main. 

We were seated just between the front room and the back room with a view of the entire restaurant. The menu is modern French. I adored the red burgundy by the glass. 

The food is exquisite. Leeks with hazelnuts and the lobster tail to start were both excellent. The leeks were incredible tender with crunchy hazelnuts sprinkled on top. The lobster was perfectly cooked and served with butter lettuce and a lauris sauce (mayonnaise, cream and paprika). 

I adored the Dover sole with mushrooms and concord grapes. The sauce elevated this dish as it was rich and buttery. Bourride was a black bass that was clean and very light with a main white fish served with a pot of shellfish including langostine, mussels, clams and peewee potatoes. 

Pavé was recommended for dessert and it was fantastic. A rich chocolate tarte of sorts was accompanied by praline ice cream and a bit of a caramel mousse. 

Service was polished and professional.

Getting a reservation was a challenge but it was worth it. Very elegant, exuberant  and quaint setting . Our dining experience was so exceptional that this is indeed one of the hottest restaurants in NYC, by EATER NYC.
Service: A+ or 5 stars; from the maitre D to the wait staff, they exemplify what the real definition of customer service.
Food: A+ or 5 starsCelery  root- very flavorful, Quenelle de brochet- the lobster sauce was so delicious, Dover sole, was cooked to perfection with chanterelles mushroom to top was amazing.
Desserts:  we had choosen 2 cheeses from California plus chocolate mousse... both just closed the satisfaction of our palate.
Everything was wonderful. We will definitely put Le Coucou as one of our favorite restaurants in NYC!

Came here for dinner with my boyfriend and wish I could give 4.5 stars.  

We had an 8:30 reservation on a Saturday, which took a couple months of trying to finally be able to get.  Definitely worth the wait!  The decor of the restaurant is very elegant and romantic.  The burning candles are a nice touch, and according to our server, they are replaced for every new guest.

Service was spectacular, from the hostesses, to the bartender to our server, everyone was very attentive.  We ordered glasses of champagne at the bar and then ordered glasses of white to go with our appetizers, glasses of red with our main, and an after dinner drink with desert (oops).  As for the food, we were impressed that only 2 items on the menu were not gluten free.  
We shared two appetizers and two deserts and each got a main dish:
Veal terrine.  This was not my favorite dish of the night, but it was still quite good.  It was pretty meaty, had a nice herby flavor and good texture. 
Lobster salad.  This was delicious.  They give you a pretty generous lobster tail, a wedge of lettuce and one cooked tomato.  The sauce for the lobster is divine and the lobster was perfectly cooked.
Duck.  I got the duck as my main dish and thought it was the star of the night.  The fat was perfectly rendered and the olives offered a nice salty balance to the sweetness of the fig and the sauce. There's also duck heart on the dish, which I was very surprised I liked, it was very tender. I just wish they gave you more duck - you only get 3 pieces.  But, you get a generous portion of foie gras, which was out of this world.
Filet.  My boyfriend got the filet, which was a huge portion.  It came with a side dish of oxtail potatoes, which could have been a main dish by itself.  I tried a bite of the filet and it was cooked to a wonderful medium rare.  The jus was delicious and the steak had a nice peppercorn flavor.  Note though, that according to my boyfriend the bone marrow that sits on top of the filet was not good (maybe he just doesn't like bone marrow).
Cheese course.  We got one of the cheeses as a pre-desert course.  I thought the cheese was yummy, but probably could have done without.  They only have about 5 cheeses on the cheese board, so the selection is not that vast, especially considering I don't like blue cheese which was one of the options.
Chocolate mousse.  I thought the chocolate shavings sprinkled on top were very good,  but again I probably could've skipped this desert.

Overall, I'm happy we finally came and I will definitely be back to try out other items on the menu!

It's so far over the top that I can't see the top from here. 

A #528 (exceptional), #6 (also exceptional), a bottle of white, a bottle of red, and two glasses of sherry later, our party disappeared into the night. But first, we made notes on the meal over cappuccinos and petit fours.

-ABSOLUTE MUST-
1. Anguille frite au sarrasin (buckwheat fried Montauk eel with curry vinaigrette) - Like nothing you've ever had before, or will ever have again.
2. Crépinette de volaille with foie gras & stone fruit - Think chicken burger, topped with a slab of foie gras and jammy, roasted plum.
3. Tout le lapin (all of the rabbit) - Bunny, 3 ways. Ever had a 3-way? This is better, albeit barely less hectic. 
4. Chiboust aux figues with port wine & cinnamon - Blows every french dessert made of cream away. Talk about crème brûLAME. 

-WORTH IT-
1. Celeri remoulade with apple, smoked salmon & walnuts - The lightest dish that's worth the stomach space.
2. Quenelle de brochet (pike) with lobster sauce - A rare treat, done in a suspiciously light and fluffy manner. A must try if you never have. Puts gefilte to shame.
3. Pavé au chocolat with hazelnut praline ice cream - You can get this elsewhere, but it doesn't mean you should.

-SKIP IT-
1. Poireaux (leeks) with hazelnuts - Simply not as special as the other hors d'oeuvre.
2. Canard (duck) with mission figs, foie gras, & black olives - Decadent and flavorful, but less unique and tender than the crépinette.
3. Riz au lait (rice pudding) with pistachios - Mild, bland, and less sexy than the other desserts. 

Write drunk, edit sober, Yelp somewhere in between.

Daniel Rose and Stephen Starr's new restaurant is an exquisite combination of French cooking and sophisticated elegant style. Le coucou had a similar unique feel to Starr's other NYC restaurants (think Budakkan, Morimoto, El Vez). It's hard to get a reservation for regular dinner hours so make sure to make one on OpenTable exactly when they open at midnight about a month ahead of the desired date.

The meal itself was delicious and all the hostesses / service worked great together. Water was filled within seconds of being sipped and all the food came at the perfect time. Our waitress not only explained what each dish was but recommended how to eat each one. This was one of the few restaurants where the service was not only accepting but PROACTIVE about food allergies, pointing out menu items in each section that we could order.

We had an excellent dinner experience and my boyfriend even preferred Le Coucou to Le Bernadin (known as one of the top French seafood restaurants in NYC) as the food portions were larger and the atmosphere was more casual. Most guests still wore jackets although not required. I especially loved the atmosphere created by tall thin white candles burning in the middle of each table that slowly shortened throughout the meal.

We tried:
Drinks:
***Cocktail #2 - rose, aquavit, elderflower with a slice of cucumber
***there is an extensive wine list with bottles from regions all over the world. A few are also offered by the glass

Appetizers:
***Endives with Iberico ham bits
***poireaux (Leeks with hazelnut) - pricey for leeks but I found this way of cooking interesting
***everyone is offered a basket of bread with butter and lard spread

Entrees:
***Tout Le lapin - rabbit 3 ways (Hind leg with onions and mustard, front left stew with carrots and turnips, medallion with liver jus)..the stew was so savory and my favorite
***bourride - black bass with shrimp and various shellfish in a delicious stew, served with garlic aioli

Dessert:
***poached quince, ginger sorbet, almond financier - it was my birthday so they even stuck a candle on the plate!

The place is beautiful but the food is really sub par. I went there for brunch and had a very mixed experience  the pasties and clafoutis were delicious , however the baked eggs, the avocado toast and croque monsieur were very average to say the least . The eggs came uncooked and all of us had to send them back for additional heat. 

In summary . Probably one of the most beautiful restaurant  in nyc but need a major improvement on the food quality . Will give it another try in a couple of months.

Kheuanne kham is why this review is so low.... service was lackluster and downright rude.. never encountered such unfriendly behavior

Good: 4.5
Decor: 4.5
Service: 1
Absolutely loved this place other than the sarcastically unfriendly staff kheuanne. The duck is a must have and so is the fried eel. The decor is very beautiful.

The restaurant is beautiful.  Service amazing.  Food was excellent. The chicken & foie gras dish was by far my favorite.  I literally said OMG, it was love at first bite. 
We were a party of 5 and spent over 2 hours there & never felt rushed.
Love the open kitchen (& chef hats!) where you can see everyone so focused and dedicated.
It was such a wonderful experience!

When I first called the person (man) taking the call Saturday 12/3 at 11 am was very rude. I asked if we could come for brunch without a reservation. He was angry because he said there was no more room and that I should not even try. My girlfriend really wanted to go for her birthday so we ended up going getting to the restaurant at 1:30 pm. We walked right in with no wait. The female hostess is as very nice. I had the  wrapped with chicken. My girlfriend had the ribeye steak with foie gras. Both were wonderful. With a mimosa and red wine the meal an waiter service was great. Getting a glass of water and bread was challenging. So to sum it up, the location was lovely (great bar), the meal and waiter were very good. But for the price I was upset about experience of getting into the restaurant. Would I recommend it? Well they need to up the service and speak too whoever took my call Saturday 12/3 at 11:00 am (male). I would not have gone if my girlfriend did not insist ... she really enjoyed it.

I wanted to love this place. I've traveled all over the world, entertain clients in all of NYC's restaurants and tend to always try focus on the good. However, nothing in this restaurant was very memorable or anything I'd need to come back for and I love French food.  Everything for me fell short, but most of all the service, as our waitress barely cracked a smile, it really put a damper on our experience, not to mention the service was very slow.  Additionally, there's a lot of hype about getting a reservation here and I for one as instructed, set my alarm clock to midnight in order to reserve on Open table 28 days out, only to be told the next morning at 8:45 am over the phone that I wasn't quick enough, nor was I the only person trying to secure a reservation this way, that they were sorry, but they were already overbooked for the day I was seeking.  I found it really hard to believe, but I persevered, eventually agreeing to a different date and a 5pm table.  When I needed to push the reservation back by an hour, they agreed with the caveat that I'd be out by 8pm.  And if this story so far isn't irritating or frustrating enough, when we arrived and when we left, there were at least three empty tables. The space is beautiful and some of the dishes were good, but not good enough for indifferent service, a non-memorable meal and the battle that you'll ensue for a table.  You can skip this and you wont' be missing out on anything.
When you're fancy but not stuffy & boring, you come here. Amazing service, amazing food...date night never had it so good.

Getting a reservation here was quite the challenge and without the help of the 11 Howard concierge, we would have missed dinner here.  The dining room is indeed beautiful - it's also warm and inviting.

Our main server was formal but not uninvitingly so.  The French server assisting him was a totally different story.  He was just so sour - wonder why he is so disdainful when he works in the service industry.  Even in the nicest restaurants in NYC and Paris, I have never found someone who acted so formally and unfriendly.  It didn't mar our experience but it's worth mentioning.

The food is what I describe as excellent refined bistro food.  There were four of us so we were able to sample a fair number of dishes.  My favorite was the duck prepared three ways - seared foie, the breast and duck livers.  I was in heaven!!!  The whole rabbit and tenderloin were both great entrees with a number of sides - bring your appetites.  For the appetizer, I ordered the lobster salad which was well-prepared but did not stand out for me.  The leeks surprisingly was very good and light on its feet (if it had any!!!) - I'm normally not likely to order a vegetarian appetizer and will likely not but it was fun taking bites.  The veal terrine was DELICIOUS!!!  My brother-in-law ordered this and decided to stop after eating half of it.  I happily helped him out and finished it!

Dessert was not memorable.  To be honest, it's only been a couple of weeks and I can't remember what we had.  I am going to get on my soapbox for a minute - restaurants need to make sure that the desserts are as good as the food.  It feels like dessert was an afterthought which is too bad because it's one of my favorite parts of the meal.

On a side note, I've been to Spring which is Daniel Rose's restaurant in Paris.  I have to say that the patrons are so much better at Le Cou Cou as we sat next to the most obnoxious American couple at Spring a couple of years ago who felt the need to do impressions of Jerry Seinfeld and Fran Drescher all throughout dinner.  It really spoiled our dinner so it was great to have a lovely dinner at this restaurant.

I'm a New Yorker so I'm always looking for the next hot spot. Le Cou Cou made The NY Times list of top 10 new restaurants. It's an intimate space with subdued lighting in a well designed space. Thee are only about 30 tables so small. The wine list is extensive but very expensive. We got one of there lower priced bottles of white wine at 60 dollars. The menu is limited to seasonal offerings and heavy on fat heavy entrees. There serve a plate of lard as an accompaniment to the bread.  The food was very good. I had warm oysters with a butter sauce and sea bass in a seafood stew. All wonderful. My major complaint about this restaurant is the service.  From the minute you walk in the door you feel like you are inconveniencing the staff by being there. The restaurant was empty for our 530 reservation on a frigid NY night and the staff made us wait by the coat room until our whole party arrived. At least have a decent bar area or lounge to wait in or let parties sit when at least half the party has arrived. Our waitress was unfriendly and condescending. Not appealing when you are spending over 400 for4 people. I would go back again but I hope there is an attitude adjustment in the staff. This is not Paris there are too many great restaurants in NYC and New Yorkers expect more.

I read all the rave reviews and braved the daunting reservation process to finally secure a late (10:00 p.m.) dinner reservation mid-week. We got there right on time, and it immediately became clear that our meal wasn't going to be the experience we had hoped for. The maître d' was quite unwelcoming and told us tersely to wait as our table wasn't ready. It soon became clear that another guest was taking up all his attention as the coat check staff appeared to have lost his coat. Eventually (about 15 minutes later) the coat was found, and at about the same time we were told our table was ready. Conspicuous in its absence was any explanation or apology for the delay, which surprised us (in my experience, most top-tier restaurants will offer an apology). 

The food was not memorable.  As appetizers, we had the veal terrine, sweetbreads, lobster tail and pike quenelles (a signature dish). All were mediocre. The sweetbreads and quenelle were in rich sauces that had the texture and flavor of Indian chicken tikka masala sauce without the heat. The quenelles had the texture of British nursery food, and while I appreciate that it's a classic dish, reviving it isn't a good idea. Entrees were the rabbit (another signature dish), the Dover sole (the best dish of the evening), lamb chops and the fillet of beef. The rabbit was done three ways (saddle, legs in a dashi-like broth with what tasted like lemongrass, and with onions in a sauce that tasted like au-gratin) and had nothing compelling about any of the presentations. The lamb had a vaguely middle eastern/Indian vibe because of a tomato and eggplant accompaniment. I really have nothing to say about the beef other than that it was pleasant and unassuming. Desserts were chocolate mousse, chocolate pave and rice pudding. The first two were acceptable (about the standard of desserts in a hotel restaurant), the rice pudding was awful. Overall, dessert is the weakest point in the unremarkable food at Le Coucou.

Service is on the unfriendly side. Things didn't pick up after our interaction with the maître d'. The waiter who took our order was not particularly helpful in describing dishes or making recommendations. Bread was dumped on the table. Wine glasses weren't promptly refilled. No one paid any attention to us as we left. At the top end, these lapses are unacceptable. 

The one bright spot is the wine list, with a mix of marquee producers and some interesting selections from less-known areas and producers. There are quite a few fairly priced wines on the list. The sommelier recommended a rather nice Bandol at a good price.

At bottom, Le Coucou doesn't seem ready to compete against NYC's best, past or present. The food isn't original or distinctive. The service is competent but unwelcoming. Perhaps its best recommendation is that it doesn't force guests to endure a long tasting menu, permitting a la carte selection. But it still has a long way to go to catch up to stalwarts like Jean Georges, Daniel and Gramercy Tavern, or newcomers like Gabriel Kreuther and Fowler and Wells.

Brunch is my favorite meal, so I went here for brunch.  I had gotten one of the last two remaining brunch time reservations.  When I arrived, I was seated at the table closest to and facing the kitchen and counter where a server was making french press coffee. Only half of the tables were filled, so I certainly could have been seated at a better table.  The service and food were fine.  I ordered the Coucou Compleat.  It was a nice meal, but I should have been seated at a better table.
Best restaurant in Nyc right now period end of the story. Food is outstanding service is remarkable.

Le Coucou is in a league of its own - no other meal I've eaten in 2016 can compare.

To begin, the staff is incredible - from the minute you step inside the beautiful, dimly lit restaurant you are treated as a friend by the hostess, then the waiters, and then the sommelier. Although an upscale restaurant, the staff were friendly, funny and helpful.

We had the most wonderful table seated near the open kitchen, where we watched Chef Daniel Rose and his team at work. It was high energy and fun.

The food is out of this world. Truly - it's totally otherworldly. Well actually it's perfectly worldly for traditional French food but this is a cuisine that I am not very familiar with and greatly enjoyed the unique flavors and precise cooking techniques.

Highlights : the pike quenelle with lobster, the unbelievable sweetbreads, the celery root, the chicken with foie gras:grilled pineapple and the bourride. Oh my god the bourride. This out of all the wonderful food was number one. Prepare yourself for the most delicious fish stew - bass, shrimp, clams, mussels and potatoes in a delicate but flavorful fish broth served with a side of garlic aioli, meant to be stirred into the soup. Don't miss this dish!!!

The only dish that didn't blow me away was the fried Montauk eel, because to be honest it tasted as though it could have been any white fish. I expected the eel to have a more unique taste but it didn't. However, it was still perfectly cooked and very tasty in a curry sauce but it wasn't as shocking and memorable as the other things we ate.

What really stands out at Le Coucou is the simplicity of each dish and the outstanding sauces. I wanted to lick each plate clean - tarragon sauce, and lobster sauce, and curry sauce, and garlic aioli. 

We ended on the loveliest note with a simple dessert of cooked quince, ginger sorbet and an almond financier. 

I can't imagine a more perfect meal - from the food to the setting to the service to the excitement and uniqueness. I cannot wait to return.

We had a great time at Le Coucou on Xmas Day. Place is great and staff are awesome. Appetizers were amazing - warm oysters, scallops with celery root were both outstanding. so much so we ordered them twice.

My only issue is that I was not crazy about my entree - and for $50 for Dover sole, you'd better wow me. I can't stand shitake mushrooms and it was covered with them, so that didn't help, but overall, the flavor combo was disappointing.

Avoid dessert as well. Nothing to write home about.

Divine perfection! The world is a better place post Le Coucou. For a few minutes last night, I forgot about The Donald, the loss of my fav musicians, & that i've ever eaten a cold wrap sandwich from Pret A Manger.  It was the perfect anti-dote to the horrors of 2016. The chef & entire ensemble experience was heaven sent from start to finish. We went all out & it was well worth it every savory bite of the way.  Each dish was outstanding but some particularly noteworthy to me - celery remoulade, duck, chicken with foie gras & plum, and rice pudding. The cherry on top was having reasonable wine prices to choose from. If there were more stars, I'd gladly use them!

It's an accomplishment just to get a table at Le Coucou, and once you're in you are rewarded with a thoroughly French experience. It's not the kind of food you can eat everyday, maybe not even monthly, but what they do with food truly seemed like something you would experience in France. The food is froufrou, but the ambience and service are not. It's dark and slightly medieval, but intimate with long candlesticks on every table. The waitstaff could've been more attentive, but were very good at explaining the menu (for someone who does not each French food often, it definitely helped guide my expectations). 

Great: 
Sweetbreads: a very substantial portion, supple, with an amazing sauce. They leave the pan of sauce at the table. I requested more bread to sop up the sauce, so I won't judge you for doing the same.
Tout de Lapin: all of the rabbit, aka one of the most famous dishes of 2016. Spectacular presentation of 3 separate dishes, each showcasing a different preparation of rabbit. Tasty enough, but imo this was more about celebrating the entire animal. Very French, at least 1 person should order this.
Filet de bouef: perfect, more perfect with the bone marrow jus. They threw in a side of oxtail potatoes to make it over-the-top good. The oxtail is cooked melting, topped with crisp thinly sliced potatoes. 

Okay: 
Pike Quenelle: reminds me of a fluffy fishcake, which doesn't sound that appetizing but I actually enjoyed (or rather appeciated) the interesting texture and the sauce it comes with is so good. A few bites was enough though, the portion is too large. 

Skip: 
Warmed oysters, which taught me that oysters should always be cold. 
Endives au jambon: pretty vinegary, which just enhanced the bitterness of the endive. 

The main meal is very rich, so we kept dessert light. The Poire rôtie is a whole poached pear with ice cream inside, elegant and not too sweet. The Chiboist aux figues was like a cloud made of cream, also very nice. 

My main gripe is the service, which I expected more from considering the prices. I was disappointed that they forgot to note that it was a special occasion. Otherwise, an eye-opening meal into French cuisine in the middle of NYC and a good option for date night.

Okay, I just stayed up past midnight to try to book a table here for 28 days hence and despite repeatedly refreshing the page, Open Table went from telling me right before midnight that it was too soon to book IMMEDIATELY to telling me at midnight that there were no tables available for the day I was trying to reserve a table for.  And we tried this last night too.  Sorry, but this is BS way to handle restaurant reservations.

Went for brunch with a friend and had to see what all of the hype was about.  Started with a Kouign amann, which tasted like cheesy popover perfection.   Shared the french pancake, apples, crème fraîche.  To call that dish delicious would be an understatement.  Also had the Oeufs Basquaise, which were satisfying with a Bloody Mary to cap over a perfect brunch experience.  Looking forward to scoring a dinner reservation next.

Here is what we ordered from the $48 Prix Fix lunch menu, with 1-5 ratings:

- Anguille frite au sarrasin -- 5
- Salad d'automne (endive, celery, bibb lettuce, walnuts, arethusa blue cheese, Iberico hama) -- 3
- Tartare de bœuf -- 5
- Côte d'agneau grillé, saveurs du sud -- 3
- Salade de homard (poached lobster, grilled romaine, citrus, sauce lauris) -- 5
- Desserts -- rice pudding with Chartreuse (3), Baba au Rum (3), Chocolate (4)

So, food was mixed. 

For wine there are many excellent choices, but pretty expensive from high double digits to mid four digits. We ordered a $176 Cabernet Franc -- 5+.

Now, service was extremely good, a solid 5: pleasantly informal, very professional, very friendly, very attentive, without ever being intrusive.  What was cool is that when we complained about the near absence of Chartreuse in the rice pudding, the waiter poured us a nice glass of this delicious witches' brew. A good & smart gesture. The kind of thing that stands out and makes you want to come back.  Which we will.

I gotta break my recent Yelp absence to review this gem of a restaurant - and I'd give it 5 stars, except I haven't tried the dinner tasting menu yet and that probably wouldn't be fair! For the brunch though - 5 stars for sure.

(Also, my bf said this was one of the best restaurants I've dragged him to. And that's saying a lot!)

Le Coucou shone in both the delicious homey food and ambience. I'm not a huge Stephen Starr fan since some of his concepts are a bit hit or miss, or end up placing less emphasis on the quality of the food. But Le Coucou was a real delight. 

The food: because we didn't want to shell out the $$$ and couldn't get a reservation for dinner anyway (lol), we came by for brunch, a little unsure of what to expect. The food was rich and so scrumptious. Le Coucou is not the type of restaurant that attempts to dazzle with overly contrived dishes or incomprehensible menu descriptions. Its dishes are classic, but are done so so well.

My bf had the lobster crepe. Of course the lobster portions weren't that substantial but it was still so worth it. The crepe was creamy, fluffy. Every mouthful went so well together. 
I had the poached eggs on potato pancakes, with some insanely sweet diced tomatoes on the side, and literally mopped up every bit of the sauce and yolk. 

We also shared a pastry basket, which included a croissant, 2 chocolate croissants and a giant gruyere bread thing with melted cheese inside as it fell apart in our hands. It was waaay too much food but no regrets!! Overall, the price was also very reasonable for brunch in NY, and a steal for the quality of the food! 

The ambience: not stuffy at all, perfect for a leisurely chatty brunch, service was attentive but not overbearing or excessive. I appreciated that our server got me a grapefruit mimosa that wasn't on the menu. Also, we were there on New Years Eve and watched them hang up enormous bunches of pastel pink and transparent balloons in preparation for the night. Very pretty. 
The only minus was that we waited 15 mins to be seated, despite turning up on time for our reservation. But by the time we had finished eating, we couldn't care less. 

Note to self to come back again, hopefully soon!

Le Coucou has quickly become one of my favorite brunch spots in Manhattan and my go to whenever I am looking for a nicer brunch option. If you love French cuisine and are a sucker for stunning ambiance, this is your place. I have tried every item that is Pescitarian friendly on their brunch menu and one cannot go wrong with their clafoutis with seasonal fruit paired with a cappuccino. Bon appetit.

Only had two dishes, but both felt off to me. The quenelles (I'll just call them souffle dumplings) were wonderfully fluffy but came with a lobster sauce so intense it saturated my palate after two sips, and lingered even after a glass of water. Half the portion would have been just as satisfying without the salt overload. Rabbit three-ways delivered on two: the onions with the hind leg could have been caramelized more to ease the sharpness. The saddle roulade with mince was moist if unremarkable (except for the bits of bone I had to spit out), but the pot-au-feu truly saved the dinner with its heady melange of herbs and hint of Asian aromatics (lemongrass? kaffir lime?). Service was on point if a bit sterile. Overall, a tad too rich for me, though the classique/nouvelle menu intrigues enough that I might visit again.

Hot mess of a lunch.  This was one of the most disappointing restaurant experiences. I had two dishes highly recommended by the NY Times restaurant critic--the eel and the pike quenelles.  The eel arrives as three thick, greasy tubes that proved near impossible to cut--the extensive breading and the fish were just that tough.  After a piece went flying I gave up. The staff noticed the mostly uneaten dish and offered to get me something else but the part that I did manage to consume weighted like lead on my stomach, so was no longer interested in another appetizer.  The pike quenelles were similarly very heavy, but that was not the problem--both myself and my lunch companion ordered the dish and it was extremely heavily salted.  When asked how everything was my companion told the waiter he should let the chef know that the sauce was badly over-salted.  After the eel episode I wasn't going to say anything, but as he did, I concurred.  More food was again offered. we decided against dessert but they brought one anyway for us to share (ironically, a chocolate tarte with salted caramel ice cream) that was good.  The wait staff were lovely, too bad about the food. The food was so heavy I had a stomach ache for the rest of the day (my companion was French and I spend a lot of time in France, so rich food is by no means foreign, but the ensuing stomach ache was).

A testament to how decadent and rich everything was here: the day after dinner, I got a pimple. Maybe my second one in a year.

But don't let that deter you (or do, so I can get reservations easier next time)! This meal lived up to all the hype, and there was a lot of it. I came in a group of four for a late dinner (9:15) on a Wednesday night, and we rolled out of the restaurant well after midnight.

The food was divine, cocktails well-made, ambience lively, and service extremely friendly. I won't comment on the wine we had except to say that it was a reasonably priced red, and that's about all I remember (this speaks less about the wine and more about my own palate).

Food ordered included the sweetbreads, pike quenelle, and fried eel to share as starters (first two were amazing, third was still good but not mindblowing). I chose the rabbit as the main, while my friends got the duck, bourride, and squab. Everyone was more than happy with not only the taste, but also the portion sizes, of each dish. Seriously - that rabbit, while pricey, could've easily fed two (unlike at many other restaurants of this price point). Same with the bourride and squab.

After reading reviews, I didn't expect much from the desserts, but they were also fantastic. At the GM's recommendation we ordered the poached quince (I wasn't the biggest fan, but one of my friends loved it), lemon chiboust (MUST GET, this is fantastic and I'm still dreaming about the light citrus meringue), and pave au chocolat (rich, delicious, amazing, basically nutella ice cream and a solid block of chocolate ganache). The amazing GM also saw that someone at the table really wanted the chocolate mousse and sent a complimentary one out for us.

Overall a fantastic meal. I can't wait to come back, if only reservations didn't require so much dedication to get...

Shout out to Troy and Chad for helping to make that night really great :)

Lunch 2 people

Salat and duck confit which was great
Eel and halibut. The eel came in a curry sauce which was a little twist. The classic halibut with beurre blanc so was simple and so well prepared.

Pear for dessert which was filled with ice cream. 
We liked all the dished
Service was great

Sommelier was helpful.

Only negative was they listed the bougogne we had as a premier cru when in fact it is not.

Since I can't get a ressie for dinner even though I called 28 days in advance, I decided to try the luck for lunch without a reservation and just walked in.  The gentleman at the front was very nice and gave us a small table at the side though throughout my time dining, there was definitely open tables still but non the less I was grateful to be able to have a delicious birthday lunch with my auntie.

We came for lunch on a Saturday and it was a brunch menu... how boring, so much  hype and press for a classically well decorated SoHo place with a basic overpriced eggy menu? You really could have been anywhere. 

The gougères were delicious but the oysters were disliked by most of the table. Throwing foie gras over a dry piece of beef will not hide the dry pice of beef. Make it clear to Americans that a "crépinette" really is a single chicken meatball.  The sommelier did a good job, she must be sorry she works there with all those slow people and that boring menu.

There's a reason why Le Cou Cou has been named the best restaurant of 2016 by various food critics. This is the hottest restaurant in NYC right now and I don't see that slowing down anytime soon. The space is beautiful and grand yet cozy at the same time. The service is impeccable, not stuffy or pretentious as you may find at other fine dining establishments. Everything we ordered was delicious, you can't go wrong with any dish. The handsome sommelier, Aaron, was amazing as was Kat. Thank you both for such a fun, delicious meal with my family. We can't wait to return. Best restaurant of the year!

Came here for dinner and brunch in December and got a fair sense of the run.  I have to say, the food - proteins especially were some of the best French food I've had.  The interior is also very beautiful and appetizing.  Open, spacious, not too loud, not too quiet.  Real candle stick light on every table during dinner service.  I love the extremely open kitchen.  You can see all the actions but none of the mess.  Front of house was great, bartender was very friendly.  Solid wine list and a small array of classic cocktails.  Le Coucou has everything it needs to be 5 star.  However, I had to deduct one star for small and large oversights on seafood and service.    

I agree with some of the reviewers.  Skip the oysters.  In fact, to ensure an amazing experience, I suggest skipping all seafood.  I happen to love oysters both warm and cold but the warm oyster with seaweed butter just wasn't interesting.  The raw bay scallops were delicious though.  Succulent, clean, refreshing and carried all the good notes of the sea.  Bourride had good flavors, but I couldn't figure out why they decided to leave a completely shriveled mussel in the pot.  Also found a piece of fish scale in the bass.  And then during brunch, found a small piece of lobster shell in the lobster.  

Here are wows: They really know how to treat their land animals.  All the meat dishes were phenomenal.  Veal tongue was a thick slab of juicy and tender goodness.  Canard et cerises was my favorite dish and I don't even like ducks in general.  Duck meat was perfectly cooked, together with the divine companionship of figs, fois gras and olives to deliver layers of delicious flavors and texture.  Rich, satisfying but not heavy.  Veal Terrine was also really tasty and is available at Dinner and Brunch.  Very clean and texture was just right. 

What went wrong? Servers were great but water service was surprisingly not careful.  Attentive but sloppy.  Our table was wet over and over again and my iPhone nesting next to the glass was showered. What's worse?  The water guy didn't even notice.  The pace of the courses was a little off that night.  And then brunch had a major mood killer as they were setting up dozens of balloon clusters throughout for NYE during the busiest hour of brunch service.  Balloons were popping left and right creating unpleasant surprises of noises and dust. The balloon manager was also walking around talking on speaker phone.  Discretion completely out of the door.

A few last tips: 1. Avoid the bathroom if you easily get songs stuck in your head. (Catchy song playing on infinite loop). And the hot water at the sink gets extremely hot in a split second.  2. Bread service during dinner is great and free. However they charge $4 for a few slices of toasts if you ask for it at brunch.  3. Order the duck.  4.  If you have to do brunch, don't order brunch food.
Excellent breakfast,attentive service, charming charming atmosphere. Just delightful!! Will go back soon!

We dined here Christmas night great experience  chef & staff were extremely hospitable. It's a cozy place decorated nicely staff is on point we ate almost everything on the menu. The wine list is very good. The food is simplistic in style/design but not in flavor! Clean flavors not overpowering or heavy we had allot of food h three stunning vintage wines along with some great cocktails  the desserts were also on point best rice pudding I have ever had. Defenitly a must visit restaurant!!! It was really nice to get some time to talk with Chef as well as the head sommelier very nice people solid food & wine program!!!! Keep up the good work!

Le Coucou appeared on almost every list of best new restaurants of 2016, so it was with great anticipation that I visited Le Coucou for the first time this weekend, to celebrate my wife's birthday.

I will cut right to the chase and explain why I only give Le Coucou three stars:
--portion size: the leek appetizer consisted of six two-inch pieces of leeks for $12 and the bourride, although delicious, could have benefited from a few more clams and maybe a piece of lobster for $38
--service lapses: we found the service to be most attentive for the first half of our meal.  However, we were barely given a moment between the clearing of our main course and presentation of the dessert menu and delivery of the dessert.  We also observed issues with communications between servers at nearby tables.  It took several minutes to get the attention of a server to order coffee
--comfort: there are two tables in the room that seem to be poorly situated and we were seated at one of them.  One was just in front of the captain's station (our table) and captains and servers frequently approached this station, crowding our table somewhat.  The other table is located right in the doorway between the outer and inner dining rooms.  Avoid this table at all costs.

Strong points: raw scallop gourmandise was delicious.  Leeks, although portioned small, were also delicious.  Bourride was wonderful, but could have been served warmer.  Wine list broad and fairly priced.  Wine servers knowledgeable.  Room is lovely.  
Dinner for two with one starter, one gourmandise, two mains, one dessert, one coffee and a $70 bottle of wine was $250, including tax and tip.  I would certainly return, but, overall, think nearby Batard does similar food at a better value.

So far, this is the best French Restaurant that I've been to in NYC. It's been described as rustic, elegant and spacious. It is all of those things. Each dish that was brought out had an extreme originality. The menu description gave no indication of how great each dish was. I was able to share a French styled lunch with multiple dishes and wines over a three hour period at this beautiful venue. I will return again. FYI it's has a great location for those coming from the UES as it's close to the 4,5,6 train. I'd love to be able to try everything on the menu.
Great ambiance.  Brunch was very good but not amazing.  A good place to catch up with friends.

Best place in NYC my fave I love an open kitchen here though it's as if they dance the waltz while cooking it's gorgeous , if you go and love food I'd say sit near kitchen . Chef is amazing genius , I love everything about this place and I'll go to any new venue he launches

Great meal, beautiful space, totally worth it. Madison was fantastic along with the rest of the team. Prime filet with bone marrow was fuego along with oxtail potatoes. I tried my sister's duck and died a little bit, it was so good. I tried my gf's scallops too and those were on point.

The staff is knowledgeable and give you lots of time to chat while you peruse the menu. Go with a decent size group so you can try lots of stuff! Or go for a fun date night.

The food was pretty good although heavy. I had to ask for a croissant four times until they eventually brought it. The decor inside is nice and the food was fresh and tasty but they can improve on service.

Taking one star off because my very first impression from hosts were not very good however the food was great and service at the table was superb. It was a busy night, but it really was not best way to start the evening, with an attitude.

We came on a Friday night and sat by the kitchen. Such a beautiful restaurant. My favs are the beef with oxtail, crispy tripe, lobster in squash blossom. The fish with the boulibasse was just ok. Will def return to try the rest of the menu.
