As someone who's been in NYC for almost five years, I've had my time of chasing after the latest restaurant opening and recently reviewed hotspot. More often than not, I've left the venue with with mediocre, if not disappointing, impressions, so I arrived at the latest charmer, Le Coucou, with a fair amount of skepticism. The restaurant opened in 2016 under the oversight of restaurateur Stephen Starr (of Upland, Morimoto, and El Vez fame) with Chef Daniel Rose overseeing the kitchen; while the chef is originally from Chicago, his previous kitchen experience has been solely concentrated in Paris, France (at Spring and La Bourse et La Vie).

It should go without saying that reservations here are nothing short of difficult to obtain. I was lucky enough to snag a table for lunch on Christmas Eve and the three of us arrived here on a chilly Saturday afternoon. Even upon first entering through the impressive front doors, there's a sense of opulence and elegance throughout the entire restaurant. Le Coucou calls itself a "bistro", but the cavernous ceilings, the concrete and brick walls, and the mullioned windows are more reminiscent of a castle than a casual lunch spot. Just as refined are the white tableclothed tables, each with its own flower vase and sugar cube holder.

The brunch menu has a number of classics, across savory and egg-based dishes to some sweeter offerings, and also has several heartier dishes that can be found on their dinner menu as well, including the pan-roasted chicken and rib eye. Our trio decided to start with a Pastry Basket for the table, which included a Croissant, two Pain au Chocolat, and a Kouign Amann. I personally prefer savory pastries, so I have to admit I loved the flaky, airy layers and textures of the standard croissant over the denser and sweeter chocolate-filled pain au chocolat. I was most delighted by the Kouign Amann, though, which is a more savory take on the typically sugar-crusted pastry, and features a fragrant, cheese-filled center.

As my friend and I couldn't settle on either a savory or sweet dish, we opted to split the Oeufs Coucou and the Comme un Clafoutis. The first is a take on the traditional Eggs Benedict, plating a poached egg on top of a pomme darphin and generously topping it with Choron sauce. Every single element on this dish was done to perfection; the eggs were beautifully and evenly poached with the quintessential runny yolk, the potatoes were crisp and well-seasoned, and the sauce choron was creamy and rich, with the distinct edge of tomato blending throughout. For those with a sweeter tooth, I would recommend getting the Comme un Clafoutis, or "like a clafoutis", a traditional French custard-like dessert. Le Coucou's version is more like an oversized pancake, and the version we had featured sliced and spiced apples topped with a generous spoonful of crème fraîche. It's well-portioned and not overly sweet, although I do wish that the pancake wasn't as monotonous in texture. I believe the fruits featured changed seasonally as well, but I believe a tarter, more acidic fruit would hold up better in this dish, especially with the addition of a syrup.

It's difficult to gauge the caliber of a restaurant based solely on one visit, especially if that meal is brunch, but I have to say that I left feeling impressed and looking forward to making a return visit for dinner. From what I have seen so far, Le Coucou has done well with keeping to the principles of traditional French cuisine and delivering an excellent final plate.

From the outside the beautiful design is everywhere thru the entire inside and the food not complicated or overly rich but well prepared and delicious. Service excellent. GO! Lobster salad a must. Best fillet of sole. Wonderful desserts. Great lighting, high ceilings, a candle on every table. Glad I went and will return!

One of my best fine dining experiences where the rare occurrence of me liking everything I tried meets the bill not breaking the bank. But then again, I have a soft spot for French cuisine. Our party of four tried the following...

Appetizers:
Leeks & hazelnuts ($12) - need to get those veggies in eh. Jokes aside a great simple dish to get our appetites going.

Chicken & Foie Gras ($26) - how can anyone not like foie gras especially when it's enclosed in a chicken meatball?

Pike quenelle & lobster sauce ($33) - AMAZING must recommend this soft fish and with sauce I would drink up as soup!

Veal tongue & caviar ($38) - simply delightful, tied with pike quenelle as my favorite appetizers

Main dishes:

My friend and I shared the Duck Breast & Foie Gras ($43) and the Lamb Rack ($45) so I can only comment on these two, but they were delicious. Both meats were done well at medium rare. I especially liked the foie gras and duck breast pairing with fig sauce, my favorite sweet & salty combo. 

Deserts:

We really went all out and tried every dessert that wasn't simply sorbet or ice cream (not indulgent enough, we joked) and each got a tea.

Chocolate mousse ($13) - Mmmm so decadent and heavy, a bittersweet cocoa lovers dream

Rice pudding ($12) - My favorite along with the chocolate mousse. It's light and fruity making me feel like I can gobble up bite after bite of this

Roasted pineapple and sorbet ($12) - can't go wrong with cake and ice cream! 

Lemon confit and shortbread ($12) - tasty but not too memorable tbh

Every with the bottle of red we split the bill came out to be ~$120 per person. Great value considering the amazing dining experience I had. 

Can't wait to come back for brunch!!

4 on a Sunday, 630p, winter

Veal terrine - solid and good
Quenelle de brochet - technically beautiful, very large, messed with the sauce/quenelle ratio in each bite.  
Sweetbreads - great display of ingredient, I wanted more contrast between crunch and creamy, very fine, delicate crust that didn't overshadow sweetbread
Raw scallops - quite good, great texture and balance

Beurre blanc halibut - so incredibly satisfying.  textbook clarity and intensity of flavor.  It makes you understand why the saucier position exists.
Pigeon and lobster - very good, hard to share and get a good taste.  The pair competed rather than complimented.  A dainty reference to the gruff, gaudy surf and turf. 
Bourride, seafood stew - very light, clean, depending on mood, may not be satisfying 
Duck - superbly cooked, addition of olives was a bit of a delight, delicious

Rice pudding - nice, familiar, but not elevated enough to want something else
Citrus chiboust - good, hadn't ever heard of this preparation
Cheese - all from the united states, all impressively delicious

Cocktails, wine, coffee

Excellent and elegant service.
Excellent food, satisfyingly technical and precise.
We got what I thought was a great table.  Center banquette, a good view of the open kitchen.  It was very immersive.

Great details throughout - table service, decor, food, but not overly complicated or exaggeratedly ceremonious.  It was one of the most thorough, composed experiences I've had recently.

The only reason it's not five stars is because I'm not dying to go back.
Beautiful Place.  Been here three times in the past year.  Best breakfast ever! Dinner is amazing too.  Staff is very elegant and friendly.  They know what they are doing here.  Definitely go!

I can't say that I've ever had a better dining experience in NYC.  This team and property truly delivered on all levels.
  
1.  Accommodating host that was able to squeeze me in last minute.  I had no expeditions of being able to dine here but it happened. 

2. Decor...amazing light in space and felt warm and comfortable the entire space has amazing components that few may see if eating in a group.  Pay attention...

3.  Ryan my waiter rocked it on the food recommendation

4.  Arron the bad ass wine guy hooked me up with the perfect wine for my meal.

It felt great to have someone else drive my decisions for once.  Make a reservation, sit back....enjoy and appreciate what you are experiencing.  This isn't a place you want to rush through.

Cheers

I just came back from a business lunch and my was I more than impressed.  This restaurant harkens back to the 'old' days of glamorous but refined NYC restaurants. From the decor, service, presentation, attention to detail and of course food everything about this experience was superb. 

We started with the lentil soup and salad and excellent bread and butter.  The lentil soup was served in the pot it was prepared in and layered with pieces of ham and spring lettuce. Just incredible.  For my entree, I ordered the grilled lamb chops and side of pommes frites. It was incredibly tasty , not gamy at all and cooked to perfection.  My clients had the halibut which was just amazing and the beef tartare with the best mix of ingredients.  Simply put, one of the best meals I've ever had and I am a native New Yorker!

As for the ambience, it is a perfect setting for a business lunch.  We were seated in the back room with a view of the working kitchen which was just so impressive.

Unfortunately, we couldn't stay for dessert but was offered 3 pieces of chocholate and small cookies.  They were very good.

Le Coucou is an instant NYC classic restaurant that will be here for a long, long time.

My friends and I settled for brunch at Le Coucou since we could not get reservations for dinner. The first thing that captured my attention when I first entered was the gorgeous bar! We loved the interior of the restaurant (the chandeliers reminded us of Harry Potter and the open kitchen was charming too) and how the sunlight streamed in from the large floor to ceiling windows. Plus points for providing Aesop scrub and soap at the restroom! This place exuded the vibe of a hidden sanctuary in the Chinatown/Little Italy area. Ambience aside, we did find our brunch experience a tad underwhelming. We started with a pastry basket to share, which came with 2 pain au chocolat, 1 croissant and 1 gougère. Sadly, we did not get any kouign amann in the pastry basket. But we enjoyed all the pastries - the croissant was very flaky and buttery, loved the cheese used in the gougère, but the pain au chocolat was the standout!

We skipped over the usual eggy brunch items and picked the 3 entrees available on the menu instead:
1) Chicken and foie gras, roasted pineapple: this was my order. I was initially contemplating between this and a lobster, egg & buckwheat crepe, but our server recommended this - "a little more interesting", he said. And indeed it was. We were all surprised when the dish was laid down before me. Mostly for two reasons: Firstly, it looked like a meatball / burger patty! Secondly, it was small... But I guess, never judge a book by its cover. This was actually our favorite of the 3 entrees. The foie gras was enclosed in the chicken meatball/patty. The chicken meat was very tender and the combination of all the flavors from the chicken, foie gras, roasted pineapple and sauce (don't know what it was) was umami.

2) Whole poached lobster tail, grilled romaine, citrus, sauce lauris: the lobster was undoubtedly fresh and poached well. A very light salad dish.

3) Thinly sliced ribeye seared on the plancha, relaxed foie gras and a side of potato pancake: Looked a bit "blah", but tasted fine. Nothing to shout about imho, and I thought the potato pancake was a little greasy.

Portions were French-sized, so we still had space for dessert. Unfortunately, the dessert menu did not entice us so we didn't order any. Based on our experience, I would rate this place 3.5 stars. We were impartial as to whether to still give this place a shot for dinner.

P.S. The menu on the website is not updated...

Ambiance: Classy, elegant. The bar is also exquisite. 5 / 5.

Food: Each dish was truly fantastic. I admire the work of the chefs and the staff here. The food was the best I've had in New York City. That Le Coucou did not receive a Michelin a star is a travesty. 5 / 5.

Staff: Extremely knowledgeable and polite. Great detail is put into service. For example, while pouring your water, the staff guards your glass with a napkin to prevent any splashes from getting on you. Further, when rearranging the table to fit dishes, the staff ensures to put your glasses / silverware back into virtually the same exact place. The level of service was truly remarkable. 5 /5. 

Bottom Line: The food is of comparable quality to the big boys in NYC (Eleven Madison, Daniel, etc.). If Le Coucou maintains its same level of service and quality of food, I think it will get the Michelin star it deserves. I will certainly return.

I heard more about Le Coucou than any other restaurant in 2016. It heralded the return of fancy French cuisine, the revival of grand, white tablecloth dining, and it was the best thing to happen to Manhattan since Hamilton. As I am perpetually behind the times, I just got here in early 2017 (and judging by the difficulty in obtaining a mere weekday lunch reservation, I will never get here again).

While we did dine as a foursome, for me this was really a platonic man-date with my perpetual heterosexual food/life partner, Ruggeford H.J. As I gazed into his dreamy eyes, the rest of the room just melted away. My only regret is that he made me go Dutch (because this is not a cheap meal), and that he made me pronounce the hard French words to our server (because I looked like the uncultured asshole that I am). 

Let us be clear: 

This is a wonderful restaurant. The room, the service, the flatware, the wine, the cocktails, the freaking hand soap in the bathroom...it is all exceptional. I don't dine at this price point often, but Stephen Starr knows how to make it feel like a special occasion. 

I started with a yellow chartreuse cocktail whose name escapes me (and is no longer listed on the menu online), and it was impeccable. From there, we progressed to the two-course prix fixe, sharing as heterosexual food/life partners are wont to do.

HORS D'OEUVRES

Both the céleri rémoulade and the poireaux (leeks) were delicate, interesting, and tasty. That said, somewhat forgettable. I appreciate the smoked salmon and apple combination with the celery root, but neither that nor the carefully braised leeks left me aching for more. I wouldn't say I was disappointed in either dish, just not blown away.

POISSONS ET VIANDES

The Pike Quenelle is worth discussion. Instead of merely cooking a piece of fish, the chef has whipped the pike with cream and egg and reconstructed it into an impossibly tender flan of fish. Texturally, it is unlike anything you've had before, and anything laid into a bowl of their sauce américaine (essentially an even more buttery lobster bisque) will be absolutely delicious. Down to and including cardboard. 

Similarly, the chicken and foie gras was not quite what I was expecting, but notable nonetheless. It was a richer and better chicken meatball, for lack of a better comparison. The pommes purée was delicate and also rich, and the roasted pineapple a welcome sweetness.

These two dishes far outshone the starters, and I thoroughly enjoyed them. My criticism, if anything, is that I might've preferred more texture from both the mains. They were both rich and soft on rich and soft...not that I have anything against butter, but it was decadent and verging on too much, and almost one-note for such an acclaimed kitchen. The quenelle technique is extremely impressive, but I wonder if it's technique just for technique's sake. I don't know if whipping the fish makes it a better dish, or simply more interesting. 

If this at times sounds like a negative review, I apologize. This restaurant is almost inarguably fantastic, but whenever I enter this rarified and luxurious price point, I can't help but be more critical. It's difficult for a working man to justify these prices, and I find myself trying to do just that.

In any case, if you don't enjoy your meal at Le Coucou, you don't enjoy dining out. But if you enjoy receiving a check for $150/person at lunch (no, YOU drank too much), you're buying next time.
Fantastic food and service. One of those places you want to tell your friends about; will go back soon.

My 5 star goes out to breakfast at Le Coucou, and I canNOT wait to come back for dinner.  I was luckily sat at the very end of the hall where I got to see both dining areas. Every part of the restaurant I could probably snap a photo and have it be "Instagram worthy". The chandeliers, brick walls, high ceilings, and flower decor all made the interior one of the most gorgeous places I've been to in NYC. I see why Le Coucou has been talked about so much among food enthusiasts for the past couple of months - the whole dining experience is definitely something else. Considering the fact that this is a $$$$ restaurant, I didn't think that the breakfast menu was too crazy. Everything ranged from approximately $15~$30, which in NYC is considered "normal" for some people. 

As a party of two, we ordered coffee, chocolate croissant, avocado toast, side of sausage, and the typical breakfast combo. The warm and soft chocolate croissant was pretty fantastic, and it complimented our coffees super well. Trying out pastries from here is a MUST, as they accurately replicate the famous pastries of France. My dish of scrambled eggs, bacon, toast, hash brown, and greens ($16) was perfect both portion and taste wise, and I don't even remember what about the food I didn't like, because I was too distracted by the crispy bacon to focus on anything else. The avocado toast also looked delicious, but I'm not the biggest fan of avocado, so I can't tell you much on how that was. Regardless, everything we ordered was worth the money, and if I could, I would come here for breakfast everyday.

I also realized that the ambiance, mood, plating, great service, and interior all made my food taste so much better. I was blown away by how stunning my table looked (as you can see in my photo) after we placed everything. I swear the lighting was also designed so that when you take pictures of the food, it HAS to look delicious. It's really hard to forget the reinvented feel of dining in a rustic yet modern, classy yet comfortable, and Parisian+Scandinavian environment in NYC. The dinner menu definitely does look expensive, but I would love to come here with people I truly love because every trip here would be end up being memorable. 

I heard you have to make reservations weeks in advance for lunch or dinner. Do it. It's worth the hype.

An absolutely beautiful setting combined with very solid food, but I can't give the place a perfect score on two counts: 1) I've never seen stingier pours than from the sommelier here ... when paying $24 per glass, it would behoove you to be more generous; 2) the service was a bit frayed and unprofessional. Again, with a setting that's so beautiful, perhaps management should polish the staff to match.

My fiancée brought me here for my 24th birthday. 
Let me tell you it was the most magical dinner. Better than 11 Madison park. Yeah I said it.
I still talk about it and it's been 7 months.
Our server was awesome, I wish I got his name. 
Can't wait to be back :)

We went to this restaurant for our third anniversary last week. I must say that it was one of the best dinners we've ever had in NYC. Very tasty food. We've tried le bernardin and 11 madison before. This meal is def tastier than 11 Madison and is very close to the level of le bernardin.
Outstanding food, service was amazing, French waiter really gave it its authenticity. Still don't understand how me and my gf got 2 free deserts but well appreciated.

Excellent, upscale and in a class of it's own. Food is comparable if not better to the signature New York french restaurants. The is innovative without being fussy.
Service is excellent.  Anecdotally, the glass partition next to our table was accidentally cracked by the gentleman next to us, the staff handled the incident professionally, attending to our comfort with the minimum of fuss, no big deal. 
We had dinner but I would go back for breakfast and lunch as well.
Slow to seat us, at 9:15pm, on a sunday. Pretty shitty table and everything else was fine. the decor is as pretty as the plaiting.Go for the sweetbreads.

My boyfriend and I had lunch here today and it was delightful. The restaurant is just gorgeous, airy and yet warm. You feel like you are in Europe. The entire staff from the front desk to the waitstaff was exceptionally helpful and kind. We were lucky enough to be seated at one of the tables where you are literally able to watch everything that goes on in the kitchen, what a treat. They are absolute pros, it is like dining in a theater. However, the best part by far was the food. Everything was just perfect and delicious. I got the salmon roulade to start, so good! Light and flavorful, I didn't want it to end! And, the bread they give you is made in house and is so, so good. For my main I had the poached lobster tail over grilled lettuce with grapefruit. It comes with a side of a creamy/buttery sauce. If you like lobster then you must order this, it was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. My boyfriend (who tends to be pickier than I am) got the leeks with hazelnuts which he loved and the lamb which he raved about. I really don't think you can go wrong here. Everything looks just delicious and the presentation is perfect. I can't wait to go back. Really an all around delightful and fun experience, from the gorgeous decor, to the unpretentious but attentive and helpful service, to the perfectly executed meals, this is a true 5 star dining experience!

Loved the food but they have to do something about the cloak girl. 

My mom and I checked in our coats and the guy that greeted us was super nice and gave us a ticket. We were quickly seated and our server was super sweet and so was everyone else. Dessert was on spot as well and overall we had a great experience and loved the decor! 
But... as we picked up our coats I gave the cloak girl our ticket and she brought mine only back. So I said we actually have another coat, and said it's a "purple coat with fur". She came back two minutes later with a TOTAL attitude and handed us a coat and said "Do you call this coat purple?". WOW. You don't have to be so rude just because you've never seen different shades of purple. It's a grayish light purple. I'm sorry I didn't think I needed to explain in that depth, guess this chick has never bought anything in Italy? RUDE. Ended our experience in a bad note.

Everything Peter D wrote echoes my sentiments on this highly-acclaimed restaurant - in fact, we dined together at the lunch he refers to in his review (you wouldn't know it since he only had eyes for Ruggy). The space itself is beautiful and the service was impeccable. The wine program was a real standout - recommendations were expertly paired and I enjoyed every last drop along with my meal.  

I started with the poireaux which was oh-so-French and not too heavy but also not entirely memorable. Next I moved on to the pike quenelle which was an impressive display of technique. The sauce américaine was over-the-top indulgent and the lobster claw provided a meaty bit of contrasting texture to the dish. Absolutely delicious. 

I am a lover of fancy things and Le Coucou is no exception. Though lunch was a pretty big splurge, I was impressed enough to want to return. And if someone else is footing the bill, even better.

By far one of our favorite new spots in NYC. It's so amazing that it's hard to know where to start. The space has huge ceilings with white distressed brick walls and huge perfect chandeliers. The entire space feels like you stepped into a French secret spot that only you and the ladies that lunch know about. 

We were here twice in a week, yes it's that good. Between the champagne cocktail w Meyer lemon bitters w a raw sugar cube to the great wine selection, you are taken cRe of. The entire staff were cordial and very friendly. We were given some great insight about a specific wine region growing facts. 

The food was to die for. The rib eye steak and eggs sounds normal till you put it in your mouth. There is nothing normal about the best cut of meat cooked and seasoned to perfection with perfectly cooked eggs. The Gougere that Brian had was huge but who cares. It was dense and yet airy the size of a large softball. The Oeuf special with the sauce Choron, basically hollandaise w tomato, served on potato pancake was beyond anything I've had in this category. 

Needless to say we have only had breakfast here and want to try their dinner next time we visit. I'd recommend this place without hesitation.

Le Coucou was everything I wanted it to be and a little more. I went for brunch and had a truly delightful experience. Not only was the staff friendly and attentive, but the food was tremendous. I had the Crépinette de volaille au foie gras et fruits d'automne - highly recommend. My friend had the Quenelle de brochet, sauce américaine and also raved. In addition to those dishes, I had to try a chocolate croissant because that a staple of any great French breakfast / brunch. Unsurprisingly, they make a fantastic croissant. If you've been wanting to come to this restaurant or try it - I say book now! If you can't get into dinner, go for a weekend brunch or morning breakfast.

I'm not sure if all New Yorkers eat like this every night, but Le Coucou was a pretty fancy experience, which also comes with a price. Either way it was worth every penny. The wife and I checked it out with another couple just recently. The atmosphere is perfect for a classic French experience with soft lighting and you would think yourself in a Parisian restaurant. I was pleasantly surprised that the tables were not all jammed together and that the noise level in a full dining room was not really noticeable and no shouting was needed to carry on a conversation. Noise level was not even affected by us being seated almost in the kitchen, all the while being able to see the kitchen in full action.

We started off with drinks which meant that the table was full of wine, cocktails, beer and fine bourbons when all orders were put in. All options for drink were good and plentiful. Both signature drinks that I had were great and original flavors. Bread comes out quickly accompanied with butter and some lardo spread, which was phenomenal. For hors d'oeuvres and appetizers we chose the leeks, scallops crudo, quenelle and 2 orders of sweetbreads. Yes 2 orders, because I wasn't giving up my order and our server told us that we needed 2 and would not regret it. Well, our server definitely knew what he was talking about and all diners partook in the sweetbreads, even the wife who was enticed back to the dark side of meat eating. The leeks were perfectly cooked and refreshing in contrast to all the heavy sauces from the sweetbreads and quenelle. The quenelle was ordered so that we could experience it. It was delicate and the flavor in the lobster sauce was intense. The wife's lobster allergy precluded her eating any, and overall the sweetbreads were the star of this round and quite likely the whole evening. 

Onto mains, our table was full of duck, halibut, bass and rabbit. I didn't taste the duck, but both fish were expertly cooked with the bass beating out the halibut for me as the butter sauce was a little too rich for me. I, of course, had the rabbit mostly to myself which came prepared 3 ways and included everything from the legs to the loin and liver served up in a roulade. Another great round of food, but we were all still talking and thinking about the sweetbreads. Sadly no more sweetbreads for us, but rather dessert was next. Our table shared the chocolate pavé, the omelette norvégienne and the rhubarb dessert. All were good depending on which one falls in your flavor profile but the rhubarb was voted the best.

Overall the food was probably 4 star plus, but the service and attention to detail was definitely 5 stars and put Le Coucou over the top. With no fractional star rating from yelp, I will upgrade the experience to a 5 star night.

DOUBLING DOWN AT NYC's HOTTEST NEW RESTAURANT: LE COUCOU

[This is Part 1 of a 2 part review.  Click below for Part 2.]

***Shortly after I wrote this review, LCC won the 2017 James Beard Award for "Best New Restaurant in the US."  Congratulations!"***

Philadelphia mega-restraunteur Steven Starr, best known for his hugely popular (but in my opinion ultimately uninspiring) "concept" restaurants such as Buddakan (Philly & NYC), has in recent years turned over a brand-new leaf: partnering with exciting culinary talents and setting them free to do what they do best.  My favorite example of this being Philly's brilliant Serpico, a showcase for Chef Peter Serpico, the Michelin-starred, James Beard Award-winning ex-chef of Momofuko Ko.   Amiee Oxley's Talula's Garden is another.

SoHo's Le Coucou, is the latest Starr venture in this vein, featuring the talents of Chef Daniel Rose who, although from Chicago, has gained acclaim in Paris for his restaurants Spring Restaurant and La Bourse et La Vie.  Le Coucou is his first US restaurant (another is reportedly on its way, again with Starr).

Opening less than a year ago, LCC quickly became the talk of the foodie press, so I was very excited to join my good friend Dave on his second visit here.  This being a quick overnight trip, I decided to make things easy by staying at the hip new 11 Howard hotel in which LCC is located.

Arriving around lunchtime, our first thoughts were about where could we grab a quick bite to eat before heading off to see the Morgan Library...hmmm...lol, how far is Papaya King?  But wait, can you believe that LCC actually has one table for two remaining in what was otherwise a packed weekday lunchtime crowd?  How about that???  Two meals at the same French restaurant in the same day--sure, I'm game!

FOR LUNCH, we enjoyed (two $48 2-course prix fix lunches; a la carte is not available):

~~Pétoncles, vinaigrette à la clémentine (raw bay scallops, celery, chestnut, clementine)...Given our dinner plans, something light appealed to me, and this was a charming plate with the strong, fresh scallopy flavor enhanced by mild citrus

~~Anguille frite au sarrasin (buckwheat fried Montauk eel, vinaigrette au curry)...A dish that is also on the dinner menu (as are several of the other dishes, presenting the opportunity to try LCC without breaking the bank); imagine the best fish & chips you have ever had and then make it even better!

~~Tartare de bœuf (traditional condiments, horseradish, pommes frites)...I can never pass up beef tartare, and this was an excellent, classically flavored version, with the individual components beautifully presented so that I could mix them to taste.  My only criticism of this dish was the decidedly unpleasant frites that accompanied it, mostly composed of tiny bits that had been fried too long.  Also, a simple Romaine salad.

~~Merlan Colbert (fried whiting, maître d' butter)...A beautiful-looking dish, the small bite I tried was both crispy and tender.

LCC has an outstanding wine list, not huge, but diverse and very well represented.  From a dozen wines by the glass, the assistant Sommelier recommended two excellent pairings: 

~~2011 Le Clos des la Meslerie Chenin Blanc Vouvray...I thought this was outstanding, although pricey for what is a $32 bottle of wine at retail ($21 for a good-sized pour)

~~? Clos Cibonne Tibouren Côtes de Provence...also a nice, unusual wine ($17)

FOR DINNER, looking for a refreshing start to our second meal here of the day, we started with a "Cock-Tail" (hyphenated!) and a glass of wine:

~~#1 (Pear cider, lemon, bitter)...I love anything with pear cidre, and this was delicious, refreshing, and reinvigorated my appetite (lol, we had also visited nearby, famous Kee's Chocolates after lunch) ($15)

~~ NV Jacky Blot Domaine de La Taille aux Loups 'Brut Tradition' Chenin Blanc, Montlouis-sur-Loire ($15; retail is $21 a bottle)

A LA CARTE, since there is no tasting menu, we ordered 3 dishes each from the HORS D'OEUVRES, GOURMANDISES, and POISSONS ET VIANDES sections of the menu:

~~Poireaux (leeks, hazelnuts)...Again, I chose something light given this was the second French meal of the day.  This was classic French simplicity on the plate, perfectly prepared and presented.  Not a dish that you will rave about, but exactly what it should be.  Unfortunately, the vinaigrette was not a great pairing with Champagne ($12)

~~Quenelle de brochet, sauce américaine (pike quenelle, lobster sauce)...This seems to be one of their most commented on dishes, and I'm not surprised since it was the best quenelle I've ever had (sorry Bibou!).  Amazingly light and airy, not a traditional, denser dumpling in that sense.  And a lovely, light lobster sauce (again, not the traditional tomato preparation) with an accompanying small lobster claw.  Little known fact: Sauce Américaine is not named after America, but Armorica! ($33)

[This is the 1st part of a two-part review of Le Coucou.  Click below for Part 2.]

This is our second time back and it was a good meal, but unfortunately the service needs improvement. You check in for your reservation and you always have to wait atleast 10-15 mins before you are seated so you are standing in the crowded lobby and the hosts are not the friendliest. We were finally seated and our waiter was nice, and we told her about a time that we needed to leave by and ordered our starters and mains. The starters took about 35 mins for them to come and they were cold. We had to ask twice for them and I think the server forgot to put the order in. We ordered the salmon as an appetizer and there were 4 of us and they brought us 2 slices of bread for it. We asked for more since a 3rd was sharing and they brought out a basket with 3 slices of bread. The manager apologized for the delay of the order. We were surprised and shocked that when we received our bill that they charged us for extra bread, $4. We felt that was uncalled for since we had to wait forever and they didn't serve enough bread for the appetizer to be enjoyed. We also asked for a refill on our coffee and we never received it. The server did not pay attention to us after our mains came or to check if we had everything. It was just a really disappointing experience as we really like this restaurant but the service is a turn off.

I loved the ambience in this restaurant cozy and romantic. The signature cocktail that I ordered was very refreshing and light. The food is AMAZING. The Dover Sole was my favorite, very delicious, flavorful. Fresh and soft almost melts in your mouth. The sweetbread is also very good. The Filet de boeuf is to die for! Everything we had here from the appetizer to the desserts were amazing. 

Service was good but the only thing I didn't like was the Maître D. He was rude and was not helpful. He told me that since my brother was late for dinner we need to be mindful of the time and that they only give 2 hours per table. I was shocked when he told me that. He wasn't to welcoming and he kept checking on our table if we're finishing up. We stayed over the time he mentioned since we ordered a bunch of desserts. I just felt that he was inappropriate and I didn't like his attitude. Disappointed about the service of such a nice French restaurant such as this.
What a beautiful restaurant, amazing staff : the food is delicious : it was for me and my friend a beautiful evening !

Another lovely revisit to Le Coucou. A place I can't get enough of its sophisticated, flavorful and well-balanced taste, the gorgeous ambiance, and perfect service. Highly recommend the pastry basket, whole wheat crepe with lobster and egg, and the chicken with foie gras. Nice consistency with my last revisit.

Note: constantly checking OpenTable is the one and only way to secure a reservation!

A bit on the pricey side, but a very nice meal with a nice ambiance.

We ordered several dishes to share as a party of four, and we split the chicken crepinette and the raw diver scallops as appetizers, both of which were pretty shareable; they were both quite tasty, especially the crepinette, which was more or less a meatball with foie gras inside. It was extremely tasty, and I recommend dipping the bread (also very good) in the sauce afterwards. For our entrees, we split two orders of the rabbit, as well as an order of the bourride and the lamb rack. The rabbit was very well prepared, especially the first of three "cuts" they serve, while the lamb rack was also very tasty as was the tomato and eggplant that accompanied it; the meats throughout the meal were prepared exquisitely well. The fish I didn't enjoy as much unfortunately as it was prepared nicely but just didn't have as much flavor as I liked. We split their version of a baked Alaska and the rice pudding, the latter of which was just okay but the former I found to be nicely prepared. 

The service was very nice and helpful throughout, and the environment is very elegant with just  the right noise level. I'd definitely recommend a stop here if you're able to secure a reservation.

Best birthday dinner! The pike quenelle and dover sole were unlike anything we'd ever tasted! The leeks are not to be passed over. Service was amazing; the host donated to my charity that he overheard us talking about. Beautiful atmosphere. Amazing meal!

Such a romantic and intimate place, I was very happy with my experience here! First of all, the decoration is wonderful, and the tables are set up closed to the bar on one side and closed to the kitchen on the other- so you can't go wrong! I personally like more the area closer to the bar because of the windows so try to get there early enough to enjoy some sun!

Even though the restaurant is very elegant, you can really dress however you like! I have seen men with baseball hats and jeans in the dining space, so they are really laid back with that.

As for the food, everything I have tried has been amazing. My personal favorite is the beof with the oxtail potatoes for main course! It even has some bone marrow as well, making the portion more than enough and extremely tasteful! The halibut is also really good and comes with a rich butter/lemon sauce.

For appetizers, I really like the lobster and chicken&foie gras.

For dessert, the baked alaska was really fun and completely different- although I preferred the cheese platter.

Looking forward to trying more main courses on the menu when I return!

We went expecting a great meal. Needless to say, it did not live up to our expectations. 

We arrived on time for our lunch table. The table was not quite ready so we took a seat in the bar. The wine steward walk by twice without saying anything. The bartender ignored us. When I asked for a wine list, he said he'd be with us in a minute. We ordered a bottle of rose champagne. It came fairly quickly. The bar tender managed to pour the wine down the side of my glass. When I asked for a napkin to dry my glass, he handed me a bar towel. 

We sat at a table in the front area. Water was served, then nothing. We sat and waited. The menus were finally brought and our orders placed. I asked to see the wine steward. No one came. Our appetizers arrived, with still no wine steward. I asked again, pointing out that the food had arrived before we had even ordered wine. The wine steward arrived quickly and recommended a beautiful Chablis. It arrived as we were finishing the course with which it was paired. 

The appetizers were mixed. The asparagus and tuna was delicious. The oysters were tiny and appeared to have been sitting under a heat lamp for quite some time. They almost appeared to have been broiled. They could have been great, but they were not. The lentil soup was good. 

The wine steward helped us select a delicious Pinot noir. Unfortunately, the wine eclipsed the food. The tartar was acceptable but the pomme frites over cooked. The sea food stew was barely warm. The chicken was quite good. 

The citrus tart and the rhubarb dessert were delicious

All in all, we were very disappointed. I almost felt we had pissed someone off when we walked in. The service was off, at best. The food was just ok. Was the boss away?

Beautiful bar and dining room. Had a leisurely 3 hour lunch with a great Pommard wine. 
Attentive and professional service. Terrific food. I've already emailed friends with recommendation to go. Looking forward to the next time.

A beautiful space  deserving 5 stars for ambiance and service.
But the food ?????
 
Expected more chef talent in food preparations.

The  appetizers we tried were all mediocre.,the veal terrine , you could have bought from any gourmet market, and the Eal nothing to mention. the leeks were just tasteless.

For entree, the black bass was a good fish, but again no chef talent in the taste of the sauce.
Rack of lamb had a very strong lamb odor/taste-- and not well marinated and for 2 pieces at $45, left me hungry, because the side dish was 2 cherry tomatoes with a tasty stuffing , but hardly a spoon full.

Same went for the duck. Nothing special.. 

The 2 bottles of wine were delicious!!!

I

My new favorite French restaurant in NY. Food was out of this world! Drinks were good but not worth the price tag. Service was good but not as attentive as I assumed it would be. Yellow cactus flower had a great balance between smokiness from the mezcal, spice and not overwhelmingly sweet. The rum and true religion was not too sweet nor bitter. We had the St. Jacques Printaniere. It was a refreshing start and the rhubarbe was something I've never had with a scallop before. But it had great flavor. The Ris de veau a l'estragon was out of this world. The best sweetbreads I've had in my life. The sauce was extremely creamy and rich. We drank every sip of that sauce. My wife had the filet de bouf. Melts in your mouth once you put it in your mouth. If you're into meat, this is the dish for you as it comes with a bed of potatoes over shredded oxtail! Amazing dish! The 3 way rabbit was complex in each preparation. Each dish brought out the rabbit's flavor and texture. The pave au chocolate was for dessert. It's great if you like dark chocolate. We can't wait to come back!

My boyfriend and I enjoyed a lovely anniversary dinner at Le Coucou. The food was truly delicious - we savored every bite - and the atmosphere & service was impeccable. After we placed our dinner order, the sommelier came to our table and recommended a perfect bottle of wine to suit each course. The pacing of the meal was on point, empty dishes were promptly cleared, and my water and wine glasses were never left empty. At the end of the meal, the staff placed candles on our dessert plates and wished us a Happy Anniversary (so thoughtful). 

I would highly recommend:
Terrine de veau (veal terrine, pickled girolles)
Ris de veau a l'estragon (sweetbreads, cream, tarragon, maitake mushrooms)
Crépinette de volaille aux foie gras et fruits (chicken and foie gras, roasted pineapple)
Canard et fruits (duck breast, foie gras, almonds, kumquats and olives)
Tout le lapin (All of the Rabbit)
Pavé au chocolat (hazelnut praline ice cream)
Poire rôtie au vin de Muscadet (vanilla ice cream, almond dragée)

Make sure to make a reservation well in advance - they book up quickly!

It's rare for a meal to be excellent from top to bottom and dessert is usually not given the attention it deserves.  Le Coucou is the exception!  Everyone at our table had four courses each and not one of us had a complaint about any course and were extremely happy with the dessert finale.  It left us wanting more and trying to figure out how to score another dinner reservation.

Hype raises expectation, was really looking forward to dinner here after waiting a month with reservation on a Monday 5:30pm seating.
Our party of four each had appetizers,raw diver scallops, 
and leek with hazelnuts. Both were bland tasting.
For Entrees, two of us had Chicken with Foie Gras, ground up meat mixture, was a disappointment for a Foie Gras lover. The Monkfish with mussel broth was in such small portion, I think my friend have to eat again after this meal. There was one good dish at the table,Grilled squab with fricasse lobster, was tasty and come in good portion. We order two desserts to share, and this was the best part of the meal, rice pudding and poached rhubarb. Prepared perfectly with just the right amount of sweetness. Ambience and service was good. But for this kind of money, there are many other great choices in the city.

Lunch with friends at the vaunted coo coo was a pretty lovely affair but since one's impression is formed by expectation plus the actual experience, it amounted to pretty lovely. The service is stellar, and that includes the highly professional and friendly sommelier.  The wine list is massive and massively expensive but we found a good Loire Valley Chenin Blanc and were happy.
At lunch, one can choose two dishes and the selection is very good, with a slight preponderance of fish dishes.   Among the appetizers, the crackling crust of the fried eel was a bit thick, detracting from the eel, the a small mound of leeks appetizer was a delicious choice.   The lobster salad (it came with a surcharge) was well composed and executed, the piece of halibut in beurre blanc was perfect, moist and sweet, but the mountain of daikon radish below it was tough and overpowering - not a good companion to the wonderful fish (I would have preferred pretty much anything else).  The quenelle was text-book good
The desserts were disappointing.  The rhubarb selection brought pieces of rhubarb in a lots of cream, meringue and what seemed a bit of classic crème anglaise - not very exciting. Neither was the rum baba, competent but not any better than the ones you buy in better pastry shops in Naples.  Thin chocolate thins and small butter cookies as mignardises - banal.
Back to rating a place such as coucou whose hype is enormous (best NYC restaurant by James Beard Foundation): you expect something special in all facets of the meal and while a meal here will be very good, there are enough run-of-the-mill dishes that do not warrant such accolades.
Food 4
Service 5
Experience 3.5

Le Coucou is exceptional.   The high-ceilinged rooms are gorgeous and inviting, the personnel are friendly and helpful, and the food is wonderful.   The Dover sole in particular is heavenly.   They manage to take the food seriously without becoming stiff or off-putting.   Even the doggie bag has a sense of humor!
They know what they doing in this place, beautiful room, good service , and DELICIOUS FOOD.

We had a delightful meal here. The restaurant, which formally how's the bank, had an elegant ambience. The wait staff was extremely solicitous and the food was out of sight. Of course, it is almost impossible to get in so it'll probably be a while before we are fortunate enough to have another meal there but I certainly look forward to that day.
Outstanding!  The place is romantic and warm.  The sommelier was my favorite part.  He was very enthusiastic and gave great recommendations.  The food was prompt and very good.

Shortest love affair ever. Could the James Beard hype already have ruined Le Coucou? 

I've had flawless meals at Le Coucou but brunch today was massively disappointing. Our favorite dish--chicken and foie gras crepinette--came out room temp and was nowhere as moist as in the past. Pomme darphin was greasy, lacking crisp. Oh and definitely skip the saumom and croque monsieur-- I've had better at my neighborhood bistro. 

Pacing was terribly off. I kept seeing dishes sitting around with servers nowhere to be found. Also appetite killer: a black trash bag was overflowing in the bathrooms and blocking one of the sinks.

Daniel Rose needs to run a tighter ship... We loved his Paris resto and would give dinner here another shot, but I'm afraid Le Coucou's best days may be behind it.

Went for lunch literally the day after James Beard Award. Everybody must've been hung over because there were some misses  in our dishes and I left feeling a bit disappointed. Hope the hype doesn't ruin this place. If you want a flawless meal every single time, try Le Coq Rico.

Oh mondure! J'adore Le coucou! Or as we agfectionally call it, Le CuCu - Cynthia Lee Fontaine style!

We had met here just for drinks and apps but it was such a lovely experience. Truthfully, we weren't going to eat but we had a second round of wine and didn't wanna get too tipsy. So we shared the escargot and the terrain. The bread was the best - but that's not saying the rest wasn't also the best.

Service was super professional, I absolutely loved it! Prices are high, especially for wine and booze but don't you dare complain! It's gorgeous!
Everything we ordered was a home run: scallops, tete de veau, quenelles, duck, rabbit, and crepes souffle. They have real respect for the food, and it definitely shows in the finished product.

Brunch today I'm afraid was disappointing  One. we had to request oyster forks and no butter was provided for basket of breakfast rolls Two. A requested whiskey sour came back as straight bourbon on the rocks    Three.  poached eggs served on a warm plate we're stone cold Four. my wife's wool sweater was covered with lint ifrom a cheap cloth napkin  Five. at checkout time my wife's raincoat was found on the check room floor Six. Two white wines (by the glass) were forgettable 
ordinary and overpriced  Seven. Baba a Rhum  was served on more like a lunch roll than a spongy cake. Aside from delicious oysters at 5$ pop the outing was forgetable. Sorry.
Love this place. Great atmosphere and food. Brunch is incredible. https://instagram.com/p/BUCWQmRAIpt/

The service was great - everyone from the maitre d, manager to the waitress were very friendly, considerate and helpful. But the food really did not live up to the hype. I read many food critics reviews and Yelp reviews that were all very very positive, but to me, a neighborhood French restaurant can offer this level of food.

The food was delicious but the over pretentious staff and poor service was not worth it. It is Soho, not Paris. I have had better service from Parisians themselves. New Yorkers need to stop pretending to be French.

Had dinner with my husband Sunday. leCoucou did not disappoint. Simply wow and special occasion restaurant.
First the service was attentive and prompt. The cocktails were incredible and the wine list selection was good.
We had some appetizers: tongue with caviar and tuna. Tongue prep and taste simply spectacular, tuna was good too but not memorable.
For mains, we had the halibut and filet..again simply wowed by prep, presentation, flavor etc. especially the bone marrow on top of the filet added for nice flavor. 
Finally desert options were on point as well, chocolate mousse and baked Alaska type desert with pistachio ice cream. 
Really incredible evening, look forward to returning.

I wish I could give this a 4.5 instead of a 4, but I guess it's fine. We had a late reservation yet still had to wait 15 minutes upon arrival to be seated. We couldn't even enjoy a drink at the bar while we waited, as the bar is small, uninviting, and dry. Our servers seemed somewhat aloof and judgmental, acting as if because my friends and I were under the average age of the other diners, we shouldn't be taken as seriously. Also, I think the designer of the chairs in the restaurant is a sadist, as they were fucking uncomfortable. The food was very good, and deff deserving of a full 5, however, I found the menu to be nothing extraordinary. I wouldn't rush back, but I can't say it was bad. Definitely too hyped up for what it really is, but honestly that's not surprising for NYC hot spots.

Amazing dining experience. Excellent service, spectacular food. Started with the Asperges blanches de Provence. The sauce mousseline was perfection. Onto the Quenelle de brochet, sauce américaine.  Hands down, the best quenelle I have EVER had.  I have never had such a light quenelle - they are usually so dense.  The texture was the perfect balance between airy and dense.  Hard to describe, but you must get this dish. We moved onto the Halibut, beurre blanc with daikon prepared as choucroute (basically, a saurkraut). I love halibut and I loved this dish it has spoiled me for all other preparations.  The product was top notch, cooked perfectly, and the daikon was an amazing accompaniment with the perfect amount of acid to balance out the richness of the fish and sauce.  So, you must get this dish, too.

The only disappointment of the evening was the Canard et fruits - duck breast, foie gras, almonds, kumquats and olives.  It was fine, well executed, nice product, just not great. Maybe it paled in comparison to all the other standouts.  

Can't speak to dessert, as we opted for cheese, which was a nice variety, including many American ones.  

Service started off a bit stuffy for me, but the cast of thousands that attended to us was all very charming and professional.

Fantastic evening.

This place is all sizzle and no steak.  Like everyone else, we fell for the hype, but the product was disappointing.  As others have noted, the space is truly spectacular,  like all Starr restaurants.  Unfortunately, also like all Starr restaurants, the focus on the space led to shortcomings with the food.

The lamb was underwhelming.  It had no flavor and I could make it better at home.  The squab was equally mediocre. We found our mains so disappointing that we didn't bother to stay around for dessert, and instead made our way to Gramercy Tavern where we had had a much better meal recently.  

I had a slight twinge that we were making a mistake when I saw a car service from Jersey pull up and let out two people my parents age as we were entering.   I should have gone with my gut and went elsewhere for a dining experience that merits the absurd prices.   

In a city that has spectacular dining options, this place was a waste of time and money.   Would not recommend it.  

And before I forget, the service wasn't good either!

Went to Le cou cou for the first time a few weeks ago with some friends and we all loved it! The reservation process was really intense - took me a week of refreshing opentable at 11:59:59pm to finally get a good time slot! Aside from that, the staff were all very knowledgeable and accommodating - we had wine pairing recommendations with our meals as well.  Ambiance was very intimidate with low dimmed lights and one large statement candle on the table.  Overall an amazing experience! By the way, the white asparagus with caviar..SO DELICIOUS.

Vegan-friendly brunch at the most hyped French restaurant in New York? Oui, s'il vous plaît! Who would have thought... called the restaurant in advance to make sure they can accommodate vegan dinners and won't kick us out... (a realistic option in Paris - ha!) As everybody already mentioned, it is a beautiful restaurant, Paris-meets-NYC-ambiance, very classy and surprisingly enough - not a bit pretentious. Enjoyed excellent soy lattes, leeks with hazelnuts, toasted bread with marmalade, sunflower avocado toast (without the poached eggs) and seasonal fruit salad with coconut milk. All made from excellent ingredients and equally delicious. Spot on service as well (thanks, Noli!). I do recommend, however, to all vegan patrons out there - make reservations for breakfast/brunch. I believe dinner would be much less satisfying :)

A fellow designer had recommended Le Coucou based on the charming interiors by Roman & Williams. Vintage bentwood chairs with patinaed velvet upholstery, whitewashed brick, a lovely, moody pastoral mural at the bar featuring a vaulted ceiling, wavy antique glass at the divided light transoms and perimeter windows, along with tall ceilings create a thoughtfully detailed, comfortable and chic ambiance. We were here for breakfast and started with a flaky and light-as-air chocolate croissant, mmmm! It went quickly downhill as each subsequent breakfast item, including lettuce, was tinged with a hint of an oily, smoky residue, as if perhaps every kitchen utensil had a sheen of this "flavor" transferring it's gift forward. Maybe the contaminant was the peculiarly vile bacon, and sidenote: shouldn't the pay-off for a heavily processed, decidedly unhealthy, nitrate-laden food be deliciousness at the least? Our very adept server was perfection, but alas, we were left, quite literally, with a bad taste in our mouth!

We went there a year ago on their opening week, and realized this place is now very popular, so I owed this place a good review. 
"Amazing" is the word to describe this place - the vibe, the food, the service.  Everything was well delivered.

Phe-nom-enal spot. I've been there 3 times for brunch, lunch, and dinner and been delighted every time. Service, food, and ambience are all 5 star. One of the best restaurants to open in NYC in quite some time. I just hope they maintain their quality over time!

Items Selected:
Croque Madame - Ham, Gruyere, Egg, Bechamel 
Crepenette de Volaille aux Foie Gras et Fruits - Chicken and Foie Gras, Roasted Pineapple
Galette de Sarrasin - Buckwheat Crepe, Lobster, Egg, Basil
Comme un Clafoutis - French Pancake, Roasted Apples, Lime Zest, Crème Fraiche
Baba au Rhum - Rum, Cream

Recently taking home the James Beard Foundation Award for Best New Restaurant, a Stephen Starr project featuring Daniel Rose of Paris' Spring, it was with high expectation that a party of three sat down at Le Coucou for Brunch, the service top notch from podium to presentation of the check while the food was just fair-to-middling, particularly considering the recent increase in quality of French Brasserie fare across the United States.

Located in the 11 Howard Hotel, a nice looking property that necessitates three-meal service each day, the space containing Le Coucou is an elegant one with wood floors, stone walls and white pillars, a turn around the far corner bringing diners face-to-face with a kitchen that runs long and narrow, classic copper cookware hanging above with the pass up front, a young female Chef on the line heard complaining about her workload at least twice during the meal as it appeared Chef Rose was not there.

Offering a concise menu throughout the day and evening, small changes differentiating Brunch from Lunch with Dinner expanding the number of choices slightly, it was with glasses of water filled and the announcement of "there are no specials today" that the decision was made to order Pastries followed by entrees, the sold-out Gougeres rendering that choice invalid and thus limiting the order to three savories and two Desserts.

Sitting and watching both the Kitchen and Sommelier at work, the restaurant completely full with plates coming over the pass almost nonstop, it was after perhaps twenty minutes that three dishes landed on the table along with share plates, a first taste of the Croque Madame showing the Brioche to be crisp although a bit thick while the Ham, Gruyere and Bechamel were good if not memorable, the lasting image one of a Sunny-side Egg that was overcooked.

Using good ingredients and priced accordingly, both the Crepenette de Volaille aux Foie Gras et Fruits and Galette de Sarrasin topping $25, it would be difficult to suggest that the serving of Lobster on the Crepe was anything more than skimpy while the Liver-centered ball of Meat was expectedly rich, though the roasted Fruit did do an admirable job of bringing some needed levity into the fold.

Receiving the piping-hot Pancake approximately ten minutes later, a result of the plate's preparation time rather than anything intentional, those looking for Le Coucou's Brunch standout are encouraged to order one to share amidst 2-4 individuals, the center thick 'like a Clafoutis' while the edges cook crisp, the Dessert menu completely different from that online yielding a reference-standard Baba Au Rhum completely soaked with Booze atop Citrus segments and filled with sweet Cream.

Believe the hype! Everything from the service to the food to the atmosphere was absolutely perfect. I came here last night with my dad and his girlfriend and we all had the most amazing experience. The decor is stunning, and we couldn't stop oohing and ahhing over light fixtures, bustling open kitchen and other details. The food is obviously the star here, and we all shared everything:

-Asparagus with bigeye tuna with smoked wood vinegar: Spears of asparagus were perfectly cooked and draped with generous portions of raw bigeye tuna. The smoked wood vinegar was delicious and lent the most elusive and delicious flavor to this dish, taking it from delicate to very powerful.
-Buckwheat fried eel with curry vinaigrette: This was one of my favorites. The eel was lightly battered and perfectly cooked. The batter was crispy and light and the eel was meaty and just done. The curry vinaigrette was inspired, and something I never would have thought would work, but it was incredible.
-Pike quenelle with lobster sauce: Light as a cloud, this pike quenelle floated in an umami-bomb of a bright orange lobster sauce. Rich and foamy, we all went straight in with our spoons.
-Halibut with beurre blanc: I don't love beurre blanc, so I liked this dish least, but the fish was super fresh and perfectly cooked. I just find beurre blanc a bit too rich, but I suppose if you're going to have it, have it at Le Coucou!
-"All of the rabbit": This was definitely the star of the table: loins of rabbit are cooked and "dusted" with ground rabbit meat, which has been lightly charred. This plate is accompanied by a copper pot of broth, in which there is the rabbit leg and some dark greens. You are meant to spoon the broth over the rabbit, and it turns into a sort of light stew. Also accompanying this dish is an incredible treatment of the front of the rabbit (the breast?), which is in a small copper skillet and has been cooked underneath a broiled lid of sweetly caramelized onions. It was sheer heaven.
-Grilled squab, fricassé of lobster and squab bits: Also a huge hit. The squab comes on the most ethereal and light potato puree and is accompanied by meaty lobster. We finished everything!

We ordered champagne and wines by the glass, as we couldn't decide on just one bottle. The sommelier is delightful and gave us great recommendations. We were too full for dessert, but certainly enjoyed the petit fours that come out at the end of the meal. 

This was an experience to remember and I hope to come back soon!

Haven't enjoyed a dinner like this in New York for a long time! The setting isn't too stuffy, the service is attentive but not overbearing, and the food is delectable. Think Old French in a new way! These dishes are full of flavor and fat, and oh so satisfying. The Crépinette de volaille aux foie gras et fruits was a perfect starter, rich and light at the same time. I had the perfectly prepared Dover Sole and my husband had the steak. The steak was tender and the oxtail potatoes could have been a dish on their own. The chiboust à la rhubarbe was light, creamy, and just the right tartness from the rhubarb and the Omelette Norvégienne was like a great version of a baked alaska! Just a perfect dinner. Yes, it will set you back a few dollars but so worth it. Go for a special occasion.

Don't go!!!  Rude chef.  Not worth going and eating expensive food and the chef you supported for years is too snotty to say hello. After a $1,500 check for 4 people and knowing him for years and he was too busy. Done. He will fail. Too many great restaurants with appreciative chefs and not ones who let ego get the best of them. Don't recommend

The place is beautiful and the service is absolutely impeccable!   My wine glass was never empty.  They always appeared just when you needed something.  But the problem is - the good they bring you in with all the service flourishes fell flat.  I went for brunch - we had the gougere (delicious a bit eggier than I like), the oeufs basqueáis (a favorite but this version did not include eggplant, herbs, or a ham product - it needed one of them), the lobster crepe, and the fancy potato cake.  Everything was well executed precision cooking but none of it hit home.  We could have used way more oomph.  This is food for rich older people who don't like interesting things to happen on their palate.  We looked so forward to going - and are glad we went - but feel no interest in returning...

You need to make a reservation here!  Its located in the 11 Howard hotel, behind the black door on your left when you walk in.  The decor is stunning and the food/service match!  We came here for breakfast and it was a lovely experience.  Try the croissants they are crisp, light, and airy--just like the ones in France.  I had the avocado toast and it was delicious--dont let the pictures deceive you its pretty massive and very filling.  This is my favorite new breakfast place in New York.  Definitely recommend and we definitely will be back.

BEAUTIFUL place, nice people, but the food doesn't live up to the price (and the drinks were a little stingy).

It's just not there yet.  You can get much better, for much less.  I don't mind paying, as long as it's worth it.  I heard they missed out a Michelin Star this time around (if I am correct), and after dining, I can see.  I too feel that the food just misses the mark, at least right now. It's almost like they are trying too hard?

Still, a lovely experience.  Very romantic!

I will write this as I go along on my meal. Came in as a party for 1 on a Monday so thought I should be ok without a reservation. Front of house pretended to have some "cancelations" and said they can squeeze me in. They gave me a crap table that looked like they just set it up by the service station and the bathrooms. I didn't mind as I had a direct view of open kitchen and love to watch the inner workings of a smooth machine.
I started with  raw scallop and it was perfect and delivered by Melissa, my waitress who was great from the start. Tried Sweetbread for the first time and was blown away by the sauce and a tender entree.
Finally, the duck which was perfectly prepared and loved every bite. It has a cherry sauce which was nice but served with foie gras which I dont love  but thats a personal preference. All in all a great spot and reccomend if you like french..
The most fabulous the most chic and the food ? Outstanding and service impeccable. I highly  recommend it here and the patrons? Stunning

This is hands down my new favorite restaurant. I went for breakfast, due to its convenient location- hooked to 11 Howard, which I was staying in.  I ordered the French pancakes, which were delicious. It was fluffy and sweet, with citrus creme fraiche to balance it.  The atmosphere was so beautiful, and he service was the best I have had in NYC.

Le Coucou is not typically the type of restaurant I would feature here, but after much anticipation I was finally able to give it a try last weekend and I'm still excited about it. So here it is... 

I'll preface this by saying that our dinner reservation (most likely because we were a party of 5) was for 9:30pm on Sunday, which is, on any other day, late enough for me to have already digested my dinner like the old lady that I am. Even so, we walked into a full house with a bunch of tables for two filled with couples on dates all dressed up. 

The interiors are beautifully designed. There's a gorgeous bar immediately on the right upon walking in that's illuminated with a warm orange light from behind and carefully curated flowers on both ends of it. Even though there is a hint of uptightness that I normally don't enjoy, it's to a much lesser extent than what you would expect at a typical white tablecloth French restaurant. 

We tried quite a few items off the menu and it goes without saying that everything was absolutely exquisite. There is a sense of purpose attached to each plate; each one is simple, yet complex, with nothing extra or nothing lacking from it. Some of my favorite items were the poireaux (leeks with hazelnuts), white asparagus and lobster tail for appetizer; the monkfish soup and black bass for entree; and the fraises Coucou, pavé au chocolate, and the chocolate mousse for dessert.

All in all, Le Coucou lived up to my expectations. We could've gone without the super pretentious, very extra, over-the-top snobby service provided abundantly by our waitress, but I would definitely return. Maybe they're somewhat laid-back during brunch service...(?)

Great Brunch!

Starting off, Le Coucou had a great ambiance. The restaurant is lovely and has been featured in publications like Mr Porter as a result. Another advantage is that you can make a breakfast/brunch reservation here, so it's not like a lot of other great brunch spots where a 45 min wait is just part of the deal.

We had the pancake with apples and creme fraiche, which was amazing and surprisingly light in a good way. On the other side of the spectrum, if you want something big and hearty that croque madam was fantastic, but probably worth sharing as it's big and with the beschemel is pretty heavy. Pastries were also some of the best I've had in NYC.

My only complaint is that our coffees came out after our food, but the waiter appeared distressed this happened and apologized, so it was probably just a random backlog at the coffee machine.

Overall would definitely come back, especially since it's so easy to book - great for when people are in town.

Came here for an early breakfast in April. Somehow my party was seated with the beautiful people at the banquet in the center of the restaurant. I enjoyed the oufs basques, and my friend enjoyed the omelette and a side of white sausage. Tea and coffee were nicely presented and the drinks were pretty stiff. 
The service could have been bit more friendly and less formal. Overall very nice breakfast.

Don't believe the hype. We had planned our Saturday night dinner with high expectations and very sorely disappointed. Expecting proper good French food focussed on quality ingredients, however food is bland, boring and is if it's bought from the local supermarket. Duck breast and Halibut were like cardboard. Service was poor at best. I don't know why this place has good reviews. Certainly not for the food or service.

The food was excellent, we had raw diver scallop, beef cheek and foie gras terrine to start, then Dover sole and beef for main and lemon crepe and strawberry le Coucou for dessert. 

All the food was absolutely delicious and perfectly executed and plated. What really let everything down is the service. We were seated for 30 minutes prior to anyone inquiring with us for our order, with one confused member of wait staff attempting to remove our wine glasses when we hadn't even had a chance to order any wine yet! However, they did apologise and subsequent service was quite smooth. The only other minor hiccup is that I ordered coffee at the same time as dessert and had to wait quite a while for the coffee after we finished dessert, and it was only bought over once i reminded the server. Another detractor is the person who bought it seemed very disgruntled and practically slammed down the sugar, creamer and French press. 

This is my second time at Le Coucou. First experience was for brunch and again, food was excellent though service was a bit spotty. 

In summary, go for food and ambiance. Service is very spotty and I would probably not suggest this restaurant for a special occasion due to the issues with service.

BEWARE OF THE FLIMSY CHAIRS. THEY FALL APART. Seriously. I barely sat down in a chair at the bar and the thing fell apart. When we got seated we noticed that other chairs in the dining room had loose screws hanging out. ???? James Beard must be rolling over in his grave. Lovely place with great food and mostly great service but they have to do a better job maintaining the furniture. Have never seen anything like this in a NYC restaurant. And, regarding the service, they offered nothing in the way of a free drink or dessert to compensate for my tumble to the floor. Won't be going back. Not really worth the hype if I have to risk injury & humiliation to get a meal. Very disappointed.

PS: unless you like the barking sounds of a kitchen hustle, don't sit in the 'open kitchen' area. My date and I were often rudely interrupted by the screams of cook staff announcing God knows what. Silly choice for a restaurant that promises such refinement in its food.

This place has a wonderful ambiance and all the food is wonderfully presented.  I've had breakfast, lunch and dinners here and am always extremely satsfied!  The staff is also extremely friendly and helpful when describing the menu and are very knowledgeable about the ingredients.  I love their recommendations and they always listen to what I am in the mood for and help me choose items that complement one another.  Always a pleasant experience!

A "destination" restaurant in NYC to get classical French food. Every dishes are well executed! You can't get wrong with anyone of them. Great selection of wines though the pricing could be inflated more for some of the wines. Service is always spot-on.
Exceeded expectations. Menu has some very unique dishes, we took a risk and tried several, they were delicious. It is a pricey restaurant, but you get what you pay for. We will be going back.

Hands down, the best French restaurant in NYC. 100% worth the wait and hype. Everything on the menu is delicious - but the pike quenelle with lobster sauce is definitely a favorite. And the duck with foie gras.... just too much love on the plate! :)

The decor is oh so elegant, I understand why it is the new darling of the restaurant scene.  It is a celebrity mecca, however our servers were very attentive.  It is very french, and everything is on the menu.  I however am not as adventurous as my dinner companions, they enjoyed organ meats, rabbit and octopus.  My dinner was delicious, I had lamb chops, they were a bit on the rare side, I can only describe the flavor as soft, it was velvety and stimulated all of your senses.  My dinner companions thoroughly enjoyed their meals as well, and since they live close by, hoped to make this their weekly spot.

Exceptional food and service. Just celebrated a friend's birthday here and it was a "wow". Delighted to find this gem. Our server Noy, was wonderful. I had a couple questions about items on the menu and was thoroughly impressed with her explanation of each plate down to the fine nuances. We started with the fried veal head and sweatbreads.  The veal was incredible light and crispy with a delightful sauce. I am always intrigued when I see sweatbreads offered and will say these were indeed the best I've ever tasted. Superb texture accompanied by a wonderful sauce.  More bread please! I had to soak up the goodness and could care less who was watching! 

For the mains, we both went with the Dover sole. Nice to have real Dover.  Just perfectly true to classic French preparation.  Again, spectacular sauce while keeping the fish as the star.  The only drawback here was that the sole was already filleted  and de-boned in the kitchen. Sometimes it's nice to have the old school table side service. Not a deal breaker after the first bite hits your tongue though. Dessert was a pleasant offering but overwhelmed but the previous courses.  I will be back, soon!

My first time pre-fix lunch here. Servers here dress very stylish. For appetizer, Crème de concombre - cucumber was fresh and the soup was creamy, very good balance. Anguille frite au sarrasin was also popular. We had Salade de homard and Pot au feu de lapin for main dish. Never thought lobster can match romaine but it turned out great. Rabbit leg soup was tasty. Cock-tail was the highlight, Matin Sur La Seine tasted more like soda and and Yellow Cactus Flower was drier.

Having heard great things about le coucou AND being a francophile & francofoodophile I just had to try it! I think most people go here for dinner to try signatures like quenelles--however I chose brunch because we were bringing a toddler & prix fixe fancy dinner just inherently seems less kid friendly than sunday brunch.  We did get to try 2 of three dishes offered at brunch though that the waiter told us were from dinner menu.  

I think this is definitely a treat/special event type restaurant and we came for a birthday!  

We got the chicken crepinette, coueur d'entrecote dix pour dix aux foie gras, eggs coucou & a side potato pancake.  My favorite was the coueur d'entrecote (ribeye with relaxed foie gras).  The chicken crepinette was also foie gras inside with roasted pineapple . The crepinette & coueur were from dinner menu--the other stuff was inherently more brunchy (eggs, pancakes pastries)

Kids friendliness: they accommodated us witn booth seating which my toddler likes--but no kids menu or change table in bathroom.  If you're going to bring kids go brunch not dinner!!

Had a great dinner experience. No pretentious tasting menu. Not even daily specials - love it! Just solid food. My favorite was Ris de veau a l'estragon. Lamb was amazing too.
The price is fairly reasonable. Would love to go back again. Love to try brunch as well.

The food here was great. I love French food and this place didn't disappoint. Also of note is the ambience, which is also quite striking and picture worthy. We decided upon the oysters, the leeks (to be able to cook something as simple as a leek and make it so delicious and unique is really a feat in itself), the pike quenelle, the duck, and the prime filet. Everything was outstanding, but I remember thinking that I needed more of the delicious sauce!!! If I had to pick one dish I think the duck with foie gras was outstanding. I would get that again, no questions asked! On the downside, I wish service was a little more attentive and it's definitely pricey so save it for a special occasion.

I've been waiting for over 24 hours for a stroke of inspiration to begin writing this review, but I'm determined not to let perfect be the enemy of good.

In the case of Le Coucou, funny enough, perfect was the best friend of good, as the food was both perfect and good. This meal ranked among my top two or three in recent memory. From the castle-like ambiance to the complex, deep, transcendental sauces, this place does it right. I don't agree with James Beard on much, but he certainly found a gem of a new restaurant here. 

To start we got the buckwheat crepe with lobster, the buckwheat fried Montauk eel, the chicken and foie gras, and the pike quenelle. When the smoke had cleared, three of the four of us ranked the dishes 3, 4, 1, 2, respectively. The chicken and foie gras was next level, while the pike quenelle was a masterpiece of pike "flan" (go figure!). The eel, we thought, could have been any white fish and would have performed similarly.

For main courses, we got "all of the rabbit", the grilled squab with lobster, the duck, and the prime fillet. A few things I would note here: first, squab means pigeon - just a heads up (my friend goes, "what is this a park to table restaurant" - haha). Second, I like how everything was served in a few ways. Interesting. The dishes were all awesome - each moistening in their own decadent sauce. 

No dessert. Not this time. But we'll be back. And maybe we'll do it that time. Stay tuned.

Excellent brunch spot for anyone who loves French cuisine in a fancy ambience. 

To start off, we got a cocktail from their drink menu, specifically, the Matin Sur La Seine which was a bit to tangy for me, but later paired well with main dish.
