For appetizers, we tried the Pain au chocolat and gougère. These were definitely nothing like store-bought pastries; these were fresh out the oven, light and airy. Very delicious. 

As the main course, I highly highly recommend Galette de Darrasin. This dish is what really did it for me. The sauce the dish had really complimented the lobster and egg combination and will have you licking your plate towards the end of it! My friend had the Le Californien which was well-portioned and excellent especially if you love avocados and poached eggs. 

Finally for dessert, we had the Mousse au chocolat which was divine.

The interior design of Le Coucou was splendid with high ceilings and elegant chandeliers / table settings. Lastly the service was quick and delightful. Highly recommended.

This was quite the experience, which begins the moment you walk in the door and are greeted by the maitre'd and a hostess who actually tells you, "We're so happy you can join us."  This warm reception is mirrored across ALL the staff, who were all nothing short of impeccable in their service.  The wine list was thorough, and it was refreshing to see a list that catered to all budgets, not just high-end exorbitant fare.  Now, when perusing the menu, one might - as I did - assume that the hors d'oeuvres are simply tiny bite-sized portion, but that would be inaccurate.  They're every bit as sizable as the gourmandises.  The missus ordered the crab under a crisp crepe to start, and I ordered the fried eel.  The crab was superb, just sweet and delicate enough.  The eel was a tad tough, but nothing offensive because the entire package worked so well.  For mains, the missus ordered the chicken and foie gras patty that was topped with half a roasted plum, while I ordered the monkfish cooked in a mussel broth.  Combining the chicken to the foie gras was genius because it really lightened the experience by still giving you a pronounced liver flavor without being overbearing.  Now, the monkfish in mussel broth - that was something else.  All I wanted to do was bathe in that mussel broth.  Truly one of the most flavorful things I've ever tasted.  Dessert was a shared order of strawberries with candied tarragon, which complimentary sherbet sandwiches.  But it didn't stop there.  Even more complimentary sweets followed: a berry pastille, an impossibly thin sliver of chocolate, and a tiny cookie.  We left feeling quite full - not stuffed, mind you, just perfect - and stepped out of the restaurant reminiscing about all the flavors we'd experienced.  And what an incredible experience it was.  Absolutely worthy of a repeat performance.

This is one of the rare restaurants that lives up to the hype. It won the James Beard Award for Best New Restaurant in the US in May, 2017 and I agree. The food, service, wine list, waitstaff, and ambiance are all top notch.The modern French food was outstanding and the plating and service were as well I can heartily recommend this restaurant without reservations.

What we got didn't measure up to the hype. No amuse, most of the dishes were precooked and sitting around, after we finished our cocktails and asked for by the glass recommendation for the chicken, the server sent the most expensive glass, $32 we later saw when we got the bill. Quelle horreur!

Went for lunch with friends - had the prix fixe menu - started with the cucumber soup which was fantastic followed by the poussin that was ok - my friend got the chicken and fois gras crepinette and that was delicious. Overall it was a very nice lunch - will return.

Sadly it was disappointing and I wanted it to be good. I found the staff snobby and borderline condescending. I don't think they really cared if I liked it or not - asking was just part of their check list. Our waiter was almost never there, but the water guy was great (give credit where credit is due). The food was underwhelming for a place like this. The best thing was the French wine. Dessert was boring, the appetizers ok and the main dish (I ordered rabbit) was a-ok. Upon tasting, my immediate reaction was "my grandmother's rabbit was better." I had a hard time finishing it. The decor is beautiful but overall it didn't live to the hype at all.

Just had dinner here tonight and absolutely loved it! I loved French food and have gone to numerous French restaurants over the years and even ones ,much pricier but this is by far one of the best I've had. Foods are refine, with quality ingredients that are combined well, cooked to perfection. Taste is superb. Normally, I find French food to be quite salty but this dinner was cooked with precision. Highly recommended and Bon Appetit!

I was here for the sunday brunch. The food is just average and is over rated. The oyster with seaweed ice is very good. The gougere is not hot enough. The steak with foie gras is just ok but with bad visual presentation. The cocktail come in  after I finishing appetizers with melted ice. The reason that I am giving 3 stars instead of 1 star is because the waiter take off the charge for gougere and remake the cocktail.

Stellar! Thank God proper elegant service has returned to the decaying dining scene in Manhattan! Could not be more grateful! I was in dire need of great service, attention to detail and terrific classic, elegant cuisine. And to top it off, the room is lovely; people are rather well-dressed! Makes you feel right at home. What a relief! 
This is my secret haven away from the undesired Asian yelpers and cheapskate tourists of midtown!

Ambiance is top notch, its beautiful in here, makes you feel like someones home. The cartoon birds are really cool as well.  The price fix for lunch is a great way to try a couple dishes. Both things I had were great. I'm not a huge classical French fan, but if you are this is a must visit.  I probably wouldn't come back, but I had a good time.
This place is one of the best restaurants anywhere. Service is impecable , food is presented and taste so good. Strongly recommended

Le Coucou was one of the highlight when we had the duck with foie gras. It was simply outstanding. You put everything into a single bite and it just blows your mind away. You always feel like there are dishes where they just put stuff on a plate to look fancy, but for the duck with foie gras, everything stands out. It's the perfect puzzle when you have a small bite of the fruit, the duck, and the foie gras. It just works.

Everything was pretty great and it's just a big wow when you walk in. It's really fancy throughout the restaurant even to the restrooms. I think it's probably a wonderful place to take your gf to for any special occasion(mainly special occasion just because it's on the pricey side). If i had to name any flaws, it would be our waitress that just kinda seem like she was looking down on us simply because "we didn't order enough." It almost is like a common theme here in NY where people/waiter/waitresses just have that terrible attitude because you don't meet the standards. 

Besides that, It was a wonderful experience and I would recommend Le Coucou.

After waiting till midnight to book tables on opentable on several days, we finally got a table, and I was super excited. Le coucou did not disappoint. Great ambiance, service, and food. What a delight to sample French cuisine in a candle lit dinner. We sample a variety of dishes on the menu, and nothing disappointed. The fish balls were amazing and we were fighting over every last chunk of it. 

All of the rabbit is an interesting dish - it is literally all parts of a rabbit cooked in different ways. We shared this, and so glad that we did because it was quite a lot of meat! Excellently stewed and the meat was extremely tender, highly recommended. 

Although we were stuffed to the brim after the main, we had to sample their desserts because they looked gorgeous among the other tables. Tried the crepe and chocolate torte - seriously though, can't go wrong with anything at Le Coucou!

Le Coucou makes me so happy; like so happy. I have been waiting a long time to have such an exquisite dining experience. Everything I desire in a restaurant is what Le Coucou provides. The only mishap we had was a conflict with our reservation, but it was sorted out within 40 minutes and we were able to enjoy the amazing bar meanwhile. Old school, classic, beautiful. The barkeepers were extremely attentive and the drinks were impeccable. 

Once you get past the snooty hostess, you have stepped into one of the most exquisite dining spaces I have seen in a while. The white enamel brick, glass, and impressive chandeliers offer a sleek dining environment. 

Where do I begin with this restaurant; Le CouCou is a true dining experience. There is so much attention to detail and an immense amount of creativity. The wait staff is attentive without being overbearing, the flavors are bold, but not overpowering; you can watch the dishes being made in the open kitchen or engage with the sommelier; there are no mistakes here. Everything is well thought out and for that it is truly a wonderful restaurant. 

Between two people I can say we ordered about ten dishes, with pride. Unfortunately I can't remember everything we ate, but every dish was perfection. The chef understands a perfect balance of flavors, which makes for a great dish. Must haves:

-lobster salad- juicy, fresh, elegant 
-poached skate- fresh, fresh, fresh, fresh! So good! The flavors are light, airy, and lend the perfect balance to such a plain fish. 
-squash blossoms: savory, succulent, rich!!!! 
-foie gras- to die! bold flavors but not overpowering; perfect transition into main courses.
- mussels and shrimp in broth: if you missed out on this dish, you should be very sad. An explosion of hearty and beautiful flavors: acid, buttery, full-bodied! 
-halibut- again full of flavor with the perfect balance of acid and fat. 
-monkfish- robustly flavorful; fish was cooked to perfection! 
- I can't recall what the dessert was, but it was like a panna cotta covered with pistachio, crisps.. again.. amazeee! 

Since September 2016, I have been back three times and I don't even live in New York! There is a reason this restaurant was named "Best New Restaurant" at the James Beard Awards. Le CouCou takes us back to Parisian history as a reminder of how simplicity is often the most elegant.

The "IT" place in NYC lives up to the hype. The menu is innovative whilst remaining classical, the atmosphere is a perfect mix of cool sophistication and the service was flawless. 

The expert sommelier thoughtfully interrogated our palates and our lunch choices and offered a wine that perfectly hit the mark. The front of house staff are professionals, I couldn't fault timing, engagement or execution.

The food was an exceptionally good mix of french classic and trend which is perfect for the Soho location.

The dining room is beautiful, from the bar to the open kitchen. If you're lucky enough to get a booking my one suggestion is to request the table next to the kitchen to watch the action.

It's not cheap, but worth every penny and would definitely be a regular for me if I lived in NYC.

Good ambiance. OK/decent food.

Food:
Crab crepe - thought the crab was slightly fishy for my taste but overall this was decent
Lobster tail - lobster was very good but the lettuce part was ok
Sweetbreads - good
Foie gras with duck - very good
Pistachio cake with meringue - good

the food was fine....not stupendous as I expected from the hype, but better than usual.  the service was haughty and condescending...and really removed any excitement from what could have been a better experience.   good, not great.  and in need of a major attitude adjustment....or change your dress code to jackets and move your location from chinatown meets lil' italy.  :0
Beautiful restaurant with elegant ambiance. Pastry was the highlight with an amazing blueberry ice cream that you will remember long after.
Amazing breakfast, the avocado toast with poached eggs are the best. Coffee is amazing...nice place to go for breakfast in the Soho area.

Dined here a week ago and it was amazing. Sat right by the open kitchen. Here's how it all went.

Drinks:

Yellow Cactus Flower: Great drink but serving size is too small.

Variations on a Theme: Nice blend of sweet and spicy

Food: 

Bread: Amazing

Steak: Brilliant. Seems small when it comes but then given a huge plate of oxtail potatoes and shreds of beef on side. 

Had a flaming Baked Alaska which had meringue icing, pistachio ice cream, and was topped with cherries.

4 stars for service. 4 for food.
Go for breakfast. Dinner is great, but breakfast is way cheaper, and you can get the best items.
The best kouign amann in NYC. 
Incredible pate, expertly pressed and seasoned.
Life changing gougeres. Like, go just for those they must be tried. Seriously insane, massive, crispy, cheesy, and served piping hot. 
4 stars because the omelette wasn't perfect. A little too much color, and texture not quite airy enough. For a restaurant of that style and price, the omelette should be perfect. 
A french chef is only as good as his  last omelette.

Overrated. 
Hype not worth it
Food is ok -- a bit foofy
Rather fly to paris and have a delicious meal

My mother and I had a wonderful lunch at Le Coucou. She made the reservation and I didn't know much about the place except that it was pricey and upscale and obviously French. I think I was expecting like a real classic formal French restaurant and was pleasantly surprised by how fun and relaxed and straight-up cute the place was, even with its impeccable service and precise, serious food.

The space was charming as hell, from the ubiquitous little bird line drawings to the cheery abundance of chandeliers. The street-facing walls were windowed top to bottom, letting in plenty of natural light. We sat in the dining area right next to the open kitchen, which looked pretty happening.

Service was excellent. Our server was polite and professional, warm and exceedingly helpful. She did a great job guiding us through the menu, and we ended up loving every single thing we ordered. The only blip was that we got the wrong dessert--we'd been waffling between two options, and got sent the one we'd passed on. The result was that we got two desserts, one of them free. We were very happy about this mix-up.

I couldn't resist a cocktail with my lunch--the list looked great, with a few options that roused my curiosity. I got the Yellow Cactus Flower, and it was excellent, made with Suze, mezcal, yellow chartreuse, and pineapple. A lot of strong flavors in there, but it was really balanced and refreshing.

The food was truly superb. We were welcomed with a bread basket, thick, rustic slices of sunflower spelt served with butter and salt. Le Coucou's lunch is a $52 two course prix fixe, which isn't a steal or anything, but not a bad way to try the food if you're not ready for the full-on dinner extravaganza. We must have been in a seafood mood--we shared two seafood appetizers and two seafood entrees, and this made for a lovely, luxurious lunch.

We started with the crêpe "souvenir de Lannilis" and the raie au poivron et câpres. The first was a dish of crab mixed with lime, chives, herbs, and something creamy and saucy to bind it all together, then covered with a delicate buckwheat crêpe. The crab meat was juicy and sweet, shredded into satisfying hunks, and it went wonderfully with the nutty crêpe. I liked the raie au poivron et câpres even better. This was a cold appetizer of poached skate topped with capers, herbs, and croutons, all in a pool of sweet pepper vinaigrette. The skate was beautifully cooked, and I loved the bite of the pepper sauce.

For our mains, we chose the salade de homard (an extra $10) and the quenelle de brochet with sauce américaine, evidently a house specialty. Both were tremendous. The salad was my favorite kind of salad: mostly meat, with top notch accompaniments. It featured a whole poached lobster tail with grapefruit over grilled romaine, with a side of sauce lauris, a blend of paprika and mayonnaise. The lobster was perfectly cooked, and both the sweet, bright segments of grapefruit and the hearty grilled lettuce helped it shine. The quenelle de brochet, or pike quenelle, was a fascinating dish, a mousse of pike served with a foamy sea of lobster sauce. This was essentially a big fluffy French oden, like the airiest fishcake you've ever had, but instead of an austere bit of Japanese broth, you eat it with big spoonfuls of rich, complex lobster sauce. Definitely a must.

We decided to keep things light with dessert, and ordered the coupe myrtille to share. Our plans changed when the baba au rhum came out instead, and our waitress apologized for the mistake and said it was on the house. This was an extremely favorable accident, as the baba au rhum ended up being the better dessert. It was fantastic, a rummed up brioche filled with crème légère and plated with plump, sweet slices of apricot, all in a sweet sauce ideal for sopping. The coupe myrtille was also great, a lighter dessert of crème fraîche ice cream with blueberries and buckwheat. Tart and refreshing, with nice texture from the buckwheat crumble. We got two last sweet treats with the check--bite-sized butter cookies and strawberry pâte de fruit.

This is probably about as close as you can get to a Ratatouille-style experience (sans rodents) in the U.S., and I was definitely feeling the fantasy. Our meal was remarkable, every bite of it exquisitely delicious. If you're looking for a special place to dine French and fancy, you can't really do better than Le Coucou.

I dined at Le Cou Cou for a very impromptu "Valentine's Day" dinner a day before Valentine's day- a review months late... I know. I wasn't sure what to expect as this was a last minute reservation made by a friend, who hyped this place up to be everything and more. 

Let me tell you... Le Cou Cou far exceeds the hype!

Upon arrival, I checked in with the host and grabbed a drink at the bar to the far right. Small and cozy, I was able to squeeze my way in and have the bar tender mix me something fruity... as I like my drinks to leave me borderline diabetic. He nails it and already I'm off to a good start, a good drink before dinner always sets the tone for me, Why? because it all else fails, I can down a couple of tequilas and my night won't get completely ruined. 

Truly, I can't quite remember the name of the dishes because we tried so many. What I do recall is the presentation of each dish, the combination of flavors and the richness in each bite. I was truly blown away dish, after dish after dish. Aside from that customer service is exceptional, our server was divine and paid attention to all details that night. 

I am looking forward to dining here again....

Brunch here was quite excellent. Had the stingray for an appetizer (delicious and incredibly tender!) and the omelette with caviar, which was light and fluffy. You would expect a fancier restaurant like this to be stuffy, but the interior is charming -- perfect place for brunch.

Amazing food and service!!!! Been wanting to check Le Coucou for awhile for my love of french food. Finally got to try the nice buttery savory dishes with wonderful combination of flavors. 

A friend and I shared the Fluke appetizer which was refreshing and citrusy with sliced cucumbers basil and caviar. For entrees we had the Duck with Foie Gras and the Filet with Bone Marrow which came with Potato Oxtail. Both dishes is a must try!  

If you are a desserts person must must try the desserts. We tried the Praline and the Chocolate Mousse. Praline hazelnut was smooth and decadent but not overly sweet. The mousse was good as well however my friend thought it was heavy on the dark chocolate shavings which made it a bit bitter than her wanting.

Service was amazing. As such a hyped up place was expecting it to be a bit on the stuffy side. However, everyone from the hostess to our server were great and attentive without over doing it. Cup of water was always refilled right away. This is definitely a place worth trying!

Holy Smoke...
This placed knocked my socks off!!!
The taste and textures and flavor manipulation was off the charts. 
An absolute come back!!

Have been for brunch a few times. The food deserves 5+ stars. The service is wonderful with the exception of the reservation policy. Despite the fact that they do have tables intended for 4 people, but definitely could squeeze in a 5th or combine a smaller table to allow for a bigger party size, they don't allow it. I've been there twice now where they will not accommodate a slightly larger party than the reservation is for, even when the restaurant is only half full. Sometimes the French press coffee has grounds in it, but the wait staff fixes the problem with a smile. The croissants are the best in the city and the prices are extremely reasonable considering the caliber of food that is put out.

Just ate here this weekend and didn't love it. We had dined at the chef's restaurant Spring, in Paris, and it was truly one of the best meals of my life. While the food at Le Coucou was good, it wasn't the caliber I was hoping for after such a great experience in Paris. 

The worst part of our dining experience was the team. The service was very stuffy. Everyone that was helping our table seemed miserable to be working there, including our table's head waiter and wine specialist. No one smiled. When I told the somm that we wanted to spend under $100 on a bottle of wine she looked like the wind was taken out of her sails and was uninterested in discussing options. 

Additionally, the paper towels were overflowing the waste bin in the bathroom and the toilet stall was out of toilet paper. Not what you'd expect at a restaurant of this reputation.

The dining area was beautiful. The rumbling of the subway every few minutes incited a deep seeded flight reaction after living in northern California for years, but thankfully the shaking weren't earthquakes.
Fantastic dining experience in a superb space and innovative menu. Food as well was outstanding.  Dishes are prepared with the utmost attention.  A must go and worth th wait for a reservation!!!

My husband made dinner reservations for our anniversary here at Le CouCou. It's a beautiful building with a beautiful interior. The wine list is extensive although quite QUITE pricey. There are hardly any options below $100. We did end up ordering a very lovely cab sauv blend. I was a little confused with the wait staff arrangement as it seemed like we constantly had someone else bringing our food and explaining it to us. Our main waitress seemed to disappear but often spent much more time it seemed at other tables. 

I'll be honest that I wasn't that impressed with the menu options. While I absolutely adore French food, I didn't find many of the items listed to be that enticing. One was veal tongue, another was squab, another sweet bread. Perhaps I like more modern and mainstream dishes but I've eaten at plenty of French restaurants and enjoyed them but wasn't taken by any of these menu items. I settled on the prime fillet which came with bone barrow and oxtail potatoes. I was quite full still from the large lunch eaten earlier in the day but the only thing I enjoyed really were the two small medallions of meat. My husband ordered the Sole which had a really delicious buttery cream sauce on it. 

For dessert my husband ordered the lemon crepe with lemon gelato and I ordered a pound-like-cake that came with soaked peaches in wine. The peaches didn't carry much flavor nor did the cake. 

I was a little disappointed that the waitress never asked if we were celebrating anything. Often times when I've gone to very expensive restaurants they ask up front if you are there to celebrate something in which they will often bring a dessert with writing or a candle to make the evening more special to those patrons. Various people in the restaurant seemed to be celebrating anniversaries or birthdays as I saw MANY dessert plates coming out with candles and writing. Even the table next to us and behind us. Our waitress didn't seem to have much personality she even used the same cheesy line about "oh you must have hated that dessert" after seeing it finished, that she used on the table next to us. Overall, I wasn't blown away by this place. It's beautiful and elegant but there are other French restaurants I'd sooner try out than come back here. It did make for a lovely evening and the food is prepared well though.

Super friendly staff, great ambience, and even better food!
I went here for lunch and dinner few months ago, and went back here for lunch during my most recent business trip to NY. 

I went back for breakfast at 8AM by myself since I was staying at 11 Howard. 
Definitely going back the next time I am in town!

Went to lunch on Sunday after reserving in open table the night before . I've been excited to see the room for months now and it was beautiful no disappointments there. We arrived and were seated at a table for two of which there were 4 open tables in view to me. Our table was the worst and so I told the staff I wasn't sitting there. And asked to be moved which they accommodated. This restaurant trick of filling the bad tables first always annoys me. We ordered.  The  food was not great and very overpriced on this prifix menu. I had the skate appetizer which was drenched in a sweet red pepper which killed any flavor the cold skate might have had. Main course I had the whole baby chicken which was deep fried and seemed reheated. It was disappointing ..... I've had much better fried chicken. I was thinking the deep fry technique was a way of keeping the chicken very moist but it didn't work. All in all the dining experience was ordinary at best. I gave three stars because the coffee was great !

We enjoyed weekend brunch at Le Coucou (I believe they just call it "weekend lunch?"). It was a 2-course menu for $52/person. My dining companion ordered a summer bibb salad (with goat cheese and summer vegetables) and it was delicious. I ordered skate for my first course and did not care for it.

For our second course, we both had the lobster/egg galette and really enjoyed it. It was quite a lot of lobster meat, and we were pleasantly surprised.

The interior was SO BEAUTIFUL. Seriously worth going to see the interior alone.

The atmosphere of the place is really gorgeous. We tried this place on a Saturday at 1pm and there was no brunch menu, only a 2 course prix fixe ($54) was available. The option of the menu are not very appealing for this price point (tartare, buckwheat crepe, quenelle, chicken). They were not very accommodating too - my wife asked if the eggs in the buckwheat crepe can be scrambled and they say it was not possible. Being French and having a Breton grandfather (this recipe is from Brittany), i knew that it was totally possible and felt quite exfuriated. On my side, i took the poached skate as a starter that was good and the grand aioli that was bland and very disappointing -  use of a very cheap fish in a small quantity without seasoning + the sauce that taste everything but aiolï. I don't even know if they used garlic in this sauce where it is supposed to be the main ingredient. 

Another French restaurant that believes they can't serve expensive food just because it's written in French on the menu.

I came here on a Sunday for a birthday lunch and boy was I extremely disappointed. This review is more for the staff than the food. The weekend lunch menu is limited, and there is nothing for children but I had the salad to start and the young chicken as my main meal. This together on the menu says it is $52.. fine
Prior to ordering our meals we decided to order wine..we told the women that was helping us named STEPHANIE which bottle we wanted and she started to question us about if we knew where the wine came from and what region it was from and how we think it would taste... UM EXCUSE ME? You are supposed to take my order without asking 183587 questions as to why I chose the wine I chose... unreal 
So our $80 bottle of wine was out of stock, and we were forced to get one that was more expensive... fine 
After each person left our table they would huddle around in a group and make it very obvious that they were speaking about our table I mean COME ON is this an upscale restaurant or what? Completely unacceptable.. I WILL NEVER RETURN 
Such rude, obnoxious workers especially the wine wiz Stephanie.. if I wanted the history on the wine I am ordering I would have asked.
On top of all of this, they charged $54 per person on the bill, but it clearly says $52 on the menu..
Go somewhere else, many better options

I truly loved this place.The staff were fantastic. So professional, knowledgeable, friendly & efficient. Drinks were perfect. Food was delish esp the dover sole. Will absolutely return. My only gripe was the AC was too low. It's hard to find fault with the place.

As someone else said: Daniel Rose needs to run a tighter ship! 

The review is more for the staff performance ( Monday 9/25)! They kinda ruined my total experience! The place is beautiful and food was pretty good and creative. However, the staff showed amazing disrespect from the beginning; we got there 3 min earlier than our reservation ( well first dinner setting at 5!) however 3 ,almost useless, hostess managed to totally ignore us sitting at the bar waiting and sit 3 other parties before us!!! How rude!


Then the Asian woman who was our waitress took her time to bring us the menu and was probably the most "sour" waitress I have ever had! So indifferent and her unhappy face and aggressive tone of voice was not matching the beautiful place! 

The food was very good but I would not recommend this just because in a city with this much variety you don't want to spend your money and time somewhere that the staff could  ruin or diminish your total experience!

Le Coucou promises heavily sauced French food, and completely delivers on that promise. The sweetbreads had a nice heavy and buttery sauce, while the quenelles had a sauce that spectacularly tasted of the ocean. Unfortunately, the halibut made me feel a little sick eating it for unknown reasons. Terrine was alright, could have used more fat. My personal issue is that I just don't think I'm as interested in this food anymore. Le Coucou delivered on its promise, but I just don't really want what it promises. Still intrigued by the rabbit though, but a little worried that it will disappoint me the same. 

On an unrelated note, service was a bit stiff. Staff made my SO and I feel like we didn't belong there. They also complained a bit loudly behind us that we hadn't ordered enough. My SO doesn't eat that much, didn't really feel like drinking, and the desserts looked mediocre. Sometimes people just don't feel like spending a lot.

This is the sort of restaurant where a slight delay in being seated is something to hope for! Because to arrive and wait at Le Coucou is to spend some time in the beautiful trompe l'oueil aerie that is their "garden" bar. I had a virgin version of their signature cucumber cocktail and was in heaven by the time the gracious and affable maitre d lead us to our table. 

We started slow, working our way patiently and delectably through the appetizers and small plates. The "pike pudding" is something I still recall fondly and will go back for. It was a casual and beautiful symphony of classic French cooking, without the fuss and with a downtown ease. By the time we went into our mains we were in bliss. We shared the Norwegian for dessert and bounced out through the bevy of beautiful people that populate their lobby.

Le Coucou is a beautiful restaurant, and their food is fantastic as well.  The exposed brick and chandeliers are just lovely.

The food was excellent too--we tried the iberico ham and melon dish and the chicken and foie gras dish with pomme puree.  Both were excellent, seriously.  The drink menu was great as well, and I loved the warm, fresh bread that they served with the meal.

Service was very nice, though frankly too attentive to the point that it very much interrupted our enjoyment of our meal.  At one point near the end of the meal, we were still enjoying our drinks and bread, and we finally resigned and gave up our plates when the FOURTH server came to our table to ask to clear it.

I was not impressed by anything in the restaurant. My sister really wanted to go as it was highly rated. We had a reservation for a Sunday lunch which is a prix fixe at $54. I don't mind that but did not feel that this was worth the cost. I thought that the menu was difficult and that maybe giving diners the choice of either a starter or a dessert to be included in the prix fixe would have been better for me. They were out of the entree that my daughter wanted so it it didn't start off well. I started with the bibb lettuce, fall vegetables, o'banon goat cheese, honey vinaigrette. It was fine. My sister enjoyed her entree of the pike quenelle, lobster sauce. I had the chicken and foie fall vegetables roasted fruit, pommes purée, and my daughter ordered the Colorado lamb neck, steamed eggplant, tomatoes. My daughter did not like the lamb so I switched with her and it really wasn't my favorite preparation of lamb. The chicken and foie was okay. I ordered dessert because I was still hungry not having eaten a full entree. Dessert was a lemon tart and that was just okay too. The service was okay, nothing outstanding. I had to ask for ice tea a number of times before it being served. We did notice that there was a flower on every table and each and every flower that we saw was half dried and wilted. I wanted to ask about it to see if it was part of the ambience to have it that way but my daughter begged us not to say anything out of embarrassment. There are other French restaurants in New York that I enjoy much more so I will return to those the next time that I visit.

3 stars is being generous. I was really looking forward to Le coucou after a friend's recommendation and all the Hamiltonesque hype around it, but it was such a let down unlike Hamilton. Service was probably equal or if not worse than lesser upscale restaurants with a server bringing us desserts for another table, unengaged wait staff, and no good bye or acknowledgement from the hosts when leaving. Boy bye! 

The food was again good, but not great and throughout the night we kept on talking about dishes from other restaurants, which obviously is not a great sign. My favorite dishes were the quenelle de brochet, the scallops, and the side bone marrow dish that comes with filet (the actual filet was just okay). The rabbit was once again good, not great and I honestly can't remember the other appetizer we ordered- that's how forgetful it was, like what's her name with Beyoncé and Kelly.

Also the prices went up (some items even up 35%) in one year, which is crazy considering you know that it can't be because of rent cause the restaurant sits above a subway line and you can feel and hear the trains passing by underneath your dinner. Also, we went for a birthday dinner, which I mentioned in the reservation, but nothing was done. I saw another table with a candle, but I didn't feel like talking with the staff so I just let it go. The inside ambiance was beautiful with candles everywhere, but I can get that going to a cathedral for free. Is the place trendy? Yes. Is it terrible? No, but if you actually want good French food I would recommend Daniel. I know it's not hip or cool, but neither is spending a lot of money on a mediocre meal with okay service.

We go there every five weeks and are continued to be amazed by the excellence of the restaurant and how it continues to improve in subtle ways. The sommelier is very knowledgeable in matching the patron's pricing, food pairings and grape needs. It is easy to select the well-known names, but what is terrific about Le Coucou is they can match that to your overall expectations to wines that aren't familiar. Although I have tried nearly every dish on the menu several times, I am continually impressed by the clarity of the taste of each dish where the ingredients are allowed to shine. When I go to Le Coucou, it reminds me of new wave Parisian restaurants that are extremely popular because of tastes and are great places to gather. My favorite gourmandises are the veal sweetbreads and pike quenelles. The sauces are light and packed with a flavor unlike anything available in the USA. All the entrees are excellent but I like the duck with foie gras, Dover Sole, rabbit three ways and the beef filet. The duck is better than anything I have had in Paris. It is perfection. The Dover sole sauteed expertly and matched with a perfectly prepared velvety sauce. The rabbit three ways is an enormous portion in three excellent preparations. Finally, the beef filet has the most delicious potato oxtail gratin ever. If you have room for dessert the fall menu item - an apple Napolean is unbelievably favorful. It may be the best-tasting apple dessert I have ever had.

The dining room is perfect for conversation, and its warmth is enhanced by a long single white candle at each table and the high ceiling with beautiful chandeliers emitting a warm light. The tastes of the food are why you go to Le Coucou. If you are looking for fancy food towers, gold leaf desserts, sculptured foods this is not the place for you. Le Coucou has it all. The food tastes, the service, and the decor are perfect. It is a place where you and your group can enjoy your dining experience without the pretense of stuffy service, needless formality and overtly rich and tired food from old-time French restaurants.

Go there and give it a try and you won't regret it.

This is really the definitive New French spot in the city. Not crazy about the location near Chinatown, but once inside the ambience envelopes you.
The Food is spot-on. Had the St Jacques scallop crudo with a Riesling wine gelee, apple & horseradish--innovative, attractive and tasty. Dover sole and the duck 3-ways (breast, heart & liver aka Foie Gras) are delish. Desserts are must--what seems simple--a raspberry mille-feuille is executed to perfection, and the pastry layers so crisp, the raspberry coulis so tart and tasty. The more complex--a souffle "Omelette" is again a stunner. Wine list has some different unique choices and we enjoyed a Vouvray-based sparkling wine. Service overall is fairly good--the bussers and servers are excellent. Unfortunately,  our waitress/captain whilst pleasant was lacking in full effort, too quick ask about dessert beverages without mentioning our remaining wine, and too quick to retrieve our payment--while forgetting to give us the de rigeur petit fours. Otherwise, this would be a 5-star rating.
We plan to eat here again...
incredible.  sweet breads and skate were the stars of the show.  great service and wine selection.

What a wonderful restaurant.  We were greeted warmly and seated immediately.  The room itself is beautiful.  The servers and wine steward were attentive and efficient.  I don't understand the reviews that criticized the staff.  We had no such problems.  The food was wonderful.  I had the Sole Veronique.  Others at the table had pigeon and beef.  All were prepared beautifully.  All in all, Le Coucou was a special experience and I will definitely be back.  Highly recommended.

"DON'T BELIEVE THE HYPE!" would be the wise words I can offer anyone interested in going to Le CouCou. Since it opened its doors, I have had a longing to dine at the well-known, hotspot. Friends, family, and acquaintances alike posted pictures on social media, raved about the French cuisine, and boasted about their nights at Le CouCou...and I ate the bait!  

We arrived to Le CouCou with high hopes. Arriving punctual to our reservation time, we were asked to wait at the bar!  No problem, my husband and I like to drink. The bar was beautiful.  The bartender, however, was a dark cloud looming over the beauty of the brass hardware and wonderfully lit marble.  Very unhelpful and unfriendly, she couldn't be bothered with mundane questions like, "What exactly is the 'In Memoriam' cocktail?" By the look on her face you would have thought we asked, "Are you currently taking any anti-itch vaginal cream?"  Seriously. She was snooty, aggressive, and the "In Memoriam" cocktail was as sour as the mixologist. But we still stayed positive....

We were soon escorted to our table. A lovely table. We sat down at 9:15. After a few bus boys, a waitress I think (I still don't know what her role was in the dining experience,) a slow sommelier, and finally a manager, 40 minutes into seating, we had finally placed our order.  The staff was unengaged, indifferent, and bored. I wasn't expecting a dinner show, but our servers seemed less than interested in being there.  Lots of arrogance and pomp for taking an order and clearing a table.  

I won't go into the details of our food because I'm not a food critic and can't tell you if the "Quenelle de Brochet" was really how Julia Child would cook it.  But I will say the food was below average. The "beef fois gras" was as good as a Gerber Vienna Sausage. And finding the "Quenelle" in the Quenelle was like looking for the golden egg at the Easter egg hunt.  Hard to find and the prize is not worth the hunt.  The night before my Le CouCou dinner I had eaten at Majorelle, a cozy, quiet, beautiful, little jewel-box of a restaurant.  This isn't the Majorelle review, but Le CouCou didn't compare to the Upper Eastside French eatery.  Poor attitude and mediocre food. I like Daniel Rose's Spring restaurant in Paris... Le CouCou is a far cry.  

I will not be returning, and I doubt Le CouCou cares.  I have never written a review about a restaurant but after last night's disappointment I felt compelled to warn others from falling into the trap of Le PooPoo.  Hope this review helped a bit.
I don't know what else to say other than perfection.  The food was amazing and the service was even better. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone. The beef was particularly spectacular!

I agree with Linda S. review.  3 1/2 stars.  We tried about 6 or 7 dishes.  Mostly the recommended ones from reviews we'd read online, including the quenelles.  We also had the $65 dover sole which was very good but definitely overhyped.  The sauces were really good.  There is a fair amount of butter involved in French cuisine and butter can make everything taste delicious.  But there's no edge beyond that.  It's not particularly creative.  It's classic upscale French cuisine.

We arrived 30 minutes late.  My husband was still driving around looking for parking.  The manager informed me that the table would be needed in 2.5 hours.  I ordered for both of us before my husband arrived.  And, it came out in ridiculously quick succession.  The staff was nice enough but disengaged.  We skipped dessert and after dinner tea/ coffee.  In the end we finished 45 minutes before we had to give up the table.  No one said good bye to us when we left.  

The food was very nice but not amazing.  I'm in no rush to go back, if ever.
French pancake...so delicious! My friend had the avocado toast with a poached egg and it was also very good. Great cappuccino and coffee. Service was amazing and prices are good. ($15-$20/entree)

I do not understand the extreme hype behind Le Coucou, or the shock that they still do not have a Michelin star for 2018.

First impressions are bad.  The host stand is neither particularly welcoming or polite.  Then when we got seated it was 5 minutes before anybody talked to us or gave us a cocktail menu, then another 5 minutes to order cocktails and even see a food menu, no discussion of the food menu when it was given, and we're talking about a 5:15pm reservation where most of the tables were still empty and tons of staff just standing around being unhelpful.  I'm not exaggerating, I was actually looking at my watch.

The food is good, but not mind blowingly good or innovative.  Same with dessert, the pastry chef is not exactly phoning it in but they aren't doing anything noteworthy either with respect to flavor, composition, or presentation.  The high points are the deconstructed whole rabbit, the crab crepe.

Also, our main waitress, while not exactly rude, was not very welcoming, didn't talk much about the food, and was generally the most snobby waitress I've ever seen at a fancy restaurant.  The other staff who came by the table as runners were much better and more friendly.

It is beautiful inside and is definitely an oasis in this "edge of chinatown" neighborhood but considering it's priced like a place that already has a michelin star, but lacks both the service and quality of food I would expect from a place charging those kinds of prices.

Maybe they will up their game but for now, I'd save my money if I were you.

Delicious food, attentive service and gorgeous space. Better to go with a group so you can taste a little bit of everything since the menu is prix fixe. I especially liked the pike quenelle with lobster sauce. The fish is a cake-like texture, which sounds weird, but the sauce is rich and flavorful and really is the star of the dish.

Came here with a party of 4 on a Saturday for lunch at 12:30PM. Had to stay up well past midnight the month before in order to get the reservation. And when we arrived, it really was packed. Maybe only one table unused. 

Overall the food was really good -- but I wouldn't say it was the best value. Saturday brunch is a two-course pre-fix menu at $52 pp. You choose one appetizer and one entree. Dessert and drinks are separate. There was a good selection and with a party of 4 we got to try a good amount of the menu. We all were happy with our choices but felt slightly underwhelmed. 

The space is beautiful, very chic and well done. But the atmosphere wasn't very enjoyable. Not sure if it's always like this but the tables next to us where overly pretentious clientele - who were talking at the top of their lungs about what Seth Rogen said to them at a party. Like, cmon guys - you're right in Chinatown; I could literally walk one block at have a delicious cheap meal at a whole in the wall. The staff was friendly enough (some more than others) and efficient.

Overall I'm glad we tried it but for the price tag, I would pass.

Beautiful, expensive, delicious. What more to say that has not already been said? Traditional French fare with some updating. Attentive service that peaks into a swarm at some moments. Expensive tiny cocktails. Very good wine. Lots of meat and fish, so vegetarians are SOL. The duck is great. The lamb neck is almost two dishes, great value. More fatty than anything I would normally eat, but in this context pretended it didn't count and swallowed all of it. I guess there was butter everywhere, but somehow we manged to leave full of meat and cream and bread, and did not feel gross. Really appreciate no music blaring here, so thanks to management for that. (The ambient noise is plenty.)

Wonderful restaurant and fully deserves all the praise it has received from many different reviewers.

We shared the skate with lobster sauce, which was delicious.  I had the beef filet and my wife had the duck.  Great flavor.  Plus they have Sauternes Chateau d'Yquiem by the glass.

Not CooCoo for Coucou. Big production made by a weird staff in a cozy environment with very overblown presentations of way too "saucy" foods. I know it is a throwback to the good old days of French food, but I think that s##t is in the rear view mirror for a reason. I think Coucou is a "gimmick" and won't endure. Although it was very crowded for at least three seatings last night given the overblown hype, I would much prefer to go to Dirty French (assuming that my guests and I are miked up with ear pieces so that we can actually hear each other speak) or Chirche Midi. Add an extra star for an awesome wine list.

Sunday brunch is out. Breakfast ends at 10:30. Lunch starts at 11:00. If you enjoy snails and an entire chicken for breakfast, you're in luck!  At &54 prix fixe, plus coffee etc., you're into one pricy breakfast!

Beautiful dining room.  A culinary experience -- excellent food, but not large portions.  Not cheap but not ridiculously expensive either.  Would recommend for special occasions.  The wine pours (if ordering by the glass) could be more generous.  But still a great memorable place.

This was an incredible dining experience! I absolutely adored the grand yet cozy decor filled with interesting objects, warm lighting and cozy seating. It is truly an inviting and special  atmosphere. With the exception of the bartenders' snooty attitude, it was perfection. 

We were sent a delicious amuse-bouche before our first course. From the hors d'oeuvres menu my friend ordered the "Poireaux", a beautifully braised serving of whole leeks with hazelnuts. This was not something I would have ordered but it was surprisingly wonderful and so light it could also be a nice side. "Raie au poivron et câpres" or poached skate was light and full of flavor with balance with capers and sweet pepper vinaigrette. And the Crêpe "souvenir de Lannilis" was a light crepe
with crab, buckwheat, and tangy lime which balanced the sweetness. 

From the Gourmandises we had the 
lobster tail which was delicious but essentially a salad with basil, tomato, and sauce lauris, a paprika infused mayonnaise. For me, the pièce de résistance was the "Ris de veau a l'estragon", sweetbreads with crème de tomate, and tarragon. The dish was served ceremonially - presented in a shiny Cooper pot from which the sweetbreads were removed and placed on a plate, while the copper pan of rich sauce was left for my dipping pleasure. It was truly divine! Thankfully I anticipated the incredible richness of the sweetbreads and ordered "Sole Véronique" aka Dover sole for my entrée or as they call it at Le CouCou, "Poissons et Viandes". The fish was a very large portion served with grapes and mushrooms. I loved the balance of sweet and savory. My friend ordered the "Côte d'agneau grillé", Colorado lamb with steamed eggplant, and tomatoes. The dish was served with a perfectly cooked lamb chop, and the incredible flavorful crispy neck. Both were delicious. 

At our waiters urging, for dessert we ordered the "Crêpe souvenir de Lannilis", a crepe with lemon ice cream and citron confit. It was delicious and refreshing. A friend sent us the "Mille-feuille d'automne", a gorgeous flavor explosion pairing roasted apples, pastry and light creme; and the "Omelette Norvégienne flambée à l'eau de vie",  pistachio ice cream dotted with cherries and cake flambéed with brandy. Had we planned on three desserts I'd have ordered the "Mousse au chocolat", which would have been a nice  accompaniment to the crepe.

Everything was delicious. Service was impeccable.  I highly recommend - and look forward to returning.

I wish I could give half stars. The lunch I had deserves 3.5 stars rather than 3. I was rather disappointed with my meal since Daniel Rose is supposed to be some sort of prodigy.  And Spring is one of the more innovative restaurants in Paris. The food was fine-I would say it was at the level of a good but not life changing French restaurant. In Paris it would be considered ok for this price range.  In New York we might call it good but boring. It certainly does not live up to the hype. My main course of foie gras with chicken was lovely-the highlight of the meal. But the egg en meurette was not as good as Le Coq Rico's. And the dessert was fine but basic. I was served corked wine that I had to send back.  I am sure many New Yorkers will appreciate it given this city's obsession with ok French food and the fact that they serve weekend brunch. But it does not live up to expectations/prices. There are far more exciting meals to be had at other restaurants in the city.

Do not eat here - food poisoned.  After the one month advance booking I felt lucky to have secured a reservation for my husband's recent birthday dinner.  I wanted only to love the experience and invited two friends to join us in doing so.  The ambience was beautiful and staff very friendly, which can make or break a meal.  The unfortunate reality which hit that evening and persevered for the 36 hours following was an intense bout of food poisoning.  We did not ingest anything else following this dinner. 
 Foodbourne illness is a serious issue no to be ignored, particularly at an establishment recognized by institutions such as the James Beard Foundation.  My husband is an emergency room physician and an Associate Professor at a very large hospital/medical school in Manhattan.  He and one of our friends, also a physician, both found themselves under severe duress for almost two days following our meal.  My husband felt it was his duty to speak with the Department of Health, which he is in the process of doing.  We also contacted the restaurant, whose response left much to be desired.  It is unfortunate that I have to write this yet we feel it is our responsibility to warn others.

Very fun night! We were there for almost three hours and it flew by. With the exception of two sort of boring dishes, all the food was incredible. Service was what you would expect from a place at this level, but there was something off-putting about it. We were being treated and I asked myself if I had to come here and pay, would I? We ate at Momofuku Ko a few months ago and I would much rather go back there again. There was only one or two dishes that blew my socks off, versus at Ko it was every bite.

Decadent, beautiful, and delicious. Highly recommend for any special occasion. Was lucky to make reservations last minute for Sunday brunch- the host was great and accommodating. I wasn't aware of the prefix menu when arriving but was delighted with the options as everything tasted magnificent. A must visit for anyone enthused by great food and decor.

Brunch before the show. While in NYC before seeing a play I decided to stop at Le Coucou and check out Stephen Starr's creation. The ambiance was quaint and the decor was lovely. The chandeliers and exposed brick was rich and regal. 

To start the meal we had the bread basket. The basket was served with various kinds of croissants, raisin bread, and some type of cheese bread. The cheese bread was rather tart and was not to my liking. The waiter was very accommodating and when noted that I didn't like it, he brought me out another croissant to replace the uneaten bread.  

I had the omelette for my meal. The omelette was perfectly prepared and had a wonderful hint of gruyere cheese and herbs. Although I am a bacon person, I tried a side of sausage instead as I was informed that the sausage was made in house. The sausage was delectable. Seeing as though I have traveled to Paris before, I suggested my companion try the  croque monsier. The croque monsier was delicious as well. This is definitely a place that I will return to.

I really thought I was going to be blow away. I had heard all the hype and was so excited. I did think the ambiance was great, and the service was probably about as good as any restaurant in NYC. Great service. But you are paying top dollar. And maybe I ordered wrong, I started with the Leeks, which were decent. Then I had the Skate appetizer which was average at best. Then I had as my main the Monk Fish. Perhaps these are their three worst dishes? I don't know. I had expected so much. And I thought I could make every thing here better myself at home. which is not what you expect when the tab is well north of $200 for two.

Great food, cozy atmosphere. Was there for lunch and had the oysters and whole young chicken, highly recommend. Horrendous service for a classy restaurant. Expect to get major attitude from waiters, especially the woman with short gel'd back hair with clear glasses, felt like she hated her job. Otherwise, food is delicious.

This is the type of restaurant that you either love or hate. You either love it because it ticks off all the boxes when it comes to classical French food executed flawlessly. Or you just don't have a big love for French food and think it's too much work to get a table here given it can take weeks to months to get a table here. In any event, I will say I was a bit annoyed that I couldn't get here till a few months ago but when we sat down and had dinner all my annoyance and frustration simply went away. We started off with cocktails upstairs at the blond and when it was time we made our way to the restaurant. On an aesthetics level, this space is beautiful. The ambient lighting gives everyone in the restaurant that gorgeous glow. On the service front, the staff has been trained well. This was a long meal for us. We started with a bottle of Chateauneuf on recommendation from the sommelier. Smooth and velvety with great depth.  The house baked bread is yummo. I am usually not a bread and big carbs person but when its warm and comes with house butter, ya gotta give it a try! The poached skate with capers and sweet pepper vinaigrette is not something I normally order but we tried it and it was so tender moist and tasty. The vinaigrette being a hint tangy made for this to be a great starter. Great to work up that appetite and those taste buds. The veal tongue with golden Osetra and creme fraiche was awesome. It did not have any tongue-y weird texture or flavor. The beef cheeks and foie gras was also very good! Beef cheeks were so smooth and the foie was butter! The jelly cut through the heaviness of the foie and this went well with the wine! The sweetbreads with creme de tomate and tarragon was decadent but the acidity tomato and tarragon made this delicious! The halibut buerre blanc was another winner. It looked heavy but didn't taste heavy probably because of the daikon choucroute. For dessert, we shared the crepe suzette. We paired that with a glass of the Macon Clesse to finish. C'est Bonne on all levels!!

Scratching our heads over all the hype?? Looks like any other nice-ish restaurant in the city. We were expecting yummy old European ambiance, not.
The food was just eh. One dish was not good at all. The Pomme frites... fat and greasy. No bueno.
Geez McDonald's fries are even better! Tiny portions and the food bill outrageous! $600.00 for 3 ladies for lunch....and SO not worth it my friends! There's many other wonderful eateries in nyc that have a friendlier atmosphere better food, and a fraction of the cost. Never going back. Sorry guys. Check that one off the list.

Le Coucou is a tough reservation to get, and I got lucky enough to snag one far ahead of time - albeit at 5 PM, which I think is when they just open for dinner. Even though this isn't that far off from the Canal Street subway stop I've used many times, the entrance is pretty innocuous, with only a bit of decorative trees outside the entrance signaling that there's a restaurant nearby. Once inside, you're in a very dimly-lit area (unless you are close to the kitchen) that evokes Old World elegance and is definitely a nice spot to go on a dinner date. Service is formal but not overly so, with drinks and food coming out at a reasonably-timed pace. The wine list, as at any good French restaurant, is extensive, but I stuck with a cocktail and a session-style IPA - both pretty decent despite the relatively limited selection.

The food was excellent all around, with every dish being delicious and little to find fault with. We started off with a half-dozen oysters (the menu is only for 4, but you can add on extras at the same per-oyster price). While perhaps not the best oysters the outright that I have had, I really did enjoy the light seaweed ice it was topped with, giving it a mellow saltiness that was a nice, subtle complement to the clean finish of the oysters. Our other starter was the pike quenelle, which I really enjoyed - the quenelle was very light an airy, with a very rich lobster sauce (as well as a piece of lobster claw) served alongside it. It came off as very light but much heartier than it would seem given how flavorful the broth was. For our entree, we decided that since we were at a really good French restaurant, we had to do the duck for two. Served 3 ways - seared foie gras, heart(!), and sliced duck breast and prepared by the server in front of you hot off the pan - it's an excellent assortment of duck, with the heart being very meaty and the breast cooked just right. It is also served with a pickled vegetable very closely resembling sauerkraut; our server mentioned this was meant to be inspired by the Jewish way of preparing this dish in France. We ended the meal with a pave au chocolat - a deliciously dense slice of chocolate cake, served alongside a nutty hazelnut ice cream.

In all, I can understand why Le Coucou has been so popular - the food is excellent, and while it doesn't go out of its way to be too adventurous, it's safe to say that it does excellent higher-end French cuisine. Make sure to get a reservation as soon as you can, because it fills up quickly ahead of time!

I have to start that I'm not a fan of French cuisine. But oh god it's not about Le Coucou. It was amazing and unforgettable! I came for dinner with a friend 3 month after it was open I don't know about reservations since I didn't make it but it was just wow. First of all the interior is everything. It's one of the most beautiful restaurants I ever been too. You can just look at the bar and enjoy the scene. We got many things to try and everything was perfect from the beginning to start. The wine list is intense but we manage to get a great bottle of wine. Servers as you aspect from this king of establishment  is   Spotless. It's expensive but worth it. I have been in many great restaurants but it was a memorable dinner for sure. I been in couple places by Stephen Starr in Philly and it's always a great experience. If you have a chance definitely go and enjoy thing experience. Bravo Le Coucou

Delicious, lavish, sumptuous, grandiose, sophisticated, Francophilian, indulgent, transporting, fashionable, seductive.  

All of those.
Leeks, hazelnuts, crepes, crab, sole, sauce, grapes, lamb chop, lamb neck, chocolate, Madeira....magic!

Were it easier to snag a reservation here, or somewhat less expensive, I might  have given five stars. But the difficulty of getting a table, and the size of our tab, meant that five stars required absolute perfection, not an A/A-.

Our greeting was friendly and professional, and despite our not being gliterrati, we received a prime table. Service was excellent from start to finish. Fine attention, water glasses filled, only one occasion were we felt hurried. The wine service from the sommelier was particularly fine, a shout-out to her.

My offspring had their cocktails at the bar, I had a Negroni at the table. There were mixed reviews on the martinis, but the red drink hit the spot, albeit a small spot. I commanded a glass of Sancerre for my spouse, pricey at $24.

We decided to share two of the hors d'oeuvres, while each diner chose an appetizer and entree.

A terrine of beef cheeks, enlivened with a few cubes of foie gras tasted quite similar to a much less costly one I had eaten in Normandy a few years back. A generous slice. The crepe with crab was also a winner, the crisp pancake covering large chunks of superior lump backfin. For bread, the house serves nice slices of pain de campagne, with soft butter. Retain that bread for mopping up sauces. Do not surrender it. 

Our gourmandises were uniformly excellent, hard to pick a winner, The homard in the lobster salad was firm, well chilled and plentiful. The crepinette of chicken and foie gras savory. My quenelles de brochet came as a single piece, large and oblate. Sauce Nantua was replaced with an sauce styled as an americaine, which seemed more like brown butter. (The original homard a l'Armoricaine, a forgotten appellation.) Nevertheless, the dish was light and delicious. The sweepstakes winner -- the ris de veau perfectly cooked and tender in a mushroom sauce. But all of the appetizers were great.

With our first courses we shared a 1/2 bottle of a Chablis Premier Cru. It was handled well, but was not memorable.

The same cannot be said of all the main courses. The rabbit was the clear winner, served three ways, roulade of the breast, a sort of fricasee, and a broth with the legs. The broth had an exceptional subtle savor. The choucroute with duck was an interesting variation, Tender slices of breast meat were good, but slightly overdone for this eater. The single cuisse was segmented into leg and thigh, crisp, almost like confit. A nice finger of foie gras. Revelation came in the preparation of the heart, more tender than expected, a fine small viand. The sauerkraut had picked up a rich flavor from the bird. Still at $98 (for two) I would have liked to have received a whole duck, or at least half of a larger one, even if they have to charge a bit more for fowl. My son also found his pheasant, in a curry sauce, to be a small portion, A bowl of fruited rice filled the gap somewhat.

With the main courses we shared a half bottle of Volnay that was quite nice.

We had room for dessert. The Mont Blanc, at $18 is worth more than the less costly choices. It is a work of art, which reminds me of of an artichoke in its construction. The mille feuille d'automne, with apples and cream, was more filling than expected, and a good sized portion. Two desserts should suffice for four.

A complimentary plate of sweets arrives at the close, with cookies and a sort of crisp thin spiced chocolate square,

Overall this was a fine meal, but considering that four people could easily blow a grand here, it is a debatable proposition whether the cuisine is commensurate with the cost.

I will likely return for brunch if I can.

Beautiful space, fabulous menu, $10 large coffee. FYI - because this was unclear to me - the brunch situation is $50 for two courses. You choose one plate from two different sections. I had the Lobster Buckwheat Crepe and it was PERFECT. Started with a Fall salad which was also really lovely.

Dover sole was amazing. It was $62, the priciest item, but the best dish. The monkfish, also amazing, second best dish. The rabbit is so-so as was the beef-cheek-and-foie gras tarine appetizer. 
But the service and ambiance was very nice and listed items were great. Great place, underrated

Beautiful and warm atmosphere. Service was excellent. Food was superb. The crab crepe was delicious. We had the skate appetizer that was brought out complimentary and was excellent. The Bibb lettuce salad with lobster was perfect. The monk fish was exceptional. And lastly, the bread pudding was the perfect end to a perfect meal!

Finally I was able to get the table here. It's not surprise why this is the hottest restaurant in NY. Beautiful, Cozy, comfortable vibe and warm service. Everyone look very presentable and charm. Food is delicious and creative. Lunch menu is fair reasonable 54 per two courses. Highly recommend. Just personal feeling, I always don't understand why prefix menu is not included dessert. That's it. That's the only turn off part

Absolutely sensational dining experience at Le CouCou. Came here to celebrate my boyfriend's bday on a Saturday evening. Booked the reservation exactly 28 days out and could still only get a 530pm timeslot. Really would have preferred a couple hours later but I'll take what I can get!

To my surprise, when we arrived at 530pm, a majority of the tables were already full. Like to believe this was foreshadowing the upcoming greatness we would experience. 

The waitress and wine sommelier were both extremely helpful when we asked questions about a few dishes and bottles of wine we were deciding between. Didn't feel like they were pushing you to try anything specific, they really made it all about your experience. After we decided on our entrees and wine, they brought over two types of bread and butter (spelt and another type!)

We ordered the veal tongue with foie gras, sweetbreads in a mushroom sauce, and the duck for two. The waitress brought these all out separately as 3 courses. Sweetbreads stood out because of the sauce poured on and around it inside a pot brought to the table. Literally could have drank the sauce in a glass. Definitely asked for more bread for dipping. Veal tongue was so tender and melted in your mouth, which was a perfect combo with the foie gras and creme fraiche. Duck for two was a great portion. There was duck confit, duck heart and then the seared duck slices on top of daikon radish which was similar to a sauerkraut. We were so satisfied after these 3 dishes and probably wouldn't have needed dessert if it wasn't a bday dinner. My boyfriend opted with the apple three ways which was like a deconstructed apple crisp with cream.

Fantastic dinner and will most definitely be coming back.

The dark, candle lit, open kitchen ambiance sets the tone for a fantastic meal. The sweatbread appetizer is the best sweatbreads we have ever eaten - it is a must order if you like sweatbreads. The sauce is what makes it - deliciously savory. The pike appetizer is also very good. They formed the pike into a soft mousse concoction with some very nice sauce and flanked by lobster meat. The lamb was very tasty, it was served in two parts, more traditional and then a meaty portion to really fill you up. The monkfish was only good, but nothing too special with the flavor of the broth. We loved the Mont Blanc dessert. It is a light, but very sweet cake based treat constructed on top of candied apricots.

SOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO GOOD! I loved my dining experience at LeCoucou last weekend when I was in town from California. I love the decor and the space and the service was exquisite. It was expensive, but you get what you pay for. I definitely recommend this restaurant for date night, a fancy celebration, or if you are trying to impress some clients. Good luck getting a reservation though. :)

Le Coucou has been one of my most enjoyable and fulfilling food experiences. It truly embodies the definition and quality of French fine dining. 

Although the portions are on the small end of the spectrum, the flavors are so intense and comforting that you don't tend to mind too much. Their wine selection is impressive and surprisingly reasonably priced and the sommeliers are incredibly helpful in picking the best bottle (it is difficult to understand if you are not fluent in French). 

Like most fine dining restaurants it is on the pricier side and requires a reservation well in advance. But trust me, it is very worth it. If you're looking to impress bougie family members or a special someone on a date then this is a great choice! If you are looking for a low key meal with no frills, you may want to order pizza.

First time here. Everything was very good. Warm, cozy ambience. Not too loud. Great for a date or celebration. Service was impeccable.  We had the pike quenelle, veal tongue, and beef cheeks and would rate them in that order. All very good, but the quenelle is something different and rare to find. We had the duck for 2. All parts perfectly cooked and seasoned just right. One of the best duck meals I've had. And I've had a lot of duck in my life. Nice that it is served with daikon that is a bit sour (like sauer kraut but lighter) to balance the richness of the duck. It came with foie gras, not seared, but cooked just right to complement everything. For desert we had the pistachio ice cream flambé. Awesome! Also had the choco mousse that was good with the various textures but not as special as the pistachio.  This is a place worth your effort in getting a reservation.  Some places are hard to book because of a lot of hype or frequented by celebrities, but this place backs it up with excellent food and service.

The food and service are though the roof.  The rabbit is perhaps a best ever, I crave it.  Sure there is lots of hype, but the hype is because the experience is remarkable in every way.  This is a restaurant that others should benchmark against.

This place is one of my favorite restaurant experiences in the city. 

I came here for my most recent birthday dinner and ate a truly obscene amount of French food, and I'm here to tell you it was SO worth it. The food here is far from what you could describe as 'comfort food' and incorporates its fair share of unique ingredients (the French don't let anything go to waste). But each morsel of food & drop of sauce feels as if it's been so vigorously vetted to ensure its perfect harmony on your plate that...one really has nothing to complain about.  

Dishes you must try: the pike quenelle & the duck entree (canard et figues). If you have a sweet tooth - also try out their mille-feuille (it's seasonal so the fruit flavoring will depend on what time you decide to go). 

If you're curious about my other thoughts on the spot (and other things I eat in general) - feel free to check out my blog at: cardinaldirections-blog.com.

Cheers!

Great breakfast with reasonable price. Ordered an omelette and a side sausage. The omelette is probably one of the best I've had so far. The egg is so smooth and soft, with a good blend of taste with the Gruyere. The sausage is excellent, crispy on the outside and juicy and tasty inside. Besides, the omelette only costs you like $15, which is very standard in nyc brunch menu.

I've been hearing about this place for such a long time, and always thought it would have been over rated. Boy was i wrong. I regret not coming here sooner. Food was great, service excellent, amazing room, super comfy and terrific experience all around. Le coucou is a great classroom example of how a proper restaurant should have been run. TAKE NOTES, start up restaurants.

I really don't have words or enough starts to give to this place from food to the service, everything was outstanding!

Place is absolutely gorgeous, staff is friendly, drinks are great, don't hesitate to come here.

Came here late the other night for a post theatre dinner. Despite leaving past midnight I didn't feel rushed at all. The staff were patient and attentive. They were very helpful with explaining the menu.

Their #1 cocktail was delicious. I really wanted a second glass. (Very proud of myself that I was able to limit myself to only one.) I had the beef cheeks and foie gras terrine to start. It tasted ok, but I couldn't get past the texture. As an entrée I had the rabbit. The pot au feu was my favorite. That stock (or broth whatever) was delicious. Nice warm soup for a cold night. So I took it home so I could enjoy it longer. The mille-feuille was fantastic. Loved the roasted apples. I regret not ordering another one to go. I also tried my friend's dishes. She had the sweetbreads and the filet. I like her food better than my own. The chiboust aux chocolat was good but I preferred the Mille-fruitlessly. Overall a nice enjoyable dinner.

The ambience is a 10 but the entrance is too dark for me.  I could not tell if it was open or not in spite of our reservation.

The chandeliers remind me of the beautiful mosques I saw in Istanbul.  Makes a statement!

Food is complex to prepare.  The buckwheat crepe is good with the fresh crab meat in lime aioli but pricey.

My Lobster quenelle was well done with foam broth.

The rabbit in 3 ways was very good if you like rabbit.

The dessert which is like a small cake but really a miniature baked Alaska was good but not a knockout for me.  Just beautifully presented.  I would have rather had a slice of regular Baked Alaska because I like the egg white meringue on top browned.  This had very thin coat of the egg white meringue I look forward to in a Baked Alaska.
Amazing place. Phenomenal food. Beautiful decor. Friendly staff. Obviously slightly pricey but definitely worth it.

Beautiful Ambience - Horrible Service - OK cuisine.  Always dining at Jean Georges, Marea, Milos and every other fine restaurant in Manhattan.  This restaurant had a horrible waitress with a rude attitude that kept recommending how we should order less food, and get it cooked at the temperature she liked vs. the temperature we like.  We kept sending it back to be cooked more as they prefer blood red, and we went out to eat after the meal.  Wine was nicely served at proper temperature.  For $500 to $1,000 meal, we would not think of going back.

Restaurant is down near Canal Street and a cozy decor that is very romantic.  The service was upbeat and impeccable. The food is very classically French, which is sometimes less approachable for some.  We had a great meal overall.  I had the beef cheeks and foie gras (it was tasty, but the beef overwhelmed the foie a bit), the pheasant in curry was a standout (pheasant can be dry, but this was cooked perfectly, tender and perfectly executed French-Asian fusion), and the crepe dessert with lemon curd ice cream hits just the right spot. 

Pricey but worth it.

Dined here with friends on a rainy Saturday evening.  Reservations were hard to snag as they only have one table that seats more than 4.  My friend who is the king of reservations was persistent enough to get us off the waiting list.  The ambience of Le Coucou is the opposite of Daniel Rose's restaurant in Paris- Spring, which had bright, simple decor and menu. This is where we had conversation with him as he was working in an open kitchen in front of our table.  When he served the dessert course and we questioned if we should eat the figs or tarte first he said to us with a whimsical smile,  "I don't tell you when to eat it,  I only tell you what to eat"- Very socratic for a philosopher turned chef, an American in Paris.  First of all the the name of the restaurant Le Coucou is wonderful- The Cuckoo,The Hello or perhaps, The Sweetly Crazy- is a creative play on words for this opulent traditional French restaurant.  From the moment you walk in the ambience created by the high ceilings, candlelit tables, chandeliers,  silverware,  floors  and art makes you feel like you are in a French Palace. The menu is simple and divided into three parts: Hors D'Oeuvres; Gourmandises (more hearty appetizers), and Main courses that include Poissons (fish) and Viandes (meat). The favorites included: Ris de veau a l'estragon (sweetbreads, crème de tomate, tarragon),Quenelle de brochet, sauce américaine (pike quenelle, lobster sauce), chicken and foie gras with warm fruit, Filet de boeuf, jus à la moelle, queue dans la boulangère (prime filet, bone marrow jus, served with oxtail potatoes), 'Choucroute' à la juive (for two)
duckling, foie gras, daikon radish prepared Alsatian style, Navarin de lotte (monkfish in a mussel broth with turnips).  All dishes were beautifully plated, service was outstanding- our waitress was a bit on the abrupt side at times but she expertly recommended dishes for us. 
We shared a cheese plate, desserts and port and at the end of our 3 hour meal we all agreed that we would come back again to Le Coucou. My chef stalking led me to the back where I eyed Chef Rose in the open kitchen. I smiled as I passed by because he's come to share his talents in New York.

reservations for this place is plain difficult.  I was seated at 6:30pm and the place was empty.  When we left around 8:30pm, the place was only at 2/3 capacity....
They charge $$$$ like a michelin star, but lack it.

The food was great and the service was excellent.  Why only 4 stars?  Venison is hit or miss, and in this case it was a miss.

just about everything else made up for it, though.

I'd come back but for lunch.
