There will be folks in blazers and dresses more than likely, so keep that in mind. During our short wait, we took to the bar and got an EXCELLENT vanilla cocktail. It was memorably good. 

For starters, my two friends and I shared the foie gras chicken and fried octopus. I thought the foie gras chicken was out of this world. They also bring out bread which is freshly baked. Be careful not to fill up on this... I'm serious. No really.

As far as entreés, my buddy got the sole and the other got the monkfish. They wanted to try something unique and different. I opted for the filet and was not disappointed. One of the best cuts of meat I had in my entire life. Err on the side of medium when ordering this dish. It also comes with Oxtail Potatoes, which are probably almost as good as the cut itself. I finished all my food, and was full, but not sick, after coming in very hungry. 

For desert, we kept it simple and shared a strawberry shortcake. The server brought us complimentary chocolates at the end of the meal, which were a nice touch. Service was on point all night. We sat near the kitchen so it was pretty awe-striking watching the magic happen all night. 

I can't for the life of me understand why this place didn't get a star, or why people are leaving anything less than 5-stars on yelp. Presentation was stellar. This is now one of my favorite spots in nyc and I'll be back in the near future. Great place for a date of any kind, celebration, anniversary, etc.

Went for brunch with a friend and her cousin. We had bloody Mary's which was pretty decent . Food was great but super heavy and rich for me. But no complaints about that I just can't eat as much as I want hahahahaha. Beautiful space and the service was good too :)

Had a great lunch at Le Coucou. The restaurant is very elegant. They did a great job with the interior and the open kitchen is a nice touch. The fixed price lunch had lots of good options. The presentation was very strong for each course. The chicken with foie gras was delicious and is not to be missed!

Boy, I really wanted to like this place. I've heard and read such incredible reviews. It is possible that without the expectation and the crazy high pricing, I would have given it a better review.
Service: not what you'd expect from a 3 star New York Times review. We waited almost 3 minutes by the host's desk for someone to greet us with no other customers around. Our waiter and the busboys were MIA. 
Food: in general, very good, but extremely limited menu with ridiculously tiny portions-- and this was what I was thinking before seeing the bill... A few items did stand out: the veal head, the quenelles, and the pigeon. The oysters however were "blah", the lobster appetizer was a joke, and the monkfish was just okay. 
Desserts were very good. 
The wine list is probably the most expensive wine list in the city.
Then came the bill.

I want come here few month ago but alway full house and gotta make restorations so don't have time to do that so today finally go in try again finally have space available for two people @5pm I order 6 dishes my favorite one is oysters, other few dishes it's okay! cocktail drink is wonderful I love it a lot!! Service is great . Inside the restaurant is romantic and comfortable!! Definitely will be back try other thing again

Overrated French trash, don't eat here unless you like pretentious food that is uninteresting and boring, any tasting menu in the city would be better than this one. Not to mention the amateur team of chefs (if you can call them that) barely know how to cook. you can watch them while you eat through their open kitchen and luckily my table had a Front row seat and it's almost a comedy act to watch them fumble around trying their best to put together "French" cuisine. My wife's duck was over cooked (thanks to one of the sous chefs who I saw put it back under the salamander after the line cook finished it). And their menu while trying to be different was just downright boring, they serve a raw mussel with almost no unique flavor or texture on top of a giant bed of salt and call this an appetizer, along with some mushy leeks and hazelnuts. The only good thing I had here was their cheese board which wasn't even made by the foul mouth chefs who kept openly swearing in the kitchen when there was a table next to us with young children, even the chef de cuisine covered in arm tattoos and a dark haired woman who I assume was his sous chef were dropping f bombs and swearing like sailors in the kitchen, very unprofessional for a place that considers itself to be a "fine dining restaurant"

I keep a list of every restaurant I've ever been to in New York City.  I refuse to admit that that's lame, so here we are.  

After thinking I went to my 1000th restaurant (Pepolino), someone aptly pointed out to me that I had only been to 999 restaurants.  I got a *little* emotional, therefore we booked Le Coucou immediately for a Saturday afternoon.

We made a 1:30 reservation for lunch and decided to be very casual about it / not make a huge deal about this being my 1000th restaurant.  We were seated promptly and the server asked if we were celebrating anything.  "IT'S MY 1000TH RESTAURANT" I pretty much screamed at him.  My date cowered in embarrassment.  It's fine; I have no shame.

The restaurant itself is quite elegant and the service is absolutely top notch.  The servers are all knowledgable and professional without being condescending.  Pretty sure every employee in the restaurant told me congratulations at some point or another. 

Lunch is $54 a person for two courses which, given the quality, is appropriate.  We got:

COURSE ONE:

VELOUTE DE POMMES DE TERRE: Came highly recommended, and this dish delivered.  Potato soup topped with caviar.  What's not to love? 

SKATE: Poached skate in some sort of sauce that contained both sweet pepper and fairy magic.  Highlight of the meal, NOT to be missed.  Our server recommended this to me and I feel like I owe him a drink.  I ate this about two weeks ago and am still thinking about it.  

COURSE TWO:

CHICKEN & FOIE GRAS: I had a small bite of this and didn't like it, which must mean they're doing something right because I've never liked foie gras.

QUENELLE W/ MIXED SEAFOOD: First quenelle ever, and this will be the quenelle which all other quenelles will be measured up to.  The sauce this was in was produced by the same magic sorcerer who created the skate sauce.  The mussels were absolutely perfect.

DESSERT:

I ordered a decaf cappuccino which was lovely, and we got some melon sorbet which was super refreshing after lunch.  They also brought out some petit fours.  One was a dense berry confection and, although I was so full I was not convinced I'd be able to stand up, I still managed to down all of this dessert.  

Le Coucou: not a cheap lunch, but worth every penny.  Thank you for making my #1000 so memorable!

Not as good as I had expected. Two out of the five dishes were excellent. However the service and ambiance were spot on.  Not sure I would dine here again. There are so many very good French restaurants to choose from.

Lovely setting (though no music) & good service but hugely overpriced. I was disappointed with the small portions - and sides weren't even on the menu - charged at about $30 a plate. 

My north with monkfish was tasty but lacked any carbs to soak up the juice! Aside the bread on table. Rather a rip-off.

Not a fan and I won't go back. Much rather find a nice rustic family-run place with equally good ambience & far better value!

Beautiful decor, high-class vibes, impressive wine list, a decent pretentious Manhattan fine dining experience.  Overall experience was a bit lackluster.  While the food was all very delicious, meticulously prepared balancing the richness and subtlety of French cuisine, for the price point I expected something a bit more refined and interesting.  There are many French restaurants throughout Manhattan that deliver similar quality for a much lower price. In the NYC context, the deliciousness to $$$$ ratio is a bit off here.  If I am paying top dollar I expect some sort of above and beyond authentic palatial experience. Here you get great french food, in a bit of a contrived theatrical setting, which for some compensates for the otherwise ordinary flavors presented. Great place if you want to impress a date with your wine knowledge and perhaps a good spot for a tourist to get a trendy Manhattan fine dining experience.

Le Coucou has been attracting a lot of attention from Eater.com-type outlets, many of which have been frothing at the mouth annually over its being denied a "vaunted" Michelin star again, again, and again. 

Michelin stars are kind of a dying European relic of empire to me. But that aside, the Le Coucou hype at once intrigued my interest and made me skeptical. Having just had fancy food out west that actually lived up to the hype, though, I decided to see if this was SPAGO EAST.

The verdict: YES!!!!! I was worried the snob factor would be off the charts, but it really isn't. Plenty of people wearing casual clothing, and no death stares like the one I got when I entered Everest (in Chicago) rocking a Chicago Bulls hoodie and the Gold Coast crowd looked like they wanted to kill me.

Moving on to the food: the egg/mushroom dish is surreal. Lobster thing isn't bad, but honestly, just get 2-3 of the egg/mushroom things to split. I had the much-hyped quenelle fish dish (it's kinda got the texture of a quiche, only made out of fish), and OMGGGGGGGGGGGGGGG. My main event was the pigeon, and I have to say I wasn't crazy about it. I'm sure it was fine, but texture was just a bit rough, and I kept thinking about Central Park and bird poop. Desserts were surreal. I definitely recommend the flambe (sp). Amazing theater. They pour rum on it and light it on fire. Just don't be stupid and remember to blow it out. We almost didn't, and our flambe (sp) almost turned into charcoal. Chocolate mousse thing pretty great as well.

Decor is dark mood lighting with these large candles on the table. If it's too tall, and there's flame in your face the whole meal, I'd ask them to swap it out. We didn't do this until it was too late. By then, we'd had flame searing into our eyeballs for most of the meal. Oh, well. You live, you eat, and you learn.

It gets the vaunted #MERLINFIIIIIIIIVE.
Fantastic restaurant! The ambiance, the service, and of course the food is amazing! Would love to come back one day!

Very posh and if you aren't used to this type of atmosphere then don't go - it'll make you feel out of place. I had to fill myself up with bread which was ok, hard but nice... if it wasn't for the bread I would of walked out hungry. The food is WAY OVERPRICED! - don't go in for a special occasion and expect to be treated with special attention or a little extra cuz they won't do that! They might throw a candle but hey the desert is not even worth the calories. The food again is overpriced and I would never go back again. Too overrated and not somewhere I would wanna be taken to on a first , second third or any other date! I had a recommendation from someone and booked it for my anniversary with my man and it was a complete disappointment ;/ I wish I went somewhere else especially cuz it was out last night in NYC :/

How can I write a helpful 5 star review?

I went to le coucou for my 30th birthday dinner, and was happy from start to finish. I've had the opportunity to eat at many of New York's finest restaurants and this one ranks amongst my favorites.

Ambiance: white washed brick walls, restoration hardware style windows, long tapered candles, a kitchen that's open to the dining room. Velvet sofas and chairs. Modern romantic done right. 


Service: top notch all night. Our server was knowledgeable, the gentleman who brought us our food was equally knowledgeable and I appreciated that they described each dish, where it was from etc before serving. They make it a point to serve dishes to the whole table at the same moment. The sommeliers were knowledgeable but not pushy. A fourth gentleman helped us navigate the dessert menu and drink menu with enthusiasm and personality and brought us one of my favorite bites of the night--apricots soaked in cognac which was absolutely delicious. Ask for them.

Food: the bread is the only thing they don't make in house buts delicious and accompanied by Vermont butter. I started with the quenelle. I never order white fish. This stuff is rich, thick and heavenly. If you like butter, you'll like this. It's also just a terribly rare thing to eat. For dinner we had the duck for two. The steak and the rabbit. The rabbit is good and prepared 3 ways, but was the least exciting of the three. The steak is cooked perfectly in a perfect sauce- I could have licked the plate. The accompaniments are perfect potatoes and in the middle is a soft brisket like meat. My dad and I split the duck and if I returned I'd do it again. The duck parts are many and accompanied by foie grad. The dates that accompany this are so perfect. Dessert--my mom just wanted ice cream and while it's not listed on the menu they acquiesced and OMG the vanilla ice cream (made in house) is a perfect flavorful Madagascar vanilla. (We are ice cream snobs). The framboise and the chocolate cake are also delightful.

Overall, beautiful well done space, excellent professional service and delightful food. Will come back.

The food is good, but nowhere close to great. A decent French brasserie will have food just as good if not better, with a much more fun and laid back attitude. If I'm going to a place that's this hyped I expect to have my mind blown, instead I just had a decent meal at a very "upscale" looking restaurant.

The food is really splendid here and the service is really wellrounded. It was the only dinner I had in New York City for I only had a day trip. It was a tiring day but the environment in the restaurant was so relaxing. I had a wonderful night and I would definitely come back again.
Awesome food, services and ambience. Would definitely come back and recommend to anyone who'd appreciate fine French cuisine

Was staying at the 11 Howard and came by for lunch one afternoon being rained in. Service was top notch, interiors were beautiful.. lunch was ok.. I'd been expecting really good food from all the hype here... the flavor, textures, presentation were pretty unexciting but execution was well done.

The food is very good here.  George gave us great service. The oysters and lobster app were very good. The monkfish was amazing with great flavor. The halibut was cooked perfectly and tasted great
The chocolate mousse was decadent.

The reviews are right - a five star dining experience with beautiful atmosphere and decor. Service is very attentive as expected, the menu is interesting, and the candle lit ambience makes this an ideal spot for a romantic celebration.

I have never been for dinner, as reservations are impossible, but the clafoutis is my favorite breakfast in NYC. Setting is gorgeous, service is impeccable, and the clafoutis is nothing short of devine. I love this place!!!

I've been wanting to come here for a while now but kept putting it off because for some reason I had it in my head that this was a prix fixe sort of place. And my stomach just doesn't seem to agree with 7+ courses. Anyway, happily surprised to discover it's not. The service and food surpassed my expectations--our server was super personable and the fish was so well done. The ambiance is unbeatable, the interior is just absolutely beautiful.
I wish I could formulate the words to describe how excellent the breakfast is here. The omelette is incredible, the latte is to die for, and the bacon is perfect. EAT HERE!

Went to le coucou for a birthday dinner.  Despite having reservations, we waited over 30 minutes for a 10:30 seating.  Once seated, we did indeed experience delicious food and wonderful service.  But there was a catch....within hours I experienced severe food poisoning, likely as a response to eating fish.  Severe enough that it warranted a visit to an urgent care center and a round of antibiotics.

That day, I emailed the restaurant and received no response.  Bothered by the lack of communication, I called the restaurant a few days later to let them know.  The person handling the call first validated my reservation and whether I actually ate there (I did) and then secondly apologized.  That's it, no follow up.

While I certainly understand why le coucou is a wonderful dining experience in NYC, I am troubled by their lack of concern when things don't go so well.

We came to Le Coucou for brunch. Well turns out they only have breakfast early and only options were lunch. That's fine, but not clear on their website, unless I missed it. The restaurant itself is a lovely space. But the food doesn't love up to the hype. The sweetbreads were a good interpretation but overall we were underwhelmed.

My boyfriend and I recently enjoyed a wonderful evening at Le Coucou.
You will enter into an elegantly decorated setting with high ceiling. And adding to the romantic ambiance , a tall candle placed on every table. You will be welcomed by an unpretentious wait staff that provides excellent service.
We enjoyed the chicken and foie gras, leeks , halibut and the prime filet. All were excellent and especially the filet, which was the best I've had. We shared the Omelette Norvegienne to complete our perfect meal. You will also find the wine list to be quite extensive with many excellent selections.
Overall, our experience was delightful and we are looking forward to returning soon!

It was my second time here and I really think the food is just okay. Old-school French. The chicken and foie gras was very interesting and tasty but the last two courses were extremely salty that my friend and I couldn't eat anymore, the rabbit and lamb neck. The service and atmosphere is lovely but I was expecting better food.

How this place has such good reviews floors me. Staggeringly overpriced. Rude and awkward staff. Mediocre food (at best).  All the dishes we received were either a strange texture, unappetizing temperature or bland flavor.  Could not even finish the dishes even though we were still hungry.  Good drinks and that was about it. Depressing.

I honestly can't remember the last time I had such a bad meal. It was so uninventive and bland. Which wouldn't be that big of a deal, but every dish was over $30 and bite-size. It's pretty hard to screw up French food but they did. Not one dish was great. Everything was very uninspired and lacked flavor. The leeks for example, are literally just 4 boiled leaks with peanuts on them. Our Bill was almost $600 for a party of four. Even the foie gras was bad. It's very hard to make foie taste bad. However all the textures of every dish were just dismal. Additionally the servers were very rude. They hovered over us the entire time. The ambience is great and the drinks were solid. I would absolutely not recommend this restaurant. It's unfortunate because the location has potential.

The food is excellent, no question whatsoever. Original, interesting, tasty, healthy, excellent ingredients, fulfilling. The price is high but well worth it. What I didn't like was even though I made advanced reservation, I was given a horrible table. The ambiance is not attractive. Loud. Felt uncomfortable throughout even though the service was fast and efficient. If you are going there with a date, demand and make sure to get an okay table.

I adore this place. It looks fancy, but it's also loud, so you don't have to pretend you are at some super fancy place where you need to be careful with your knife and fork to not make any sound. You can also talk and laugh with your friends. Every dish was well presented, at the same time, all of them tastes great and down-to-earth, and it doesn't have any of those foam that is so popular in other fancy modern French restaurants. I almost think it's American style french food. Booking at prime dinner time is not easy. Make sure you book a month ahead of time if you plan to dine here on a Friday or Sat night. There is a good reason why this place is so popular. I'll be back for sure

No one cooks like Daniel Rose. The food is spectacular, the staff knowledgeable, and the atmosphere sophisticated without snobbery. One of the best in NYC!

My husband and I have eaten everything on the menu (not all in one sitting, of course!), and we highly recommend: 

Sweet Breads
Poireaux (leeks and hazelnuts) 
Blood sausage
Fried veal head
All of the Rabbit
Grilled ducking 

Everything is wonderful... and I mean EVERYTHING. The above list is just a few of our favorites. The menu changes, and we go back often to try new things.

The end of our brunch at Le Coucou two weeks ago put a damper on our entire experience. While the food and presentation is excellent, management needs to remind themselves of two things  (1) this not a parisian restaurant, and (2) therefore cannot behave like one. 

The waitstaff were for the most part quite pretentious and lacked a personableness that you find in fine dining experiences. Due to the inflexibility of the kitchen/chef, one of our guests was not able to find anything on the menu suitable to eat (again in a top restaurant the chef will go above and beyond to serve guest needs). So the guest decided not to eat and enjoy the company.

At the end of our meal, the maitre d' came over to ask us to leave as there was another party needing the table. The non-eating guest made a joke and the maitre d' had the chutzpah to say that typically non-eating guests are charged the full prix fixe. This response was uncalled for and rude. You simply do not treat customers / guests in this manner.

where to begin...  Made reservation for anytime after 8pm. They said there are none available but will call me back if someone cancels. Next day they didn't call back but I decided to call to confirm and they said they have a spot available at 9:35pm. I said that is fine, I get a call at 9:15 asking if we are still coming, I said yes the reservation is at 9:35pm and we went back and forth on the reservation time, finally the man said it's fine just come. We got there, had another back and forth situation... I am so close to leaving already. Regardless ended up sitting at a table at 10:15pm. Already over this pretentious place. 

Another thing i hate is when you ask your waiter what is the best on the menu and he goes everything. -.-"!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

ordered lobster for appetizer -- ok, mediocre 
lamb - good 
fish seabass - bad 
service - bad 

To top it off, I requested a desert to say happy anniversary for us because it's our 10th year. They did not do that and I did not bother asking for it anymore. 

Will not return.
Nice ambiance. Good portion. My favorites were definitely the Sweetbread and Quenelle for appetizers and Pigeons for the main entree.

Attended a birthday dinner on a Saturday night. Although we had to wait about a half hour for our table after our reservation time in my opinion it was worth the wait. Although expensive, the food was outstanding as was the service. I'll still rate it with some of the very best of New York. From appetizers through desert everything was fantastic. Our only complaint was the very pricey wine list especially the Cabernets. I'll definitely return.

Went here for Sat brunch. The food was delicious and the presentation was exquisite but not overly pretentious. My favorite dish was the lobster salad as the lobster tasted super fresh. It's a pricey place, otherwise it will be one of my regular brunch spots.
i was making googly eyes at the candle sticks that's how romantic this place is.    take your loved one  you wont regret it :)

Nearly impossible to get a reservation, but worth coming for a meal. The restaurant itself is beautiful, and the food is very good. Get their duck for 2. It's the famous dish here, and it is REALLY juicy and delicious. It's also quite rich -- definitely a heavy meal. Not sure if I would rush back, but I'm glad I experienced it.

For all the hype and this restaurant being featured on every Top Ten restaurant list in NYC, it was a bit disappointing. If you want to stop reading now - the food was good, but not great. If you want more deets, keep reading...

We were greeted warmly, coats checked and taken to our table. That's when things took a disappointing turn with the uppity waiter who was just an uptight snob for no reason. He made our whole table feel uncomfortable the way he talked down to us, never once smiled. In the hospitality industry, I believe you should check the attitude at the door. I'm a paying customer and you should do your best to be personable and friendly - not a cold, judgmental jerk.

At our table of four, we each ordered different drinks - I enjoyed my red wine. To start, I had the salade de homard (grilled lobster refreshed with lime and mustard and exotic pears), which was good and had much more lobster meat than I expected. It was quite filling, but I didn't care for the odd taste of tangy and spicy mustard next to the sweet pear. Without the mustard, it would've been great. For my main, I had the filet de boeuf (prime filet, bone marrow jus, oxtail potatoes) - it was good, but not great, I've had better. My entree came out on two plates - one that had the filet and the other a small dish with more meat (the oxtail) and potatoes. The oxtail and potatoes was actually the star of the entree. It was a big portion, I had to share some of my plate with my friends because I couldn't finish it all. 

For dessert, we shared both the chocolate cake and the "Vacherin Aux Framboises" (coconut meringue, raspberry sorbet). While the chocolate cake was ok, the coconut meringue and raspberry sorbet was out of this world! Best part of the entire meal! So refreshing and light and delicious.

You do need to make your reservation a month ahead of time as this place is booked solid. Great ambiance - it is romantic for a date or intimate get together with friends.

If you're out to drink, scream, and pay a fortune to feel hip, this is your place.  If you're over thirty and know something about what it means to have a wonderful evening out, look elsewhere. This place hasn't a clue. They think you can just throw the elements together and it will work.  Not so. As far as the food itself is concerned, I can give mixed reviews. The lobster appetizer had almost no taste except for the heavy mustard sauce - a totally unbalanced and very disappointing preparation. The dover sole was fantastic in every way - delicate, flavorful, nuanced - really superb.  Dessert was very special as well. The light, delicate meringue interwoven with its raspberry accompaniment was just barely, but totally sweet enough without even a hint of heaviness - understated and perfect.
That said, we detested the noise level. Even at a small corner table, we actually had to scream at one another to have any sort of conversation. This is romantic? I don't get it. People love this place? I don't get it.  While the service was attentive, it seemed scripted rather than sincere. No one did anything wrong, yet saying the right words without so much as a smile seems forced and unwelcoming to me. Only an unsophisticated crowd could be pleased with an atmosphere like this. They don't seem to know how to combine casual with elegant here.  This is definitely NOT a French restaurant. By the way, be prepared for the wine list.

Service was very professional, but not overly friendly.

Decor and atmosphere was nice and felt special, if not relaxed.

Now for the food. I judge my food primarily on whether I like the taste.

Fried Veal Head - I appreciate the effort and uniqueness of the dish, but it just doesn't taste very nice, especially the glutenous fatty pieces, that were frankly unpleasant to eat. Would not recommend.

Bavette with escargots - this was nice, but nothing special. Perhaps my fault for picking a pretty standard dish. Wish I'd gone more daring.

Pomme frites - were nice but nothing special.

Oysters - were nice but we've had better.

Drinks - nothing special but be warned that wine and beer is around $25 a glass...cocktails were fine, but again nothing special.

Overall, it is a nice restaurant, with several unusual dishes, but don't go expecting the nicest meal you've ever had.

We were there for lunch.

So fabulous ~ This is how we start the celebration right.  Went with my best friends (actually a last minute lucky reservation); we believe we had the best seats in the house to enjoy the scene and less noise.  The service was fabulous; the food was amazing beyond description.  Such a good time ~ it's worth every penny.
Great atmosphere ( if you are looking for a quiet place ) good cocktails. Traditional service style

Not sure why yelp says closed. They are Very much open- we were there last night to check it out. Must say- quite bourgeoisie (boogie) the staff (especially the host/hostesses) seemed to think who they are, that's NEVER good. 
The only thing special about the food were the prices. The drinks weren't well crafted at all. And equally as important, there wasn't a smile on the staff that corralled the host/hostess stand at all, from the moment we walked in until we left- rather scowls and poor attitudes as well being as poorly dressed... 
I must say- we over heard an issue at the host/hostess stand that was mind boggling. We heard everything. A party came in, from what we heard- seemed like they were 30 mins late for an 8:00 reservation, and had called and were told it was fine. Mind you there were several empty tables. As all of us opentable users know you get a 20 minute window to be late, which is one of the reasons we use the app. NYC is a place where on time is often difficult. So- we heard the host tell them they were 30 mins late- so in all actually they were only 10 mins late, which is no big deal right? Considering the restaurant clearly has tables to accommodate them. nope. STRIKE ONE! 
Then the host told them because they had arrived with an extra guest they would have to wait 30-40 mins. STRIKE TWO! let me tell you, after 20 years in the business I know what that means- it means, get out of here- you are not welcome. Looked like prejudice to us, for sure. 
The conversation continued and the host pointed to a table for 4 and said they held the table for them & have turned away guests. We didn't see anyone come it and get turned away- EXCEPT THIS GROUP.... the guest said, great let's just add a chair in between the 2 that were backed up against the windowed frontage- should be a no brainer right..? Nope. The host said nope. We don't do that, you'll be in the way. IN THE WAY OF WHAT? The cold draft from glass? We immediately started talking amongst our selves about how absurd that statement the host made was. that an added chair would be in the way of what? Whom? NOTHING & NO ONE.  STRIKE THREE! 
Oh my- what an experience. I'll tell you, the hostess with the huge awful dress parading back & forth like she's the queen of England strutting like she's modeling evening wear was quite hilarious and amusing. The no 5th seat thing at the round table for 4- totally appalling.

Overpriced for what they offer.

Ambience was very nice, elegant, thoughtfully lit and decorated, and reasonably quiet for a Sunday lunch.

The service was OK. It started off pretty well, but they should have checked in with us for each course and they did not. Lastly, when. We did need to communicate with the waitstaff it was unreasonably difficult to get their attention.

Cocktails were well put together but nothing special. The wines by the glass seemed expensive, but I can't say for sure since I haven't had those specific wines before.

For starters we got the quenelle with a champagne buerre blanc, and vegetable terrine with foie gras. The quenelle was rich, but a bit flavorless, and the caviar on top didn't help. The upcharge of $15 for this dish was not worth it. Personally I would remove the caviar (it was likely American paddlefish and was a bit soggy and sad), and replace it with crispy fish skin to add some much needed texture to the dish. The terrine was actually quite good, an excellent contrast of flavors and textures, and the foie gras really worked well to add a bit of richness to it.

For the mains we got the chicken crepinette and the bavette steak. The crepinette was stuffed with foie gras and served on a potato puree. Unfortunately it was bland and tasted too oily. Since the foi gras was in the middle it was just barely cooked through, and may have been a bit too rare for some. The steak was very well made with good seasoning and served at the correct temperature. The snails that accompanied the steak were not so great, texture was borderline mushy and tasted of not much at all.

We finished the meal with a French press coffee. The coffee was weak and there were large bits of coffee grinder in the cups from the pour.

Not worth a Michelin star in my opinion. I don't see a reason to go back. The three star rating is because of the high expectations and correspondingly highish prices. Would have given most of the meal 4 stars if it didn't cost $200.

This is our second time and it is as good and memorable as the first time. Between the two times, we have tried everything on the menu as there are usually four of us. Standout include the swordfish which melts in the mouth. Swordfish usually gets a bad rap as it tends to be tough, but not here. Dessert is equally well done. Service is impeccable, with the timing between courses perfectly executed.

I was a little hesitant to dine here after reading some of the mediocre reviews lately, but I have to say I was extremely pleasantly surprised. First, regarding the service, I, in no way, thought it was pretentious or snobby. It is definitely more formal and less warm, but it was very professional.

Now for the food and drinks. The food was excellent! We ordered the St-Jacques, souvenirs de l'Aber Wrac'h (cauliflower, scallop, cider vinegar) which was light and refreshing. Second, we had the Quenelle de Brochet which was rich and creamy without being over the top filling. For our main course, I had the filet which was perfectly cooked and my husband had the dover sole. We both found our main courses to be perfectly cooked and delicious.

We both felt Le Cou Cou is well worth the price and the critics' praise.

Lovely meal service and surroundings. Party of three had a simply great meal with excellent quality. Make no mistake extremely expensive lunch 3 courses, bottle of good wine and coffee about $140 per. Exquisite duck,fried veal head, outstanding braise endive outstanding desserts especially a Carmel hazelnut and cholesterol Carmel torte. I've read some of the negative reviews none of them did we experience a really special place which you will love but be ready for the bill, it came as no shock and was on balance worth it.

Our group of 3 had a perfect dinner at Le Coucou last night. This is one of the top restaurants in NYC and my personal favorite. Yes, it is expensive and worth every penny for an extraordinary night out. For starters we had the oysters, the leeks with hazel nuts and the pike quenelles, followed by grilled duck for two and the Dover sole. Chocolate mousse cake and the apple Napoleon was a great finish. Every bite was amazing, the sauces luscious and the service was lovely. Le Coucou is NYC dining at it's very finest.

this is my fav French restaurant in the city now. They have a lot of exotic dishes like veal head, sweetbread and pigeon. They all taste very amazing! Veal head and sweetbread are very juicy and pigeon and duck are very rich. I did not like that rabbit dish so much though. The restaurant is a pity it dark.

I expected more professionalism and better service standards from a Michelin Star restaurant. My family and I had brunch at Le CouCou recently. Overall our dining experience was fine--the food was good, our waiter and Sommelier were pleasant and helpful--but I am unlikely to return because of a very negative interaction with the bar tender as we were leaving and management's lack of response to rude and condescending behavior. My husband was making small talk with the bar tender as we waited for our coats. My husband is a friendly person who is used to engaging with a range of people as we have moved around the world extensively for our jobs. The bar tender upon hearing we were from Washington DC immediately became even more aloof and condescending, making several judgmental and small minded comments about DC--even though we made absolutely no reference to politics. His comments were hostile and unwelcoming and were based purely on our association with a city. This left a very bad final impression of the restaurant, which was made worse by management's lack of effort to apologize or address the rude unprofessional behavior unfitting of a Michelin Star establishment. I find this even more ironic because the owner of this restaurant also owns a well-known French restaurant in DC as well. Next time I am in New York I will seek out establishments that are welcoming and inclusive and which take the principle of hospitality seriously, especially when you are paying a premium for high quality service.

Please forgive the expression I'm about to use.  
        "Fine Dining Experience"
I eat in hundreds of restaurants.  I love to eat good food and drink good wine and of course laugh and be with friends.  But I have forgotten about fine French dining until last night.  
This was the best fine dining I've been in the past 20 years.  It deserves the proper attire, although they do not require it.  It deserves great friends and family.  It's food is pure French and done perfectly.  Nothing is commonplace, and yet nothing is ridiculously hi-tech.  The service-spectacular.  The food -spectacular.  The ambience -spectacular.  The wines fabulous.  The prices are what you'd expect with all the spectaculars above.   I should have used astronomical.  But that didn't stop the great array of diners. Even they were spectacular.  NO POSERS.  This is a 2 star restaurant at least.  Nevertheless, this is whatever you want it to be.  Romantic, a special family restaurant, a celebration restaurant, or a business restaurant.  
It is really the best of my French Food experiences.

I had dinner with two girl friends at Le Coucou on a Tuesday night.  The short story - food was fantastic, service was completely lacking and left us wondering how they got a Michelin star? If I could - I would give Le Coucou 3.5 stars. If you want a well-rounded fine dining experience, especially for a special occasion, I strongly recommend go elsewhere.  There are too many nice restaurants in NYC at this price point to deal w/ the lack of service and warmth at Le Coucou.

First - the food at Le Coucou was great.  We shared the fish mousse and terrine as starters. For entrees, two of us got the rabbit, and the other ordered dover sole.  Both the rabbit and dover sole were delicious.  The rabbit entree is a big portion (it's tout le lapin - the whole rabbit).  The food is classic french, but still updated and modern. The Mont Blanc dessert was also delicious. Two of us got cocktails, both were good but nothing to write home about.

The service was a completely different story.  Maybe we had an inexperienced server, but our whole dining experience was just weird and felt uncared for.  After we sat down and she took our drink orders, she said she would come back to explain the menu.  It took her forever to come back to our table.  At one point she was standing near our table while the three of us were clearly looking around hoping someone would come to take our order.  Maybe she forgot she had our table, and when she did come back, I had to remind her, weren't you going to explain the menu? After she took our order, she kind of just fell out of the picture.  Other servers (dressed more like busboys) served our food, and I don't recall her ever checking in to see if everything was alright.  At the end of the meal, another server (again dressed differently from the girl who took our order) gave us our check.  While they were processing the credit card, our original server came by with the check AGAIN.  Clearly there was some breakdown in communication.  Also, there was no shortage of servers and busboys in the restaurant.  In fact, over the course of dinner, it looked to me that there were too many servers/busboys and that may be the cause of service issues.  Like others have said, there's no warmth to the service - I don't think any of the staff (except the hostesses) smiled at us or each other throughout the night.  It looked like Le Coucou was a miserable place to work, and that showed on the servers' faces.  All in all, a super bizarre dining experience.

This restaurant is magnificent and so elegant. This is hands-down the BEST restaurant I have ever eaten at. It is really quite pricey, but I think out of all the extremely fancy restaurants, the price point is pretty good for what you get. I've gone to a bunch of restaurants since Le Coucou and all I can say is, this is still the best meal I've ever had yet. 

For hors d'oeuvres we got the oysters and you could just taste the freshness of them. The seaweed ice was a nice touch as well. As for the rest, we started off with the ris de veau a l'estragon which was so buttery soft and tender.It also had this sweetbread and cream mixture that was to die for. The buttery tenderness of the veal paired with the cream was just such a great combination for the palate. 

As for our main entrees we got the sole veronique which was dover sole and filet de boeuf. Both really well made. I got so happy at dessert since we ordered the omlette norvegienne which had pistachio ice cream and the outside cream portion was torched in front of us. The flambee part really made the experience. 

This restaurant is an experience all on its own. I would highly recommend eating here at least once in your life. It's a really pretty date spot and was very charming.

Solid food but I was not over the top impressed. I was expecting more. Service was very good and we had an interesting table where we watched the chefs plate and prepare meals. I had the beef tartar,and a tomato appetizer. These were ok. My friend had a fish dish, good but I wouldn't order it again. Perhaps I made poor choices. I may try the place more time.
Excellent service, romantic ambiance, and exquisite food. I had the veal sweetbread and the sole. Perfectly tender and full of flavor. Delicious, would definitely recommend!

After Le Coucou first opened mid-2016, they were excluded from Michelin's 2017 and 2018 list, but made it on the 2019 list. I typically find the most value and surprises in one-star Michelins but this restaurant met expectations given its pricier menu and hype. 

The interior design and decor was wonderfully executed by Roman and Williams. If you love the atmosphere of Le Coucou don't miss La Mercerie, also done by Roman and Williams. Le Coucou has a lovely soft, quiet and intimate ambiance. 

I would suggest grabbing a drink at their aesthetic bar (see photo) if you're waiting on other guests. The bartender made me a refreshing champagne cocktail (I told him flavors I like, not on menu). I came here for lunch with visiting friends. They offer the two course pre-fixe lunch for $58 per person. I had the oysters then the chicken and foie gras. Both were good but not outstanding. I uploaded photos of the courses and entrance bar as well. Service did leave something to be desired, nothing flagrantly wrong but definitely cold. While lunch overall was enjoyable and I'm glad I went for the experience, I do not think I would return. As Michelin describes its one-star rating, it's worth a stop.

There are few pleasures as enjoyable as a wonderful breakfast, complement it with tremendous service and a stunning venue and you have Le Coucou.

So civilized you forget all the issues of the day and leave prepared to tackle all the world can throw at you.

And just when you thought it could not possibly get any better, there's dinner!

Rarely do I ever frequent the same restaurant twice in one day, however Le Coucou was that exception.

Just delightful!

I heard about Le Coucou in 2016 and thought about going and then didn't. On my last solo trip to NYC in July 2018, I decided I needed to make it happen. So, I scored a last minute reservation for 1 at like 5pm. I was seated in a corner 2-topper and honestly, a phenomenal seat to take it all in and not have anyone or anything behind me. 

The restaurant is very chic. The tiny bar in the front is beautiful and something I'd love to have in my house. The chandeliers are unique and provide the right amount of ambiance. This is a total date night spot - but if you aren't afraid of eating out solo, surprisingly welcome for that as well. Service was SO good. The dishes were even better. The cocktails were impeccable. 

I couldn't get enough of the Belle Reve.(gin, beach plum liqueur, dolin rouge, honey, lemon, cremant.) The comme un gibson was perfect with the sweetbreads I ordered. 

Do not sleep on the Poireaux. The preparation of leeks will brighten your day and transport you to a happy place. the sweetbreads were rich and in the most amazing tomato & taragon bisque. To polish it all off, I ordered the vacherin aux framoises. The raspberry sorbet & coconut meringue were light & bright and just what I needed to finish the evening. 

Normally, I would have tried more dishes but there was only one of me and I had just come from a baby shower with a full meal - so I consider myself a champ. 

Highly recommend.

Fine food. The fish soup - souvenir de Marseille - had rich broth with a faint flavor of bouillabaisse; one of the best dishes I have ever ordered. The two-course lunch is a pretty good value. Good service, with low noise level. Two thumbs up.

My reservation was for 10pm. We waited until 10:30 and decided to leave as we stood there for a half hour with no where to sit. They could have easily just called me and told me my table wasn't ready yet. Disappointed to say the least, seems very unorganized and chaotic. Disappointed to say the least :(

A trip to NYC wouldn't be complete without a stop to one of the new additions on the Michelin Guide! Le Coucou had been on my radar for a while. When the dates for my trip were confirmed, I made reservations online for a nice lunch. Immediately upon entering Le Coucou, I was transported into a space of warmth & elegance. From the attentiveness of the staff to the welcoming bartender I was delighted but not overwhelmed. After checking in our coats, we were promptly seated & served menus. Having reviewed the courses & Instagram tags beforehand I had an idea of what I wanted, but our waitress was pleasant & knowledgeable of the menu & helped my guest decide there course. 

We started with a half bottle of R.H. Coutier which was suggested by the gracious Sommelier & complimented the meal nicely. For the first course, I had St-Jacques, souvenirs de l'Aber Wrac'h which provided a nice play of textures & was served at the perfect temperature. My guest had Quenelle de brochet "Route de Reims" which I tasted & was stunned by how well the flavors worked together. The caviar had the optimal amount of tang & once again the textures for her plate played perfectly with one another. I highly recommend trying this course. 

For the second course, I ordered the Halibut, beurre blanc which had to be one of the most aesthetically pleasing yet practical plating presentation I've seen. The Halibut was light & almost fluffy while the daikon provided as a nice contrast to the fish. My guest ordered the Crépinette de Volaille au Foie Gras et Fruits which unfortunately I didn't try as I was so caught up in my own meal, but they were delighted with there choice as well. 

Overall my experience at Le Coucou was seamless & soothing. I've had my share of Michelin restaurant experience to where you feel as if you're being monitored so often that it takes away from focusing on your company or the meal. I appreciate the relaxed & quality food that Le Coucou brings to the restaurant scene in NYC, and I can't wait to go back for dinner.

One of the best french restaurants in New York.

Food: Came here for lunch on a weekend. I had the $58 2-course set. My appetizer is a pate with foie gras and fruit in it. It is very refreshing. My main is chicken with foie gras, which is really chicken meat ball with foie gras filling. It is a unique combination, but it tastes really good. Chicken meatball is very flavorful while foie gras is sooo soft! 

Atmosphere and service: the restaurant has very beautiful interior and a romantic vibe. Service is impeccable. All servers are friendly and polite. One interesting detail is that they have the song Le Coucou (yes, same as the restaurant name) played in the restroom

Overall, an impeccable experience!
Good food, delicious and very good service. Like appetizer the most, especially the cabbage one.

Met friends here for an early dinner and for all the hype we all found it somewhat disappointing. The venue was beautiful, the dining room and service flawless but the food, not so much.
Diners had the pidgeon, rabbit and fish. Although the food was fresh and well plated but pretty uninspired. With all the choices in Manhattan we won't be dining here again.

My husband and I keep a running list of our top ten favorite dining experiences. Le Coucou makes that list hands down. We went expecting a stuffy French restaurant. It's very fancy but the staff is anything but stuffy. Everyone was warm, friendly and accommodating.  Staff members would stop and visit with us about their favorite dish or thing to do in NYC. Each course of food was better than the one before. Can't wait to return.
Have been to this outstanding French restaurant 3 times and each time has been a superlative experience from start to finish.   One of the best restaurants in NYC.
Great special occasion restaurant. The ambience is extremely romantic. Love the beautiful bar and view of the open kitchen. Must gets: foie gras, filet de boeuf and paris brest.

Simply amazing! My fiancée took me here for my birthday and we had a great dinner.

The ambiance for dinner is romantic with a large candle placed at each table. We were sat near the kitchen and it was enjoyable to see the chefs working in unison. Overall, the service was good. Super attentive and really efficient! 
 
We ordered the leeks and the foie gras terrine to start. Leeks were incredible and a definite order for everybody. I enjoyed the foie gras terrine- the rich foie gras was nicely balanced with the sweet fruits. I got the dover sole which was probably the best piece of fish I've ever had! Amazing flavor in the fish and the sauce. I was eating slowly so that I could savor the taste as long as possible (lol). My fiancee got the filet with the oxtail potatoes which she thought was delicious but maybe tad too salty. For dessert, we shared the omelette norvegienne. They flambé it at the table! We both really enjoyed our meal and hope to come back someday.

A couple of questions/things that I need to answer right away:

1)Is it worth the money? If you split it with two people and need to celebrate somewhere... YES. I felt like a king which is what you pay for. We had incredible service which I can give an example of: I drink a lot of water at restaurants and I can always tell you how observant the server is depending on the number of times they refill my water. An average meal over 1.5 hrs is 3-5 times. During our 2.5 hrs meal, I got my water refilled over 15 times and had my silverware plus plates change 4 or 5 times.  How amazing!

2)Would I go again? Yes? There are a lot of fancy French restaurants in NYC but I had the sweetbreads and if let they me just order those, I would come back in a heartbeat. One of my favorite dishes in 2018.  My dilemma and why I put the question mark is this: as a New New Yorker, my list of restaurants I need to try is at least 100. I rarely eat the same place twice unless it has a single dish I need to have again because I can never be sure that my new favorite restaurant is going to be the next restaurant I eat at OR someone is visiting and I need something that is either a for sure home run or I know they will like it. So to answer the question after that thought process, I would likely not be back unless I came back for the sweetbreads which I honestly come back for when I need a pick me up!

3)What blew my mind? Our Sommelier was named Andrew I think, and he was very gracious. He walked us through the extensive wine list with ease and helped us decide based on what we were going to eat. The red wine we had was very nice. Could I tell you the exact region it came from? No, but it was nice.  If you sit close to the kitchen you can watch them plate the food and try it. I thought this was so cool! At one point, I saw a guy try a dish, nod no and the dish got sent away. I wish I could have understood why he thought it was wrong but I guess I would have to work at a restaurant to do that! 

Food: Just wow, seriously though. We ordered:
bread and butter: Butter is from Vermont
 4 oysters
silent salad
sweetbreads
lobster with cabbage
halibut
rabbit
baked Alaska
bottle of red wine
chartreuse dessert wine

I do not think I could give each of them the love they need but seriously, a restaurant that felt like a once in the lifetime experience that I hope others are privileged enough to share.

Finally got back here, and it's still amazing. We started with the leeks and the lobster/scallop-stuffed cabbage, followed by the roasted duckling for two, and then three cheeses and the chocolate mousse with white coffee ice cream for dessert. We loved everything -- I wrote last time that I wasn't crazy about the leeks, but I came away really loving them this time. 

The duck was basically perfect -- my wife was initially leaning toward the dover sole, but she was really glad we ended up getting this. The breast is what gets most of the love in the photos on here, but the leg is really what stood out for us -- this is one of the best new things I've eaten in a while. 

Just about all of the desserts on the menu intrigued me, but it would be hard to not do the mousse / ice cream, which was just incredible. The cheeses were great too, particularly with the amazing honey that came with them, but I could see some argument for going with a second sweet dessert rather than cheese.

If there's anything we probably wouldn't need to get again, it was the cabbage. This was very good, and the sauce it comes in was great, but there are enough other interesting items on the menu that I'd probably get one of the others next time.

All in all, an amazing dinner at an amazing place. We'll definitely be back.

Delicious French Cuisine!

Tasted the lunch menu.

Started with a complimentary Hama Hama oyster which was a pleasant surprise. Meaty, juicy and fresh taste of the ocean. 

The complimentary bread was fresh and went well with the Terrine de fruits et légumes au foie gras
celeriac and quince, sherry vinaigrette and hazelnuts

The roasted hazelnuts were awesome! The textures were great!

The Canette l'orange came in 2 dishes. The breast was perfectly tender, juicy and flavorful with the skin crispy and a thin layer of fat between that was rendered perfectly! The grilled duck heart on the side was smoky seared on the outside and juicy inside and literally melted in my mouth!

The confit duck leg was tender but too salty with the thick sauce on it. The chanterelles surrounding were delicious but make sure not to dip in the duck l'orange sauce as it would over overpower the delicate flavour and texture. 

The Paris Brest was amazing! Hazelnut praline cream inside a tasty pastry that was so good I groaned in pleasure! The textures and tastes were better than any patisserie I've had in Paris though it was definitely a fork and knife adventure!

Finished with complimentary butter cookies and raspberry chocolate wafers.

Overall, a fowl meal with a hazelnut theme that was amazing!  Definitely worthy of its Michelin star!
Great service! The interior is lovely, high ceilings and very spacious. Not loud, great place for sleeping babies(during lunch). The steak was delicious, and the chicken was okay.

Upon walking into the grand, chic space just before 10, it was clear to tell what matters to the staff. No bar seats, softly lit, candlelit tables with plenty of space, open kitchen facing the back half of the dining room. We waited for 40 minutes for our reservation (on the tail end of reasonable for a 9:45) but enjoyed a prime seating arrangement in view of the kitchen and the main dining area. On to the food...

We got three dishes brought out individually, each building upon the last both in substance and flavor. We began with a buzzy favorite and classic feature of French cuisine: Quenelle de Brouchet "Route de Reims". Could be described as a soufflé consistency dumpling of pike, cream, and eggs, served in an absolute dream of a champagne sauce. This dish delivers the elegance of classic French without leaving an over indulgent trail in your palette.
Next, the veal sweetbreads, featured in a tarragon sauce, served in a copper pot. What a delight the crispy bites were when paired with a few of the sautéed maitake mushrooms!
Finally, the meal comes to top form both in substance and preparation with the grilled chop and braised lamb neck. The chop's finish was minty, exactly what we needed after two rich dishes. The neck was crisp on the outside and creamy on the inside, paired with a chard. These two felt like the yin and yang of the lamb game.

Well worth the price tag and the wait - bravo Daniel Rose.

The food and drinks were great but the service was disappointed. The waitress seemed like she didn't like us and are food was forgotten about and served to us cold. I'm sure the dish would of been more rememberable if it was served when it was hot instead of barely warm. I hope this one was just
a random bad day because it would otherwise
be a great brunch spot to take family or a date too. Atmosphere is really nice and the food is good. This
Restaurant just needed better service.
Beautiful atmosphere! Great food and service! Treat yourself to an elaborate breakfast!
Everything was phenomenal, especially the dish with sweetbread and the cabbage wrap with foamy broth. These 2 dishes were spectacular. Balanced and delicate. Hope they are still on the menu.

The whole experience at Le Coucou was mind blowing. From the elegant ambiance when you walk in to the chic open kitchen where the action is happening. FOH were very attentive and had great guidance from the sommelier. The uni was flavorful and very visually creative. As for the sweetbreads, they will go down as my favorite starter I have ever had because the sauce was divine and the texture was on point. Transitioning over to the Duck a L'Orange provided me the time to indulge on a well executed Burbon drink... but needless to say I thoroughly cherished the duck as there were two stages to the dish involving the breast and heart followed by the leg. Highly recommend, on my list to revisit ASAP.

There are some instances where restaurants live up to your expectations, and other instances where they exceed them. Le coucou falls into the latter category. 

I came here with a friend on a cold Sunday evening. We had a 5:30 reservation, and were seated immediately, at a table in front of the open kitchen. The service was impeccable, and we were taken care of from start to finish. The dining 

We decided on two appetizers, and two entrees each. Each dish was presented fairly quickly after ordering. My friend had the sweetbreads, while I had the foie gras. The foie gras was served in a novel way, baked into a pastry-like concoction, and garnished with a slightly sweet pineapple sauce that complemented the rich foie gras. The sweetbreads were cooked well, with that quintessential chewy texture that only innards can possess. 

After finishing our dishes, our mains were again served quickly. My friend had the rabbit, while I had the catalan style pigeon. Both entrees were on the larger side for a restaurant of this calibre. My pigeon was rich and succulent, accompanied with a sweet-tasting sauce that brought out its flavor. My friend said her rabbit was very good, which I agreed on, but was somewhat confused by the serving style of broth and meat separately. Though she liked it, she said it wasn't a dish she would have ordered again, would she come back.

The positioning of our seats towards the open kitchen meant that we could see everything that was going on. As I like to watch chefs at their craft, I was watching the goings on of the evening, and engaged in an awkward game of eye contact with the host and head chef all evening. Either way, still an excellent dinner that we enjoyed tremendously. 

With appetizers going up to $28, and most entrees priced over $40, this is not a cheap meal, but an affordable extravagance, and one that is well worth it. I would probably say this place is now my favorite French restaurant in the city. Thanks for an excellent dinner!

Not sure our 2-course $250 (for two) lunch was worth it. The worst part is their menu reminds me of a restaurant week menu, which charges supplements for half of the items. What's the point? $58 is not cheap to start w for a one star Michelin. Also it's kinda obnoxious to charge "filtered" water and house sparkling water. We found out we had to pay $12 just for that when the bill came. My husbands steak was awful, bad cut w no flavor. That was a total waste of money. The rest of the food was pretty good (duck was cooked to perfection) but again, not a $250 worthy good for lunch.
The most beautiful experience in New York i have ever had. Perfect service , amazing dishes looks for Michelin for sure. Pigeon and rabbit was impressed.
Beautiful setting, great service, and good food. Le Coucou is formal without being stuffy or pretentious.

Spectacular food,service and decor. I took off one star for the bar. As beautiful as it is,it's pretty useless. Not a bar you can sit at and have a drink. Something I always look forward to. Guess they were afraid it would turn into a post work hangout. Understandable.

If there existed a zero star rating, I'd give it.  Had a birthday dinner there that completely underwhelmed though service was good and the setting beautiful - the old Holiday Inn space!  Beyond the dining experience, I left my Prada sunglasses in my dark cushy seat and called the next day.  They'd been found and the manager would be mailing them to me, said the hostess, who diligently took down my address.  Today makes one month and no sunglasses have surfaced.  I've called several times and get the run-around from Nicole and some other hostess person of questionable English skills - not what you expect from a supposedly top French restaurant (its not even French by Bouley or Robuchon standards).  Basically, they stole my sunglasses.  How low-rent and fitting for the space they're trying to gentrify.

Pretty brilliant. 
Was afraid it would be too mainstream French, but luckily it wasn't! Decent wine list. We had a non filtered wild fermentation wine from Roussillon, which was excellent. Have the oysters! They are the best! Amazing! I normally don't like my oysters anything but plane, but this way, I could have them always, with a bit of frozen lemon juice and seaweed, delicious!!!!
The sauces are all very good! The rabbit was not my favorite dish, although the thigh in caramelized onion and mustard is good! The sauce of the sweetbreads and the pigeon are both phenomenal, but for me the sweetbreads could be crispier and the pigeon meet itself wasn't as outspoken gamy as I would have expected, but cooked to perfection! Which is rare!
Deserts were good! The white coffee ice cream with pieces of freshly roasted coffee beans: delish! 
And before I forget, the bread, butter and olive oil are all top notch!

The ambiance was perfect as my husband and I were celebrating our 7th wedding anniversary.  The St Jacques is delicious, as well as the grilled fois gras (not the fois gras with chicken - reminds me of a meatball!).  I had the lamb chops were great too.

Here we are at Le Coucou, the place was packed with customers.  We were greeted upon arrival by the maitre de and his staff, who directed us toward the couch.  We went to the bar area since we had to wait for our table.  The maitre de was a tall blonde guy.  He was a bit deceiving in his attitude, he wasn't welcoming at all.  Then we were directed toward a table and a young woman brought us our cocktails.  We were seated and a few minutes greeted by our waitress.  She didn't attempt to give us a smile (wtf), she answeed the few qustions we had in a robotic tone.Then she disappeared.  The only thing that comes to my mind is a self absorved staff who doesnt care.  The food was good, but a sort of motley crew described the dishes as they came to the table..  Finally, a breath of fresh air - our main course came and the dishes were explained by a french speaking waiter who explained everything clearly.  We felt like we were in Paris at that moment. Then the waitress came back and asked if we were enjoying our meal.  We had the chocolate mousse for dessert.

Food was good but expected more from the head wait staff.  They were inattentive except for that French guy.

?????? I don't get it why is this place so popular????
Foods are salty, eek wasn't good...
Service wasn't that good people are so loud.
The guy behind my table was playing some dirty music on his phone doing some dirty move...no one stopped them.
Its typical soho restaurant ‍
Just pretty bar to take a picture.
Expensive but the food is outstanding. If you want to eat well in my come here and eat the soufflé for dessert as well as the oysters

Best place I have ever dined? No. But close? Maybe. 

I loved the service. Very friendly and knowledgeable. They really knew the food well and helped us make decisions. The food? Good. I would say some of the dishes had a less than satisfactory portion size, which is why I docked a star. I had the filet and it was wonderful. However, for $4 MORE, my mom got the fish, and it was tiny. She was very unsatisfied with the size. I ended up sharing some of mine so she would go hungry (for $66????). 

Other than that, the food was delicious and the desserts are to die for! You will be treated like a king! Enjoy.

Let me start, by saying this review is about the wine list -- not the food, the room, or, the service.  Dining out, for my wife and I, is to an important extent about the wine offerings to pair with the food - in hope that the "third thing" happens.  At home, we drink wine with our dinner.  This is not snobbish , its a beverage to enhance the food experience.
Restaurants in France see wine in the same way, that is, they do the heavy lifting for you, and have made selections - a modest number, reasonably priced to enjoy - that they feel go well with their menu.  Many American restaurants - NOT ALL - see the wine list as an opportunity to appeal to snobbery, befuddle the unknowing, and, pick your pocket!  Le Coucou falls into the second group.  The wine list is half the length of a bible, so it must be good.  Finding a $22 bottle ( a just fair wine) on the list offered at more than $100 proves my point.  And, this is not the only example.  Do your own "homework", don't take my word for it.

We had had a very, very memorable dinner at Spring in Paris, so we had high hopes for our dinner on Saturday at Le Coucou. 

Service: The sommelier was excellent. Our waiter was not. She was casual and informal. She also encouraged us to order much more food than we needed. Lastly, I left unfinished nearly all of my halibut, which was not remarked on at all. When the waiters cleared our plates, no one asked why 90% of my plate was untouched. 

Meal: We ordered the terrine, which was excellent. We ordered the oysters, two of which were lovely, one of which was gritty and had pieces of broken shell in the mignonette. A turn off. We also had the souffle-like lake trout (I think it was trout) topped with caviar, which was very good. We then had the rabbit, which was good, the bouillabaisse, which was interesting, and the halibut, which was disappointing. The plate was completely beige with no contrast in colour or texture. The halibut is served on top of wilted daikon in ribbons, covered in a very nice sauce, and the halibut was seemingly poached or softly cooked. No char, no grill, no browning. A pity. A high point was the mille feuille, which was light, tasty and not at all rich, and the coffee service.

I have long heard about Le Coucou before about it's traditional and unique take on Parisien cuisine, I was looking for an authentic experience but I have to say I'm extremely disappointed. Compared to other french restaurant in New York like cafe boulud, Daniel, the food is just way below average, not to mention food in Paris. To be fair, I think the decoration and ambience are good, very romantic atmosphere. The service during dining is good, but they totally missed my girlfriend's checked coat. I came for a lunch two course menu. I also ordered pomme frites and a bottle of cider. I have to say the dishes we tried are so disappointing. The foie gras terrine is fine, but the skate cheeks is simply horrible. I don't think the fish is well prepared, the smell is so strong you just cannot enjoy it by itself. You could cover it up by the sauce but the sauce is just so sour for me. For the main course, the chicken and foie gras is ok, but just too rich. Bavette à la Bourguignonne is also so rich you simply cannot finish everything. There is no balance of the dish. The steak itself is so hard on the outside and not tender at all inside. So in general I'm really disappointed. I really like French cuisine and I would really love to say a good word, but Le Coucou just didn't give me much of a choice. I don't know if it's because the lunch menu is significantly worse than the dinner. If that's the case then don't bother to have a lunch menu because people would want to have the same quality of food.

I wish I could give them - 5 stars. I dont care how fancy this restaurant is or how good the service was but they served me raw steak which is an absolute no no in my books. 

So I went to have lunch in this restaurant Sunday and everything was nice, almost. The interior, plates, seating was pleasant and the staffs were attentive. They made sure to refill my water each time even before I asked. So I could give 5 stars for all of that.

Now comes the bad part. So I did the $58 2 course lunch menu. I ordered the skate cheeks for appetizer which was tangy and well cooked. The rosé wine was delicious. So all this could give the place more than 5 stars, right? WRONG!

I ordered the steak and the waiter forgot to ask how I wanted my steak and I forgot to tell him too. But honestly in every restaurant the waiter always asks me that question. ALWAYS! You would think in a fancy Michellin star restaurant they would ask that but no. Two other people in my table also asked for steak and the waiter didnt ask them too. When you dont ask people how they want their meat cooked, what do you do? You cook them well done or atleast medium. I got rare. My meat was half red. My friends also got rare meat. But mine was more rare than theirs. Granted, I like my steak medium rare but this was too rare, it was raw. The knives couldnt cut any of our steaks and it required a lot of chewing. I was so hungry since I didnt have breakfast and was starving. I swallowed half of the meat and left the other half. I wish I didnt eat it at all. The horror didnt end. I had to wait for a while to get the train in the subway and once I got home I threw up, the steak was still in my throat. I love steak, this place just made me hate it. That was literally $100 down the drain.

I wont be coming back here which is a pity cause I really liked the ambience and the restaurant itself.

I was torn between rating a four or five.  However - due to the food which is incredibly delicious & ambiance, one cannot help but to congratulate Le Coucou on their Michelin Star & a round of applause for serving up absolute deliciousness!

On arrival you will find a fashionable & chic crowd, all decked out in the latest fashions. Even their staff are dressed to impress & fashion forward.  

My two friends and myself dined on two courses which were $58 per person.  Call us adventurous- we made it easy for the kitchen by ordering the same thing.  Our dining experience included Terrine de fruits et légumes au foie gras
celeriac and pears, sherry vinaigrette and hazelnuts.  Followed by Filet de boeuf 'Bourse et la Vie' (additional $15)
prime filet, sauce au poivre, pommes frites. For dessert we ordered Chocolat Noir salted caramel ice cream & Paris-Brest hazelnut praline, pâte choux. 

We were beyond elated diners with our meal.  I cannot recommend the pleasure of dining at LeCouCou enough. The waitstaff is well versed in the menu and are engaging & polite. 

My issue is with the FOH. If I'm the hostess and the reservation is in my name - I call the bloody shots period. Not to mention I was courteous enough to call and touch base with you.  Relay the same favor so not to upset my day. FOH at the hostess stand requires proper training. For the price point - get it right!

Chef, Food & Waitress earn FIVE STARS!!!!!

I took my fiancé to Le Coucou for his birthday. 

We started off with the Poireaux, which were leeks with hazelnut. This was absolutely amazing. Super flavorful. Please get this, you won't regret it!

Next, we got the Terrine de fruits et legumes au foie gras. Honestly, I'm not super into foie gras, so I wasn't really into it, but my fiancé liked it. I would've rather ordered 2 more Poireaux. 

Sole Veronique - This was a Dover sole with grapes on the side. This. Is. So. Good. I think this dish is now on my top 3 things I've ever eaten. The sauce is to die for. Just get it. 

Filet de beouf - This came with oxtail potatoes. This was a really large portion!!! It was alright. I do think that the beef was too salty for my liking (had large chunks of salt on top) but was still good. The oxtail potatoes were good and hearty! 

We finished off with the Omelette Norvegienne for our dessert. They light some alcohol on fire at the table and then pour it over the dessert. It was good, but I think the alcohol flavor was a bit too much for me. I'm much more of a chocolate person, so I think a chocolate dessert would've been better for me. 

If I came back here, I would definitely still get the Poireaux and the Sole Veronique again, and I don't usually like to order the same thing over again. But they were THAT good!

The **stars are for the beautiful restaurant - great fit-out and superb lighting.  I went for breakfast and ordered the omelette thinking the French sure can make this dish perfectly.  It was so disappointing - solid all the way through, no colour on the outside, certainly not creamy, silky and caramelised a little on the outside as I was expecting.  I will give the restaurant another chance for dinner.

I am impressed with this place. 

I chose to do the 2 courses for 58 dollar lunch. I ordered the St-Jacques, souvenirs de l'Aber Wrac'h (scallops) and the Crépinette de Volaille au Foie Gras et Fruits (chicken and foie gras). I also added on a dessert (Paris-Brest) that was not included in the lunch prix fixe. 

The scallops were very well presented with a good amount of acidity to balance out the seafood. The chicken was very tender and filling. I would highly recommend the Paris-Brest if you are a fan of Ferrero Rocher. This is the pastry version of the chocolate confectionery.

This Michelin Star restaurant lives up to its high expectations with good service and great food.

Although the decor is modern, the food is traditionally French. No deconstructed bouillabaisse here.  I adored the tall wax candle on our table that burned and dripped throughout dinner forming cool shadows on the table and wax shapes on the candle holder. Even though the rest of the decor was a bit more New York industrial, it made me feel like I was back in Paris, enjoying a bite and a few glasses of wine at night at a tucked away table. 

Dinner and food were really post on. Service was attentive without being overbearing.  The food was oh so French and delicious. Don't shy away from the sweetbreads and escargot, they're really done right.

This was a wonderful experience. The service was excellent and no push. You need reservations. The wine lis is extensive and we enjoyed a wonderful saint emillon. The rabbit, especially the lion as delicious. The pork terrine was fantastic. Then when you think you can't me impressed more the dessert is delicious. The table next to us helped us select delicious dessert. The decor is a rustic chic and the lighting makes it all so gorgeous. So worth it.

I've been here a couple of times. The food is really creative and the ambience is incredible. It's a great place to have a special, romantic evening. They absolutely deserve their Michelin star -- I really don't get why they don't have two. No questions asked, this is one of the best restaurants in Manhattan.

I'm taking off one star because the staff here really lets you know where you fall on society's totem pole, and it does take away from the experience a bit if you're not amongst the group who is getting treated as though you are on the top of the totem pole. People whose clothes are nicer get better tables and get seated before people who had earlier reservations. This happens everywhere but it is very noticeable here and hurts the quality of your experience overall.

Great place. Love the setup and the atmosphere. There are many positive reviews on Yelp, and I agree how amazing this restaurant is. Excellence in everything. I had an outstanding dinner with my friends. Thank you.

OK five stars, instead of four
After 5th time dinning here, I gotta say they are consistent with the quality of food. 
I wanted to take a star off only because last Saturday 2pm was still very busy and there may be a slight oversight on excellent service. 
I shut my mouth complaining about service after the Chicken Foie Gras filled my mouth. Speechlessly heavenly deliciousness. Bravo!
Quenelle--- how did they make it so delicious¿?
Oh... So good.. can I order one more?

OK, I will suck it up and come back again, and again... And again...

Really enjoyed the space and ambiance but I must admit, the food was underwhelming. I expected to be wowed by the food, but wasn't at all. I ordered the Halibut which was the best part of the meal. Glad we experienced le coucou but sadly I wouldn't recommend it or go back. Beautiful space however!

I recently brought a friend for a celebratory lunch at Le Coucou. Reviews and waits are well known so we came with substantial expectations. The restaurant itself is quite lovely with its soaring ceilings, exposed bricks and glowing, concentric circle lighting. But the woman at the reception desk, with the straight brown hair and her glasses perched on her pinched nose, was without a doubt the most unwelcoming host I have encountered in my last decade of fine dining in NYC. When we introduced ourselves she looked us up and down, junior high school girl style, and with narrowed eyes grudgingly took us to our table.
