The restaurant was nearly empty and yet she placed us at a terrible, small table facing the waiter station. Really? My friend looked at me with confusion and asked another employee, this time an elegant gentleman, if we could move to a different table? He demurred and said he had to check with with "lovely" woman who had checked us in. So we stood awkwardly in the empty dining room, waiting for a new table. 
Once installed and at a new table, things brightened considerably and our waitress was kind and lovely and attentive. The food was not bad. I have lived in France and my mother was French and I am well familiar with amazing French food and this was not. The plates were well composed but, for example, the skate cheeks were rubbery, flavorless balls sitting in a puddle of overly acidic, mustard-based vinaigrette. The entrees were better - the chicken was tender and sauced in an elegant, flavorful reduction in a scant portion of mashed potatoes while the other entree came with a small copper saucepan with a few pieces of boiled vegetables. 
We did not have dessert - it's not an extensive dessert menu with just four choices - so I can't comment on them. We ended the meal with an excellent press pot of La Colombe coffee and to their credit, no one rushed us from our table while we lingered and talked. 
So will I return? No, absolutely not. If you want better French food with an incredibly and uniformly welcoming staff try Le CoCo Rico. And my advice to Le Coucou's owners: get rid of the woman at your front desk. She behaved like an old, musty-fusty stereotype who sets an inappropriate and unwelcoming tone for your establishment.  You can and should do better if you want to survive in NYC's notoriously competitive dining environment.

Lovely atmosphere. Very romantic. The servers were all nice but nothing extra ordinary. The menu is very limited but nicely presented. The only issue we had is when we went to order the sea urchin. It was sold out. I just wish she would have told us when we first sat down that we were not able to order it. Overall I would go back but my fiancé says he wouldn't so you decide.

We came here on mother's day without a reservation. Got extremely lucky someone had cancelled and were seated promptly. The waiter was incredibly knowledgeable and attentive. We had a bottle of the Rose Bordeaux and it was amazing. Highly recommend their Foie Gras and pigeon. I found the rabbit a bit tasteless for me but my best friend loved it. Really good desserts as well!
super nice with excellent service, presentation, technique and taste! Rather overpriced but worth it at least once. Steak tartare and mussel soup was extraordinary

#michelin1star #french #nyc Had a lunch with my friend. The price wise, it was worth it to go. Our service and severs were outstanding flawless. Loved their service. First starter, my mocktail was pretty amazing. Bread was moist and good. Other food was just okay. Maybe I am not big fan of seafood or French food..? But the vibe was so good and romantic!

One of a kind gem. 

I absolutely adore this place. I wish I could dine here once a week. From the moment you walk in the door you are transported to heaven. Everything here is perfection. The service is top notch. 

If you dine here for breakfast or brunch the Comme un Clafoutis = French pancake topped with blueberries and creme fraiche is life changing. If they ever take this off their menu there would be a mutiny. Lol. Seriously this dish is like a combination of a crepe and a pancake.  The other entrees are delicious as well however this one is the BEST! The craft drinks are also a hit and wonderful to accompany with brunch. 

The restaurant's building exterior is unassuming yet the interior is spectacularly designed. The silverware down to the gender neutral restrooms are beautifully done. 

Finally, the service is some of the best I've ever had. I have never experienced an inkling of bad service at this place. The staff is impeccable and refreshingly pleasant and most them even smiling. I do not have to have this level of service when I dine out but I certainly welcome it. 

Open Table is a great way to make a reservation which I highly recommend.

After having a dinner here, I tried again for the breakfast, sadly found the centerpiece rose was almost dead so I asked my waiter to move it away. The breakfast avocado toast was fine, egg was boiled not poached, I prefer poached eggs as the egg white will be thinner. The vegetables was dressed with too much vinegar but overall a good breakfast.

Came here for our anniversary and it did not disappoint. We ordered the sweet bread as always, as well as the oysters. I highly recommend both. The ox tongue is no longer on the menu but we went with the quenelle, grilled lamb chop, and the steak. Everything was amazing. 

The bone marrow was generous and was basically meat butter on the steak. The steak itself was cooked to perfection. The oxtail boulangere was just enough without being too much. The lamb neck had the perfect amount of fat and complemented the Swiss chard. 

We finished the meal with the rhubarb dessert. It was super refreshing and the buck wheat ice cream was not too sweet. 

I highly recommend this place. 

The one thing I would comment on is that the waitress was having a really bad night. She dropped a coffee cup on the floor. Then dropped a knife that luckily didn't fall on my girlfriend's lap. And finally, she wished us a happy birthday instead of an anniversary. She was not very good at all.

I just finished eating the best lunch of my life!   I am completely serious... the two course $58 fixed price lunch features starter choices like Huitres (oysters), potage Billy Bay (mussel soup), quenelle de brochettes (warm like pate in champagne sauce with caviar), skate cheeks and crazy exotics like tete de beau ravigotee (rolled and fried veal head).  While I have to admit I am nowhere near brave enough to order rolled veal head... the warm pike quenelle might be the single best appetizer I have ever had... which leads to the abiding theme that binds the Le Coucou menu together.. the sauces for every dish are subtle, sublimely nuanced and exquisite!   Whoever the restaurant's saucier is, he/she is a genius!!!

The choice of main courses was equally distinctive... halibut with fermented daikon, bouillabaisse, tartar de boeuf, bavette steak, perfectly prepared filet mignonette, poached chicken in a brass pot and on and on!  My group shared everything and everything was absolutely superb!!!  It is very important to point out the I do not like fussy or over-the-top fancy food... Le Coucou's sauces are amazingly flavorful without being anywhere near too rich, too strong or too anything... they are simply perfect!

Dessert was great (5 different sorbets and rum babba), the coffee was smooth as can be and piping hot, and staff starting with the hostess, our waiter (Nash) and the sommelier were as professional, courteous and considerate as you could ever want!

P.S. Dinner is "a la carte" and the wine list is extensive... bottles of good red run from $155 to $4,950!
Very good typical French place. Fine dining. As expected, shi-shi and pricey. And was expecting whole duck....hahaha. It was quite good
Went there for my birthday. Special place. Had a great time. Food was wonderful. Had a $65 shot of tequila. That was fun and definitely random for a cheap skate like me!
This is a great place to eat. Service and food were both excellent!! Duck was especially wonderful.
Food, service, ambiance: 10/10. We had an incredible experience here and would absolutely come back of I was in the area. Here the food is all about the experience and it beyond exceeds expectations!
Love this place!  The set up makes for a very romantic date spot with it's warm and cozy feel.

Absolutely amazing breakfast! One of the best Omelette I have ever eaten! Ambience was so charming and service was exquisite. We had a reservation and had no problems when seating. Waitress was so kind. I recommend this place to everyone who wants to have a classy, beautiful & a delicious breakfast! Will go again & again. Mersi!!
It had a great atmosphere. Everyone was spaced out and very intimate. Very attentive staff, they were on it. Had the duck for two.

wonderful guests sitting next to us who wanted to join in conversation as seating is close in some areas. Came for a 12 lunch and left at 3 pm. From the food to the decor, we felt like we were in Paris.

Came here for a birthday celebration. Was very excited to have the Le Coucou experience given all the hype and prestige surrounding it. When my date and I walked in I was immediately taken with how beautiful the interior was- high ceilings, intricate french wallpaper, tall candles- very romantic. We were promptly seated and ordered from their "half bottle" selection (price ranges from $60 and up on the half bottles). We ordered the mussel special, the duck for two and the omelette norvegienne. The mussel special was bites of mussel, parsnip and urchin- although the cut of the parsnip my date and I found to be slightly too large- overall the ingredients really complimented each other. The duck for two featured perfectly cooked heart, breast and leg and was the highlight of the evening. Rich, succulent and featuring a variety of textures there is a reason the duck is always on the menu. While fun to watch the flambe- I don't think it burned off enough of the alcohol as the bottom of our norvegienne was so strong I couldn't eat it (although I really enjoyed the rest of the dessert. 
Overall my date and I really enjoyed ourselves however I do think with so many amazing restaurants in NYC (french and otherwise) the food does feel overpriced. The service and atmosphere is up to snuff but the fact that our duck was cold when it reached our table I felt was unacceptable considering how much we were paying for it. Le Coucou does classic french food well but it does seem like they are maybe a little too comfortable...

This was a three for me. Beautiful space. A bit precious. Two of the wines by the glass were dull. Two were good. Server uniforms a tad affected. Staff was over solicitous and affected without being truly excellent. Most of the dishes were not memorable, but a couple were inventive, fresh and flavorful. Don't go in jeans.

The service was Michelin but the food was not interesting nor great. The lunch service amounts to approximately $70 without tips, but the food did not seem worth that price. I expect a Michelin restaurant to be interesting or excellent, but it was neither. I had food left over because it wasn't good. I don't speak for the dinner menu, but the lunch was average or less.

Lovely restaurant with attentive service. 

We ordered something from each section:

Saumon aux concombres, vinaigrette citronnee - simply delicious and light. Delicate on the palate and the lemon was not overpowering. A refreshing start to dinner. 

Ris de veau a l'estragon - this was okay. The texture was a bit more mushy than what I'm used to but the flavors were there. It was my lease favorite dish of the night but it's still a decent dish. 

Filet de boeuf, jus a la moelle, quelle dans la boulangere - a beautifully cooked steak, so tender it melted in my mouth. The jus was flavorful but didn't over power the meat. Would definitely order this dish again. 

Omelette norvegienne - a great presentation involving fire accompanied this dish. I wasn't sure what I was getting because of the omelette in it's name but you can't go wrong with pistachio ice cream. Was a light dessert, which is a nice way to end the dinner without feeling too heavy when you leave.

Grateful experience of French cuisine accompanied by a delicious and particular interpeetacion New York style, in a charming atmosphere, French style decoration transports you to Europe.

Grata experiencia de la cocina francesa acompañada de una deliciosa y particular interpeetacion al estilo New York, en una atmosfera encantadora, la decoracion al estilo frances te transporta a Europa .
Food is delicious French. Service is great. Ambiance is beautiful. Coming here more often.

I would really give Le Coucou 3.5 stars - 3 stars for the food, but 4 stars for the ambiance​ and service. I've been here twice now, once for breakfast and another for dinner. The breakfast is definitely worth it because it is a bit cheaper and the portions are reasonable, and with that you get great service too. Dinner was 2-course and although the options were quite interesting looking, flavor-wise I was pretty disappointed. Waiters are always extremely proper and constantly there to check on your table- which is so nice but can be quite burdensome. If you have a celebration or would like to treat yourself to a good brunch, this is a great place to go. But not just on any regular day.
Best fancy meal I've had in the city. Everyone of the 8 dishes I tried was a hit. They should have 2 Michelin stars.

What a wonderful birthday dinner I had here! First off, we had the best seats in the house...the chefs table! (Trust me, it took a lot of work to get the reservation, never mind one of the best table in the place). Anyway, it was really exciting to watch all of the chefs prepping the food, cooking the dishes, answering to the head chef and watching them make the desserts. The restaurant itself has a very eclectic menu, but everything was delicious. I was a little bummed out they didn't have a bar here, but they do have the ability to make any cocktail you desire. We started off with a round of cocktails and sat deliberating over the menu for quite some time. I sort of thought they would have brought over a little tasting from the chef as many high end restaurants do, but they didn't. In any case...

For first courses we went with: morilles, sabayon au vin jaune (peas, ham and confit egg yolk), Navets en guise d'escargots* (turnip, mussel and sea urchin disguised as snails) & Ris de veau a l'estragon  (sweetbreads, cream, tarragon, maitake mushrooms). My favorite was the sweetbread dish. The waiter did say the sauce was excellent, so he sold me on that.  Sauce was incredible and everything was cooked just right. The 'fake' escargot dish was interesting. It was made with turnips and mussels in an escargot sauce. Very unique. The morilles dish was very unique too...interesting flavor combination of creamy sauce, peas and egg yolk. 

For mains we split the dover sole and the roasted duck with olives. The dover sole was made with a creamy sauce with mushrooms on top. It was delightful and just the right amount of food for me. My parents split the duck which came 2-3 pieces of each of them lightly seared with spinach on the side. Then in a pan in the middle of the table they left them the remainder of the dish which included: a piece of duck breast, green olives, sweet onions, and a delicious broth. We were all pleased with our menu selections.

For dessert we ordered the chocolate mousse with white coffee ice cream, which was excellent. 

Overall service was great. All the waiters were impeccably dressed in fitted suits, which I adore. Everyone was super friendly and hospitable. We had a bit of trouble getting amazing service when the place got pretty crowded come 7:30pm, but before that, it was excellent. I didn't think it was terribly expensive either!

- In short, fancy delicious French food 
- Very simple exterior, plain black doors
- I honestly walked past it twice before I saw the sign 
- Cute bar with a few seats available
- Absolutely stunning interior (candlelit, chandeliers, comfortable chairs, flowers on the tables)
- We had the terrine de veau, tout le lapin and crepinette de volaille aux foie gras et fruits d'automne to share
- Everything was divine 
- Great service
- People were dressed well 
- The only thing I didn't like was the open kitchen. I understand that's an attraction, but the smoke from the cooking would float towards the tables (obviously)
- Reserve a table here for special occasions
- Or if you just want some really good French food

The food is 5 stars. The service is meh. We came here for our anniversary and I admit my expectations were pretty high since it took some effort to get a reservation. We started out ok although our wait staff was pretty stuffy they were getting the job done. Then everything fell apart when I wasn't happy with the temp of my food. I said don't make another one just heat it up a bit. Nope 30 minutes later when my husband is done and I'm not hungry anymore I get a whole new entree. Then we sat there after I was done for about 20 minutes and had to ask for the table to be cleared. Which totally freaked the wait staff out. Then they brought a little plate of chocolates with the check which they give to everyone. Ours had a candle on it which I guess was their way of saying happy anniversary.

I had friends in from out of town who love great food and fantastic wine.  Le Coucou did not disappoint!  First off the cocktails great delicious and everyone was very attentive- I don't think my water glass was ever half empty.  The food was amazing- collectively we had the morielles, oysters, sweetbreads, quenelle, duck, lamb chop and filet.  It was a nice variety and everyone was completely satisfied- more than. 

The sommelier was perfection in providing wonderful suggestions- indulged in several bottles.

Again, fabulous food and top notch service made for a wonderful evening!

This is a fancy place and all the servers wear uniforms and tables with white tablecloth and candlelight. We had splendid food with attentive, thoughtful service. I don't understand the more critical comments. The Quenelle de Brochet were feather light with a Beurre Blanc sauce, the Sweetbreads tender and tasty, husband had the Rabbit in 3 parts. Friends had a contemporary Boullibaise which was excellent. The menu is amazing. Any dish with a sauce is worth trying. The sweetbreads were divine as The quenelle with caviar sublime. The lamb and beef entrees a must. The surprise was that all meals were of generous portions , supplemented by a large choice of local and French wines.

Had high expectation but a few entrees were ok (thought they'd be amazing). Loved the environment. Not too quiet but vibrant enough. 

Omelette is a must though. The flavor is rich and loved the presentation. Recommend pigeon and escargot. Dover sole was alright.

French by way of Buddakan. Don't bother unless that's what you want. The service is only superficially concerned with whether the experience is good.  Really Impersonal -- a factory of French cooking. We could have used guidance on whether the wine was appropriate to what we ordered. Lots of folks on social media while they ate. All in all, not worth the hassle or the price.

The service is amazing and the atmosphere very pleasant. The hazelnut praline dessert we got was very impressive and exceeded expectations. We went for the prefix lunch menu and my husband and I both felt that the  aim meal didn't not meet our high expectations. I opted for a more adventurous meal (veal's head) and it was very gelatinous and rich. Unfortunately, my appetizer had a similar texture and taste so it was more of the same. My Husband's bavette steak was good but on the salty side.

*Every time when i come in this restaurant i know i will have amazing food and great service . 
So thankful for never disappointing my expectations and keeping high standards for all this time.  
*Everything is so delicious so be prepared to order even more than you can eat ... but they have beautiful bags for to go 
*Ambient is so peacefully designed and they even have my favorite  Aesop hand-gel
Atmosphere is outstanding, service was impeccable and just coming from France can say the food comparable and flavorful. I will return on my next trip to NYC. Thank you, Le Coucou.
Beautiful ambience, delicious food and outstanding service. Sweetbreads was one of the most delicious dishes I've ever had.

When you go to a restaurant, you are thinking about the food that you really want to eat. You are looking for the perfect flavor, color and texture that you want in your meal. In this case, my case I was amused for the quality of service in this restaurant, it was speckless. 
Otherwise my dinner wasn't what I was expecting. 

"Agneau du Colorado en Deux Services" I pictured this meal all day in my little trip to the city, until the moment that I had my first bite. Lamb is a difficult protein to cook in perfection; in this experience the flavor was messy, strong and over cook, that it made me miss the flavor of the Lamb, grease and bad clean of the bone made my plate looking without color and texture. 

The question is, when you are going to eat in a Michelin restaurant what are you looking for? The best service? Or the best bite of your life? 

Unfortunately I just paid for the speckless service no for the food.

We had a very disappointing dining experience at Le Coucou tonight.  My wife and I have been going to Le Coucou since they opened and have noticed a steady decline since the success of their first Michelin Star and a wholesale change in management.  The food remains outstanding but the menu has changed very little and has become unimaginative.  The staff has gone from welcoming and professional to arrogant and mediocre.  We noted numerous empty table tonight, telling us that many now feel the way we do.  The Star is falling and Le Coucou is no longer a special dining destination.  I have recommended this restaurant as one of the best in New York and beyond in the past.  Management needs to get back to what made Le Coucou one of the most desired restaurants in NYC....vision, performance and excellence. We dined in Bardot in Las Vegas two weeks ago and Le Coucou has fallen far behind Bardot in every category.   We will not be back soon.

Of course I adore  the interior + pretty much every single detail  just like everyone else. I am obsessed with the vintage french interior, the green velvet Thonet chairs, the antique silver carafes, the open kitchen, the gorgeous bar, etc. Loved the chilled cucumber soup, the skate cheeks, the tartar, the halibut beurre blanc with fermented daikon and the amazing wine from burgundy at approximately $150. Also, the bread (from Roberta's which is arguably the best bread in New York. The service was also excellent. The one thing I did not like is how often they come and pour wine. A couple of times we only would have had one sip and they were there to pour again. I appreciate the attentiveness, it certainly makes you feel taken care of, but I personally would have preferred a bit less of the pouring. Will go back for sure!

Really great food. Excellent place for a date night, although the tables nearer to the kitchen are more fun as you can see what's happening on the pass. If you want more quiet as for a table further away from the kitchen. The baked Alaska dessert is one of my favorite desserts of ALL TIME. Cold, hot, soft, crunchy; texture, flavor and everything was amazing. 

One issue: there is not much for vegetarians (non-fish/seafood/meat). They were nice to offer the vegetarian in our party an off-menu vegetarian pot-au-feu, but it was essentially a soup with veggies. Just a note to the vegetarians.

We came here for birthday celebration.  This restaurant offers impeccable Michelin star service with a romantic ambience.  Each food was nicely crafted.  Dessert was a bit weaker.  But overall, we are very fond of this restaurant.  I am glad we came here right before it was awarded the Michelin star.
It would been a lot harder to get reservation.

Beautiful and elegant place with impeccable service. Stand outs included the lightly cured salmon starter (a bit of a French riff on sushi), halibut in a ethereal beurre blanc sauce and the indulgent crepe dessert. The sole, while deliciously accompanied by a brown butter sauce, trumpet mushrooms and grapes, was just a bit over cooked in our estimation. Overall however, a wonderful high end French addition to the area. Perfect for a special evening.

Perfect date spot.  The low, warm lighting in the simultaneously rustic and contemporary style dining room creates a romantic atmosphere and the lack of background music (just the ambient chatter of other guests) allows you to actually hear your date while not feeling like everyone is listening to your conversation.

The service is on point, as you would expect at this sort of establishment.  Honestly I don't frequent $$$$ spots too often (or ever), so was sort of intimidated w the wine list, about how many items to order, pronouncing the french food, etc. but whatev you get over it.  Our server was courteous and explained how many items to order, and wasn't imposing on our decisions.  He seemed to cater to whomever he was serving because the table next to us was super chatty and he reciprocated well. I guess just be yourself and the staff will match your personality haha

We got the navets en guise d'escargots ($29), which was my favorite part of the meal.  The fake escargots made up of uni, mussels, and turnips in classic escargot flavor was super flavorful and well crafted.  The crepinette de volaille au foi gras et fruits ($28) was like a chicken and basil meatball w a little chunk of fatty liver in the middle-- pretty much the right amount of foie gras for someone like me who isn't all that into organ meats.  The tout le lapin ($46) is fun.  The rabbit comes in three dishes: kidney and liver pates, a soup w greens, and a honey dijon sauerkraut bake.  Try the sauerkraut w the table bread for a reuben-like filler if you're worried about being hungry afterward (surprisingly, we were not even though we usually eat big-portioned meals-- I think it was all the bread we ate).  The pigeon "cote de provence" ($42) is fine, tasted like chicken and came w roasted veggies and little fried, artichoke-filled raviolis.  I think next time, I'd opt to have one person get fish to switch it up.  The rabbit and pigeon tasted kind of similar to my, albeit unrefined, taste.

The 2016 yves cuilleron cavanos ($55, half bottle) was such a pleasant addition to the meal.  And, of course I couldn't not have dessert.  The omelette norvegienne ($17) aka a bombed alaska had pistachio ice cream in sponge cake inside a toasty meringue outer layer that was flambed at the table.  Though I didn't love the liqueur that seeped into the cake and sort of tarnished the otherwise sweet taste of the dessert, it was still a real crowd pleaser.

Overall, I'd go again to try other items on the menu.  I really appreciated their attention to detail apparent in their service and the food itself-- really set the right ambiance for our anniversary! (They added a candle to our omelette and said happy anniversary multiple times)

CAUTION: RICH SAUCES AHEAD! 

Decadent French delicacies and romantic ambiance! We did a celebration dinner here for my husband. The food was genuinely amazing and the service spotless, without the pretentiousness. The menu was simple and to the point with great variety for adventurous and reserve eaters alike. Again, sauces are so rich I don't know why they don't have a medic onsite for potential sudden cardiac arrest. Must get the sweetbread and grilled chop!

We had to wait about 15 min or so for our table while we had a reservation so they gave us a complimentary glass of wine, which was very nice of them. The interior is beautiful. I thought the food was delicious. One item on the menu caught my attention and it was the turnip, mussels, and sea urchin disguised as escargot and it was very good, as a escargot lover I thought this was very interesting. Portions are not big but I prefer that. Had four desserts and they were all delicious. Our waitress was lovely and super bubbly. Had a great time. Will be back!

Typical French fare, what's impressive was the duck and the foie. Prepared multiple ways - either seared (my favourite) or in a parfait. All à la carte. 

Service was just ok - not too talkative nor rude: seemed they had a mission to get through as many customers as possible. I wouldn't go here and splurge but it is a one star Michelin restaurant so prepare to pay at least $150-200 per person with drinks.

I liked the rabbit. That was delicious.

I had dinner here back in July, and my god, was it wonderful. The restaurant is beautiful, intimate, and romantic (too bad I went with a friend). 

Everyone, from the host to our server to the sommelier, was very knowledgable, friendly, and helpful. When we asked for recommendations, they provided the perfect responses. 

Every single dish we ordered was perfection. The chef was able to take classic French dishes and put a modern spin on them. Do be mindful that the sauces are still classically done, and everything was super rich and creamy. Definitely do not come here if you don't eat dairy - everything was cooked with either butter or cream!!!

Wine list was extensive. Dessert list was sophisticated. If you want to seal the deal, definitely take the person you're wooing (whether business- or personal-related) to Le CouCou. Just make sure you can afford it.

If there's one fine dining in NY I'll recommend to my friends if they ask me, this will be the one. The whole rabbit dinner was tender and juicy. The place is rather cute than intimidating. The food is authentic than most of the French bistro I've been in Paris.
My husband and I came here to celebrate my 30th birthday. As good as the dishes were, I do have to say we were not impressed with our waiter, who was at most, quite dismissive.
The food and decor live up to the hype . Good service . But how can a French restaurant have such mediocre deserts ? That was a disappointment. The rabbit done three ways is exceptional

I only gave 2 stars because the tartar was one of the best I had in my life. However, the need to order 2 courses of the menu and charge U$49 for one plate of leafy greens and one tartar is very expensive. My mom ordered the quenelle and when it arrived at the table she tasted it and realized there was some egg in it, she is allergic to eggs.. when they asked why she didn't eat her plate, she said that she was allergic to it and they just left it there, without even trying to change something or give her a new one that she could eat.. I am not talking about hard politics or what is in the protocol, but the human touch and the empathy for the customer, the little gestures. At the end, they charged us for the 4 people in the table, with the quenelle left untouched. We paid and gave the tip, and just called the manager politely to say that it should be nice from his part to have not charged us for her, since she just ate leafy greens, and that we would not come back there. He just said, "ok bye". He was very insensitive..

Thank you to your team for such a wonderful breakfast celebration for my husband's birthday. I can't remember the last time I enjoyed breakfast as much as I did yesterday! Our server, Alicia, was especially kind, and attentive. The food and service were top notch. The restaurant itself was beautiful and it's clear the team takes pride in what they do. I can't wait to go back!

This is an elegant place for a couple or four good friends. There are high ceilings with chandeliers dangling to offer light. Each table had a candle burning. The kitchen is open and in the back of the restaurant. You can see the chef and his staff prepare your meal. The volume of noise was low so you can have a conversation and hear each other.  The food was delicious!  The filet of sole was tender and had a yummy sauce.  The beef dish had a nice presentation. I would suggest the server put the sauce on the site. It was salty! It too away from the medallions. The accompanying side was interesting and tasty.  Don't forget to top the meal off with coffee and dessert.  Desserts, plural in our case. They had such tempting, decadent desserts.  The fig dessert was unique. Flambé dessert was entertaining and amazing.  A good time was had by all!  Definitely a place worth coming back for!!!

Le CouCou is what upscale French food should be - utterly decadent! The vibe is fancy but the crowd is trendy enough to not make the restaurant seem too uptight.

We started with the quenelle de brochet, the foie gras (this particular one was a special I think), and the sweetbreads. Everything was simultaneously delicate and rich. If you enjoy foie gras, do not miss it here. For larger dishes, we had the duck for two and honestly I do not remember what else (halibut maybe) because the duck was perfection! 

And if you're feeling especially indulgent, the desserts are delicious and executed beautifully. The omelette norvegienne is popular for its presentation, but the coconut meringue dessert was my favorite.

4th time here, still LOVING EVERYTHING.

Ugh you really can't go wrong with anything from the menu! My personal favorite entrees are the steak and duck, but I've tried the fish and rabbit before and everything was so tasty.

I've always considered this place reasonably priced for the quality of food you are getting! And I can't get over how pretty the interior is!

Can't wait to come back for more

My husband arranged a birthday dinner here. As other reviews have said, you really cannot go wrong with anything. Service was phenomenal and the ambiance was warm and intimate. I highly recommend the sweetbreads and duckling for 2. We tried the chocolate mousse, crepe souffle and the poached pear - all heavenly. We will definitely return. The prices were reasonable and I can understand why it is very difficult to secure a reservation here. Plan in advance! Thank you for a very special birthday dinner.

My personal experience after one visit diverges from the glowing NYT review of some years ago now. The service, we found, was inefficient and not particularly friendly and I don't think I'm an overly critical person.  The food was just okay not great, is the way I like to put it, again based on only one meal there. That's a small sample size, I realize.

I kept telling my friend as we sat down the table "what a great choice! this place looks awesome!" and it was.  French restaurant done wonderfully down to the very core. The food was decadent, the service lavish, the decor beautiful.  I can't remember the names of the dishes in french, but if I try to describe: egg in aspic (divine!), leeks, fish poached in champagne butter sauce, foie gras, halbut in beurre blanc, dover sole and for dessert, the must have chocolate mousse and the crepe souffle.  Just visiting New York for a week, and this restaurant is the highlight of my trip so far.  Will come back!

Great solid restaurant. Wanted to like it as much as Spring in in Paris. That was one of the best experiences I've ever had at a restaurant. Maybe my expectations were too high, but I think is still a good place. 

I would recommend this restaurant to anyone. It lacked a little on specialness, and the service was good, but not great. 

Lobster was amazing, as was most of the food. The bread was weirdly not great. 

I would like to try it again on someone else's dime, too many other places for me to try.

It seems hard to make a reservation but you shouldn't give up with it;) 
I finally got a table at  9 pm  for dinner on Friday.

Actually, my friend who came here often told me that there are so many tourist lately and the food has been bit changed since they open.

But I think there are not many tourist like other famous French restaurants.  And food was still excellent afterword !

Every where you looked it was so aesthetically pleasing. Loved the ambiance! The food was delicious too. My husband said that the quenelle de brochet was the best thing he has ever eaten. My filet de boeuf was cooked perfectly, but the fries were so mediocre. How can they go wrong with fries? They were hard and greasy. We came here for lunch and the only reason why I gave it 4 stars instead of five is because they add an extra charge for half of the items on their menu! We ended up spending a lot more money than we intended to,  but it was still worth it!

Let me start with the very pretty space this restaurant is in.  It is warm and inviting.  The service, from all wait staff, was friendly and excellent.  The food, however, left me sorely disappointed.  Although others in my group were happy I was not.  The appetizer of crépinette of chicken and foie gras tasted more of chopped unspiced chicken with no hint of foie gras.  I then had the "whole rabbit" prepared 3 ways.  1) The tenderloin of rabbit was served barely warm.  When I tied to slice it with my knife (certainly not fork tender) it broke apart into flavorless chunks.  2) The rabbit leg was served in a flavorful consommé, but the leg itself tasted like boiled & boring chicken.  3) The saddle of rabbit served with a mustard sauce and sauerkraut (I think) had barely a smidge of mustard flavor.  The chocolate cake was rich, chocolatey and delicious.  The restaurant lost an additional star since the decaf cappuccino was NOT decaf.  I was up most of the night with my heart pounding at 90 BPM.  I believe that if I am going to spend over $300 for dinner for 2 the food should be remarkable and unforgettable.  There are many other restaurants, in New York, that offer better than this.

Listen, I get why this place is popular - it's a trifecta of great ambiance, decent food, and polished service.  And that is why after spending weeks contemplating where to take my girlfriend for her 29th birthday and I chose Le Coucou over EMP and Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare.  So I was quite excited to come here and see a big smile on her face as soon as we walked in.  The dining room is expansive, ornate, but not overly stuffy.  It's the kind of place you know right away things will be great.  It's tuned to cater the fickle New Yorkers for years.  Onto food - we didn't love everything on the menu (skip the crab dish) but impressed by the beet+caviar appetizer and the prime filet dish that came with bone marrow oxtail potatoes.  But there was one weirdest thing that happened that absolutely ruined our entire experience.  Per my happy girlfriend's request, I sat next to her for a second as it was taking quite a while to get our food.  Out of nowhere, the Maitre D' pops up, asking me to go back to my seat?!?! It was the most bizarre experiences I've had.  They knew we were here for a special occasion, we weren't bothering anyone - we were just two adults having a conversation.  If people next to us complained, they could have put it a little more gently.  It was so rude and embarrassing.  I've never once had a similar experience 11 years living in New York City (and I'm a hospitality business investor).  For that, I will never come back here.  For the record, I still tipped 20% because the rest of the staff were quite professional.  But boy, I feel like I just dropped $600 on the street for nothing. Truly disappointing after weeks of planning!

Went to Le Coucou with two others a few months ago.  I had made a reservation a month in advance, and it wasn't too difficult to get a seating at a standard seating time when booked out that early.

The restaurant is dimly lit, large, and very beautifully decorated.  Service from start to finish was great -- the hosts were gracious, the barstaff was excellent, and the servers were very attentive.

I tried the following dishes:

Saumon aux concombres, vinaigrette citronee (4.5/5): A very nice rendition of a classic dish.  The salmon was perfectly cooked, flaky and soft, and went really nicely with the citrus vinaigrette.  It was also presented in a really nice way.

Navets en guise d'escargots (4/5): A really interesting dish that I did enjoy.  I thought that the turnips were well-disguised as escargots, but were obviously not a perfect match.  The butter/herb sauce that it came with was great.

Quenelle de brochet "Route de Reims" (4.5/5): This quenelle was very good, and very very rich.  The fish was so soft and creamy, and the savory flavor was both light and heavy.  It worked very well.

Halibut, beurre blanc (4/5): Halibut in beurre blanc with daikon.  It was a very solid dish, but it wasn't unique.  I did enjoy it.

Bouillabaisse souvenir de Marseille (3.5/5): A decent dish.  The seafood was really fresh, as would be expected, but it was otherwise forgettable.

I had a great experience at Le Coucou and would definitely return!

This is a really pretty restaurant that is part of the star restaurant group, located in Soho and that has really pretty decor and serves French fare. Le Coucou has friendly staff and an upscale ambience, with an open kitchen and very stately lighting and exposed bricks. The restaurant has an extensive wine and beverage menu, and includes typical French food, which I tend to find a bit too buttery and over priced. Overall, this is a romantic spot for date night, or a group dinner with friends, but the food is the least memorable part.
Terrible customer service and an average of $200 person for a mediocre brunch.  Truly the worst of what NYC has become.

Le Couou for sure is traditional french cuisine at it's best with some modern touch. I was absolutely convinced by the crab as a starter and the halibut beurre blanc as main course accompanied by a fine glass of chenin blanc from Loire poured from a magnum bottle. 5 stars also for the service, location and interiour design. Only 2 things i was missing: an amouse gueule and petit four served with the coffee  which is internationally common in high end restaurants.

Delicious high end but friendly restaurant.  I had the 4 course option and everything was good.  Lobster in pepper sauce was an unusual but delicious combination and the potatoes dauphinois were amazing.  The crowning jewel, however, was the tarte tatin .  Not only the best tarte tatin I have ever had, I think the best DESSERT I have ever had.  We will be back!

Foods were mediocre. It's a pretty restaurant and that's about it. Went with two of my friends and I gotta say the service was disappointing. Inconsistent and slow although the place was not busy at all.  (Which I believe has a lot to do with the fact that we were a group of young Asian girls)

The food I chose sweetbreads - the best ever for me and the filet were wonderful. Slight wait getting to table. Wine seemed overpriced, an fact that produces a feeling of being taken advantage of. Servers were friendly and pretty knowledgeable. I would go back

We had lunch reservations at 2pm to celebrate our anniversary. We were running a little late and were told that our table would be given away if we were more than 15 minutes late. We arrived at 2:07 and were seated at 2:45. The host apologized but we were not offered any compensation, we were charged for everything including our drinks while we waited. After we were seated it was another 10 minutes until the waiter checked in with us. He was hurried the whole meal and didn't check how our food or drink were until we were almost done. The bread we were served was burnt from being reheated. The quenelle was out of this world, but the sea bass appetizer was just ok, not worth the upcharge. We were then served someone else's espresso shots accidentally. Then our main course came--the beef tartare was ok, and the halibut was good, though its sauce was excellent. Decided to cut our losses and leave before dessert. Hostess asked how everything was and we told her not very good, and we had to wait 45 minutes for our reservation. Her response was  "oh, I'm sorry" and handed us our jackets...not a bad experience, but not what you'd desire from a $250 lunch.
The ambiance definitely takes me back to France. The staff are welcoming and friendly. The food was simply amazing.

I cannot say enough great things about Le Coucou! I eat breakfast here often and consistently have a great experience. The food, ambiance, and service are impeccable. Tonight was my first time having dinner here and, unsurprisingly, it was phenomenal. It is a stunning space and the food is the best I've had in NYC. The most impressive part of the experience was undoubtedly the service. I am always made to feel like family by the spectacularly charming hostess, Karen (who always remembers my name!). Our server, Ethan, was accommodating, knowledgable, attentive, and very friendly--he is a true expert. Every single member of the Le Coucou team goes above and beyond to create a memorable experience, start to finish. The maître d', Robert, introduced himself and ensured we had a great experience...which we absolutely did! Le Coucou tops other French NYC staples (Cafe Boulud, La Grenouille, etc). What a treat. Cannot wait to return.

This is a wonderful restaurant in every sense of the word.
The atmosphere, the service,  the food, all outstanding and worth the money.
First time in this establishment and I was impressed! I loved the ambiance, food, and service! I will be back!! ​
Dark bread was the best I've had in my life. Love the combination of light and rich components. Flavorful and balanced.

High ceilings, spacious, dim lit beautiful place for dinner or lunch. Came here for lunch with the hubby for a special date. The service was amazing, food was delicious and so were the drinks. We really liked the place.

We had a great time having breakfast here. The space is beautiful. The staff were very nice and attentive. We each had the Californian breakfast with poached eggs, avacado, special bread, and mixed greens. Other customers' food also looked good. We were happy with the value, people who are not familiar with Manhattan prices might not be but IMHO the quantity and the quality of the food was much better than you will get at many places with equivalent or higher prices. (The restaurant is attached to the 11 Howard hotel so I assume many customers are from outside NYC)

Practically sublime. Needed a little "me time" so treated myself to a NYC trip. Some ex-New York friends who are foodies gave me the rec to go to Le Coucou. From the moment you walk in everything was wonderful. The staff was especially friendly. The maitre d, the bus boy and everyone in-between were delightful. I was seated at a table for one in a primo spot right in front of the kitchen, which is an open concept. So thrilling to watch and listen to these experts orchestrate their craft. I started with the sweetbreads paired with a chenin blanc. The wine was perfect, with a subtle tartness that cut through the divine fatty richness of the pillows. The sauce of course was perfection with a hint of tarragon, my favorite herb. The salt was a little too heavy handed though and was threatening to over power the subtle players in this dish that did not need competition. Main course was the pigeon. The meat was the most tender meat I have ever had in my life. This includes Kobe in Japan. The veggies paired were cooked perfectly al dente and not over seasoned so I could really taste what each veg had to offer. Highly recommend pairing with the burgundy which had luxurious mouthfeel, soft and smooth to compliment the subtle and buttery pigeon. For dessert I got the baked Alaska (omelette norvegienne). Table side drama with the flambee but the dessert itself fell a little flat for me. I kept thinking a little layer of marzipan would bring more life to this visually beautiful little gem. Overall very outstanding meal, well executed, fantastic attention to detail, would return.

Beautiful and romantic, but the food is just good. Also, I was ripped off 2 oysters! I ordered the appetizer which comes with 5, everyone I know who has been there has confirmed it. Their insta page shows five we asked for 2 orders of the oysters and got 8! Very upsetting. Taking my money and not giving me the product I paid for! Thieves.

I went here for lunch time. Food is great. Service is good.
I decided the restaurant on the last minute and went in pretty casual. All other customers were little dressed up. So if you are going, be aware.  Nothing extensive but heels will be nice

Upon arriving, place looked nice, no one there yet, great! 

We sat, open kitchen, great!

Our server, was not too inviting, strict and harsh tone, proceed to recommend the 4-course dinner to which we agreed, had a good value.

Below is what we had and what we thought/experienced; 

Salade de betterave à la crème d'esturgeon fumé
buckwheat, caviar, horseradish

Simple, well balanced, yet nothing to remember. 

Bar noir de nos côtes, saveurs Basques
marinated local sea bass, savory, sweet pepper and anchovy

Bass was cut too thick for "sashimi" like presentation, the chopped or diced peppers felt out of place.

Ris de veau a l'estragon
sweetbreads, cream, tarragon, maitake mushrooms

Dried, however arguably the best of all the dishes, the saving grace to this dish was the sauce. 

Foie gras grillé aux artichauts
moscatel vinegar and fall lettuces

The best of this dish was the toasted bread, foie gras almost made it if it wasn't for the gruesome uncooked raw piece of fat attached to it.

Homard 'Bourse et la Vie'
maine lobster, sauce au poivre, pommes dauphine

Lobster, cooked right, yet the cutter claw had the cartilages still in there, typical mistake made by new cooks. Pepper sauce did not compliment the subtle buttery taste of the lobster. Potatoes, sadly, raw in the center.

Filet de boeuf, jus à la Moelle, queue dans la boulangère
prime filet, bone marrow jus, oxtail potatoes

Potatoes and oxtail, to dry to try twice. The filet, the bottom was dry and stiff as it was left on a low flame for 1 hr, totally ruined, the bordelaise sauce and the marrow couldn't save this dish unfortunately.

Gâteau au Chocolat Coucou
chocolate mousse, white coffee ice cream

Seemed as it came from the chocolate factory, looked mass produced, no charm, forgettable and overwhipped, stiff mousse, not airy nor spongy.

Tarte Tatin
pâte feuilletée, crème fraîche ice cream

I love apple tart, this one however, meh, at best, the warmth of it or the ice cream couldn't make this dish any better.

Overall not a terrible experience, however, Michelin Star, price an all that white table cloth, we expected better, poor delivery on the food. I'd say that 1 of the stars goes to the Sommelier, proper serving, no spills or droplets on the nicely folded white table cloth, knowledgeable and good presence while at the table.

Really really pricy for what they offer. The ingredients are not very fresh, and who on earth would use cucumber as garnish in fine dining French... not to mention is bad cucumber. The sauce is overly salty. The bread is mediocre. I don't know any reason to come back again.
Treat yourself.  Beautiful decor, proper service and a strong menu.  Really tastey stuff.  But, bring your American Express card....

If you want to feel like you're in Paris without actually flying there then this is definitely the restaurant to visit. It's downright Parisian down to the slight lofty but still professional service. The main dinning hall has views of the open kitchen while the entry hall is narrower but feels very intimate. The lighting whether you go during the day or at night is always perfect, a little brighter in the hall sitting area than it is in the main dining area. 

The food is quintessential French food, no modern takes but not rustic either. I've eaten at Daniel Rose's Parisian restaurant Spring and aside from the more modern decor, feels exactly like the same restaurant. 

For me, this is the most romantic and definitely one of the prettiest restaurants in the city.

Absolutely great... this was my fourth visit and still... You cannot choose wrong on their France-focused menu, but I must say the lunch pre-fixe is of great value. Dinner is definitely more expensive. 

My personal favorite was the foie gras crepinette, but everything was great. Definitely worth the visit for a special occasion, be it a romantic spot for date night, or a group dinner with friends.

One of the top French restaurant in NYC.

First of all, the food was great.

However, the waiter who was serving us was so rude and harsh that ruined our night. 

Throughout the whole night he only spoke to us once, and that was for the order. And when we made a mistake about how 4 course menu actually works( we thought dessert was not included in the 4 courses at first), he was quite rude to us. He acted like" how could anyone possibly not know how a 4 course menu works". 

And after that, he never came to our table. Not even once! He passed by, he stood close, and he just NEVER cared to check on us. 

I tried to ask him something in the middle of the dinner and he just ignored me the whole night. However, he was very friendly to a party of 4 sitting right next to us. This really made me mad! Why?? 

My husband and I tried really hard not to look too upset at the restaurant. But guess what, he didnt even want to say goodbye to us after paying the check. He just swiped our card and asked someone else to hand over the bill. 

I was staying at the 11 Howard hotel next door so it was very easy for me and my husband to just have dinner downstairs. Our original plan was to go there twice during our two-week stay there. Well that would never happen now.

I really wish management could take this seriously. I dont know if the waitor is a racist or just dislikes us for not ordering any alcohol. His bad attitude was too obvious.
Good service, great ambiance and very well prepared food. Highly recommend the leeks and the duck for 2. Cheese options at the end were great too

Exquisite food for sure and one that speaks to those who are seeking traditionalist French fare (specifically I assume Lyonnaise) that is somehow old in France but new again in New York?  The food were so flavorful and we sought out the Michelin recommendations (aka the quennelle de brochet, the crepinette, and the rabbit). This restaurant is for sure a lovely experience with experienced staff. I was pleased to come after almost four years of thinking I should come to this spot. 

The only reason I'm holding out on the fifth star was due to lack of clarity on menu and really what I would expect as a walk through from our server. For instance, there seems to be a pre-fixe option but it was ever so subtle on side of the menu that I missed it entirely (please tell me I'm not crazy). I was probably super decisive that server didn't want to contradict my wishes, but would have loved more discussion on their specialties and what are their most recommended. 

Regardless, hoping to come back here soon and to try out so many other phenomenal things on the menu. I have also heard lots of things on their lunch set, so perhaps I will be trekking this way on a rare free day!

Incredible food and incredible restaurant. 3 stars because I feel as though service was incredibly lacking and menu was poorly explained. We had the lobster and filet and it was incredible. But the servers and what looked like a manager gathered around a podium very close to our table and we even overheard them talkIng poorly about the customers at the table next to us. Made us feel out of place and unwelcome. I commented on this to a friend of ours who frequents the restaurant while in the city. He said the same thing we did about the servers. Seems like this place might have a reputation for service with an attitude.

Even though we just came back from France, we missed French food already. Le Coucou is an old-time classic French restaurant located in Chinatown  in a hotel; a French restaurant that is half-staffed with Asians, ironically. The food is good. But good French food like this is around every corner in Nice, France where we've just visited, at about a third of the price. This place is way, way overpriced for good but not spectacular food. I left wondering how they've earned one Michelin Star. In NYC, there are many one Michelin-started restaurants that have much much better value.

Elegant  formal intimate though large space attentive waiter service very good food 
There is the feel that your are dining in someone's very large townhouse 
nothing wow in terms of food flavors  but generously sized rustic inspired truly  classic french cuisine  four course prix fixe-
Very good value -first prix fixe I have ever left full  
Stars were sweetbreads, deer,leeks, grilled pheasant and crepes suzettes 
Wine list is overly expensive most bottles in the hundred dollar range up to thousands and not good value compared to food. Cocktails not impressive. Bar /waiting area needs to be expanded given large overall restaurant .Hostess staff up front stiff and not welcoming.
Able to get adequate french rose champagne for $80
Would be nice if wine pairing offered 
Would recommend and return for a special event dining experience despite minus listed

Highly disappointing. Le Coucou fails to deliver on taste. The presentation is impeccable but frankly flavors were either completely bland, off, or plain terrible. 
The special was a cauliflower purée with lobster and caviar. The purée has a very strange tingly aftertaste. The "faux-escargots" were exactly that: faux. Turnip, mussels and uni failed to replace snails and left us perplexed. The lobster main was plain awful. The lobster was grossly over cooked and the sauce was simply inedible. Such a disappointment. 

This place has been highly recommended by so many friends and it failed to deliver.

I'd summarize Le Coucou as "400 of Garbage for Two." 

The faux escargot was gross, a chunk of Turnip topped with a bit of Uni & a Mussel is not a replacement of the original. A waiter said the essence of escargot is not the escargot, but the seasoning - he was wrong. 

My motto for lobster is similar to US Military policy, no lobster left behind. Yet I had to leave half on the plate as this dish was inedible and overcooked. To top that off, the rubber on my plate was accompanied by the sweetest sauce ever - literally inedible. 

The Foie Gras was good not great. The wine was the only enjoyable aspect of the evening.


I would have complained, but no server asked how my meal was during the evening. 

Absolutely shocked how terrible this place was, based of the amount of friends who recommend Le Coucou over the years. 

I don't know if the chef is new, but the food was genuinely horrible. $400 pissed down the drain, do not go here.

atmosphere: 5/5
service: 3/5
food: 4/5

We went for our v-day dinner here this year and they had v-day course menu for $185pp. 

First course was various small appetizers from lobster+caviar+cauliflower cream, rabbit liver ravioli, foie gras, and uni and oyster. everything was great, but oyster and uni was extremely fishy. We had better ones before so we were a bit disappointed. 

The cocktail I ordered wasn't that amusing (Bell Reve). very bland and tasteless. 

Second course we had was scallop with chestnut which was very flavorful, but scallop was sandy and a bit overcooked.. once again, we had better scallop before. We let our waiter know (we did not complain, but just wanted to let them know), then manager came to apologize to offer another dish for scallop which we kindly refused.

For main course, we ordered filet de boeuf with onion stuffed with mushroom and escargot and fish with bone marrow and turnip. beef dish deserved 5 stars for sure. We loved every bite of it. fish was pretty good as well.

We also finished all the desserts we had, but 5 stars for chocolate cake which wasn't that sweet, but had crispy pie in the bottom. During our dessert time, they provided us with complimentary dessert wine because of sandy scallop and it was delicious (Thank you!)

The other minus was from the service. service was not attentive and we ordered $300 wine bottle for the night and we had to pour ourselves for the last 2 glasses which is unusual for michelin starred restaurant.

Overall, such a great experience and this restaurant made me think like we were in South of France. Would I come back here? possibly.

Came back again for a second visit 1 year after my first one and it was way, way better! The lunch special is $49 for two courses although half of the menu is upcharged if you pick those options.

We went with the foie gras ravioli (called "Consommè de homard") and the Quenelle de brochet "Route de Reims" which consisted of champagne beurre blanc and caviar. Honestly, I wouldn't be able to tell you waht champagne beurre blanc is, but it tasted like egg + cheese and was super milky and soft! My bf loved it. The ravioli was one bite each since we shared but each bite was the best ravioli we've ever had.

For entrees, we had "Poulet " Coucou " en deux services" which was 
roasted chicken breast and stuffed wing with vinegar and mustard, leg and vegetables. (Can you tell I'm c/p straight from the menu? We wish we had some reviews help us with what they ordered because we were so confused at first, but after some data analysis from Yelp + others, we finally decided...). Our other entree was Crépinette de volaille au foie gras et fruits which consisted of chicken and foie gras, roasted fruit, pommes purée. The entrees were both so full of flavor and depth and the meat was juicy and tender. 

I'm glad I gave them another chance because it is quite a lovely restaurant with beautiful scenery (you feel like you've transported back to Europe!) and the bar at the entryway is elegant and serene. Overall a great place for lunch!

Ehh, nothing too exciting. Do not get the duck for two. This place is overhyped and not worth the 400 dollars. The sauce on the duck was way too reduced and the skin was not crispy. I was not impressed at all.

There is a nice selection of offerings to cover all food preferences and they are also accommodating, if you require, to special dietary requests.  My friend and I came in planning to do a sampling from the menu and our waiter, Travis, brought to our attention that a dinner option was a four course prix fixe would provide us with all our planned choices and dessert  as well, a great option if you are going for the full menu options.  We started with oysters  and leeks with hazelnuts. The oysters were clean and fresh tasting with a nice hint of the sea, the leeks lightly cooked in a very mild sauce with hazelnuts was a pleasant bite.  We then moved on to the foie gras in a light but delicious jus, and the toasted bread that came with the dish was well appreciated to sop up every drop of the sauce. The foie gras was melt in your mouth wonderful. We also had the faux snails which were actually a layering of a mussel, turnip, and topped with sea urchin served in a snail dish. Again a little bread will serve you well to mop up the remaining sauce in the snail cuppings . For the main courses we tried the halibut over  dakon , the fish was tender and the white sauce enhanced but didnt over power the taste, the mildly tarrt dakon was a nice counterpoint to the sweet fish. The prime filet was tender and it's accompanying side of oxtail under thinly sliced potatoes was a richly tasting  meat  lovers treat.  I'd like to mention that portions are fairly generous and you could easily order less and still have a very satisfying dinner for two.  While this is not an inexpensive restaurant, it is a good value restaurant  when you consider the quality of the food, the excellent service, comfortable  surroundings and that you will be enjoying your meal for a couple of hours at a nice leisurely pace.  An enjoyable experience from beginning to end. A special thanks to our waiter Travis who was informative and helpful throughout our meal and truly made us feel welcome, it was a pleasure to have met you.

Updating my previous review: Ryan from Le Coucou did reach out to me directly via yelp and apologized.  He wanted to know more about the situation and what they could do next time to get better. I appreciate any establishment that takes their critical reviews to improve. Again, I had no issues with the food and service- all phenomenal. It was just the attention to detail with the hosts that disappointed us. Needless to say Ryan reaching out changed our minds and we will be back.

Really don't want to sound harsh especially we went there for a date night, you don't get to do that often when you have two tiny kids! However the food was rather disappointing, especially when you are paying over $400 for a party of 2! The only OK part to me was the cocktail and the bread. Husband and I both had the Menu Le Coucou and we followed the suggestions from our waitress and waiter, both of them were super polite and nice. It's just the food failed to deliver. I didn't finish any of the 4 courses...no matter the seafood part, or the infamous rabbit dish (my first time eating and not a fan), not even the dessert. The whole meal was a disappointment and I definitely don't plan to go back again. With that price tag, you can easily find some amazing meals in the City.

we loved Le Coucou for a special date night, it was hard to get a reservation but definitely worth the effort. the restaurant is so beautiful and charming that when you walk in it feels like you stepped off the streets of SoHo and right into Paris. 

service was perfect; very friendly and attentive. the maître d' was especially kind to honor my request for a window table even when the place was packed (it was the day before valentine's) 

the food was absolutely delicious, highlights include the Quenelle de brochet "Route de Reims" (eggy soufflé looking thing with caviar), Foie gras grillé aux artichauts, and the prime filet. 
i'm still dreaming about that filet, with its tasty marrow soaked potatoes... only thing to skip is the seaweed ice oysters, they were kinda boring and we wished we had tried the clams instead. 

otherwise... une nuit parfaite

As I walked in, the ambience of this restaurant was breath taking. Truely a romantic set up for a dinner date. We waited a short while before we were served & throughout the night we had multiple servers as our main server was hard to find. I later noticed he was talking to staff more often then coming pass our table. It wasn't a smooth start as I had to make eye contact & request to order our food. We ordered the fish with a mushroom sauce and beef rib eye, finally a tarte tatin to share. When it comes to French food, I lived in France for over a year, so I was extremely excited to try this spot. I was very impressed with the chefs being proactive and splitting our meals in half as we choose to share our main dishes. Fish was delicious & the sauce very decadent. The beef was a very soft cut but I felt the accompanying dishes of cold bone marrow, sauce & potatoes were ok and no major wow factor. In addition, the French excel in pastry & my all time classic favourite is a tarte tatin - this was only made well no wow factor here too, apples were cold & not butterscotchy enough worth finger licking. It was good, but could be better. Their brunch menu looks great, so I may give them another try

4.5/5 food, 5/5 for overall ambience/service

Loved Le Coucou and highly recommend for a fancy date night. My husband and I dined here for literally no reason at all (we said it was in celebration of our first joint account, but really we just wanted an excuse to down some sweetbreads).

Upon doing some quick calc, we felt it was worth getting the 4-course prix fixe.

First off, gotta address the gratuitous carbs. The bread here is great, and perfect for soaking up the rich buttery French sauces. Did we ask for a second basket despite knowing we'd be completely stuffed by the food we were actually paying for? Yes, yes we did.

For our first course, we ordered the sea bass crudo and the razor clams. Both of these dishes were very refreshing and well-executed - their respective preparations brought out the sweetness in the seafood (especially the sea bass, with the addition of sweet peppers and fragrant EVOO).

For our second course (the most exciting one, IMO), we got the sweetbreads with maitake mushroom and the quenelle de brochet (one of their specialties). The sweetbreads were my favorite of the whole night - they were over-the-top decadent and rich and the tarragon cream sauce was amazing (and so good soaked up with bread). The quenelle (think omelette) topped with caviar was also pretty good, but the sauce was a bit too acidic for my liking.

For our main, we shared the duck for two. You only get 2 pieces each of the breast meat (which is my favorite part) so that was a mild bummer, especially because it was cooked so perfectly! The duck leg confit was less exciting, because I feel like the band between good vs bad confit is much tighter, relative to breast meat. 

By dessert, we were honestly way too full but I did thoroughly enjoy their version of baked alaska. It had an impressive tableside presentation (flaming alcohol and all), while the apple tart was a bit less exciting.

Overall, I highly recommend this spot. The service was super friendly and I felt taken care of throughout the entire well-paced meal.

Seeing there are a number of not so satisfied customers on here, I feel like I got lucky and ordered their best dishes. The chicken and maitake mushroom was in a scrumptious sauce, the foiegras was excellent and the baked alaska had an impressively complex combination of flavors (though my favourite is still the Met Opera's) Left here totally satisfied, and on top of that, it didn't break the bank
One of the best restaurants I've been to in the country. Hands down. Beautiful ambience, wonderful service, the food was Michelin star quality. Pricing was fair.

I've been there three times and I was only disappointed less than once. So it is more a 4.5/5 rounded up to 5. 

Really great service. Imaginary dishes but with a traditional root. My friend and I have this theory that one staff in the kitchen like to add extra salt. Other than that the taste is perfect. 

Of the dishes I have had there, I really enjoyed: 

Couteaux rafraîchis à la Grenobloise (razor clams, caper, lemon, croutons): the razor clams were very fresh, nice touch on the teeth. Caper and croutons added a different texture to the dish. Lemon and capers provided refreshing sourness. 

Navets en guise d'escargots (turnip, mussel and sea urchin disguised as snails): this is a very interesting dish, and it has noting to do with snail (sadly). It was served in the snail dish. It was a warm dish, with turnip, mussel and sea urchin all soaked in oil. I really enjoyed the flavor and texture of the warm turnip and the umani of the sea urchin. 

Quenelle de brochet "Route de Reims" (champagne beurre blanc, caviar): This is one of my favorite dishes here. Think of it as a firm egg custard made of Pike, very smooth texture but also with a consistency closer to fish than custard. The sauce went really well with the quenelle: the presence of lemon made the rich and flavorful beurre blanc pleasant and not burdening. 

Tout le Lapin: It consists of three dishes. The belly was sauted with liver, the front legs made into a soup with vegetables (think pot au feu but with rabbit), and the hind legs turned into a casserole with dijon mustard and onions. My favorite was the soup. Really fresh taste, minimal seasoning, allowing you to enjoy the flavor of the meat itself. 

Pigeon "Côtes de Provence" (anchovy vinaigrette and artichoke barbajuans): I really like it. The meat is done just right. Really tender and well seasoned. The artichoke barbajuans are interesting but I didn't understand what it has to do with the other components of the dish. 

I also rather enjoyed the Ris de veau a l'estragon (sweetbreads, cream, tarragon, maitake mushrooms) when I had it although my French friend thought it was too salty when he ordered the same dish. I have also had the Canette à l'orange (roasted duckling, endives braised with orange). The meat was done just right but the sauce was really, really, salty. Me and my friend were both underwhelmed. 

I had Poire "Belle Hélène" last time I was there. It is one of my favorite French dessert and I was expecting a warm poached pear with hot chocolate on top (it was winter) but it was a cold frozen pear and congealed chocolate. Maybe it is their twist on the dish. Was not the most pleasant surprise. 

Overall, I really enjoyed my experience here. Sometimes the dish can be too salty but when that doesn't happen, I usually either get what I exactly wanted or a pleasant surprise. 

Price-wise it is definitely on the pricey end. It does offer the four course dinner option (it is a lot of food...). 

The wine list is also really nice (and long), with a clear focus on French wine and offer quite a few American wine as well but no Italian wine at all (understandably).

Great restaurant , the design is done in a way where you know your in Manhattan but with a Parisian feel to it , has its own unique identity , Daniel Roses food is superb, only reason not 5 stars is because it could be more friendly in its approach , I've come dressed special and treated so, and dressed a little casual and treated less than , but when I ordered a great bottle of wine - $500 , things turned around, shouldn't be that way in this type of establishment

The restaurant is beautiful. Wonderful atmosphere and the vibe is great for romantic dates and possibly business meals. This place is definitely a little pretentious but I assumed this at a fine dining French restaurants! The sweet bread was unreal! Sauce was very deep in flavor added to the experience! Wine selections wonderful! The dish that ranked the experience for me was the lamb chop. The dish comes with one small fatty piece. The waiter upsold me by adding another small fatty chop for an extra charge of 20 dollars... I've had a better full rack of lambs for 20 dollars. I was offended. The taste was ok but realized I couldn't finish the chips because they were to fatty. Didn't taste like good fat. Tasted like unseasoned, unwanted fat. When we complained there was somewhat of an attitude with our server. She didn't seem happy to report back to the chef about this complaint. They eventually took off all extra charges off the bill. Which was nice! Thank you! But we left hungry and went and grabbed a pizza afterwards. This place is pretty good. Just not for me and that's fine.

I made it difficult for Le Coucou. I went there on a Monday, generally a quiet evening, when the best cooks of a kitchen brigade tend to stay at home. I decided not to take their most popular dishes (pike quenelles, tout le lapin, bourride). I brought my girlfriend, a hard-to-please diner. And the star Chef, Daniel Rose was not present. When the meal started, I was certain that I was going to corner the bird and accuse it of not living up to its hype. The oysters and anchovies were fine, but given the hype, they did not deliver the emotions we came for, therefore I was determined to "pluck the feathers" of the bird. But Le coucou fought back, and the bird went on cruising at exceptional altitudes. By the time the beef filet and carre d'agneau arrived at our table, the bird was out of reach, really high in the skies. Then the desserts were served, and I received a note, falling from the sky "coucou, I am not... I am actually a crowned eagle, ca te va? " Crowned eagle, you are, buddy! Can't agree more. Ca me va! Hype is always too much, oftently impossible to live up to, but Le Coucou deserves its reputation. It is, right now, a destination restaurant serving some of the very best French fares outside of France. And it happens to have an interior that is very easy on the eyes. I loved Le Coucou!

We were visiting NY for work last year, Me and my coworker had our breakfast before heading back home. The restaurant is at busy street in Soho, but once you enter the door is completely changed the vibe. The setting was quiet, intimacy yet vibrant. You can tell the level of their service from the food, setting and clean up are almost like an harmonies. It was a quick meal but very memorable.

This is one of my favorite French spots of all time. It's a beautiful spot, both at day and night. We both ordered the 4-course prix fixe, and added and additional dessert which was totally uncecessary, though not a regret. 
We began with waiting by the bar where they took our coats, but they were running behind and it was a little annoying to stand by for 20 minutes. Our table was also unfortunately placed, right next to the ordering system/utensil station for staff. Despite that, I think service could've been a little more attentive at times.
Upon seating they drop off a basket of bread at your table, along with some butter. The bread we initially got was okay, it wasn't warm at all. But the following basket they brought out was hot to the touch and far better. We started with the sea bass crudo and razor clams. Both were alright, but the sea bass was a bit on the flat side to be frank. It needed some more acid to pick it up. 
We continued with the faux escargot, made of turnips, mussels, and topped with uni, as well as the crepineette au foie gras. The escargot was alright as well, it needed something more than what just seemed like clarified butter. The crepinette was quite good, I just wish there was a bit more foie gras. 
The entrees are where this meal REALLY kicked into gear. We got the venison and rabbit, and each came in 3 dishes. The former arrived with a beautiful sauce (one I've been attempting to replicate since), a butternut squash au gratin that was rich and delectable, and a fresh radicchio salad to cut through that combined richness. The cook on the venison was perfect, though I think the poached pears were overspiced. The rabbit was great as well, the broth in th ande stew was incredible. The roulade made the loins was tasty, as were the roasted legs. 
Desserts were just as strong. The chocolate cake was a hefty portion and the white coffee ice cream was nice. The apple tarte tatin tied for my favorite-perfectly sweet and properly cooked. The crepes suzette with aniseed ice cream were a talbeside classic, but I definitely would've appreciated it if more alcohol had burned off. 
I think I'd be perfectly okay sticking to the entrees and desserts here, which I think, given the hefty portions, are enough for most people. With the extra dessert, we could barely finish everything, and I'm far from shy when it comes to food. When I return, I might give other apps a shot (perhaps the foie gras or quenelle de brochet), but the entrees and desserts were undoubtedly the stars of the show. The meal concluded with petit fours, and hefty, but not unreasonable bill.

Came here for a birthday dinner a couple months ago in the earlier part of the year. The reservation was really difficult to get because they book up so fast! So definitely recommend making the resy (on resy) ASAP.

When we arrived, there's a nice little waiting area where they can take your coats and the bar is to the immediate right. It's a good place to get a drink while you wait for everyone in the party to show up or for your table to be ready- I also like that rather than having to check out your tab at the bar you can just wait until the end of the meal to pay for it along with your food, seamless transition.

For appetizers, we got the Huîtres, Granité aux Algues (oysters), they were served with lemon and it was very fresh.

I got an old fashioned for the drink and it was good.

One of the entrees we got was tout le lapin, where they serve the rabbit in a soup, and grilled for another dish. I really like the creativity of this dish. The presentation was also really nice. The other entree we got was Côte d'agneau grillée, oignon farçi (lamb with onions). This lamb was  tender!
