For dessert, we got Poire "Belle Hélène", which is ice cream shaped in a pear with chocolate on top. It was cute they wrote happy birthday in chocolate on the plate! It wasn't super sweet which was great. The fruit at the bottom was a nice complement to the ice cream.

Recommend trying this place out but it'll definitely be a splurge since each entree is ~$40-50. The ambience is nice and the food is quality, this definitely feels upscale but without the uptight environment that sometimes comes with nice restaurants. Tout le lapin was my favorite of the meal so recommend getting that.

This is a pre-COVID review. We had lunch at Le Coucou back in winter 2019. They offered coat check once you walked into the restaurant. It was a weekday and the restaurant was already half-occupied.

Ambience wise [5/5] - Classy and elegant. Very nice place for special occasion 

Service Wise [3/5] - I found my server and sommelier a bit pretentious and cold. I know this is an "upscale" restaurant but a smile can definitely go a long way. Do know that a good dinning experience includes food and service 

Food Wise [4/5] -  We had the oysters and quenelle de brochet "route de reims" for appetizers. Oysters were alright but I enjoyed the quenelle de brochet very much. It gave you a creamy and almost melt in your mouth texture. We had halibut, bavette steak and duck for entrees. Generous portions and the duck won the show. We ended the meal with chestnut cake and chocolate tart. 

We had a pleasant afternoon and left with a satisfied belly. I definitely see myself going back in the future.

Be warned, they charge for water! I came after they opened post-covid lockdown and honestly was very disappointed. The food wasn't great (but drenched in sauce) and the plating was awful. The only reason I didn't give one star was because the service was good and ingredients seemed fresh. But for the price (over $500 for two with drinks included) it was very underwhelming.

It's a like fake news , not French , but an American French diner . The food is large size for French restaurant and also it's horrible . So this place is an example of that in nyc , feed people anything , they will eat it .

Traveled the world and have eaten at hundreds of high end restaurants and this is very middle of the road for very high end $$$ 

Service was very good , decor was perfection however the food was mediocre and overpriced. 
Plus the disrespect they have to charge 8 dollars for a glass of tap water! Tap water should clearly be free when you spend $600 for 2 people for dinner. Not sure why that irritated me more then anything but it's possibly the fact that they disguise the food as proper Michelin worthy food only to trick wealthy New Yorkers into paying for it and it's crystal clear by calling the tap water filtered water and charging $8 per glass lol. If you go please just know your going for the vibe and good service and and the food is an afterthought.
Excellent meal and service, I will be back.  The grilled  foie gras was superb and the ba ba a rum is very good too.

Went to Le Coucou for a celebratory dinner on Sunday evening. While the wonderful meal and exquisite service were important, it was the space that really made this an experience not to forget.

Quality: For an overdo special occasion we visited Le Coucou. I was immediately captured by the beautiful location. We sat down and ordered cocktails to get started, A La Folies-Bergere and La Main Danjouy. It didn't take long for the meal to start with our first course including Huitres, Daikon With Caviar, and Chickpea Fries. This was a nice light and flavorful start. This was quickly followed by the Poireaux Vinaigrette, Thon A La Portugaise, and Lotte En Salade Au Cumin. The leeks were tender and I loved the sauce. The Tuna was the weakest dish, but still very good. The lightly fried monkfish was fantastic and should always be ordered. At this point we went off track a bit with our add on of Tartare De Boeuf. It was my heaven. Succulent beef with layers of caviar and topped with an egg yolk. Each bite decadent and absolutely one of, if not the, best I've had. This was followed by the entrees, the Sole Veronique, which had a sweet butterscotch sauce was polarizing. While the Tout Le Lapin, was a masterclass in rabbit. The bits and the broth were my favorite components. We then ended with multiple dessert bites, each a showcasing a different skill.
Quantity: We ordered the Tasting Menu along with one A La Carte item and left stuffed.
Value: $185 for their Tasting Menu or dishes can be ordered A La Carte. $89 for the Tartare De Boeuf.
Ambiance: Le Coucou is located in the Soho area of Manhattan. Walking down the street and passing it, you can't help but stop and think it is a place you want to visit. Inside they have a small, but beautiful lobby bar before entering the main space. On a cool winter night, there is no where else you want to be. It reminds me of a castle, with tall candles on every table, dim chandeliers well spaced on the ceiling, and tall light brick walls. The open kitchen allows smells and sounds to circulate throughout the beautiful space. This is where you should go for a special romantic dinner.
Crowd: Reservations are absolutely required. While you may luck out with a cancellation, don't expect to be able to walk in. And while jackets are not required, I would say they are recommended.
Service: Le Coucou makes sure every moment you are inside the restaurant you are well taken care of. From host to waitress to sommelier to the runners, every single person was friendly, helpful, and knowledgable. The pacing of the meal was also perfect.
Parking: Tough area to find street parking.

Damn good..

Fantastic and thoughtful service...

Creative drinks...

Balanced and well thought out dishes...

This place is the real deal!

Thank you!

Highly enjoyed date night at Le Coucou. The atmosphere is cozy and we got a table by the window. The service was excellent.

We got a Tuna tartare, Halibut with buerre blanc, and cote the veau. Was very pleasantly surprised with the flavors of the veal which felt very home like and unlike what I've had at other French restaurants. The halibut was solid.

I recently had the chance to spend an evening at Le Coucou with a small group of four. While I was beyond excited for an experience others had raved about, I left overwhelmingly disappointed. The food isn't bad by any means, nor was our evening, but I can't imagine paying what we did for what we received ever again. 

Let's start with the dining room atmosphere. It's posh, open (without losing the sense of intimacy with your dining partners), and seductive. Dimly lit chandeliers and vaulted ceilings paired with understated table settings and hushed tones from the patrons around the room. The vibe does beckon elevated French cuisine.

Speaking of cuisine, my friend and I decided to pick out a few plates a la carte that caught our eye instead of trying the tasting menu. One hors d'oeuvre, gourmandise, and main plate each along with a dessert to share. All are listed here:

Bigeye tuna and vinaigrette (3/5)
Fried monkfish (4/5)
Quenelle de brochet with lobster sauce (4/5)
Sweetbreads (4/5)
Black Sea bass x2 (2/5)
Marjolaine (4/5)

Before we talk about the highlights, I should mention the cocktail I got... La main danjou (mezcal, elote liqueur and amaro), which was not good at all. Smelling pungent and biting in taste without any sweet or bitter notes to balance, I would recommend against it and rather go for the Armagnac and gentian drink my friend got which was much better. Ok, so the dishes... the tuna was just ok, overly reliant on the natural flavor of the fish without any additional flavors to complement it. The monkfish was probably my favorite single plate, textures of the crispy warm fish pairing well with the briny vinegar and charred onions. The quenelle was a revelation to look at and had an extravagant texture of a melt in your mouth dumpling surrounded by a savory lobster froth but it was wanting for flavor. The sweetbreads were also quite good with the cream sauce and maitakes shining here. The sea bass sadly was bland, relying on the accompanying stewed seafood medley (not quite bouillabaisse) for flavor, but the base here was just overpowered by olive oil and lemon juice which could not save the fish's lack of taste. Dessert was a rich chocolate cake with hazelnut encrusted ice cream which was pretty good but likely won't be memorable to me in a few weeks. The kitchen also sent out some added treats including bread, crispy veggie straws, mini macrons and truffles, and mini beignets, all good in their own ways.

Service was attentive and relaxed. Nothing over the top for a place with a Michelin star, but I have no complaints there.

What does set this place back is its price point. The food was ok. But at $255!!! per person including drinks and tip, I would have expected to be more satisfied. But I left still slightly hungry and wanting of better flavors. So despite the elegance of the evening and charm of the place, I wouldn't come here over the myriad of choices surrounding it.

Food 3.5/5
Service 4/5
Ambiance 4/5
Value 1/5
Overall 3.1/5 (Average)
Worst dining experience at a Michelin star restaurant I have experienced. Service was terrible. I do not recommend this restaurant.
Perfectly prepared food, impeccable service, beautiful presentation, and a warm and inviting atmosphere. We loved it!

This place is a must try if you're in the mood for French dinner. Everything from the service, ambience and food was superb! We did the a la carte menu but next time will definitely try the pre fixe because everything on the menu was so good. My favorite was the beef tartare with caviar and the apple dessert was so good I almost ordered two for the road but as I am on my January workout binge I denied myself the temptation lol. Looking forward to coming back and trying more of the items here for sure.

Wonderful dining experience overall - gorgeous space, and excellent service. We went in recently for my husband's birthday dinner. For starters we had the Foie gras et volaille en gelée and Thon à la portugaise (bigeye tuna). Both we absolutely delicious and a must. We also had the Quenelle de brochet, sauce américaine (pike dumpling) which was OK. For the mains we had the Sole Véronique (dover sole filets) and Halibut. The halibut was bland, but the dover sole was absolutely phenomenal - the best dish of the night!

I am not really fond of leaving bad reviews or anything so I apologize if this will upset anybody. This is just my personal opinion (and taste buds) and I don't want it to be of any factor here. 
It was my Birthday and I just wanted to go for dinner with my fiancé and have an intimate dinner and a lovely food experience. I have heard a lot about this place and it was a restaurant that I wanted to visit for a while. 
Service: excellent. 
Ambiance: intimate, romantic, classy, elegant. 
Noise Level: medium. 
Food: I didn't like at all. Sadly. We ordered foie gras et volaille, monk fish and oysters for apps, sweetbreads with maitake mushrooms (this was good), my main was filet basquaise and his main was Black Sea bass. 
Personally foie gras reminded me of tiered "holodez", not really spreadable and there was no toast next to it. I love foie gras I try it everywhere I go where available and this was not the best at all. My main dish is what left me really upset. I am at work right now and am still upset about it. The sauce they used for the veal and the same sauce for the pie is just way too contradicting, it has somewhat of an old world ragout taste with a hint of sweetness to it. Did not want to taste that on my pie or my veal. The consistency of the veal was great. Just the sauce was a killer. My monk fish I enjoyed but just the essence it was in was way way to strong. I basically wished I picked a different app. 
Conclusion: if you want French stick to Daniel's.

I came back here in 5 years and realized that the food sure went down... The panisse (chickpea fries with sour creamy sauce) that they gave in the beginning were already a bad sign. I didn't know why they even gave that because they weren't appetizing.
-Foie gras terraine was underseasoned. The texture of chicken wasn't smooth as foie gras that was together. 
-Monk fish was OK, it's just fried fish, with vinegar and herbs
-In sweetbread, I used to love the sauce, but it didn't taste the same as the one I had before -- no layering of flavors. Also the sweetbread wasn't crispy
-Escargot dish was OK, but some were not consistent and salty. It seemed overcooked.
-Filet basquaise w/ vegetable tart was too one dimensional. It had three salty component: foie gras, speck, and meat sauce. Sweet sour component would have been nice. The vegetable tart tasted like baked dough.

Dessert was the best, with the crunchy meringue with caramel and vanilla, the contrasting flavor was amazing. That's why I'd still keep 3 stars. (also including cocktails and service)

Wow. What a disappointment.

We went to Le CouCou for Valentine's Day. We did the tasting menu.

The experience started with cold bread and flat sparkling water. What followed was the most mediocre set of dishes I've ever experienced. Bland foie gras. Fish over saturated in sauce.

Dessert saved a little grace. The wine pairing was great. Decent service. But then it was quickly offset by a $905 bill at the end of the night. My girlfriend figured I must have overtipped so contacted the restaurant. They said their receipts "contain little detail"...so fix it?

Would have been a great restaurant for 10% of the price. I'm a regular at restaurants like this and all I can say is save your money.

The ambience is excellent for a quiet romantic dinner.  The service is top notch and responsive. I and my friend however thought that the food was relatively bland.  We had the duck, monkfish, foie gras and desert. None of them stood out, and at the prices, I wasn't satisfied that the food was worth it.    All in all I would probably chalk it up to an interesting adventure, but wouldn't repeat.

The most perfect wedding dinner! We got married at city hall before. Le coucou graciously let our professional photographer snap a few photos by the gorgeous bar. But watch out for the cranky bartender who grunted he did not want to be in photos but wouldn't move. It was only 5pm. 

If you're a party of 5-6 request the corner table by the front door. We were far from the other diners and had an amazing time. The service was impeccable. They comped us champagne and an extra dessert to celebrate. We ordered 4 desserts, but the caramel one they brought us was my fav! My husband's fav dessert was the chestnut. 

Lobster starter is a must. Next time I'll hoard this for myself. The sweetbreads were sublime and our favorite dish of the night. Beef tartare was tasty (a bit salty without bread) but prob not worth the price tag. Warm foie gras was good. Skip the mussels and pike dumpling. The halibut was nice but not special. Biggest disappointment was my lobster entree. It was a bit tough. Get the duck instead. There was a crowd of diners waiting but they never rushed us. The bill was reasonable for a restaurant of this caliber. Do not miss this gem. Or do so we can keep it for ourselves. We can't wait to celebrate our anniversary here every year. Thank you Le Coucou for a flawless wedding night!

Still giving five stars but wanted to make a comment about the CHARGE FOR WATER. So random!!! Dined here a few times pre pandemic mainly. Recently came back and overall experience was solid: gorgeous interior, lovely seating, and also great waiter and staff-- love the wine selection and pairing and also the dishes were tasty and unique enough-- not too heavy sauces and good solid dessert. However, the charge for some water which appeared to be tap--leaves a weird feeling about the restaurant. What restaurant charges for water ? If they are charging, at least bring a bottle of mineral water ? Not just tap, that we barely touched. It's six dollars per person, which can't make or break the restaurants bank-- but given that we all felt a little weird about that charge and other reviews too on here (so I realize I'm not being trite)-- that would be my suggestion for otherwise a great 1 Michelin experience in nyc.  Just don't charge for the water.

LMAO! Felt like we got scammed at Anna Delvey's favorite restaurant. How ironic...!

Wasted our time here when there's so many amazing restaurants in NY...

Food was nothing special. Taste profile was flat, service was ok - also felt a bit judgmental and pushy from our server. Host and bartender were excellent though. 

Buvette is 100x better when it comes to French cuisine.

We've been to many Michelin starred, this is the only restaurant we don't understand why it was highly praised.

Come here only for their superb bartender/cocktails he's  able to make off menu, but that's all. Please don't waste any dollar on the dinner menu, like seriously.

Le Coucou is perfect from A to Z. Decor is romantic
and modern with high ceilings, stunning chandeliers
and an open kitchen. Service from hostess to
waiters and sommelier are professional and friendly.
The cuisine is absolutely delicious, creative and
rooted in classics perfectly reinterpreted. Among
my favorites are sweetbreads. I can't wait to try the
chef menu where the chef surprises you with
courses of his choice.

Food is ok, but nothing special. But what an attitude received from lady who served us, you can't ask her anything, she won't help with anything. Such a nasty one. One star only for hostess, nice and pleasant . The rest with this girl attitude ruin the dinner.

I have been here a grand total of 1 times. 

The food is excellent - delicious and exciting, but that's not the only reason to dine here.

The ambiance is reason enough visit, and all diners are on display.

Dress well, check your makeup before you go because the bathroom is way too dark, order dessert, enjoy yourself

love it. excellent service. I did lunch there with three courses and drinks. The champagne was excellent. We finished with the lemon tart and baba rum (dessert is a MUST). My starter was a sliced crab (almost like a ceviche/salad hybrid) which was spot on and did the chicken thigh with ju (no idea what it was actually called). There were whole carrots/onions in the side pot of stock and it was sooooo good. Will be back and I love this place.

Good is great, service is excellent. Definitely recommend trying this restaurant if you are near by.

I especially like the service, I could tell they had put extra miles on it which made me feel very satisfied and comfortable. For example, we were a group of 4 and the sharing plates they gave us were warm. Every time they need to changed the plates after we finished it, the staff would come to cleaned our table and changed our dishes, the whole process was less than 1 minutes and there was no awkward moment

I'm so sad I wasted a meal at this price point at Le Coucou. For 4 people, we had a bill of over 1000 dollars and the food was mediocre at best. 

If you are looking for a special occasion place, I highly recommend finding an alternative restaurant. Nearly everyone I know who had gone here gave the same opinion about eating here so I am not sure why this place is so popular..
Outstanding food and service. The complimentary Madeline's were addictive. I will be back!

Such an eloquent and divine experience. I absolutely loved the ambience of the restaurant. Everything we ordered tasted amazing and the service was impeccable. I would love to come back here again and sit near the kitchen to be able to witness all the action going on!

I would come here again, but, maybe not so late next time. Best oysters I've had in awhile. The staff was great but definitely practiced, hard
 to get them to go "off script". Wine paring was decent, but not bad. Desserts were fantastic. The vibe was... I will describe it in two parts: the restaurant itself is beautiful in that very cool soho/European reflective way. However, the second part to the vibe, it definitely is a place popular with near centenarian men who bring their teenage 'company'. As we were leaving, the last diners were an older older man and his companion whom he was propping up to prevent her from spilling wine all over herself while she was slightly falling forward; the scene felt r@pe-y, I felt uncomfortable observing it. Then another woman who had walked in with us, but now was solo, had jumped into the car we had called and then fought crying & inebriated-ly with the driver. In California, we have these types of places too, the lobby/tea room of The Plaza Beverly Hills is one of them. But, it's not the scene I'm used to after paying $1,000 for a meal. #stayclassy

Absolutely gorgeous space. Really friendly service. Fancy but not stuffy, as in, it was totally fine that I brought my toddler, and that she wandered around a little bit. The food was good, but expensive. Liked the beef tartare, the lobster, and the chocolate tarte. The leek salad was OK. The fish dumpling was interesting, but I wouldn't get it again. Overall portions were kind of small.

Nice ambient and great service.
Food was awful; it serves minuscule portions charging high price.
Problem is I had to return my fish; it was spoiled and submerged by in abundant vinaigrette to cover up the bad taste 
I do not recommend it

You'd have to be coocoo not to love Le Coucou.  I've been for lunch and dinner several times over the years and recently returned for lunch on a Saturday.  It was remarkable how the experience is so consistently excellent after all these years.  The space, food, and service all meet the expectations for a fine dining experience.  I loved the Vol-au-vent "Coucou" - it was a pleasure to eat and I'm still thinking about that sauce.

The service was absolutely amazing. The workers here were so nice & I cannot emphasize their good service enough. 5/5 stars on service alone. 

The food was not amazing... the dishes were simple & there was nothing I was served that I would say sparked my tastebuds. If you are a foodie & you want HUGE UMAMI & flavors then this place isn't for you. 

***A lot of the food here is for those that are used to fine dining and are fine with paying 200$ for a 45$ valued meal. ***

As they brought out each dish, I finished the dishes thinking "what the heck is this? They gotta stop playing with me because this is NOTTT worth my money." 

I've learned a valuable lesson through this experience: 

GOOD FOOD is NOT expensive. & expensive food isn't always good food. 

If you're a regular at Le Cou Cou... good for you, you can probably afford giving away money but if you're a person who values your money... get something else.

disclaimer*** 
I think that I came to Le Cou Cou with the wrong expectations. When I think of good food, I think of food that is BUSSIN, SLAPS & should make you want to dig into the dish even more. OR maybe all the dishes I got were just bad? And all the good dishes swerved me? ‍ 
Simple ingredients should have their best attributes brought out to be enjoyed but Le Cou Cou was just not for me. It may be for the average New Yorker but it just wasn't for me. It doesn't check the boxes for me: 

- Umami (how GOOD is the flavor of the food?) 
- Food Balance (If the dish is fatty, is there an ingredient that counters the fattiness?) 
- Purpose (does the food presented have purpose?) 
- Comparison (where does the food hold up compared to other foods?) 
- Value (are you satisfied after finishing the course? Was it worth your money?) 

Important note: THE SERVICE WAS ABSOLUTELY THE BEST. I hope the workers are getting paid well because they're giving amazing service.

Have always been wanting to visit Le Coucou and finally made my way here for lunch on a rainy day.

Love the decor, makes you feel like you're in Paris!

Menu is pretty straight forward, and flavors were amazing.

Definitely save room for dessert!! The St. Honoré that I had was so delicious!!!! 

Can't wait to come back for dinner another time!!

Don't ever think about going to this restaurant... Bad service, and they want you to be in a certain level of style so they can be nice to you, otherwise, expect a bad service. Even the food is NOT good at all. I swear even Chipotle can treat their customers with a nicer attitude. Not coming againextremely stuffy and pretentious staff, unhelpful at all giving us disgusting looks as if we're not literally paying their salaries. Honestly a bunch of pretentious bricks don't bother going. Keep elitism alive.

A place with great food,cute details, good service.
Definitely worth to go.  now my favorite French food place in NYC!

Excellent French food - some of the very best in the city.  Daniel Rose is a great chef with strong bistros in Paris.  Exceptionally beautiful dining room and decor, polished service, and the food execution is very on point.  Great for brunch but even better for dinner.  Their Quenelle de Brochet, a Lyonnaise pike mousse in a Champagne beurre blanc with herbs, is incredible.  Tout le Lapin is a fun dish - where else can you get a multi-dish rabbit course - but the duck is not to be missed.  A must-do whenever I touch down in NYC.  And 11 Howard is a beautiful address, too.

Pleasant experience.
Great, high quality service.

Felt very welcome and enjoyed the food and ambience.
The kitchen and chef is open for everyone to see.
You can hear them speak to one on another and make your food.

The vibe is very classy and upscale.
The food taste is unique and strange. I've never tasted food like this before

would give this place about a 3.5
honestly pretty disappointed since this place has a Michelin star. was hoping for a really good meal, but it was quite underwhelming overall. there were still some highlights but not enough to save this review. 
the bigeye tuna was pretty warm and it just did not taste that fresh. my bf and I love raw fish and were not impressed by the quality of this. 
the lobster was really tender (we got a half) but it definitely was not worth the price point. it came with a bowl of vegetables (see pic) which did not go together in my opinion. 
the veal crepinette was tangy and I'm not sure if that was intentional but it really put me off. I had a bite and did not want anymore. the potato purée under it was very tasty, but that's all I could say. 
the pike dumpling was probably my favorite. it did take me by surprise as it has an airy egg texture, almost like a savory flan. I was a fan of it, but my bf was not. I thought it was v unique, but not sure if it was worth the price point. 
service was phenomenal though, but they seem very strict about their reservations! i was running late due to bad traffic since it was raining. I kept calling and finally after the 3rd or 4th call, someone picked up. I said I would be there about 20 mins late and she said to get there by _:__ (the exact time 20mins after my res) or my table would be forfeited.

My wife and I went here for our Anniversary. We tried the tasting menu and wasn't disappointed. We were worried it wouldn't be enough food, but it filled us both up. Great staff and the service was impressive. Very attentive to our wine and water glass.

This place is the jam!! If you are in the mood for French food, you found it. We did the cou cou dinner at $185 a person and this did not disappoint at all. We asked if our dinner could include sweetbreads and they were the most amazing sweetbreads I ever had. So rich. Yum!!! 
Great experience. Wonderful stuff. Open kitchen concept. Truly an experience that you shouldn't miss. Make reservations.

We loved this restaurant! We came here for our anniversary. They offer a tasting menu for 185 pp or order a la carte. We ordered five food items and one dessert. We felt this was enough food for us. We loved the duck a l'orange, tuna, and leeks. The frasier dessert was also amazing. The restaurant itself is gorgeous with romantic lighting from the chandeliers and the bar with trees on the walls in a dark gray. This place recently reopened after a year and half closure from the pandemic.
The restaurant was nearly empty but the hostess insisted they were booked up except she did allow a Caucasian couple in before us who did not have reservations.

Good ambiance - perfect for date night 
More on pricy side 
Food is good but not surprising

With no shortage of amazing French food in NYC, this place still stands out with their twist on some of the classics and outstanding service. My girlfriend and I, had just seen Hamilton and were driving down heading towards the restaurant, stuck in traffic I was running late, I called ahead to notify them and someone immediately picked up the phone, told us they would hold our table for us while we navigated the post-pandemic NYC traffic frenzy. I took some pictures of the dishes we ate, I always do because I like it when iPhone creates little reels of foods you ate or places you visited ;).  I ordered Navets en guise d'escargots, I love uni and I love escargot so the escargots disguised as uni was perfect for someone like me. I had the picture perfect lobster and my gf had the leeks as an appetizer and Halibut with fermented daikon with black caviar on top. That was amazing too, I know because I tasted it, what else is a friend for if you can't eat their food in the restaurant...
I will say this though, my lobster was the best but then again...I'm partial to lobster sooooo I'm not to be trusted when it comes to lobster vs anything. 

If it were me, I would end the meal there because I like the flavors of the main dish to linger in my mouth for longer, somewhat like red wine if it makes sense but can't do it with my best friend around she has to end the meal with dessert sooooo we ordered Marjolaine and to my wonderful surprise the beautiful floor manager Elisabed surprised us with another dessert and I had my "attendez la crème" moment while eating it. 

AH! and last but not least, the drinks!!! Being an amateur mixologist myself, I always appreciate a wonderfully prepared and presented cocktail, I only had one drink because I was driving...and I don't like to drink more than a glass or two of anything.

If you watched Inventing Anna, you know that a lot of her scheming happened right here in this restaurant. Le Cou Cou is a French restaurant with a Michelin star, but is it worthy of a visit (and star)?

We had:

Foie gras poché au Sauternes: This was a whole foie gras poached (?) in a consomme (broth) cooked with an expensive French wine. I've never had foie gras served like this before. It's texture was much different than a pate or seared foie gras and had a very strong and distinct aftertaste

Thon à la portugaise: This yellowfin tuna was served with a vinaigrette and raisins. The tuna was fresh but I found the raisins to not be a great complement (I'm also not a fan of raisins )

Sole Véronique- The fish was delicious! It was tender and well seasoned

Tout le lapin- This rabbit dish was a whole rabbit served in 3 different ways. One method included its meat stewed in a broth. Another was rabbit legs in an onion mustard sauce. The rabbit was very tender and not gamey.

Quenelle de brochet: This was a fish dumpling with lobster sauce. The texture was nice and the sauce was flavorful. I just expected them to look more like traditional Asian dumplings and not like an scallop

The interior is stunning, the bar is gorgeous and the whole setting is sleek, sexy and upscale. One thing I would say is that the service is EXTREMELY stiff. From hostesses to the servers and server assistants, I found they were boarder line rude and impatient. The staff were so unapproachable that we ordered without properly understanding the menu, so we just blindly chose dishes. A few items we were interested in were sold out as well.

Overall this was a very interesting culinary experience, as the dishes were more unique than ones I had when I was actually in France. Overall: I think it's worth a try, except I would strongly suggest to ask more questions about the menu than I did.

The food was tasty but I found it to be pricey 
They charged 120.00 for the duck which they claimed would feed two people - it did not!
And for that price you get two small pieces of breast  and a leg that had very little taste
Extraordinary food. Maybe the best food I have ever had. Amazing ambiance. A winner!!

Was at Le Coucou this past Tuesday to celebrate a wedding anniversary. Though food was "good," it did nothing to live up to the hype or explain why I had to be poised on OpenTable to reserve a table at the strike of midnight 30 days out. The space itself is very nice and inviting, but none of the food made us utter "wow" and the staff just felt a little green and unpolished compared to other comparably priced restaurants (Entrees are generally $40-$50 and waiters steer you to order three courses, not counting desert.) I understand it is a downtown venue, but I couldn't help but contrast the feeling to, say, a Le Bernardin, where one really feels "waited on." Little things, like folding your napkin if you left the table during the meal, were missing and it just didn't seem like the staff really could talk about the food in a way that excited you about the preparation or ingredients. Even the rap of the sommelier to a midwestern couple sitting next to us had us sort of rolling our eyes (though this was partly due to the cluelessness of the couple).  

To start, off the Hors D'oeuvres part of the menu, my wife had the warmed oysters (just 3) which were small, underwhelming and overly salty. I had a veal terrine, which was nice, but something very traditional and uninventive. The 2nd course is listed under Gourmandises. My wife had a veal tongue, caviar and creme fraiche dish which was probably the most interesting thing we ate. I ordered the sweetbreads, which were also very nicely done. For entries, my wife had tile fish with a bouillabaisse of sorts, that she was very happy with. I had the "Tout le lapin," which is a whole rabbit split into three differently prepared dishes. This was the most disappointing dish I had as none of the preparations lived up to the savoriness and heartiness that I typically associate with rabbit preparation. We shared a chocolate desert, which was good but nothing that memorable. 

So, all in all, yes the food is good, but nothing I'd jump through hoops to go back for at this price point.

An awesome place and outstanding food.
Have the Coucou special where they bring you dishes. All the dishes were on point!

Look at the menu carefully before you go.
Except to pay $26.00 for half a glass of champagne.
Expect to eat bread as your meal is served.
Except the sauces to be unexpected but not in a good way.
Very disappointed. The service, the food, the drinks, and the $300.00 tab for two
made me regret my restaurant choice!

What a wonderful dining experience! To celebrate the sale of our NY house, we made dinner reservations at Le Coucou. And it was the perfect restaurant for it. Service was excellent! Every dish was delightful. The atmosphere was superb! Highly recommended for a special occasion dinner.

Simply popped in for some drinks while waiting for an event nearby. They have an extraordinary wine menu. Some serious options including several bottle priced above $10,000. 

I had a cocktail dubbed the Danse Macabre. It was made with black tea and milk which intrigued me. Cocktail was great and it a very sophisticated block of ice. They had quaint bar area with room for about six. The bartender was super friendly. We had a very nice time at the bar.
Overall this place is good but not amazing. Can't complain about it but can't really tell what really stands out.

We hadn't been back to Le Coucou in about six years and the cooking over that time has only improved.  All of the dishes were good to excellent.  The four of us ate the leeks (good), yellowfin tuna (very good), eel (very good) mussels (good), pike (good), filet (excellent), halibut (excellent), rabbit (excellent) sea bass (good), and a variety of desserts including the baba au rhum, (excellent) pavlova (very good), chocolate sponge cake (good) and the dacquoise(good).  Service was efficient and helpful.  The wine list was absent good lower price wines.  Almost all the wines were above $100 with many into the thousands.  Even the $150 corkage fee is way beyond what most restaurants charge like Union Square Hospitality with their $35 fee and other high end restaurants NYC.  Dinner for  four was $750 with a lower priced wine and drinks, tax and tip.
Not worth the price. The appetizers are just ok--except the sweet breads which were delicious. Sole was very good. Dessert good but nothing special.

Hands down the best service I have ever received in a restaurant. The staff were extremely professional and courteous, which matched the ambiance of the restaurant. The food was very good, although the portions were on the smaller end. I ordered the uni, a salad, and the duck confit, which was amazing. 

I came down as I wanted to try a michelin star restaurant (didn't have them where I'm from) and was not disappointed. If you're looking for a place to celebrate something special, I would recommend Le Coucou.

Hands down one of the best meals of my life, worth all the hype! Brought my boyfriend here for a birthday week dinner and was looking for something to remind us of some of our favorite memories at Michelin starred restaurants in Paris, and this went above and beyond. Service was incredible, and helped us totally escape into the meal. Wine selection was amazing (we went by the glass to try a few things and the Chenin Blanc was my favorite). The food was all fresh, inventive, and delicious. We did the yellowfin tuna and quenelle for apps, the lobster and the filet for entrees and the pavlova for dessert and not a single thing disappointed. Already dreaming of coming back, even as local New Yorkers this really was a meal we'll never forget!

Absolutely love Le Coucou! Typical French decor setting, open kitchen, very comfortable and unpretentious. Excellent service, from the minute you walk in you are greeted by the maître d'hôtel and immediately seated. Reservations are required. Our server Natalia was super helpful and attentive. The food was very delicious special compliments to Cote de Veau and Bar Noir a la setoise. Both dishes were amazing! Highly recommend marjolaine for dessert. Definitely a place to visit and experience a gourmet cuisine.

Celebrated my birthday here and had a wonderful dinner. (Anna Delvey hype aside, I trust Stephen Starr.) My boyfriend and I ordered:

+ À La Folies-Bergère cocktail
+ Danse Macabre cocktail - both drinks were excellent 
+ Foie gras - decent
+ Yellowfin tuna - could have been fresher
+ Fried eel - highlight #1
+ Sea bass - highlight #2
+ Green salad (off-menu item)
+ Black Forest cake - awesome

Complimentary madelines and truffles were a nice touch. Definitely would return!

For me walking into Le Cou Cou is like Holly Golightly walking into Tiffany's. Felt that way every single time I've gone over the years. Beautiful place and fantastic dining. An experience that will elevate your spirits. Get the oysters, the leeks, the duck.

Very nice, very expensive French restaurant.  Beautiful interior, exceptional service. Exceptional prices for food and wine.  I think there are 3 bottles of red under $100.  Food is quite good, but if you've eaten this type of classic, modern French before, this is not real a good value restaurant.

Careless service and unhygienic dining environment. The candle burnt my hair due to the server's mistake. Also there was dripped wax all over the table. I even found some on my glass. See photos attached.

I had a wonderful experience at Le Coucou with a few close friends recently. It was my first time here and I wasn't sure what to expect. I've read the glowing reviews and saw it featured on shows like Inventing Anna, but was afraid that it might not live up to the expectations. I am happy to report that the food, drinks, and service were all top notch.

We indulged in the tasting menu which was $185 per person at the time of this review. There was no indication on the menu of how many courses or what would be served, so everything was truly a surprise. They ended up giving us a large selection of starters including smoked whitefish, oysters, chickpea fritters, fermented daikon with caviar, leeks & hazelnuts, and yellowfin tuna. They then served their version of "escargot" which featured mussels and sea urchin. The main course was a large portion of duck and foie gras. This was followed by an apple and bay leaf sorbet as a palate cleanser. Dessert included hazelnut dacquoise and cream, madeleines, and macarons. Overall, it was A LOT of food and there were no misses. Everything was very classically French but with a few little surprises to keep you interested. Stand outs for me included the oysters, yellowfin tuna, and duck. 

As for drinks, my friends and I started off with a few cocktails and then called the somm over who recommended a fantastic bottle of wine. Service was spot on. Friendly and seamless, never overbearing. 

Overall, I would highly recommend Le Coucou if you are looking to check out one of the best fine dining French restaurants in the city. I have had great experiences at other Stephen Starr restaurants and this one did not disappoint.
Excellent service, amazing food, great location. Simple review but all true! Highly recommend.
Very filling. The dishes were all pretty good. The flavors were amazing and very interesting. The staff were all so friendly and helpful.

Went last Friday for my birthday and had a great time, we made reservations in advance as it gets really busy and is not easy to get a table last minute, we had a great time and the food was excellent. We had the sweetbreads, the lobster, the rabbit and the tuna, everything delicious, but very impressed with the rabbit as it comes in 3 different presentations for you to try, so basically is a 3 in 1 dish. For dessert we got the pavlova and they also brought a sampler of sweets as a birthday treat. I ordered a dirty Martini off the menu and my partner got the mezcal cocktail, and another one that I cannot remember the name but was also very well made. 

Would recommend going for a special occasion or anytime you would like to experience fine dining at its best and dress up for a fancy evening. 

Service was great and very attentive, also staff was friendly and knowledgeable, only good memories to add for my special day.  Would recommend and will be definitely coming back. Well deserved Michelin Star.

We went for a special occasion and I would say the experience was...mixed. An otherwise exceptional culinary experience was really diminished by the service.

The dishes really were a journey. Seaweed granite was an elegant complement to oysters. The meatiness of the tuna was balanced with sweet Madeira vinaigrette and raisins. The crispy eel really popped with a curry vinaigrette. The mussels with uni and turnip topped with herbs tasted like pure ocean breeze in the most beautiful way. The sole, with grapes and mushrooms, hit the entire octave of flavors, from sweet and light to savory and meaty, in a single bite. 

The dishes were so perfect that I had to look into the open kitchen to see what kind of artists were back there.

But the service. It was attentive, meticulous, and knowledgeable. At times it was even friendly. You could tell that the staff could really shine. Yet there was the overarching impression they didn't want us there. They pressed us for time from the outset and perpetually reminded throughout the meal. Is that part of the quintessential French experience? Perhaps. Were they overbooked? Did they have unreasonable revenue targets?But it took otherwise 5-star (Starr?) food to a 3-star experience.

Went for a work lunch on a Thursday and was not disappointed. We changed our party from 2 to 3 at the last minute and they were very lovely about accommodating us. We started off with the leek vinagrette appetizer and the tuna sashimi with Madeira raisins. The steamed leaks were soft and beautifully seasoned with a light oil on top. The roasted hazelnuts added texture and a little smoke to the overall flavor of the dish. The sashimi tuna was thin and room temperature (please note that from my understanding that this is exactly how we should expect sashimi to be served). The sashimi was lightly seasoned but the Madeira raisins added just enough of a fragrant punch to add some pizazz to the dish. 

For mains, I had the filet with relaxed fois gras and frites because who doesn't love a steak frites from a French restaurant? The relaxed fois gras was very much like how you might put butter on a steak after its done... but with a slightly pungent more complex flavor boost. The frites came out in a basket made out of a dinner napkin which was clever and really prevented it from being too greasy. I ended up dipping the fries in that delicious fois gras goodness to get it all in. 

My two friends chose the quenelle and the sea bass which they loved. They noted that the skin of the bass was well crisped and retained a beautiful flake. The quenelle was surprisingly soft and the lobster sauce accompanying it was on par for one of the best sauces they had had in a while. 

For dessert we did the chocolate tart and the Saint Honore. The chocolate tart was garnished with gold leaf but had a nice balance of chocolate, textures from toffee and nuts, and sponge. It was paired with a fresh cream sorbet which was a very nice pallet cleanser.

Why 5 stars to start? The food was excellent, the service on point, and the atmosphere was delicious. We also managed to eat through most of the lunch menu. We were told, however, that it does change with the season so we might have to go back soon!!
Atmosphere is very subtle. The course is a great experience and has many highlights. But nothing too special about the flavor

Remains very very very good - maybe just under great... Prices are up a bit (like everywhere) but quality remains strong. All of the rabbit alone was worth the evening. Quenelle also excellent slightly less a culinary dazzle sans the surprise of one's first quenelle. My companion from 1980s France delighted in her meal which also included leeks/vinaigrette/hazelnuts (classic)! Not quite great FIVE STAR but I rounded up..... 

and amuse bouche of pomme frites and dijon - just lovely !

Had a very solid meal here, and think it's a good choice if you're in the area, but I wouldn't run back or go out of my way.  The restaurant is beautiful, and seems like a good date spot.  I started with the greek salad with lobster - it was good and the lobster was very fresh and good quality.  also has chicken with foie gras - which was ground chicken and foie gras fried.  It was good, but not wow.
My wife and my favorite NYC destination for incredible dining. The food is exquisite, service is impeccable and the restaurant is an artistic beauty. If you're in NYC, go, don't miss out on this one.

My boyfriend & I came here for dinner, we made last minute reservations and walked in ( dressed very casually ) and of course they were still able to accommodate us. The server was nice but didn't take one of my requests ( I asked for no uni on half of the " escargot's " since my boyfriend does not like uni, it still came with uni on all pieces ) but I am not going to discredit the server for one minor thing. I had very high expectations of this place since it has a Michelin star, of course those expectations were immediately crushed. 

We ordered the tasting menu, we were told that the server & chef were going to create one just for us. ( they did not everyone gets the same exact thing ) we did request for the duck to be in the menu**

The ambiance was very intimate ( it was a candle lit dinner ) I loved that. 

To sum it up the food was honestly not good. Nothing really special to rave about, my personal favorites were the duck, oysters & obviously the desserts. For me it was a  5-6/10, my boyfriend though he did not enjoy any of it at all.. he rated it a 0/10. 

The server kept on saying " ITS FUN YEAH? ", " ITS FUN! ". no it's not. 

It was a good experience overall because now we know we will never return.

TLDR: beautiful restaurant, spectacular service. Quenelle was probably one of the best bites I had but I was not too impressed with the rest of the Coucou Dinner. Willing to try it again - perhaps it was an off day!

Came to celebrate my birthday and got the Very Coucou Dinner. My friend had previous came to Le Coucou and told me it was quite good so I was very excited. We had various items that, to be honest, I don't remember we're called. Our favorites of the night were the mussels that were "disguised as escargot" and the quenelle. The mussels were in butter and garlic and basil - what isn't good in the trio? The quenelle was the show stopper for me. I was not expecting it to be as good as it was. The texture was light and airy and the sauce was buttery and full of lobster flavor. One of the best bites I had this year. Everything else we had was honestly forgettable which made me a little sad; all the dishes were attractive and cooked well but flavor was just okay to me. 

The dessert was also one of my favorite parts of the meal - the marjolaine was hazelnut dacquoise with chocolate. Again, what is not to like about that combo.

The restaurant was more romantic than I was expecting - the dinner was me and my friend and everyone else around us was a couple. Perhaps keep that in mind when you're thinking about booking this place. Service was great and had a nice conversation about the restaurant with the hostess. 

Overall, willing to come again for the quenelle, but hoping to be impressed with other dishes next time!

This place was beyond stunning. First and foremost the ambiance was elegant and classy, and the service was beyond exceptional. Their kitchen is open concept so you can watch all of your dishes being prepared. The extent of staff creating these dishes is quite impressive. We shared all of our food. We had fried eel, yellowfin tuna madeira, duck, and smoked sea bass. We had our sommelier suggest cocktails and wines to compliment our meal. This was an amazing night, with great company and I highly recommend this place. The menu and wine list is quite pricey but totally worth it.

The room is beautiful. The service is top notch. The food however was disappointing. The veal was with sweetbreads! In the description this was not mentioned! This detail ruined our meal because we do not like sweetbreads. 
The rabbit was bland & underwhelming. The Pavlova dessert was spectacular hence the 3 stars.
As soon as we did not order a bottle of wine we got our food immediately, it felt like a swift kick in the ass to get out. The fine dining is uptown don't get caught up in the hype to come here.

Le Coucou is an outstanding experience from start to finish. The space is absolutely gorgeous and well decorated, the bar when you enter is stunning and the dining room perfectly set up. Everything in the menu was to die for - starting with the Thon à la portugaise and the Navets en guise d'escargots - beautifully plated and tasty. The main artist is the Vol-au-vent "Coucou" and this is an absolute must try - sweetbreads and lobster married inside a perfect puff pastry, the combination highlights all the flavors and your palate won't forget this for a long while. The marjolaine a perfect finish to the meal. A vast and rich wine and drink menu as well, nothing will be missing from your Le Coucou experience. They may have one Michelin star in the books but they have all five (for Yelp, three for Michelin, right?) in my heart.

We loved Le Coucou from the time it was opened until it closed for covid. Last night we returned for the first time as guests of our son who is a foodie and had dinner in the main dining room which is gorgeous. We found dinner excellent but sense that the chef had a different hand. I had canelle and then sole veronique. It was wonderful. It's a great restaurant in all ways

Much anticipated evening. Warm welcoming environment with special high skills dishes and attentive service. But if I hadn't put the brakes on them trying to move us along to dessert, coffee, check and out the door, we would've run through 3 courses and a bottle of wine before dessert in under an hour and the whole meal in an hour and 10.  $500 is a lot for fast food. Back to the food--the quenelle was beautifully fluffy, the leek appetizer (the only vegetable on menu though upon inquiry we were offered a side of swiss chard, not a common favorite) lovely, and both entrees (lobster and three types of veal) also excellent.  Dessert wise, the meringue and raspberry pavlova is definitely the best and most special of the choices IMHO.

Sent from my iPad

Tasting menu is worth every penny. 

I can eat a moderate amount and feel full. My husband can eat a huge quantity before he feels full. By the end of the meal, I was at my limit. My husband was satisfied but not full.

Le Coucou has a beautiful interior. It was perfect for date night. Jackets not required but dress for a night out in the city and you'll be on point.

I personally wish the tasting menu had more of a breakdown of what to expect. I was wary to do because I didn't want my main dish to be cooked fish. I expressed this concern and I was graciously told the kitchen would be informed of my request.

Our first course was comprised of things that my goldfish memory has already forgotten for the most part. The chicken consommé was tasty and a nice touch on a rainy, winter night. 

Our second course had items I recognized from the menu: poireaux vinaigrette (leeks, hazelnuts), thon à la portugaise (yellowfin tuna, Madeira vinaigrette with raisins), anguille frite au sarrasin (buckwheat fried eel, cucumbers and curry vinaigrette), and endive. Our third course was ris de veau à l'estragon 
(sweetbreads, cream, tarragon, maitake mushrooms). The sweetbreads were our favorite and the star of the night. Ask for extra bread to sop up the rest of the delicious sauce.

Our fourth course was filet basquaise (prime filet, relaxed foie gras and ham, jus tranché, tourte with chard and red pepper). Delicious and another perfect dish to enjoy on a cold, wet night. Our fifth course was three rounds of desserts. All decadent and perfectly sized. We enjoyed them with a cup of coffee.

Drinks wise we ordered la main danjou (mezcal, amaro, eloté liqueur, chili), à la folies-bergère (armagnac, gentian(s), lemon, egg white), and
danse macabre (a clarification of rhum agricole, lavender, earl grey, milk) off of the cocktail list. Respectively I found them to be slightly rough, smooth and foamy, and refreshing and sweet. My husband also had an old fashioned with a honey syrup and old fashioned without the honey syrup. I also had a glass of white wine.

We had two persons, a man and woman, in black suits and two gentlemen with long aprons who were the ones who primarily serviced our table. We found everyone approachable and patient in answering our questions about our meal. We particularly enjoyed chatting with the two gentlemen. 

I'd recommend Le Coucou to anyone looking for a great French dining experience. It made me smile seeing the host bringing out a high chair for a toddler patron. I always appreciate a fine dining experience that'll welcome the entire family. My young children are well-behaved and used to dining out. I'd feel comfortable taking them to Le Coucou. I felt that the quality and amount of food that we received was priced fairly. Our bill for two tasting menus and all the drinks we ordered came out to under $600.

We ordered everything on their menu. Most of their dishes were ok, except the caviar beef tartar and the lobster main dish. Not sure how this restaurant received Michelin star. 
My favorite part of the restaurant was the bar. Not the drink but the atmosphere. It would've been a better experience if servers were more friendly.

A really great experience with a couple of hiccups.

Le Coucou offers dining that is both exceptional and creative.

You will enjoy many creative dishes served by candlelight on fine white linen.  Plates are small but this isn't the place to go if you are looking to stuff yourself.  The leek salad was exceptional.  There was not a speck of sand and each layer dressed perfectly.  I personally did not choose the leek salad but was pleasantly surprised when tasting.  'Disguised Escargot' is a treat (make sure to have bread ready to dip).  The lobster au poivre had the best au poivre sauce that I have ever had.  Perfect for dipping those potato croquettes that come with the meal.  Chocolate torte was perfectly decadent but would recommend more desserts without nuts (I know it's difficult)

The service is amazing at the table.  Just look up and make eye contact and a server will be right there to accommodate.  The head server could do with a bit of loosening up but he was great.  The only real issue was with the entire staff for the front room.  The hostess, coat assistant, and bartender all seem to convey a very snobby sense of themselves.  A couple of my guests had made comments....  We also had to wait quite a bit for our table even though we had reservations.  However, other than that, we had a blast

Definitely worth the $$$ if you are looking for a unique and exceptional dining experience

It's absolutely one of the best meals I've had recently. You can choose between a la carte or prix fixe menu which is basically a selection of dishes by chef from the regular menu. I personally don't think it's worth doing the prix fixe since there's no additional dishes you can "taste".
My bf and I ordered a bunch of things to share. Foie Gras, Pike Mousse and Sea Bass are the highlights of the dinner. Foie Grass is not served as spread on top of bread, instead it's very well cooked and served in broth. Pike Mousse is so soft and it immediately melted in my mouth with the taste of lobster sauce. Sea bass is well seasoned and comes with other sea foods in a pot.
The food portion is decent. I was really full at the end of the dinner. Service at this place is great. I'd say better than most of the 1 star restaurants.
Came back and although the ambiance is just as cute and romantic as I recalled, the food was not as good - a little too buttery.

I did not enjoy the food. No matter how authentic or fancy the cooking is, the food needs to taste good and it just didn't do it for me. It's like a cruel joke to the crowd of overly pretentious diners that'll probably brag about their expensive French meal anyway.

- Steak with foie gras: it was a small average steak with some foie gras in it for $80...
- Soup with some custard chunk: the soup tasted... Confusing? What was that?
- Mushrooms with mushrooms on pastry bread: this was good but in a really strange way. I really couldn't tell what they were going for with the sauce but it wasn't bad
- Whisky sticky bread dessert: bland, texture wasn't good

We had a 9:30pm reservation, came in a few minutes late and had to wait about 5 more for the table to be ready. The service was average, food was great but a little on the salty side for my taste. The ambiance was very classy and romantic, open kitchen and beautiful bar area.

Reception:
Pleasant, coats taken immediately.
The occasion: New Year's Eve early bird dinner.
Seating and ambiance was very pleasant.
Excellent wait staff, without any oppressive "snobbyness".
The food:
It was a fixed Menu that consisted of the staples of this restaurant, which you will find in the pictures and countless reviews.
As always fixed menus are a little hit and miss but quality and execution was definitely good.
The Wine list:
Phone book like, you most likely find what you like.
Conclusion:
If you don't mind time limits(90'), have deep pockets, this is a quality establishment, with a pleasant atmosphere, suitable for a romantic dinner.
Price:
650$, Wine by the glass, after dinner drink (2 people)

Not a top restaurant - owners need to review their priorities.  Selling overpriced meals of subpar quality with lousy service at the fastest possible turnover rates seems to be the name of the game now at Le Cou Cou.  While my husband was sick with diarrhea in the bathroom, and I told them that my husband was also feeling nauseated, they said it was not their problem and presented me with the check, essentially asking us to leave without even a question about how my husband was doing.  This coupled with the service staff that was worse than at our local diner - filling glasses of water all the way to the top so it's impossible to drink without spilling the water out, waiters reaching in front of you while eating to take away any possible unused dish, ultimately so as to speed the turnover of diners and maximize revenue.  Constant questions about whether you're done with this and being ushered out of the restaurant without a single I'm sorry about the food that made you ill or are you feeling better now? Where has human decency gone in the pursuit of profit?  My take is this  restaurant is relying on the Chinese tourist trade to stay afloat - single visit guests who don't know any better beyond what is attractive decor.  Beware.

On our last visit to NYC we had wished to try somewhere new & as we have always been big fans of Stephen Starr establishments we chose this fine dining french inspired NYC location. The cooking was in a very traditional French style and the food was quite rich due to heavy use of butter & cream. Overall it was a fun experience and the atmosphere and service were of top tier levels but we ultimately decided the style of cooking does not suit our tastes.

Oh my. I just stumbled upon my new favorite restaurant in NYC. This was hands down one of the best meals I've had in 2022. The service, the food, the drinks, the ambiance... Just wow. Let's get into it.

Once you are seated, you have the option between the prix fixe menu or a la carte. And if you have ever read one of my reviews, you already know I am an a la carte and sharing person - I just love to order multiple dishes, and share them, to try them all!

Before I dive into each dish, I need to emphasize that everything about this spot was amazing. The staff was super nice and walked us through any question we had (and we had plenty! the menu offers lots of options and rich sauces we had not really had before!).

As soon as you place your order, you get a complimentary bread basket and crackers to start off your night. Both were delicious. The bread was warm sourdough and the crackers were like tiny crispy pillows (I know it's a weird description, but they were crispy on the outside and SO SOFT on the inside). Our night was already off to such a great start.

We ordered 2 appetizers and 2 entrees to share.
Poireaux Vinaigrette ~ Leeks are such a difficult veggie to master so when it's done right.. It says so much about the chef. Poireaux Vinaigrette are a very typical/authentic French dish but the take Coucou took was perfect. It was my very first time tasting leeks with hazelnuts! The hazelnuts added a subtle sweet flavor and a great crunch. And obviously, the leeks were super well prepared and were deliciously soft.

Thon a la Portugaise ~ 10/10! This was such an interesting take on raw tuna! The tuna was perfectly soft and fluffy that it slides in your mouth. The vinaigrette was so refreshing and actually just the perfect sweetness, and the black pepper on top was a perfect final touch. And I can't forget the grapes... This tuna was just amazing... The sauce was so good I ended up clearing out the plate with some of the bread. 

Bar Noire ~ The way we received this black sea bass was unexpected. The staff came with a whole casserole with goodies. They were also nice enough to serve us individual plates! I've always like sea bass but never enough to rave about it - and here I am, raving about it. What I love about this dish is that other seafoods come with it, and it's like a soup because of the abundance of sauce. This fish was refreshing and, at the same time, rich.

Homard Bourse et La Vie ~ OKAY but a LOBSTER in BLACK PEPPER SAUCE? Honestly, Coucou's sauce game kept getting better and better with each dish! It was such a shocking but perfect combo. Every other lobster dish I had was with lemon, butter and herbs. This was actually so perfect I continuously crave this! I also need to mention that the lobster was so decadent, so perfectly cooked that it was buttery, and saucy, and soft and thick... Yum. They also serve this dish with crispy potatoes - they were kind of milky and soft... but also crunchy... wow.

We went to celebrate my birthday, and we of COURSE had to end with desserts. We ordered the Pavlova with is essentially cream and red fruits in between cream and meringues. It was very well executed we destroyed it in under 2 seconds. And we also got the Marjolaine ~ this is essentially a couple of layers of chocolate ganache, chocolate cream and lots of hazelnuts for some additional sweetness and delicious crunch, all covered by a thick layer of chocolate. This was also destroyed in under 2 seconds.

And if the night was not already perfect enough! We got a basket of complimentary, freshly baked and warm mini madeleines covered in sugar (YUM YUM - they tasted like fluffy pillows of heaven) and with some mini chocolates. Delicious.

I had such a great experience at Le Coucou. I will definitely be coming back, and if you were hesitant, you should book that reservation and go. This was definitely worth the hefty price tag.
Expensive but delectable.  Lovely space and delicious food. Reservations necessary as it is popular.

This restaurant is one that I've been wanting to visit but has been difficult to snag a table when they first opened and with Covid, it's only now that I'm able to go .  Glad I did !! My friend and I got there early and had a drink by the (small bar) where the bartender kept us company and took a wonderful phot of us with the beautiful backdrop of the bar .  Though we got there early , the hostess tried to see if there's an available table earlier .  We still got seated T the designated time which is fine because we had the best seat in the house . We sat across the kitchen and I got to see the efficient staff ! In terms of food , we had the escargot , noodle with eel sauce , dorado and my fave which is what I had - filet de boeuf with bone marrow .  Amazing !! The desserts were also to dine for . The ambiance is amazing , sophisticated french bistro ( much better than pastis and more elegant for me ).  I'll definitely come back and try the other dishes on the menu !
Excellent. Absolutely magical. Highly recommend the tasting menu.  Exquisite service. Came here w my niece as we didn't realize how romantic it is.

First time visiting this French restaurant in Soho. Went for lunch & everything was amazing! The food was delicious. All of the apps were great. The mussels stood out, with a escargots twist. The duck was seasoned to perfection a must for the table to share.  Fries for the table can't be beat! Plates are shareable, which I would suggest to get a bit of everything. A bit pricey but well worth it! 

Service was excellent & very helpful. The restaurant itself is super cute, with a Parisian feel.

The Chad is back on Yelp after a brief hiatus. Lest my fans think that my inner, romantic wildebeest has been tamed by the suffocating tentacles of monogamy, I'd like to take this opportunity to completely dispel any such notion. Even in this crypto-skeptic economy, my yield curve trends way upward and nothing about me is artificially inflated.

Speaking of organs, my fellow bros and I recently visited Le Coucou, a Michelin-star winning restaurant that is apparently known for its preparation of some of the traditionally undesirable parts of animals. The venue strikes a good balance between buzzy and romantic, while the service was attentive and charismatic without any kind of ostentatiousness. First impressions were positive. 

There are two ways to order a Le Coucou. The restaurant features an a la carte menu and a four course (plus dessert) prix fixe, which varies day-to-day. My bros and I opted for the latter, which turned out to be a mistake. The waiter asks, at the outset, whether anyone in your party has food allergies or if there is anything you absolutely don't want to see. Beyond these few initial parameters, the chef controls your fate. 

The issue with this approach reminds me of my brief foray into the jowls of Tinder. I found, in both situations, that when presented with a virtually unlimited smorgasbord of options to eat, you can't immediately ascertain what you don't want. It's only seeing that unworkable option do you realize, "No, this won't work for me." It didn't occur to me to filter out 18-year old CUNY art students who really like spiders and it didn't occur to me to tell our waiter not to bring organ meat. This is, incidentally, why I prefer The League. It's a more curated experience for a cultured gentlebro such as myself.

There is a reason why most menus don't feature veal thyroids - it is an acquired taste that won't necessarily resonate with everyone, even with skilled preparation. For me, the sweetbreads left a pungent aftertaste that made it difficult to register any other flavors on the plate. And since sweetbreads covered in some kind of bitter broth composed about 20% of my experience, this one dish tarnished my impression of the restaurant. 

The other courses were fine, but not nearly as special as the sweetbreads were bad. The first course consisted of a daikon covered in some fermented nonsense and chickpea French fries. The second course was my favorite - a leek and walnut dish served with a nice tuna. The tuna was cooked just the right amount but was slightly too salty for my taste. The thyroid came third and was followed by duck served several ways (breast, leg, fois grois, and heart). These were fine - the breast may have even been *slightly* overcooked, but nothing too upsetting. The fois grois preparation wasn't my favorite. The waiter encouraged us to spread the fois grois over the other parts of the duck, but I found that I couldn't appreciate its independent flavor that way. Curiously, many of the dishes were served family style. I'm personally not a fan of that from a restaurant of this caliber. It's a bit sloppy and I would have loved to see some nice plating. 

I understand that one of my idols, Anna Delvey, visited Le Coucou during her tour of New York. I have no idea if Anna is a Yelper, but if she is reading this, I'd like to offer her the opportunity to see the city with one of its cultured elites: myself. Le Coucou is fine, but if you want a candlelit dinner and questionable meats, you can just go to Olive Garden and hit Lavo after. I know these things.

WORST EXPERIENCE dining here. Had a super RUDE + RACIST server. Never came to refill the coffee or asked if we we need anything. He was clearly super chatty and nice to the table of white guys next to us. 

The food is less than mediocre. Pojarski de volaille I ordered supposedly has foie gras, which is about the size of a dime. The rest of the dish is not impressive at all. 

My friend ordered the $70 Filet de bœuf. I never knew steak can be this bad. She could barely swallow the steak. Another dish was Maine lobster, the side thing is so oily, felt like the oil had been used for several days. Lobster itself did not worth the money. 

The deco inside is quite nice, other servers are also nice, but one person really ruined our day, also the food DID NOT worth the money.
I had the pleasure of having dinner here on a week night. The food was splendid, and the service matched expectations. The veal is excellent.

Very disappointed by this restaurant. 
Waiters were coming to the table too often, couldn't read the table and that we were not ready to order. Waitress omitted to say that sweet bread was veal thymus and that we ordered it as appetizer and main entree dish.. it turned out that I ate chewy veal thymus floating on a creamy sauce twice. Dessert was nothing special.

While many of its peers have underperformed relative to their Michelin status, this one was well deserved. From food, service, ambiance, to pricing, nothing stood out to us as a big negative.  While it's not the easiest place to book, it's easy enough if you book 1+ week in advance.  

On this lovely Sunday evening, the two of us was placed next to the open kitchen and it was definitely a nice experience observing all the business behind the scenes. We got the oyster, chilled lobster as appetizers, sea bass and rabbit as main, and Mon Blanc as our dessert. The rabbit was definitely the highlight of this evening, especially the front leg w/ clear broth (very refreshing). I'd also recommend the chilled lobster as it's a very refreshing/light dish to start the dinner. The Mon Blanc was sweeter than we'd like, but that was our only concern. Also came as complementary were the chicken fries before our appetizer, as well as chocolate and lemon macaroons to wrap things up. Unlike others with complementary desserts that always disappoints, these really shined, especially the lemon macaroon in which the flavor was a good balance against everything prior. 

Service was simply excellent, you get a lot of attention as they are over staffed. Oh, and the ambiance was really nice, love the chandelier, although I'd argue it's still on the louder end.  

While they have certainly raised prices if you reference the legacy menu, pricing at ~140/p is still a very good price point. Would recommend and would not disappoint, will return again.

Le Coucou has been on my list for some time now. I've heard lots of good things and have been looking forward to it. It is also notable this would be my first time having French cuisine (and yes, it was certainly a grand introduction to what French cuisine has to offer).

I came here with a party of 4 earlier in February. Most of my party were well versed in the French culinary dishes. What french cuisine excels most is the utilization of everything into their dish; the execution, presentation, and flavor is what defines it as one the of leading culinary inspirations in fine dining. Le Coucou definitely has met the criteria and worthy of their Michelin Star status. The service we received was outstanding and was expected of a Michelin star restaurant. There is an option to order prix fixe menu versus ala carte, and we chose the latter.

Our party was adventurous and decided to go for more traditional French dishes that I normally wouldn't have ordered:
- Quenelle de brochet (pike mousse)
- Foie gras poché au Sauternes (Foie gras)
- Ris de veau à l'estragon (Sweetbreads)
- Tout le lapin (All of the rabbit)
- Calamar en escabèche (grilled squid)
- Canette a l'orange (roasted ducklings)
Dessert: Pear Sorbet

I am not one to order foie gras, liver, hearts, and other organs from animal bits, let alone trying new meats such as rabbit, but I was open in trying it during this dinner for the experience. While I did not personally enjoy eating the parts itself, I did however appreciate the intricateness and refined techniques that went into every dish. Every dish had its own story and that made the experience much more unique. The tout le lapin is a classic dish utilizing every part of the rabbit in 3 different courses. I thought that was the highlight of the meal. 

The drinks here are very good and are not to be missed! I forgot what my first drink was but it was a hit! I ended up getting an espresso martini as my second drink and it was great. 

Overall; the service is outstanding and the staff are very knowledgeable about all the dishes. The quality and attention to details on the food itself is top notch. I myself, probably would not go out of my way to get the same dishes again (since it's a bit out of my comfort zone), but I would be interested in trying the other dishes they have here! Nevertheless, I respect the work and sweat put out by the wonderful staff and chefs at Le Coucou, and appreciate the experience!.

Le Coucou

Adventurous birthday meal at Le Coucou.  Stephan Starr's French eatery in Lower Manhattan. Rustic brick framed with chandeliers charmingly skied the
ceiling. It's old school French cooking. The sweetbread (p1) aka veal thymus, remind me of slightly firmer yet creamy version of foie gras. It also reminds me of brain. The fried eel was delicious with pungent vinaigrette salad. Lobster was perfectly cooked with round potato puffs. All the rabbit (3 ways), roulade with vinaigrettemeat stewed with turnip and vegetables rabbit soup  were hit and miss. Generous freebies:
mandelein, chocolate and macarons are wonderful. Will try the duck next time.

Unfairly, I compare all French restaurants to Trois Mec and Petit Trois in LA. So, that is my personal bias. 

We had a constructed salad and tuna for an appetizer. The salad vinaigrette was a little bitter and the portion size was very small. Think an inch size bite per diner. The tuna was excellent; fresh and dressed in a lightly tangy sauce. 

For dinner we ordered the lobster in a cream based sauce with some kind of Chou/puff. Everything was prepared perfectly. The lobster dish was a sizable portion, especially for the price. The puffs were good and had a creamy smooth interior texture but they lacked flavor, which required we dip them in the sauce for the lobster. There was an unfortunate amount of sauce to account for those who wanted to try it on the lobster and still dip their puff. 

I have to say the most disappointing part was the menu selection itself. There were a lot less offerings than I saw listed online. And the dishes that were on the menu did not offer enough diversity of options. 

*personal bias alert: French Onion soup should always be on the menu!! 

The service is absolutely five star. The staff is run on military precision, yet friendly and welcoming to patrons. They were truly the star of the show!!

delicious & ambient place with amazing service. this place is definitely on the pricier side but it makes sense considering the food & service. the fixed menu consists of hors d'oeuvres, entrees and salads (appetizers), gourmandises (medium sized plates), and les plats (the food food). we tried a few items on the fixed menu & the flavors were all pretty fabulous. and, the portion sizes were great--not too much and not too little! we left feeling full but having tried a lot of items.

the staff were super attentive and explained the dishes pretty well. we also really enjoyed the complimentary appetizers and desserts! also, the vibes were amazing and the lighting set the mood well. overall, this place was well worth the visit!

Food tastes mainly of oil and salt. Not much complexity or nuance,   To boot, something I ate clearly didn't agree with my system.

The check was delivered within minutes of dessert and without us asking for it. The mediocre food and rushed service do not befit the gorgeous setting nor the $50 an entree price point.
We were expecting a lot more in terms of taste and quality of food, given the Michelin star status. Would not go back again.

Everything was immaculate: food, service and ambience. The main course was served in deconstructed parts, which I thought was very different.
