While being here was an exciting experience, the food was incredibly expensive; be prepared to spend at least a couple hundred dollars per person. Also, dress nicely, because it's a very elegant, romantic space.

Great experience. Great service. We went for lunch. Awesome cocktails.  The steak tartare with caviar was so good. My husband had the sweet breads and I was so jealous after tasting. Highly recommend getting a reservation.

The atmosphere is good here but it never seems to end well, despite its pretensions. The touch of a beautiful, white taper would have been fine if the ventilation system had not blown its smoke at me until we had it removed. The food was good but not memorable and at these prices it needs to be memorable, the service needs to be perfect and it wasn't. We were amused by the chefs in the open kitchen in their call and response, for a while anyway. The interesting imbalance of acid on the leeks was a game try, a fine quenelle, the sweetbreads overshadowed by a lovely sauce, the three-way prepared rabbit meh, the (again) acid-forward sauce on the sea bream fine for the crayfish but not the bream, the Champagne (which we selected) showing more fruit than froth, the Kermit Lynch Chinon wonderful, the dessert wine and ananas roti meh. Good, but not great, and certainly not a good value.

The restaurant was beautiful with a romantic ambience at dinner time. What sticks out to me is the service which was top notch, and the food which highlighted flavors I didn't think could be highlighted--such as leeks! Would definitely recommend for a fine dining experience that doesn't feel too stuffy.

We had a terrific experience at lunch here yesterday.  We took the train in just for a special experience and Le Coucou did not disappoint.  I was in Paris last month and enjoyed a lot of delicious food, but missed the exceptional service that really makes a great meal memorable.  The staff at Le Coucou are warm, friendly, and extremely professional.  Having worked in restaurants, it's the mutual respect and sense of fun that makes a place top notch.  The food was fantastic.  The space is pretty, interesting, and comfortable.  The open kitchen is gorgeous.  Definitely worth a visit!

First of all sorry for my broken english.
i really like the environment and decoration, high ceilings, kind of modern but feel luxury, feel like you were in somewhere in europe. We book the reservation throught resy and we were sat by the window (love it good spot for instagram). The menu (lunch) has pretty limited but i guess it cover most of popular items. Service is quick and very attentive. We dtart with beef tatare and tuna, beef tatare is tender and has very good taste on it. I'm not the fan of caviar so we end up only order beef tatare by itself (i belived it $60 for additional caviar). Tuna( i'm so sorry i don't remember the names of the dish). For my taste it was ok not bad but not excellent. For the main dish we decide to have a duck( sorry again can't read french and have pretty broken english). The duck tights probably sous vide. It has the moise and soft. You can actually use only a fork to tear it apart. I feel like it too soft to my taste. The endice in duck plate is too bitter for me. We did the Chefs choice Le Coucou experience. We got to try 14 different items. The ambiance was beautiful, the service impeccable, and the food was great. The wonderful thing about doing it this way is that your bound to get things you love, you get to try dishes you might not otherwise, and you put 100 percent trust in the chef, giving him creative control. We had a wonderful evening. It's definitely a splurge at $195 a person. So, a once in a lifetime experience for me. Wonderful evening.
Food was mediocre, oysters terrible, service tried to pressure us on a bottle of wine, and everything was twice as expensive as it should have been.  Never again, this place is for fools.

I dined here once before in the year Le Coucou first opened (2016) and got a selfie with chef proprietor Daniel Rose, who I first heard about when he appeared on Ina Garten's Barefoot Contessa show on Food Network.  I've also dined at his now-closed tasting menu place in Paris, Spring.  Originally from the Chicago area, he lived in Paris for awhile before returning to the US, and has expanded his imprint here to include Cafe Basque in Los Angeles (where I've also dined) and Chicago.  His wife, chef Marie-Aude Rose runs the nearby La Mercerie (been there too) and has also appeared on Ina's show.  Le Coucou has a Michelin star.

The restaurant is elegant, high-ceilinged and spacious, open every day for lunch and dinner.  I booked a lunch reservation for this visit because I wanted to try the Vol-au-vent "Coucou" which is only offered at lunch.  The dish, sweetbreads and lobster in puff pastry with a cream sauce, did not disappoint, nor did my foie gras terrine starter.  My dessert, the tarte au citron, was a bit heavy on the cream topping.

A lovely, relaxing and fancy mid-day meal.

This is one of those meals that will stay with me for a long time. During my recent visit to New York, this was the top place I had eagerly wanted to try, and it certainly lived up to my expectations! It absolutely blew me away. LJ, our server, provided exceptional care, and finding the right words to describe him feels like likening him to Willy Wonka while I was Charlie, about to embark on a once-in-a-lifetime experience. From the beginning to the end, LJ took us on a whimsical culinary journey featuring delectable oysters, leeks, duck confit, and delightful cheeses. It's an invitation to step inside, have fun, indulge, and be lighthearted. LJ, thank you for an incredible evening. Le Coucou, I will dream of you until our next encounter.
The food was so, so good and despite small portions, very filling in the end. My table and I appreciated the complimentary dessert plate! Would definitely return!

Le Coucou was one of if not the best culinary experience I've ever had. My husband and I came for our anniversary.

Drinks - I had a glass of Syrah and my husband had a glass of Akul mezcal. I don't normally like the smokiness of mezcal but I enjoyed this one. The drink markup is insane however.

We decided to forgo the tasting menu and ordered a la cart.

We started with a complimentary amuse-bouche. The exact name escapes me but it was some sort of tartine with anchovy.

Then came sourdough and seaweed bread served with butter. So freshly baked, you could see the steam from the bread basket.

For appetizer we had the Thon à la portugaise (yellowfin tuna, Madeira vinaigrette with raisins). All the flavors came together so nicely with the vinaigrette. This light start was the perfect first plate.

For entrees, my husband ordered the Homard "Bourse et la Vie" (Maine lobster, sauce au poivre, pommes dauphine) and I ordered the Filet de boeuf, jus à la moelle, queue dans la boulangère (beef filet, bone marrow jus, oxtail potato). All impeccable. The oxtail potato was my favorite. Braised oxtail served in the center of a circle of soft, thin potato au gratin with crispy outsides. Like what?? On the lobster pepper sauce... so so good. I never had soft peppercorn like that.

For dessert we had the Mille-Feuille (vanilla cream and caramel, fleur de sel) which was honestly just ok but then they gave us complementary dessert bites that were just AMAZING. Mini lemon macarons, decadent bites of chocolate ganache and the cutest warm lemon madeleines. Just perfect. I only wished I'd ordered an espresso to go with it all. Simply amazing. It left a smile on my face. The perfect ending to the meal.

Service and ambiance (real candles at your table) was also outstanding.
An outstanding restaurant with talent, great ambience and meals. The service was outstanding, very European. One of the best places that we have been to in NYC.

We had an amazing dinner there on Tuesday night. On a Tuesday, every table was taken and we loved having a view of the kitchen which got really hopping as the night progressed. It was like a well orchestrated show with every station working so well together. I was so impressed.
We were intrigued by the notice of a Coucou dinner for $195 and asked . It was the tasting menu and the whole table went for that. It was very much worth it. We tasted so much food and every one was better than the last. My favorites were the Onion tart with black anchovies.. so yum.
The bass with the green tomato and crawfish and the Rhubarb buttermilk sorbet with lavender liquor and toasted buckwheat. What a great meal. 
Oh and what about the earl gray chocolates and lemon macarrons brought to all tables at the end.. so, so good!
Can't wait to go back.

Definitely a piece of France in the city.
Very classic french cuisine served in a very chilled atmosphere. Took our 10 years old son for his graduation, he loved it. Very nice cozy bar in case they are running late with your table.
One of our most favorite restaurant in NYC.

Le Coucou instantly came to mind when we decided to celebrate our wedding anniversary. We visited this upscale and sophisticated restaurant on one scorching July day to mark the occasion with a delightful dinner.

Upon arrival at our reserved time, we were promptly escorted to our table, which offered a captivating view of the open kitchen.

For dinner, there were two options available: a la carte or a set menu curated by Chef Daniel Rose. Opting for the latter, we entrusted the chef to guide us on a gastronomic journey.

To accompany our meal, we selected a nice bottle of French rosé. Shortly after, we were presented with four distinct amuse-bouche, accompanied by homemade bread and butter. It proved to be a lovely way to commence our dinner. This was followed by a series of appetizers, including four pieces of oysters, leeks with hazelnuts, and yellow tuna with Madeira vinaigrette.
Moving on to the second course, we savored the veal sweetbread with cream, tarragon, and Maitake mushrooms. This was then succeeded by an array of rabbit dishes as main course.

To bring our dining experience to a satisfying conclusion, we indulged in sherbet, which was followed by other delectable delicacies. From start to finish, we thoroughly enjoyed our dinner experience at Le Coucou. It was truly a worthwhile choice for celebrating such a significant occasion.

I recently had the opportunity to dine here at Le Coucou. The first thing I will say is that I was not paying because we ordered the tasting menu, and with wine, our bill was outrageous. I love food and don't mind paying for good food and service (spoiler - this was both), but I can't help but feel guilty when my bill is obnoxiously large. 
Le Coucou is in the Howard Hotel in SoHo on Lafayette in Manhattan. Definitely worth a visit. Great location and great ambiance and vibe. It has an open kitchen and it is known for modern French cuisine so I was very excited for my dining experience. The staff that greeted us were all super friendly and welcoming, and it was really fun to be able to see the kitchen in action. We had a seat right in front of all the action. Vibe/Ambiance= 5*
We started with a beet dish, some oysters, a soup, a leek dish and pike in oyster sauce. I loved the oysters (but it's hard to f* up something that nature made) and was surprised at how much I loved the leeks. They were so tasty. I loved the pike at first, but it was very dense and there was so much of it that as I continued eating it I started to not like it as much. It really could be a miniature size of itself and would be much better. I would not want to eat it again. It almost felt like a punishment. I did not finish it. 
Next we moved on to duck course series, which was pretty much a duck cooked every way possible; duck liver, duck a l'orange,  roasted duck. It was all delicious and well done. If you don't luck duck then this obviously is not for you. The deserts were perfect as well. Overall food was delicious but I would recommend ordered off the main menu vs the set meal. Food 5*
Our server was so attentive and friendly, loved everything about my dining experience. Service 5*

The halibut was very "vinegary". The 
Foie gras was good, but a bit too vinegary also and quite veiny. I don't like saying this but I must be honest. My favorite part of the dinner was the bread and butter. I thought. The restaurant is beautiful. The staff was pompous except for Abdoul. He was super sweet and attentive and did a large part of the service. I have had fois gras for $28 that was way tastier than this $58 fois gras.

OVERALL:
There is no question that you will have a superb culinary experience of incredibly difficult to nail French cuisine. They have an experience menus for $195 or you can choose from the full menu. 

VIBE:
It feels more casual than Le Bernardin, and the staff kind of go with the subdued tone in the more casual ambiance. Friendly, but I guess I expected more pride and seriousness.

THE HICCUP:
I was disappointed that I made reservations well in advance for a special occasion and they tried to seat us next to the entrance door that isn't even in the dining room. Absolut mon pas! We had to wait 40 minutes for a table that brought us into the restaurant that wasn't in a doorway right by the front of house podium. 

WHAT WE ATE:
I had RABBIT because I figured if I'm going to experience French cuisine adventures such as rodents then I decided to trusted this this to show me why the French eat rodents. They did a good job, came with a small fire show with the flambé and all. That was fine and thankfully never need to have a rodent again.

Friends has the Ris de veau à l'estragon (VEAL SWEETBREADS) - very difficult to make.

VERDICT:
Superb food. Nice service. I guess I just prefer a restaurant with more pride at these prices.

Service and Dining Room are definitely top notch! Worthy of a 3 Michelin star restaurant.  Sadly, food falls short of expectations.

Pros:
Bread basket and delicious butter! 
Danse thingamajig cocktail was nice
Fried eel thingy
Fried bread balls that came with the Maine Lobster.
Dessert was nice as well, great balance of sweetness! 

Cons:
Beef filet is okayyy, overpriced for 2 medallions of beef.
Oxtail blob was unremarkable
Sweet shrimp? If you can find any in a blob of yellow sauce...
Maine Lobster? Too small, but nice presentation.

We saw a nice lamb medallion dish with caviar being served to the table next to us, which looked amazing! When we attempted to order it, we were told the table next to us were "special guests," and that it wasn't available for us to order.  So, perhaps if you're a special guest, your food might be better than mines.

This is such an over the top fancy French restaurant with an open kitchen you can literally see the chefs cooking and plating with tweezers.
Don't get me wrong, everything was absolutely delicious.
It is a very well decorated inside with high ceilings and would make for an intimate place for dinner.
If you like modern French food and are looking to celebrate or impress, I would definitely recommend this place.  It is five stars and $$$$$ to match.

Incredible! From the start such a wonderful experience of service, food and wine. The half bottle menu was the most extensive of have seen so far in NYC and allowed a great pairing of the menu and wine selections. 

Next time, I will have the tasting menu. But for tonight we started with the tuna crudo, eel in buckwheat (HAVE THIS!!) ant sweetbreads.  Followed by the halibut and lamb saddle. 

Every bite was so delicious and uniquely prepared.

I will be back!!!!

A spectacular dining experience without much substance. Le Coucou is a sure bet for a special occasion dinner, if you have the ability to be cavalier about the steep price. Their French wines by the glass were iconic and delicious. I thought the choice of these single glass wines was the best part of the menu. The food took second place. The kitchen's take on the classic leeks vinaigrette with a bit of hazelnut crunch was fun for the first few bites but after that I missed the velvety poached feeling of a more traditional and simpler preparation. The duck with cherries that I shared was excellent, exactingly prepared with a dizzying amount of different textures and in terms of flavors very well balanced. Dessert was forgettable. 

The host, servers and bartender were all friendly and professional. The exquisitely decorated bar and the grand scale of the dining rooms are transporting. The single candle on the table got sillier and sillier as it proceeded to drip wax on the table cloth and get in the way of dishes. All in all, a big entertaining show that I have little interest in experiencing again.

I went to this delightful restaurant with two others a couple days ago celebrating a very late birthday. The service was friendly and the atmosphere is old-school from the rather dark lighting to the fancy large candles. They were professional giving good recommendations while still maintaining the fancy atmosphere. We were seat next to the open kitchen which was an unexpected delight. To drink I had the Danse Macabre for $20 which is "a clarification of rhum agricole, lime, lavender, earl grey, milk." This was essentially their fancy take on a milk punch though with rum instead of the usual bourbon. It wasn't overly sweet and it was quite tasty. I tried a bit of the La Bêtise which was $22 with French bitters, vermouth, and cremant de bourgogne. This was described as a take on a Sbagliato and it was bitter and refreshing and I likely would get that another time. After ordering, they gave us two types of bread; a darker loaf and a lighter loaf (both very tasty) along with some butter and as a free bite from the kichen consisting of very buttery bread topped with caramelized onions and a small black anchovy. It was a mix of sweet, salt, and rich flavors and it was quite delicious.

We got two appetizers to split among the three. The Poireaux Vinaigrette for $20 with leeks and hazelnuts was my preference of the two. The marinated leeks were soft and the vinaigrette was sour but not overly so. The toasted hazelnuts was a nice touch to this traditional dish and as per usual it was topped with some chopped parsley. The other appetizer was the Paté En Croute Tradition Bourgeoise for $31 with foie gras and sweetbread terrine and drunken apricot. En croute (or rather croûte) refers to it being cooked in a pastry shell. The pastry was lightly buttery and the filling was rich and tasty though I would say I tasted the foie more than the sweetbreads not that I'm complaining. The drunken apricot was interesting though I'm not sure of the alcohol and there was also some type of gelée which had a subtle flavor.

For my main dish, two of us split the Canette Montmorency for $129 or duckling with cherries, jus au cerises and chanterelles where canette refers to a duckling and Montmorency refers to a sour cherry varietal. This dish was presented in two forms with the duck breast being roasted and separated into two different portions with a couple cherries and a mushroom and then topped with the sauce at the table and the leg done confit style being in a larger presented dish with a thicker sauce and more of the cherries and mushrooms to be split. In the former dish, the duck was perfectly cooked and the sauce was lighter but still tasty. My preference of the two was definitely the duck confit. The sauce had a good sourness which paired perfectly well with the rich perfectly cooked duck leg. The cherries in that dish also were cooked a bit longer and were a bit softer. Overall outstanding and I have basically no complaints outside of it being pricey.

The other person in the party had the Agneau Languedocienne for $68 with lamb saddle, swiss chard and red rice, and tomate farcie. Tomate farcie prefers to a stuffed tomato and in this case it was stuffed with some of the lamb neck. I tried a bit of it though I avoided the roasted tomato and it was delicious. The actual lamb itself was also perfectly cooked and the portion size was large and honestly reasonable for the price paid. 

For dessert, I had the Marjolaine for $18 with hazelnut dacquoise and cream, and chocolate ganache topped with some gold leaf. The cake which is apparently traditional reminded me of some nut based cakes found in Central Europe being barely sweetened by the chocolate. The ganache and cream was soft and the hazelnuts were crunchy. It was a delightful mix of textures and is honestly one of my favorite desserts in recent memory. It was served with some ice cream (fresh milk?) in a separate container which was tasty.

They shared the Cherries Jubilée for the same price with black cherries, vanilla ice cream, and kirsch. The kirsch, a cherry liqueur is fired up at the table. Their dish also came with some ice cream (I believe vanilla.) The flames were smaller than at some some other restaurants but it's still nicely presented and compared to other places, I found the alcohol flavor stronger but otherwise I heavily preferred mine.

They gave us three free Macarons and Chocolate for my birthday which was very nice. The macarons I believe were a mix of vanilla and lemon and were sour and surprisingly refreshing with a good texture. The latter was definitely dark chocolate based being topped with some powdered chocolate and it was rich and tasty. Nice touch. They also gave us some Madeleines which I believe are given to other tables which had a good texture as well. 

It is rare for me to have zero complaints about a restaurant but I can't think of one. 4.9. Best meal in months.

PenCou Cou has good food but it is located on Lafayette Street in Tribeca and has NO connection with cabs.  My wife has had hip surgery an  Dr new taxied den form W44th Dr and we can't walk yet and we were turned out onto the street.  Restaurant is irresponsible and we won't taxi back.  Out of town visitors.
Lovely lunch here ---------- love salad and crab dumplings. Chicken is a little bit too salty.

I came here for a party, and it was beautifully decorated and had the ideal atmosphere. The tasting menu for the Le Coucou meal provides a thorough overview of what is available. I suggest the nicely prepared fillet with roasted oxtail potatoes, the pumpkin soup with leeks and hazelnuts, and these dishes. Some dishes like sea bass or yellow fin tuna are little common, but nothing substandard. Additionally excellent is the service.

The appetizers were a bit plain, but the meal got better as we went on. We tried the wagyu coulotte, which was juicy and tender, and the sauce complimented the dish spectacularly. The bone marrow was served separately with potatoes and paired very well. The sea bass with sweet shrimp was also cooked to perfection. For dessert, we tried the hazelnut cake, which we loved. However, service was not the best. This is a great place for a nice French dinner, but we probably won't come again.

What a major disappointment of a restaurant given all the social media hype. 

The singular positive out of this this dining experience was the ambiance. The space is romantic and elegant, but the service and food were equally disappointing.

One would expect seamless and attentive service at an elegant French bistro; however, it was extremely disjointed and apathetic.  We arrived to an empty restaurant and were jammed between two tables of four. On one side was family with two young children, who kept moving around like the yellow cabs in NYC; kicking our chairs and the parents could care less. The other table was occupied by two couples who seemed curious about why two men were dining in a romantic restaurant. I think they forgot they were in NYC, one of the most accepting cities in the world! They kept staring and smirking. At least we were more presentable and better dress but whatever. We asked to be moved were told no other tables were available, yet the restaurant was nearly empty at 6:30 pm. Yes, I'm sure the tables were reserved but it was not like anyone had preassigned seats. 

The plating of the meals left one wanting; haphazard and hardly elevated. I expected better! I reset mine to take these pictures. 

The flavors were off. The buckwheat fried crab was seeped in oil and had no flavors of crab. Looked like something from a frozen food section from a cheap
Supermarket. It was inedible. The seafood tasted like it was about to go bad. The duck breast was good, but inconsistently cooked. The texture was off and the confit leg was stringy and inedible.

What a rip off! What terrible service! What a disappointment!

Beautiful spot with rude sommelier/host (tall guy with messy hair in army boots) who lectured us on where to place our menus when we were ready to order. Honey, I eat at the best restaurants in the world and you only work in a mediocre one. Know how to talk to your guests!

Set a bad tone for rest of lunch. Took 20 minutes to get mock tails. Tuna appetizer was fine though eggplant purée unappetizing. Baby chicken nothing special, undercooked. Mille Feuille was best part of meal. 

Sat two of us at minuscule table when half of restaurant was empty. Moved us to larger table but then there was a smell of gas. A borderline disaster

We had dinner here to celebrate a friend's birthday and loved the interiors and decorations. Luckily we got window seats and a lovely small round table.

The seaweed sourdough is amazing! We had tuna and four gras to kick off tonight's dinner, tuna with the creaming sauce is very fresh. Foie gras is a cold jelly slice warp with pastry, a good balance between the sour acidic, and creamy crunch.

We order seabass and lobster for the second dish, these two are very classic French styles, honestly, we get more bread to finish the lobster sauce lol

The main dish we got was the rabbit, it came with a cold dish, a soup, and pan-fried dark meat. It is nice to share with 2-3 people.

The dessert was impressive and cute, we got a hazelnut chocolate cake, and my friend got an ice cream as a birthday gift. We wrapped this meal with mini mini-size of macaron and madeleine.

Overall it is a nice place with family, friends, or dates.

Ambience was lovely, but food wasn't as good as I expected from a Michelin starred restaurant. I've been to other one starred and French restaurants and the food at Le Coucou left me disappointed. Most of all, my friend did not enjoy the food and the service. I picked this place to impress my friend but it was the opposite. Some of the sauce were too sweet and it was best to eat the duck without it. The buckwheat fried eel dish wasn't good it had a strange burnt taste. The veggies in our dishes were also too sour like they were all pickled (though the leeks were not bad). We avoided the foie gras and the bread wasn't good too. The sea bass dish was probably the best one.

To start off with it is very expensive especially the wine list. Food I can except if it lives up to the price. We both had the quenelles which were delicious and have been a staple since they opened.  i've had the leeks which are also good but nothing special. For dinner we had the lobster au poivre and dover sole. both $80 entrees so yes I expect them to be great. The lobster was nice but a pound and a quarter at best and very skimpy. One claw was the size of my toe. the dover sole was swimming in butter and a total waste for a delicate fish.  Mediocre at best and do not order. $39 for a glass of chardonnay....a joke and obnoxious. I get the feeling this has become a tourist place so let them have it.
sauces were tasty. Services can be better. Lighting was dark. desserts were wonderful. Non-alcoholic drnks were good.

One of the best restaurant experiences I've had in a while. Stylish, upscale, comfortable, dimly lit.

The oysters were absolutely amazing, but the star belonged to the Tartare de boeuf. Such an amazing dish with the earthy meat flavor and ocean salt flavor from the caviar. Perfect combination.I could eat this a week straight.

 The service was great. Everyone there made sure my friends and I were having the best experience possible.

Had a great lunch at le coucou - dining room is upscale, service is very attentive but still friendly. love the open kitchen. food is done very well here, it feels a bit expensive but it's all good stuff, the freebies are great too (canape, bread service, mignardises).

Went with the beef tartare to start, which was solid but didn't hit all the notes for me. Good quality and texture, used to a bit more flavor but there's is pretty straightforward showcasing the beef. The sweetbread and lobster vol-a-vent was insanely good, would highly recommend that to anyone. Great filling, flaky puff pastry, addicting sauce that is rich but not overly so, the dish is very well balanced. Also ordered a side salad which comes lightly dressed and provides some good acidity for the other dishes. The chicken was also very well done - nice skin and good flavor, not at all dry.
Extended wine list however slightly overpriced. Great ambiance in a warm setting. The service was exceptional and everyone is happy to please.

A really lovely spot for a romantic date or intimate dinner with friends. Servers were attentive without being intrusive. We had an allergy and each waiter was informed and assured us when each dish was placed. 
There was a small chickpea starter and bread (regular and seaweed!). We also ordered the tuna and warm oysters. The oysters were not my favorite, I think I prefer them cold and light. I loved the tuna, there was a tangy sauce underneath that added some depth and flavor!
I would recommend the lobster! It was so buttery and just the right amount. It came with some bready puffs that were crispy on the outside and soft/moist inside. The halibut was also pretty good but felt like something you could get elsewhere. They brought some cold chocolates and soft fruit candies (Turkish delights?) as we waited for the check.
I'd recommend trying Le Cou Cou once if you live in NYC. It's a great spot to bring your parents or for a corporate card.
Such a beautiful restaurant with great food. Perfect for a romantic date. Service was good too.

We came here for dinner on Monday with a reservation. Le Coucou is a Michelin one star French restaurant. I like the decor and ambience. My favorite dish was the duckling for two. It's flavorful and one of their signature dishes.

You can never go wrong when you are in Le Coucou.  They have the best young chicken in the world.    Lobster salad is well prepared.  Service is great.  The restaurant is elegant and tranquil. It is so nice to spend my birthday there

*Bar review only* 

We stopped in for a drink because I'd read about Le Coucou, it's a very romantic ambience & you can tell they all take pride in what they do. The bar had comfy couches nearby for us to enjoy our drink & people watch.

Fantastic French cuisine with a bit of a show vis a vie the open kitchen. On the quiet side for lunch but you can hear everything in the kitchen if you are interested in a traditional brigade of chefs cooking. All of the dishes were carefully executed and presented. The halibut was outstanding and worth the trip alone. The steak frites were a rather small portion but wonderfully seasoned. Dessert was incredibly delicious. Service was attentive and prompt. Very good drink and cocktail service from the bar.

Service is a 5. Food is a 5. Ambiance is a 5+. My wife searched for "best romantic restaurants in Manhattan". This came up and deservedly so. It is expensive but so is your funeral so you can at least enjoy this party in your mouth.

Overall, Le Coucou shines with attentive, detail oriented service, incredible intimate / romantic ambiance and inventive and experimental cooking and presentation that would make for a wonderful night out with a special someone, however, one area where it feel short was taste. As I sat with a friend excited to be experiencing french cuisine for the first time since I was in France over a half decade ago, looking at the menu I thought, this meal can go either very well, or poorly given the combination choice of ingredient in many of the dishes on the dinner menu. Of all the dishes we tired, taste wise the shortbread dish was my favorite as it had an amazing sauce that I ate with the bread brought to the table. The tuna was also a nice dish. I wasn't impressed by the mussels and uni and think cooked uni in general doesn't work well. The venison was cooked perfectly, but also lacked flavor to accompany the wonderful presentation. Would be open to trying again to see if my taste buds could have a better experience.

What a beautiful Christmas dinner! Even though it took a little while to seat me, it didn't matter because the delicious food and great service, plus lovely ambiance more than made up for the wait. 
Highly recommend for a celebratory meal or for any occasion really.

Le Coucou is a French eatery that is brought to you by Chef Daniel Rose.  On our last visit to the city, we came here with a couple of friends for an early dinner.

We started off with the following to share as light bites:
+Huîtres 'Isigny' - warm oysters with camambert cream and spinach; the oysters did not fresh, and not sure how we felt about the temperature
+Salade de homard - with grilled lobster, mangalica ham, crisp lettuce, and a lightly creamed vinaigrette

We then tried the Quenelle de brochet, sauce américaine, served with pike mousse and lobster sauce.

Our entrees included:
+Homard 'Bourse et la Vie' - Maine lobster with sauce au poivre and pommes dauphine; the potatoes were a bit too soft, but the lobster was well-cooked
+Filet de sole meunière "Tradition" ou "aux huitres" - dover sole with golden butter, spinach, and without oysters (there is an option to add oysters); super buttery, so butter fans will enjoy this
+Filet de boeuf - with marrow bone, pommes puree 'noir et blanc', and sauce chateaubriand; this was not good; wasn't fan of the texture and how it was prepared
+Halibut, beurre blanc - with fermented daikon and an added kristal caviar; this was prepared well, but not a unique dish by any means

Service was attentive, and the restaurant was well-decorated; I liked the hanging light fixtures.

+attentive service

2nd time at le coucou now, for a birthday dinner. It used to be one of our favorite Michelin star restaurants in NYC. The ambiance is truly romantic with its candles and chandeliers; and I can see why it's rated one of the most romantic restaurants in NYC. The food has always been great. The Foie gras is one of my favorite and probably one of the best foie gras I have had (I get foie gras everywhere i go if they have it). 2nd time around though we did notice that it was a predominantly seafood restaurant lol...but either way all the food including steak and lamb were still amazing. The napoleon dessert was like the single best piece of dessert I have had in my life, although it seems like their dessert menu changes from time to time so not sure if it's always there. Service though was a bit lacking, our server was not very friendly or attentive so there's room for improvement with that. Overall would definitely go back!

The atmosphere is ambiguous, suitable for dates, the light is soft, easy to take pictures, the presentation is beautiful, and the food is normal and delicious.
The service is flawless. I would recommend everyone to order a hot and cold appetizer and main course. Girls don't need to eat it. Most dishes have very rich and thick sauces, and you will start to feel full after two bites.

Huîtres "Isigny"
warm oysters, camembert cream, spinach
isney oysters
Soaked in hot cream sauce, camembert is a bit heavy and smells faintly, so replacing it with brie will probably make it a bit fresher.

Quenelle de brochet, américaine sauce
pike mousse and lobster sauce
Pike fish mousse
Big chunks of lobster sauce Tofu, it doesn't have a particularly chewy texture, it's gone after just one sip.

Ris de veau à l'estragon
veal sweetbreads, cream, tarragon, maitake mushrooms
Tarragon Veal Thymus Maitake Mushroom
The small  glands are a bit like pig , served with super rich cream. The first bite is amazing, the second bite is delicious, and the next time you get tired of it. If you have more maitake mushrooms, you can eat a few more bites

Homard " bourse et la vie "
Maine lobster, sauce au poivre, pommes dauphine
"Delicious lobster"
It's just an ordinary Boston  with slightly spicy creamy pepper sauce, but the meat is plump and perfectly cooked, and even feels a little bit watery. Fried potato balls, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, but a bit oily

Marjolaine hazelnut chocolate cake
hazelnut dacquoise and cream, chocolate ganache
No fuss, normal and delicious , the ganache is very silky, there are a bit too many hazelnuts, it feels too full in the mouth after one bite

 Fleur d'Ananas
mezcal, pineapple, chili, campari, lime
Apart from the smoky smell, I don't taste much of anything else.
À La Folies-Bergère
armagnac, gentian(s), lemon, egg white
Sour and silky with a little bitterness of gentian wine

Le Coucou has been an instant hit and a classic from day one. Chef Daniel Rose is leading the kitchen when he is not in Paris tending to his restaurants there. While Libertine has had a lot of hype the last year, Le Coucou is the real deal. The beautiful room, food and service are all extraordinary. Highly recommended for a special occasion or just a Tuesday night dinner. Even though Anna Delvy is no longer a regular, Le Coucou is still very much the place to see and be seen.

I'm sorry to say that I found this to be a very disappointing meal - both in terms of the food and the service. It was my birthday, and my husband and I were in the city for work and pleasure. We decided to go here Saturday night to celebrate my birthday proper. Bottom line: I would never return, and I've told others (who commented on how pretty the restaurant looked from my few instagram posts) not to come here either.

First, the good - it's a beautiful restaurant. The bar is lovely and the restaurant as a whole is well decorated. Honestly, it was one of the most aesthetically appealing restaurants I've ever been to. And the cocktails and wine menu are very good. So bravo on all that.

Now, the bad - I think the easiest way to describe the experience is that this is a restaurant that strives to serve fine French cuisine without actually having ever eaten (or eaten often enough) good French cooking. True, the dishes looked like dishes one would eat in France but "looks" was where it stopped. It was like what someone thinks French food should be without actually tasting any of the food. We started with a few of the small plates. They were mostly good - the oysters and the yellowfin tuna. The yellowfin tuna was well done. Solid. But the oysters were sitting in so much camembert that you really couldn't taste anything else. It was essentially oysters Rockefeller with a ton of camembert. Then we ordered the chicken and foie gras as a next course. This was good. No complaints. Not amazing, but perfectly fine. We then moved on to the lobster dish. It was delicious but honestly it was just steamed lobster in a butter sauce. You can't really screw that up. Very good but not because of any real preparation. Things really went down hill with the duck. We ordered the Canette a l'orange (for two) at $129. This was a good example of a restaurant trying to be French (essentially, to make duck a l'orange) and making it look pretty on the plate but evidently never taking a bite to realize that it's bad. First there was a duck breast - so incredibly chewy from being cooked poorly. Also, it was very gamey. Now, of course, duck is a gamey meat. This is true. But a well-prepared duck breast will be paired with sauces and other accompaniments that blunt the gamey taste or weave together the gamey taste with other flavors that make it delicious. No such thing here. There was a very weak orange sauce and a cute little peeled orange on the side. That was the extent of the effort. Then, this was followed by a skillet with two of the duck quarters, set amid endives of various preparations. None of this worked. The duck was whatever (fine, not great) and the endives were so incredibly bitter. The duck and the bitter did not work together. Maybe they could have with a more skillful chef but this wasn't it. But, it looked beautiful in the skillet - again, pretty food that evidently no one tasted. We ordered two desserts (the caramel sabayon and another one that I can't even remember). The caramel sabayon was fine. Nothing to write home about, but competently done. The other dessert was forgettable.

As my husband and I were talking about the meal at the end, the head waiter saw us and walked over to take our plates and ask how things were. I couldn't help myself, so I shared with him some of my observations. He seemed baffled...not that he was surprised that I had negative remarks but more that I had remarks at all. He didn't seem to know at all how to respond. As an aside, our own waiter also wasn't very helpful. For example, at the beginning of the meal we asked him if there was anything in particular that he would recommend on the menu. His response (I kid you not): "I never recommend anything. It all depends on the kind of experience you want to have. Some of these dishes are very French while some are more general crowd pleasers)." I almost had to laugh but just politely thanked him.

For two people and for all these dishes and booze, it was not worth $680. This place is all show. Michelin really needs to revisit this selection.

Visited for 2024 NYE event. The place had so many street parking. It was very accessible with the public transit as well. The place was very welcoming and accommodating. They have a coat check if you need. Place was not too packed and was not too loud.
Food courses were great. They served total of 9 dishes. Absolutely loved the main dish; mushroom, foie gras and beef steak. Very juicy and flavorful. Very distinct layers. Although, i did not do wine pairing but wine recommended went very well with selection. Definitely, recommend to ask for the recommendations. 
Staffs and servers were very polite and accommodating. They constantly checked without interruptions. I thought this would also be a great place for a dinner/meeting. 
They also had various performances which I really enjoyed!
This experience definitely worth!

My husband and I dined at Le Coucou for lunch this past Sunday. It was our last meal after a 2-night trip to the city and the perfect lunch to finish off our food trip. We enjoy classic French dining, but what Le Coucou did to take French standards and elevate them to extremely fine dishes was superb. The bar is GORGEOUS, the dining room is beautiful (and I can imagine very bright with natural light when it isn't sleeting outside), and we were fortunate to have a perfect view of the open kitchen. The deep greens and golds that made up lots of the cabinetry and the pale green and copper that stood out throughout the rest of the kitchen was beautiful. Our gracious host, Roderick, helped make this an extra special meal, and we appreciated learning more about the restaurant through our conversation.

As for our meal, we enjoyed 3 apps to share and 2 entrees - we were very delicately warned that we might be ordering too much (he was not wrong at all!), but we were there to eat and up for the challenge. The fry-shaped fritters were a delightful little bite to start off with, and we followed that up with the starters - beef tartare, pate en croute, the eggs with foie cream. All sublime and a perfect size to share, but still feel satisfied like you got to try enough to really enjoy it. We like to share, so we picked a regular entree in the vol-au-vent, plus the "Coucou Classic" roasted duckling. The vol-au-vent consisted of PERFECT pastry wrapped around sweetbreads and lobster, while the roasted duck was prepared a l'orange with separate platings/garnishes of the duck breasts and legs. Only downside is that this has ruined our chance to enjoy duck a l'orange anywhere else... theirs was too perfect!

After our fantastic cocktails - including a perfectly-executed clarified cocktail, which I have to order whenever I see one - we finished the meal with petit fours and I got excited to see Ch d'Yquem by the ounce... which was the perfect finish to our meal. 5 stars!

Indulged in an exquisite 4 hour meal here. The upscale atmosphere, coupled with generously spaced tables, created the perfect setting for seamless conversation. Started with some expertly crafted cocktails - "Le Demode," a unique take on an old fashioned, and the delightful "Fleur d'Ananas," a mezcal concoction featuring pineapple, lime, and aperol (just the right amount of sweetness). Transitioning to a crisp bottle of white wine, we were treated to enticing start of bread, olive oil, and a complimentary chickpea French fry app ft. a sardine sauce. Indulged in very rich, but delectable appetizers, including the chicken foie gras, veal sweetbreads, and hazelnut leeks. The veal sweetbread emerged as a standout recommendation. Moving to mains... While the halibut proved too rich (probably because I over did it on the appetizers), the caviar triumphed. Would recommend the steak, but worth mentioning the bone marrow sauce's breadcrumb content for those GF. For dessert, we had the coupe-chocolate-cafe (vegan chocolate espresso gelato), the marjolaine (hazelnut dacquoise and cream, chocolate ganache) and they surprised us with a birthday special apple sauce gelato PLUS complementary dessert gelatin gummies. Accompanied by a 20-year tawny port, this dining experience was nothing short of extraordinary. Bonus points for the 100% gluten-free dessert options and adaptable mains. Take me back!

I was very impressed by the ambiance of the interior. The pictures of the lights / chandeliers and the long hall way doesn't do it justice. Very dimly lit, creating a romantic and intimate feeling. The bar at the entrance usually gets a lot of photo coverage. Hostess was friendly, and they have complimentary coatcheck before seating. But the food did not meet expectations unfortunately. The only thing I was super happy with was the dessert

I went out for a business dinner at Le Coucou and everything was amazing! The ambiance, the service, the food.. it was all so great. I had the sweetbread and the sole and very much recommend those dishes. My colleague tried the seasonal venison dish and loved it. The noise level is moderate but not noisy. If you're looking for a great French restaurant, I recommend Le Coucou!

Disappointing food experience here. Went last night. First they sat us in what had to be the second worst table overlooking the kitchen. Not sure if this was because the reservation suddenly appeared randomly midweek and was meant for walk-ins and they decided to put it up on Resy at the last minute or what but we already were off to a terrible start. I thought I had scored when I got the reservation but in hindsight I should've passed. 

Bad seats could've been rectified had the food been good. However, everything we had was below average for this supposed caliber of restaurant and I've been to all the top NYC restaurants (Le Bernardin, cafe boulud, Daniel, etc). Had the warm oysters to start. They did not taste fresh and did not work well with the Camembert on top at all. It was a sloppy mess with an overpowering cheese flavor. The fois gras and chicken app was ok but can't say that was good either. The main course of filet de boeuf was underwhelming and not worth the $75 price tag for two pieces of meat that basically tasted like beef roast I could've made myself at home. The bone marrow was ok but whatever they mixed it with, overpowered the natural marrow flavor. The lobster main course was overcooked and the sauce was nothing to rave about. Even the dessert we had--multilayered hazelnut with chocolate--was bad. All in all, disappointing. Not one dish was good. Definitely not worth the price tag or the hike to Chinatown.

An interesting experience, went with 2 old friends, we usually get together for beers but 1 picked this place. I looked at the prices, not realizing what this place was, and wondered what he was thinking! Turns out he was in the middle of making a $20M deal for selling an artist's music publishing and was feeling Diamond Jim Brady. Everything was twice the price you'd expect, but creative and delicious. After some appetizers, but before we ordered mains, the 3rd guy (who had just recovered from Covid) gets faint while heading to the bathroom and falls to the floor, unconscious. Ambulance called, we are outside, consoling him. Never ordered mains or dessert

A friend and I got of the waitlist for a Sunday evening dinner reservation. We arrived on time and after checking our coats at the front were taken straight to our candlelit table in front of the kitchen. It was pretty fun having a front row seat to all of the action! Service throughout the evening was outstanding and we were given recommendations when requested. I ordered the leeks and the venison and my friend ordered the sweetbreads and and the filet. My friend definitely placed the superior order. I found the leeks to be a little on the bland side and the venison was incredibly tough and a little bit gamey for my taste. The sweetbreads were perfectly cooked with wonderful flavor and the filet was tender and decadent. Perhaps I just made bad choices but I was a touch disappointed none the less. The restaurant has a cozy/romantic vibe and the service really is so incredible, overall still a worthwhile experience.

Where should I start..

The restaurant gives a good cozy, friendly vibe. That's for sure. They have free coat check service. After 6pm there is plenty of parking outside the area which is a plus. 

The staffs all seem friendly and nice. Our server is extremely friendly. Gave us recommendations and everything.

It's a French restaurant + Michelin star restaurant so I did had a high expectation. And the price they set on the menu is just ... idk. 

They first will serve the bread with butter, and the chick pea fries.. 4 pieces. lol. 

Then our appetizers came. Which was the Navets en guise d'escargots 49 turnip, mussel and sea urchin disguised as snail AND Crépinette de volaille au foie gras 35
chicken and foie gras, autumn fruit. It's ok. But really. Nothing special. The uni in my personal experience might not even be fresh too. It brings a slight fishy taste. Unlike the Japanese restaurant where it's creamy and sweet.

Main course. We got the Homard " bourse et la vie 
Maine lobster, sauce au poivre, pommes dauphine AND Filet de bœuf marrow bone, pommes purée "noir et blanc", sauce chateaubriand. That lobster was 80. That two pieces of filet 1/3 inch thick was 75. It's just sooo over priced. 

The only good thing I have to say for this restaurant is the servers , the atmosphere, the cozy vibe. 

There is another post that a customer burn her hair or something. At first I didn't believe it and thought it's BS. But after I been to the rest myself. Its true. All the table is very close to the next table. There ain't much space. My waiting was taking care of the table next to me, and he was so close to our candle and almost burned the back of his suit. I then grab the stupid candle and move it around the table for safety. 

Please please please either take that candle away and replace it with those batteries operated candles or just use light.. like the dimming light. OR! Get bigger tables. 

Overall, the food is just ok. Don't think I will be visiting again. Cause it really doesn't wow you. 

You ever been to restaurants where after dinner you would be like .. omg that dish was so good etc etc.? It's so sad I don't even recall how the bread taste was it's so little amount and it doesn't taste special.

Gorgeous dining room and elegant service are the two strongest elements of this fine dining establishment. The food is traditionally French and beautifully presented. A perfect place for a special occasion or date night.  We enjoyed our meals and topped off dessert with an espresso martini. I have recommended this place to others and their experiences were similar to ours.

this place is very warm and welcoming, but as for the food ,i was very disappointed as it is flavorless and portion are very greedy for the price for a non Michelin star restaurant,i have been to the most famous Starr group places and had a blast with the food ,but Coucou is not deserving this success

We absolutely loved our dinner at Le Coucou last night. The service was impeccable - very attentive and great recommendations. The space itself is beautiful and each table had a long stemmed candle. The food was French perfection - I don't think you could go wrong with a dish but I wouldn't miss the sweetbreads.
Great food.  Great service.   Pricey, but so good!  Our waiter brought us the most incredible bottle of wine which was delicious with our food.   Ambiance is very nice as well.

French restaurant with beautiful atmosphere.  Great service, candlelight dinner.  

Limited food choices.  Limited beef options.   Many options are lacking in flavor.  Butter used as substitute for flavor.  

Overall visit if on your bucket list, otherwise many better tasting choices in walking distance. 

Bob appetit.
One of the best restaurants in town.  It's our favorite restaurant for celebrating birthdays and anniversaries It's elegant and superb with equally fine dining.

Le Coucou is a wonderful French restaurant in NYC. Their impressive menu boasts lots of great flavors and textures.  The service here is stellar and the ambiance is always classy.  There are lots of fine dining options in the city but not all of them are worth the $$.  This fine establishment, however, is worth every penny (and calorie).
Amazing restaurant, top notch service, excellent wine selection with quiete and intimate ambiance.

Service and food was good, but the general manager is HORRIBLE!  I've never witnessed anyone handle a situation so badly in hospitality industry.  He brought the wrong bill to a table near us 4 times! And then he threatened to call the police on them because they were upset that he might have charged them multiple times.  Never NEVER go to le coucou. They should be ashamed of themselves. Horrible horrible restaurant.

Edit:
To address the response from the general manager below: that is a very one sided portrayal of what I saw.  I do not agree with the GM's characterization of his behavior. And at the end of the day the guest was pissed and it's the restaurants job to fix it and not escalate it.  I've seen annoyed guests many times in NY, I haven't often seen it handled so badly. Please don't believe this dumb letter. He's even handling my complaints badly too.  Litterally implied I'm lying and didn't even apologize to me for the scene.  Please find somewhere else to spend your hard earned dollars.
Another epic dinner at my favorite NYC French restaurant. Delicious food, excellent "service by Richard ", great cocktails and wine pairings making for a wonderful dinner experience

rude service, okay food. i dont get the hype here. its a very medicore level french food; there are so much better places that have kinder servers AND cheaper AND easier to get a reservation. when asked for wine recommendations, we didnt understand why the server was offended and so rude. the food also was not bad but so whatever. overall it was a waste of time and money

Took my bestie here for her Bday. Restaurant was elegant and airy, would be perfect for a romantic night out. Food was classic French with a little of modern touch. It's good but lacking a bit of wow factor in my opinion. What I love the most was the basket of mini madeleine served along the petit four. It was warm, fresh and bite size. Yum! Service was a little rushed at the beginning. Light appetizers were all out before we could take a bite of the bread and chickpea sticks.

Can't say enough great things about this place! Came here on a weekend for lunch to celebrate a special day and the service was top tier all around. It was a great balance of helpful without being overbearing. 

Food was incredible too. Everything we ordered was amazing including the wine and desserts. I personally thought the chicken was the best. Sometimes I find french dishes to start to feel heavy towards the end of the meal but did not feel that whatsoever here.

The ambiance was also super nice. Beautiful interior design and that bar when you first come in is very cute.

All around a great meal and great time - recommended!

We tried le Coucou for our anniversary dinner and were very impressed, particularly by the service and all the sauces. We stayed for 3 hours in a very well timed out dinner and never felt rushed. Staff was efficient and prompt while also being very friendly. The long candles at each table added a romantic touch.

We tried the sweetbreads, rabbit, halibut and chocolate dessert. All were delicious and we appreciated they split the dishes in half for each plate. The bread they gave at the start was also delicious!

Overall a great place to celebrate a memorable night.

Fabulous! From the beautiful ambience to the professional service topped off with delicious food this was a perfect evening. Thank you LeCouCou. Definitely will return. Special shoutout to the head pastry chef! The hazelnut chocolate dacquoise

Excellent fine dining experience that's worth the splurge. Service goes above and beyond for you, and no one is uptight or rude. What's interesting is that there's no music at all...the restaurant's environment is dependent on the customers happiness and chattiness. Each dish was executed superbly. The kitchen was able to split two entrees for both my friend and I to share since we were indecisive. The filet ended up being so good and tender that we ordered a second one! The duck is a classical French dish, but it ranked second after the beef. The leeks come off as boring on paper but ended up being zesty and crunchy. Pate was a classic and a good portion. Hazelnut/ganache dessert was good, but broke apart easily which made it annoying to eat. If you're the type to go for dessert somewhere else afterwards, do that instead!

Went here for an anniversary dinner. It was a real experience in gastronomy. Restaurant and ambience is first rate. Visually pleasing. Crowded early on a Saturday night but we got a table by the window with a candle on it. They were happy to suggest wines by the glass. We ordered five courses. First was fired monkfish. A delicate fry in a delicious sauce. Was awesome. Next up were leeks. A humble dish but OMG they were delicious and memorable. They sliced them lengthwise and they were so tender. Could eat them all day. Third was some sort of pike mousse it was gelitanous and quite good with the sauce. Wife had the beef and I had the halibut. Awesome. Halibut has a butter sauce and was cooked to perfection. Desert was chocolate cake for me and a tasty three cheese plate for the missus. It's not an everyday place but go for a memorable ocasion.
Can't say enough great things about Le Coucou. Tried it for my girlfriend's birthday and we were both super impressed. Fine dining at its best.

Visiting from Los Angeles and definitely glad I was able to experience a dinner here. Inside is a gorgeous dimly lit high-ceiling space that feels very welcoming. From start to finish the delivery of food and service was on point. The sommelier Roderick was very helpful with wine pairing/options for the table. Shortly after drinks, food was coursed out seamlessly and service from all staff very attentive.
Veal sweetbreads were my favorite dish and I'd definitely come back for them.

Thank you Ethan, Roderick, and Ben!

Le Coucou was recommended to us by a friend and we are so happy it was. It is a culinary gem nestled in the heart of New York City, offering an unparalleled dining experience that marries exquisite cuisine with an enchanting atmosphere. From the moment you step through the doors, you are transported to a bygone era of elegance and charm.

The interior design of Le Coucou is a testament to refined taste and sophistication. The restaurant's ambiance is both inviting and grand, with its high ceilings, soft lighting, and classic French decor creating a sense of timeless beauty. Every detail, from the elegant table settings to the plush seating, contributes to the restaurant's luxurious atmosphere.

The service at Le Coucou is nothing short of exceptional. The staff is attentive, knowledgeable, and always eager to cater to your every need. Our server, James, was great! From the moment you are seated to the moment you leave, you are made to feel like a valued guest, adding to the overall enjoyment of the dining experience.

Of course, the true star of the show at Le Coucou is the food. The menu, crafted by renowned chef Daniel Rose, is a celebration of French culinary tradition with a modern twist. Each dish is a work of art, both visually stunning and incredibly delicious. From the delicate seafood to the rich, hearty meats, every bite is a revelation, showcasing the skill and creativity of the kitchen. I definitely recommend the duck dish - outstanding!

Le Coucou is a culinary masterpiece that deserves every bit of its acclaim. Whether you are looking for a romantic evening out or simply want to indulge in the finest French cuisine, Le Coucou is sure to exceed your expectations.
Nice ambiance but food was just okay! Expensive for what it is. The salad was the best.

Overrated. Food is ok, not great, not bad. Portions are skimpy.

Service a little snooty. 

Atmosphere is best part, but not worth the price.

This restaurant was wonderful! My husband and I went here to celebrate our 10 year anniversary and it was the best celebration. We'd had our eye on this place for a while and just never pulled the trigger. The staff was lovely and accommodating and willing to help with suggestions. Everything we ate down to the table side bread was delicious and meticulously prepared. 

We started with one of their gin cocktails which is batch made and I don't love gin but I loved this! We got two foie gras appetizers, the pate one in the slice of bread and it was flavorful and incredibly nostalgic for both of us for two different reasons. It really exemplified the stories and memories food can provide you. The other foie gras dish was in a consume and while it was delicious when we go back I am not sure we will get it again. The star of our entire meal was the veal sweetbreads which were served in this incredible creamy sauce and topped with a shiitake  mushroom. My husband and I both agreed that if we go back this dish at wind up being either an entree for us both or we eat get our own because it was exquisite. For our entree my husband and I both got the whole rabbit which is prepared three ways and served all at once in three separate dishes at the table. Out of the three dishes The mustard onion rabbit was my favorite due to the flavor profile and I think also had the most rabbit meat which is like chicken but a little more gamey. For dessert we got the cheesecake which my husband was not super impressed with (but he's biased to his mom's cheesecake). I love it. It was light and fluffy and had these little baby strawberry looking like berries on top which were beautifully sweet. Throughout the they kept refilling our bread which was good because we had a lot of soupy liquid to scoop up with it. My husband also got multiple whisky cocktails and the Ice in the glass was so clear you couldn't even see it in the glass. 

This place was just all around wonderful. They do have 1 Michelin star and there were some minor things where you can understand why they don't have more than one, but the food was beautifully prepared and the wait staff was extremely attentive. We will definitely be coming her again, we just may need to give it some time to see if anything new hits the menu. 

Highly recommend especially for a celebratory occasion.

A Great french restaurant . We have now been to it the  four times in two years, when we come to New York from Florida.
A great interior, incredible food and a wonderful friendly staff.
The most amazing dinner we've ever had! Staff went above and beyond to make sure it was a memorable night! Absolutely stunning atmosphere!

Our meal at le cou cou was absolutely stunning. The food was beautiful and well thought out. The service was warm and professional. The interior felt grand and was one of the most elegant restaurants I've seen in New York. Including all the amuse bouche we ordered the leeks, fried monkfish, sweetbread, boeuf and lamb for 3 of us. The cocktails were excellent and the bar at the entrance of the restaurant is wonderful to start at before moving to your table. Highly recommend for a special occasion!
I thought the wine was good and the service was very good. I would definitely like to come back some time. The rabbit was a unique dish and I thought the Dover sole was my favorite.
Fantastic cuisine and wine service. Our Sommelier Dylan was spectacular. Dining room- gorgeous.

For the price not worth it. Service was just okay and same with the food. Got the halibut with caviar for $120 and it was super measly and drenched in a cream sauce that was way to overpowering for the delicate fish and caviar. Wine selection also very meh. Ambiance is still nice.

Food was just okay but the service was horrendous.
2 people in my party are drinkers, I am not.  They ordered A LOT of alcohol, 12-14 drinks I believe and each time their drinks came out immediately.
I ordered two non-alcoholic drinks and BOTH TIMES I WAITED 20 MINUTES FOR MY DRINK and had to ask for it 3-4 times!  This is so rude, unprofessional and blatant disregard for your customer as you clearly just want to increase the $$$$ alcohol sales!!  In fact one of our party was late and they wouldn't let us order food, only drinks, not even one appetizer.  Another ploy to increase their drink sales.
This was a birthday dinner.  The reservation specified it, I reminded them when I came in and actually the birthday boy told them when he came in too, bc that's how he rolls.  I reminded them right before we ordered dessert and when they brought it out - nothing.  I said something and they take it back then put a candle on it.  We literally told them FOUR times and they couldn't get it right.

Additionally, they took my food away before I was finished TWICE.

THE ONLY THING THEY CARE ABOUT IS $$$$$ AND NOT A QUALITY EXPERIENCE.  I would never go here again and 0/10 DO NOT RECOMMEND.

The service here was amazing and it had really good ambience! I would definitely recommend going here for a nice date night. My favorite item was definitely the duck and they prepare the sauce on the plate for you. For the other two food items I posted I would say that they were all right and you could go without those items. The highlight of this place is definitely the service to make sure that our water cup and drinks were never low and we're constantly asking if we need anything else.

A stunning French restaurant exuding charm and elegance. The ambiance blends classic French decor with timeless beauty. The food was exquisitely prepared, and the staff were attentive and knowledgeable, offering a modern twist on French culinary traditions. Visually stunning and delicious, each dish showcased creative flair.

Couldn't give a review, wish I could...  Made a reservation for 4 for my daughter's birthday a week in advance, even had the restaurant call to confirm the very same day of the reservation... When we got there on time, we still were made to wait for over half an hour...  so we decided to head out to some place else.  When we were already out of the restaurant THEN somebody approached us.
It seems that they were waiting for a 'big table' to get done.
I wonder what would had happened if we would have been 15 minutes late.
Expérience terrible.

Elevated French food is not what I typically go for, but I enjoyed it more than I expected. We stopped by for a weekday lunch and ordered the two course lunch menu and added dessert. The waiter was super knowledgeable about the menu and was able to walk us through everything, and the ambiance is elegant and peaceful.

I ordered the pate en croute, which turned out to be a meat pie (sweetbread and foie gras) wrapped in hot water crust pastry. Definitely a heavy dish but I really liked it. I also got their duck breast with gibolette (stew of other meats) which they plate with the duck and leave the rest on the side if you want more. I personally wasn't a huge fan of the dried apricots in the dish but I love duck and this was a great preparation of it. Finally for dessert I got the Marjolaine after seeing photos of it on yelp, which is a layered chocolate/hazlenut cake which comes with a with a side of ice cream on a bed of crushed hazelnuts (forgot what kind of ice cream it was but remember thinking it was delicious). At the end they also bring out complimentary yuzu macarons and little jellies, which was a nice touch.

Overall a great fine dining experience, would definitely recommend coming here (which is saying a lot for someone who's not a huge fan of French food).

Came here for an anniversary dinner, and they had prepared written celebratory messages for us :) The place was dim-lit and romantic. 

Service was spectacular! We asked our waiter what he recommended and he described his favorites, and also considered that we'll share dishes (so they served the dishes in two plates for us). Staff also described each dish to us, describing how it was cooked.

The food presentation was amazing, it really felt like fine dining.  We were full by the end of the meal. We ordered 6 food items, and they also gave us bread. My favorite was the veal and Vacherin aux myrtilles!

Le Coucou was delightful. This restaurant gives the feeling of a location who is not fighting for Micheline stars, allowing them to just focus on good food and amazing service. 

The venue itself was beautiful and had the perfect level of noise without seeming too loud but also creating a really vibrant energy. The service was exemplary. We were treated with kindness and respect whilst still allowing for honest and personal interactions. We were guided through the menu and offered suggestions. Our sommelier was very engaging and knowledgeable and offered us great suggestions. The wine options at this location are extensive and expensive. So be ready to spend $100-300 a bottle. 

The food:
My partner and I ordered everything with the intention of sharing. 

To start: Thon à l'espelette and Galantine de pintade et foie gras à la chartreuse 
Gourmandises: Quenelle de brochet, sauce américaine and Ris de veau à l'estragon
Main: Filet de sole meunière "Tradition" ou "aux huitres" 
Dessert: Tarte au Chocolat 

The amount of food we ordered was perfect for us as we left very full and satisfied. We tried to balance our ordering to allow for a nice balance of heavier and richer dishes with some light and refreshing options. My main critique would be that the food options available made this goal a little hard as most options veered towards the richer side. However every dish was presented well and very tasty. 

The Galantine and the Tarte au Chocolate were my favorite courses of the night. The rest were yummy but not something I would order again. 

Overall I had a wonderful night, it was refreshing to be in a 'fancy' restaurant with no pretension but extreme professionalism and dedication to service.

Came here again for my birthday dinner. And decided to put up some reviews. The food is good as always. They changed the menu from my last visit. That's made me excited to come back for more. Service was elegant. Nice spot for a dinner date

Nice ambience our waiter James was great but tuna scallop Crudo was delicious my Dover soul although expensive was right on point but 80$ wines were delicious but like everything else in this restaurant overpriced expect to pay $30-$40 for a glass of wine. The duck was OK nothing exceptional. It's unfortunately too pricey for what they give you in my opinion but if you want a great Dover, so don't mind the price tag it's a great munch.

We had the chance to visit Chef Danie Rose's place in Paris (La Bourse et La Vie) earlier this year and had the great good fortune to meet Chef Rose at the restaurant while we were dining. We had such a lovely experience there that we knew there was no place we wanted to celebrate my 60th birthday in my hometown other than Le Coucou.

The vibe is definitely French, but with a New York accent. The room is gorgeous and dimly lit, with very high ceilings. In a town full of restaurants that you can't hear yourself without screaming, Le Coucou is an oasis. 

Even if they didn't serve food, I'd have to tell you that it was some of the best restaurant service I've ever experienced. The servers were professional, and kind, but not punctilious, and they had a knack for knowing exactly when to come by the table, and when to let us just savor the experience. 

The wine list is a mile wide, and several miles deep. If you can't find something you want on that list, you may wish to consider switching to beer :-)

The wine by the Glass list is small, but well chosen. As we had come off a celebration the night before where many prize bottles were opened, we ordered off the Glass list. We ordered a really lovely Merseault, and a fabulous French Chablis, both of which really well complemented the food.

As it was my birthday, the front of the house staff went above and beyond to make it feel special. Every table is lit with an honest to goodness real life taper. In front of ours was a lovely card memorializing my birthday. 

The back of the house staff treated us very well. The chef sent several complementary appetizers to us, in addition to the ones we ordered. A particular highlight was the tuna and scallop Crudo that was one of the best raw fish dishes I can recall eating. The scallop was like "buttah".

We started with leeks vinaigrette, which we enjoyed so much in Paris. It's an incredibly simple dish, but perfectly executed at this place, with the addition chopped toasted hazelnuts giving it a fantastic texture. We also ordered the foie gras torchon, because, well, foie gras.

The chef sent us an additional foie gras app, this time served with Chantrelle mushrooms in an amazing broth that I think might've had a little bit of miso in it. I could've had gallons of the stuff :-)

For our main, we chose the roasted duck breast, and the lobster. The duck was perfectly cooked, the skin rendered and crisp, and served with a sauce of apricot, and what they called "the rest of the duck" . In a copper pot on the side of the plate rested the most delectable bits of crispy, dark duck meat, swimming in the apricot sauce. It was divine.

The lobster was a thing of beauty. It was served shelled on a plateful of what I swore was the steak frites sauce that we had in Paris. The sauce was amazing with the sweet, perfectly cooked lobster meat. That sauce was also perfect for dipping the bites of soufflé potatoes that they served with the lobster. Imagine tiny, crispy potato flour popovers, and you're halfway there to experiencing them.

Dessert was a chocolate marjolaine, and assorted mignardises from the pastry chef. It was spectacular with the drip coffee which was a cup of heaven. 

It's not the cheapest restaurant I've ever eaten in, but I think that the price was a great value for the quality of the food, and the wonderful atmosphere and service. Plus, it's in New York City, and things just tend to just cost a little more "the big city"

Highest recommendation for an amazing French meal in my hometown. Bravo, Chef Rose and team!!

We went to le Coucou on a for a new york city food experience and it did not disappoint, I think it was worth the price. The service was great , we went there for lunch and they had a prix fix menu or you could order a la carte. For appetizers we ordered the leeks which were their suggestion and superb, and ordered 2 main courses which told them that we wanted to share, they brought us each dish divided in 2 separate plates, for each and separately so as not to mix the tastes. The wine was also superb, although a bit more on the pricy side. The ambience was good and quiet, and the waiters would pay attention to the smallest details

We tried this restaurant on August 17, 2024 because it was recommended by a good friend, had a one star Michelin rating, and was part of the fabulous Starr Restaurant Group. The atmosphere was great, as was the service from our waiter and the manager.
Unfortunately, the food did not measure up. 
   
I ordered three courses: tomato salad appetizer, veal sweetbreads and duck. I couldn't stand the sweetbreads and didn't eat half of them. The duck was just ok and far inferior to the duck at Buddakan, another Starr restaurant. Only the tomato tonnato salad was very good. My wife ordered steamed black bass which she disliked so much that she sent it back, which she hasn't done at any restaurant in at least five years. They replaced it with halibut that she also disliked so she ate a few bites and then we left without even ordering desert. We love dining at other Starr restaurants such as Buddakan, Pastis and   
El Vez, but we have no intention of returning to Le Coucou.

The entire experience was perfect starting with the atmosphere and open kitchen. Service was exceptional and the entire staff had extensive knowledge and training that did not go unnoticed. We had the pike mousse, foie and chicken crepinette, duck, the filet, and the tarte au chocolate for dessert. All were excellent and on par with the Michelin rating. The wine selection and suggestions from sommelier and staff were also wonderful. Will definitely be back on our next trip to the city.

Decent French food, though underwhelming given their star and service that also did not match their accolades. I ordered the oyster apps and halibut, both of which were a bit overcooked. The oyster was forgettable, lacking depth, and paled in comparison to the Le Pavillon version. The halibut was overcooked to the point where the fish was slightly rubbery and the sauce was the most basic tasting cream sauce with no exciting / new elements to it. 

Ambience was decent, with lit candles at each table; however service was on par with any random restaurant I'd walk into in NYC. They confused a Happy Anniversary with Happy Birthday and waiter was not very helpful in
providing descriptions / input into dish selection. Dish presentation at the table (e.g., pouring sauce onto the foods and adding heart to the duck) was also subpar, with one of the waiters clearly providing advice to another after the fact. Sauce and food was added ad hoc. Busboys were attentive though and waited always remained filled. +1 star for them.

Le Coucou is a textbook example of why I blindly trust the Michelin guide

I was at the Jersey Shore on vacation and felt really ... bored by the dining scene there. I also, last minute, took a Frontier flight up from Atlanta and was positive I wasn't going to make it past the E gates at Hartsfield Jackson after using the remaining points from my grad school days. 

Anyways, I figured I would continue my cheap blind luck and use NJT's "transit holiday" to go into manhattan for a few hours and try out a new 1 star spot that I haven't been to.
