Le Coucou showed up as having lunch availability 24 hours before my haphazard and impromptu trip into the city so I booked it. A $69 prix fixe is a good deal for fine dining in Manhattan, and my pseudo-materialistic obsession with claiming yet another star was exciting to me at a bare minimum. 

I'd describe Le Coucou as traditional French with a modernist twist. I decided to get the galantine as my first course and it was absolutely incredible. The course was a perfect example of creating your own experience with every single bite, due to the variety of ingredients in the galantine itself and the "green ring" that surrounded it. I decided to spend an extra $14 to get the duck course and it was worth every penny. Another example of a beautifully plated entree that is firmly planted in French roots yet allows a diner to experience the dish in an infinite number of ways. I was in what I affectionately refer to as "duck organ heaven". Seriously, everything was delicious. 

I also had 4 drinks there. Don't skip on their wine menu because they have some unique bottles that are downright impossible to get elsewhere in NYC. I was especially impressed with the dessert wine selection and ingenuity that went into crafting that menu and being able to source those selections. 

Le Coucou - I'll be back for dinner sometime soon!! I apologize for my shitty planning - but I'm glad the low tier combo of Frontier and NJT got me to your restaurant. Next time I'm up, I'll surely be on a United flight, will be staying at my usual spot on the Upper West Side, and will book well in advance because I know I'll make it. In the meantime, thanks for satisfying my palate with this impulsive lunch.

Ok, wow. This meal was superb in every meaning of the word. Perfect wine pairings and fantastic dish suggestions.

You must get the scallop starter and you must get the duck main. We were in love with the dishes and our waiter made the experience just so much fun. 

If we are ever back in NY, we will be back.

What a fabulous dining experience. The service was exceptional, everyone who was responsible for taking care of us, did an amazing service. Top notch! They started us with some seaweed bread, so delicious! Next we ordered an oyster appetizer which was so flavorful. The next dish was an order of veal sweet breads and it was so delicious. It was served with an amazing sauce, once we finished we were able to use the bread to dip in the sauce. For our entrees I had the filet de boeuf which was a piece of bone marrow with beef which was cooked perfectly. It was served with the creamiest of mashed potatoes. What an amazing dish. My girlfriend ordered the rabbit and she loved it. It was prepared 3 different ways and she loved it. The ambiance was amazing, a really nice restaurant.  I highly recommend this place but make sure you make a reservation.

I have a severe gluten, oat, and dairy allergy. I have contacted multiple Michelin star restaurants ~2 months ahead of time to find one that can accommodate my dietary restrictions, and out of the few that could my partner and I decided to choose this restaurant. I reiterated my dietary needs when creating the reservation, over the phone before arriving (at most 2 days prior), and again on arrival.

1) Service was extremely slow. We got our drinks after about 10 minutes of ordering which is fine, but it took over 30 minutes to get a waiter to take our order. Water refills also took some time.

2) The food took almost an hour after getting seated at the restaurant. They acknowledged that the kitchen was behind and I didn't mind waiting since they also had to cater around my allergies, but I was a bit frustrated that it took a lot longer than expected.

3) A few minutes after eating the second dish served, I experienced minor to moderate issues with my body that I only get when I come into contact with gluten and oats (cross contamination). My partner had to cancel the rest of the dishes that we had planned to eat and informed the manager of what was going on. We still had to pay for the dish that gave me issues and had to sit at the table awkwardly while my body could heal enough for us to walk out and Uber back to the hotel.

Overall, I would not recommend anyone with serious allergies to eat at this location. I expected more out of a Michelin star restaurant, but I guess they were too busy to acknowledge their guests needs.

The room and service were mostly outstanding. Our server was outstanding, knowledgeable about the menu and serving size. The server for the table next to us was borderline rude. We split the monkfish hor d'oeurvre. It was very good. I had poached fois gras in Sauternes for my second. The liver was very good. But the broth had a little too much of an alcohol taste. For my main I had the veal chop. This fell very short of my expectations. The meat not so tender. The presentation was bad almost caveman like. Dessert was outstanding, as you would expect in a French restaurant.

This is really a wonderful restaurant with a wonderful dining experience. The food is excellent, the service is great and overall everyone was friendly and helpful. Food portions were a little big but we are older and feel guilty of leaving just great food remaining.  A very special
Place.

I visited for lunch on a weekday with my friend who is gluten-free, and the service was excellent--they were very attentive in making sure we knew which items were gluten-free and which weren't. The lunch menu they offered was 2-course for $69. We ordered the Thon à l'espelette (yellowfin tuna and scallop crudo), Avocat crevette (organic avocado with shrimp and French cocktail sauce), Canette aux abricot (+$18, duck breast with apricots and chanterelles), and Vol-au-vent Coucou (sweetbreads, lobster, mushrooms, vermouth cream with tomato, and pâte feuilleté). Honestly, every dish was fantastic, but the two mains we had were absolutely phenomenal.

The interior was stunning, and we had fun snapping lots of pictures. I'd definitely come back again to try their dinner menu!

I would give Le Coucou 100 stars if I could! One of my absolute favorite restaurants in Manhattan. The restaurant is a beautiful and tucked away behind a wall of greenery. You walk in to see the most stunning bar and can grab a delicious handcrafted cocktail. 

The service here is top notch as well. Attentive and knowledgeable servers, plus a world class sommelier. 

Starters
- Poireaux Vinaigrette (delicious, a bit simple so I would maybe skip and try something else)
- Thon à l'espelette (fish was very fresh and high quality, fantastic)
- Tartare de boeuf (one of the best beef tartares I've had in America, MUST TRY!)

The Homard (Maine lobster) is one of the most incredible dishes I've ever had the pleasure of seeing and tasting. Delicate and tender lobster paired with a decadent peppercorn sauce and fluffy fried potatoes... something I dream about every night. 

The Filet de boeuf is also phenomenally well done. Can't even describe how much I like this dish.

For dessert, you absolutely have to get the Marjolaine. On top of being such an amazing restaurant, they also seem to run a top tier patisserie to create masterpieces such as the Marjolaine and Tarte au Chocolat.

The tiny bar is one of the most beautiful I've seen in NYC. But they can't make an old fashioned. That's very Frenchie. What isn't is the service. I arrived early and was asked if I'd like to wait in the bar for my date. I checked my coat and sat down. About five minutes later a man came up to me and asked me with great annoyance if I needed assistance. As if I'd walked off the street. This is not French. Good service entails good communication between employees. Instead of informing this dude that I was waiting for my date, nobody said anything to him and he treated me like I was a vagrant. 
There is no heart in Le Coucou. Servers have been taught to pronounce French words, but the effect makes them look and sound ridiculous, and demeans them. They offer no suggestions for glasses of wine paired with each dish. I may as well have been at McDonalds. 
The sweetbreads were okay, but way too much liquid. No balance in that dish. The filet was truly fantastic, but not worth a return visit. 
It's telling to go to an expensive French restaurant that has no French people working there. It's not really French. It's like AI followed the rules but made everything mundane. 
Gorgeous pillows in the bar, though!

While in NY, I made a reservation for what some say is the best French restaurant in the city. Le Coucou. Upon entering I really loved the rustic interior and was warmly greeted and my coat taken. The wine last was INCREDIBLE. Absolutely extensive and stunning. We started with a glass of Cremant and were served some delicious warm bread with butter. I started with the Galentine de Pintade et foie gras a La Chartreuse. Absolutely lovely. 10/10. My entree was the Canette aux abricot. Incredible. 20/10. I ended the meal with the sorbet. 10/10. Le Cou Cou should be on your list of must try restaurants when in the city. I can't wait to make a return trip.

Went for my sister's birthday and it was a great experience. Restaurant is beautiful, although I wish the lighting was a little brighter (especially in the bathrooms, it is DARK in there). Service was impeccable and I really liked our sommelier, who was clearly passionate about the food/wine and very helpful with recommendations. Starter bread is delicious, esp the sourdough (perfect crust and so light and springy on the inside). We tried the sweetbreads at our servers recommendation; first time having it and although I liked the sauce and could tell it was well-prepared, not sure it's quite for me (but then I've never been a fan of organ meat). Cheesy oysters were good  (warm, cheesy oysters are always good honestly) but didn't particularly stand out to me. Ordered the lobster for my main, which was perfectly cooked, but I think the stand out entree for the night was my sister's duck. Desserts were yummy (hazelnut chocolate cake and this pineapple rum cake) but honestly I think my favorite was the complementary chocolates (soooo smooth) and mini yuzu macarons.

We had a wonderful dining experience on a Thursday evening. My spouse started with the Poireaux vinaigrette (leeks with hazelnuts), followed by Côte de veau gratinée aux cèpes (veal chop with porcini). I had Lotte frite au sarrasin (buckwheat fried monkfish), followed by Filet de boeuf. Everything was absolutely memorable, especially the monkfish. We followed this with baba au rhum and a Tourtière Landaise aux Pruneaux, which were both extremely creative. Service was top notch, warm and friendly from the moment we walked in. The atmosphere classy, but not stuff. We will return.

I was on vacay and wanted to have a nice lunch. Luckily the boys were down to come here, so I made a last min reservation that morning. One in our party was super late, but the staff was understanding. We ended up ordering without him since we kinda share everything anyways. Family style all the way!

A fav among everyone was the beef filet - cooked perfectly. And the bone marrow made it that much more decadent. The fries of course were a hit as well. My group celebrates frydays quite frequently. I enjoyed the asparagus as it came with sea urchin cream. Added a nice umami flavor. I hadn't had sweetbreads in a while, so the vol-au-vent coucou was a treat. The added lobster was tender and a good complement puff pastry. The complimentary bread and butter were chewy and creamy. The bread and butter at French restaurants are typically extra delish. That was definitely the case here. After the meal, they gave us some petit fours / mignardises. Cocktails were a nice way to start off our meal. My manhattan was spirit forward but still nicely balance.

Le Coucou had 1 michelin star when we went and it still has it now. Definitely worth a try if you are a lover or French food. Lunch was a nice way to sample a variety of dishes without committing to dinner portions.

REVIEW #3637

My father, sister and I came here for our only annual "fancy meal" and -oh my goodness- they treated us like absolute royalty!!  Intimate, classy, and not stuffy atmosphere, we talked about how divine the food was for the rest of the night.  The layers of flavor and texture, the beautiful presentation, and the kindness and professionalism of the servers, Isaac and Francisco were the names we remember, but the whole team went above and beyond to make our dream holiday meal come true. A special memory we'll keep forever!

Le Coucou is well deserving of its Michelin Star. The French restaurant downtown delivers on high quality French dishes and is not a tasting menu like many similar spots.

The restaurant itself is beautiful, an elegant dining room with an open kitchen. The service is top notch and some of the best in the city.

Food wise everything was excellent we had;

Tartare de bouef - prime filet beef topped with caviar. Excellent albeit small portion for the price.

Foie Gras Grille - grilled foie gras that was absolutely incredible. Must order if you like foie gras.

Homard Bourse et la Vie - succulent lobster on top of a au poivre sauce, phenomenal.

Canette aux abricots - perfectly cooked duck breast packing flavor. Some of the duck is also served in a type of stew that was also excellent.

3 Cheese selection - we opted for dealers choice and each selection was great.

If you're looking for a special occasion restaurant without the need for a tasting menu  Le Coucou is it.

We visited Le Coucou for the first time with very high expectations. Unfortunately, the experience was not a perfect fit. We arrived and were greeted well, taking our coats and asked to sit at a small table to wait for our table. After offering us a drink menu, the bartender seemed preoccupied and we didn't have a chance to order before leaving for our table. Led to the kitchen area, we were seated at a round table facing the kitchen. Since this was essentially "date night" for us, eating in the kitchen wasn't interesting at all. Fortunately, when we asked to move, the staff was very accommodating. Service was excellent overall but actually somewhat intrusive. Everyone generally knows what kinds of foods they like and don't. However, when ordering, I felt the staff attempting to sway my choices rather than just providing education. At one point, I felt shamed for choosing the Sancere over the Chardonnay... only to prove myself correct, for my palate, after tasting both. My husband found the rabbit to be absolutely delicious. My duck breast was very good but certainly not the best I've had. Once finished, it took extra effort to locate our server to settle our bill. Frankly, we've had better experiences in Manhattan, Michelin star or not.
Yum! You can't go wrong here. Enjoy food here like you have a day left to live! haha.

Chose this restaurant for our Christmas dinner based on reviews. The ambiance & service were first class!  That said the table next to us turned over twice during our 3.5 hour dining experience. Wasn't sure if they were letting us enjoy the experience or just forgot about us. 
The food. Well, this is where it lost stars for us. It was a set menu for the day (7 courses). The best course was the palette cleansing orange sorbet. Each dish was beautifully presented but looks outweighed taste. Most dishes were bland. The caviar was tasteless. Another reviewer stated that it was like they were trying too hard. We would agree. Perhaps the regular menu provides more flavor but overall we expected to leave with find memories of the food yet can't recall anything memorable. 

Ohhh and then the wine list-average bottle was around $1200. Very few bottles under $200. So stick to cocktails!
Amazing meal. Worth the visit!! Incredible meal and incredible service. I can't recommend this restaurant highly enough!

very cute place for a dinner.  great 'party of 4' restaurant i think.  the ambience was great and the food is delicous.  definitely a trendy place to hit up and worth checking out if you are around the area and want to try a trendy place near chinatown.

One of the best dining experiences I've had in a long time! Went for the 2 course lunch and at $69 it is a steal! The $23 lobster add on was to die for as was the flat iron steak. The shrimp and avocado appetizers was one of the best things I've eaten in this year and will set the bar high for 2025. The ambiance of the restaurant is elegant but not stuffy!  Service was attentive but not too pushy. Can't wait to come back
What a wonderful experience.  Loved everything about it. The food was great. The wine and bubbly, devine.

Service.  Style.  Class.  But far from pretentious. You can dine simply or more complex. Or throw your credit card into the wind and order the five course tasting menu.  Everything was delicious. From the fois gras to the Lapin three ways. Classic dishes.  Simply prepared with love. An extra desert. Some red fruits gelee' exceptional coffee. A wine list that speaks your language with expert assistance.  
It's worth every moment you spend in their care.

Le Coucou restaurant is so beautiful and romantic- think Beauty and Beast castle with white brick! They have gorgeous chandeliers of candles and then long candlesticks on every table. 

Now onto the food- the bread basket is heaven! Warm soft sourdough bread with soft butter, I couldn't resist having 3 pieces. We started with the eggplant appetizer and split the lobster au poivre and filet with bone marrow. Everything was outstanding! I am biased towards steak but that was easily my favorite alongside the buttery, fluffy mashed potatoes. 

Do NOT skip out on dessert! We finished with the mango sorbet with meringue and it was incredible. This was such a special place to celebrate our anniversary and I can't wait to come back! 

The service throughout the entire experience was wonderful. Everyone was so kind and welcoming to us.
